skills.description: Use when full-length 16S amplicon reads from a long-read platform (PacBio/Nanopore) must be aligned to a reference 16S gene to detect intragenomic polymorphisms or derive strain-level substitution profiles in a microbiome sample.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-alignment-to-reference
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-alignment-to-reference Use when full-length 16S amplicon reads from a long-read platform (PacBio/Nanopore) must be aligned to a reference 16S gene to detect intragenomic polymorphisms or derive strain-level substitution profiles in a microbiome sample. The goal is to resolve insertions/deletions between intragenomic 16S copies — PacBio CCS deletion errors coincident with homopolymer runs make indel calls unreliable Only short-read sequencing of 16S variable regions (e.g., V4) is available, since it cannot achieve the taxonomic resolution of the full ~1500 bp gene The OTU clustering threshold of 99% identity is known not to separate intragenomic from inter-genomic variation for the species of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aligns full-length (~1500 bp) 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., PacBio CCS from human stool) to a reference 16S gene with Cross_match to tabulate per-position nucleotide substitution profiles that resolve intragenomic 16S gene copy variants at species/strain level. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Aligns full-length (~1500 bp) 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., PacBio CCS from human stool) to a reference 16S gene with Cross_match to tabulate per-position nucleotide substitution profiles that resolve intragenomic 16S gene copy variants at species/strain level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to resolve insertions/deletions between intragenomic 16S copies — PacBio CCS deletion errors coincident with homopolymer runs make indel calls unreliable Only short-read sequencing of 16S variable regions (e.g., V4) is available, since it cannot achieve the taxonomic resolution of the full ~1500 bp gene The OTU clustering threshold of 99% identity is known not to separate intragenomic from inter-genomic variation for the species of interest

skills.description: Use when aligning real vs simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads (e.g. Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC 16S, Phylotag) to their references and you need to test whether error profiles — especially terminal insertion spikes — are reproduced by a simulator.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-error-benchmarking
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-error-benchmarking Use when aligning real vs simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads (e.g. Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC 16S, Phylotag) to their references and you need to test whether error profiles — especially terminal insertion spikes — are reproduced by a simulator. Input is already an ASV/feature abundance table — use the abundance-correlation benchmarking workflow instead Reads are short-read or non-PacBio HiFi; the PBSIM difference-ratio model and HiFi circular-consensus error profile would not apply No reference amplicon sequences are available, since per-position error tabulation requires aligning reads to references http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Per-position error-profiling workflow that quantifies insertion/substitution/deletion rates across alignment position for PacBio HiFi 16S amplicon reads, comparing real sequencing data against MHASS/PBSIM-simulated reads to reproduce terminal-insertion error profiles. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Per-position error-profiling workflow that quantifies insertion/substitution/deletion rates across alignment position for PacBio HiFi 16S amplicon reads, comparing real sequencing data against MHASS/PBSIM-simulated reads to reproduce terminal-insertion error profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an ASV/feature abundance table — use the abundance-correlation benchmarking workflow instead Reads are short-read or non-PacBio HiFi; the PBSIM difference-ratio model and HiFi circular-consensus error profile would not apply No reference amplicon sequences are available, since per-position error tabulation requires aligning reads to references

skills.description: Use when raw demultiplexed paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (e.g. V4 2x250) must be clustered into operational taxonomic units at the 97% identity threshold with mothur, with taxonomy assigned against Silva/Greengenes/RDP training sets.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-otu-clustering
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-otu-clustering Use when raw demultiplexed paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (e.g. V4 2x250) must be clustered into operational taxonomic units at the 97% identity threshold with mothur, with taxonomy assigned against Silva/Greengenes/RDP training sets. Input is already an OTU/ASV feature table or taxonomy table rather than raw demultiplexed paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads The analysis target is shotgun metagenomics data — use the review's metagenomics workflow (metagenomics_analysis.sh) instead of the amplicon workflow Reads are not paired-end or not demultiplexed, since the workflow requires paired-end demultiplexed Illumina reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Best-practice 16S rRNA amplicon workflow that quality-filters raw paired-end reads and clusters them into OTUs at a predefined 97% identity threshold using mothur, as the OTU-based alternative to DADA2's ASV denoising path, followed by taxonomy profiling and phyloseq/ggplot2 visualization. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: Best-practice 16S rRNA amplicon workflow that quality-filters raw paired-end reads and clusters them into OTUs at a predefined 97% identity threshold using mothur, as the OTU-based alternative to DADA2's ASV denoising path, followed by taxonomy profiling and phyloseq/ggplot2 visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an OTU/ASV feature table or taxonomy table rather than raw demultiplexed paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads The analysis target is shotgun metagenomics data — use the review's metagenomics workflow (metagenomics_analysis.sh) instead of the amplicon workflow Reads are not paired-end or not demultiplexed, since the workflow requires paired-end demultiplexed Illumina reads

skills.description: Use when assessing whether a 16S variable region (e.g. V4) or full-length V1-V9 amplicon can achieve confident species-level taxonomy against a reference database such as Greengenes.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-taxonomic-classification Use when assessing whether a 16S variable region (e.g. V4) or full-length V1-V9 amplicon can achieve confident species-level taxonomy against a reference database such as Greengenes. Input is already a classified OTU/feature table or taxonomy assignment — re-classifying with classify.seqs adds nothing The goal is strain- or SNP-level discrimination of intragenomic 16S copies; the paper addresses that via full-length sequencing and 99% identity clustering, not Wang-classifier species assignment Amplicons come from a mock/in-vivo community without known source species, so the species-level failure rate against ground truth cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Classifies 16S rRNA amplicon sequences (in-silico or sequenced) against a Greengenes reference taxonomy using the mothur Wang Bayesian classifier, sweeping confidence cutoffs to quantify species-level classification failure per variable region. This skill grounds the paper's finding that the V4 sub-region fails to achieve confident species-level assignment for 56% of amplicons, while full-length V1-V9 nearly recovers it. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Classifies 16S rRNA amplicon sequences (in-silico or sequenced) against a Greengenes reference taxonomy using the mothur Wang Bayesian classifier, sweeping confidence cutoffs to quantify species-level classification failure per variable region. This skill grounds the paper's finding that the V4 sub-region fails to achieve confident species-level assignment for 56% of amplicons, while full-length V1-V9 nearly recovers it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a classified OTU/feature table or taxonomy assignment — re-classifying with classify.seqs adds nothing The goal is strain- or SNP-level discrimination of intragenomic 16S copies; the paper addresses that via full-length sequencing and 99% identity clustering, not Wang-classifier species assignment Amplicons come from a mock/in-vivo community without known source species, so the species-level failure rate against ground truth cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or reproducing taxonomic classification of 16S amplicon FASTQ data from synthetic mock communities across multiple profiler/reference-library combinations at genus and species level.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-taxonomic-profiling
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-taxonomic-profiling Use when benchmarking or reproducing taxonomic classification of 16S amplicon FASTQ data from synthetic mock communities across multiple profiler/reference-library combinations at genus and species level. Input is shotgun whole-genome metagenomic data rather than PCR-amplified 16S rRNA gene amplicon reads The goal is functional profiling or abundance estimation on an already-assembled feature table rather than taxonomic classification of raw 16S reads Reference libraries must be used exactly as retrieved from public repositories — the paper notes RefSeq versions require contamination removal before use http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce per-sample genus- and species-level taxonomic profiling of 16S amplicon mock community data by running five profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) against paired reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq 2018/2020), yielding one taxon-by-sample counts matrix per profiler–library pairing. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Reproduce per-sample genus- and species-level taxonomic profiling of 16S amplicon mock community data by running five profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) against paired reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq 2018/2020), yielding one taxon-by-sample counts matrix per profiler–library pairing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is shotgun whole-genome metagenomic data rather than PCR-amplified 16S rRNA gene amplicon reads The goal is functional profiling or abundance estimation on an already-assembled feature table rather than taxonomic classification of raw 16S reads Reference libraries must be used exactly as retrieved from public repositories — the paper notes RefSeq versions require contamination removal before use

skills.description: Use when you have a closed-reference Greengenes 13.8 OTU BIOM table (e.g., EMP 16S V4) and need to correct 16S copy-number bias or compute per-sample average copy number (ACN) to compare host-associated vs. free-living communities.
skills.name: 16s-copy-number-normalization
skills.search_text: 16s-copy-number-normalization Use when you have a closed-reference Greengenes 13.8 OTU BIOM table (e.g., EMP 16S V4) and need to correct 16S copy-number bias or compute per-sample average copy number (ACN) to compare host-associated vs. free-living communities. Input is a Deblur / exact-sequence table without Greengenes closed-reference OTU IDs — PICRUSt copy-number normalization requires Greengenes reference OTUs Data are already copy-number-normalized or you need shotgun functional profiles rather than 16S amplicon correction Samples lack environment ontology labels needed to assign free-living / plant-associated / animal-associated classes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Normalizes a 16S amplicon OTU table by predicted 16S rRNA gene copy number using PICRUSt, then computes abundance-weighted average copy number (ACN) per sample to distinguish host-associated from free-living communities in EMP 16S Release 1 data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Normalizes a 16S amplicon OTU table by predicted 16S rRNA gene copy number using PICRUSt, then computes abundance-weighted average copy number (ACN) per sample to distinguish host-associated from free-living communities in EMP 16S Release 1 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a Deblur / exact-sequence table without Greengenes closed-reference OTU IDs — PICRUSt copy-number normalization requires Greengenes reference OTUs Data are already copy-number-normalized or you need shotgun functional profiles rather than 16S amplicon correction Samples lack environment ontology labels needed to assign free-living / plant-associated / animal-associated classes

skills.description: Use when 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., QIAseq-panel Illumina libraries from sputum) need genus-level ASV profiling and Greengenes-based taxonomy, or when comparing hypervariable-region accuracy against a mock community.
skills.name: 16s-genus-level-taxonomic-profiling
skills.search_text: 16s-genus-level-taxonomic-profiling Use when 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., QIAseq-panel Illumina libraries from sputum) need genus-level ASV profiling and Greengenes-based taxonomy, or when comparing hypervariable-region accuracy against a mock community. Third-generation full-length 16S rRNA sequencing (e.g., Nanopore) is available — this skill is calibrated to the 300 bp Illumina MiSeq limit and the study did not compare against full-length reads Your pipeline requires the most current reference taxonomy — this workflow trains regions with the outdated Greengenes database rather than updated SILVA versions The sample type or regions differ (e.g., non-respiratory niches or V4–V6 comparisons) — findings are specific to sputum and the V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 combinations http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Infers bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 16S rRNA reads with Deblur and assigns Greengenes taxonomy collapsed at the genus level for respiratory (sputum) samples. Accuracy is benchmarked per combined hypervariable region (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community via ROC curves. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Infers bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 16S rRNA reads with Deblur and assigns Greengenes taxonomy collapsed at the genus level for respiratory (sputum) samples. Accuracy is benchmarked per combined hypervariable region (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community via ROC curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Third-generation full-length 16S rRNA sequencing (e.g., Nanopore) is available — this skill is calibrated to the 300 bp Illumina MiSeq limit and the study did not compare against full-length reads Your pipeline requires the most current reference taxonomy — this workflow trains regions with the outdated Greengenes database rather than updated SILVA versions The sample type or regions differ (e.g., non-respiratory niches or V4–V6 comparisons) — findings are specific to sputum and the V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 combinations

skills.description: Use when paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g. Illumina MiSeq V3–V4) from environmental water samples must be summarized as OTUs and phylum-level relative abundances to answer 'what is the prokaryotic composition?'
skills.name: 16s-metabarcoding-community-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: 16s-metabarcoding-community-composition-analysis Use when paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g. Illumina MiSeq V3–V4) from environmental water samples must be summarized as OTUs and phylum-level relative abundances to answer 'what is the prokaryotic composition?' Input is already a taxonomic/feature table rather than raw 16S FASTQ reads — the SILVAngs pipeline would be redundant The goal is eukaryotic/fungal diversity from ITS2 amplicons — those require consensus assembly and the 'Classify Sequences' tool with the Warcup V2 training set, not the 16S/SILVAngs workflow Strain-level resolution or functional profiling is needed — OTU clustering at 0.98/1.00 identity against SILVA SSU ref does not provide whole-genome resolution (the authors propose WGS-metagenomics for that) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Turns raw 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (here, V3–V4 region from trout farm inflow- and pond-water) into a phylum-level prokaryotic composition profile via the SILVAngs pipeline (SINA alignment, cd-hit-est OTU clustering, BLASTn against SILVA SSU ref). Used to quantify which bacterial taxa and relative abundances dominate a metaviromic/metabarcoding water sample. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Turns raw 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (here, V3–V4 region from trout farm inflow- and pond-water) into a phylum-level prokaryotic composition profile via the SILVAngs pipeline (SINA alignment, cd-hit-est OTU clustering, BLASTn against SILVA SSU ref). Used to quantify which bacterial taxa and relative abundances dominate a metaviromic/metabarcoding water sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomic/feature table rather than raw 16S FASTQ reads — the SILVAngs pipeline would be redundant The goal is eukaryotic/fungal diversity from ITS2 amplicons — those require consensus assembly and the 'Classify Sequences' tool with the Warcup V2 training set, not the 16S/SILVAngs workflow Strain-level resolution or functional profiling is needed — OTU clustering at 0.98/1.00 identity against SILVA SSU ref does not provide whole-genome resolution (the authors propose WGS-metagenomics for that)

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a DADA2-based amplicon workflow recovers expected taxon counts, strain-level micro-diversity, and abundance patterns from mock communities, or when measuring its wall-clock runtime scaling (1 vs 4 cores) on small datasets.
skills.name: 16s-mock-community-benchmarking
skills.search_text: 16s-mock-community-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a DADA2-based amplicon workflow recovers expected taxon counts, strain-level micro-diversity, and abundance patterns from mock communities, or when measuring its wall-clock runtime scaling (1 vs 4 cores) on small datasets. The input is already a feature/ASV table or processed OTU table rather than raw fastq reads You need relative read abundances to serve as estimates of true taxon abundances — the mock community results show read abundance does not correlate with ground-truth taxon abundance You need to resolve strain-level micro-diversity where classification confidence matters — 1 of the 3 Fusarium strains was misclassified despite correct micro-diversity detection http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark an amplicon ASV pipeline (dadasnake/DADA2) against ground-truth mock communities of bacteria/archaea (16S, e.g. ERR777696, PRJNA517390) and fungi (ITS2, PRJNA626434) by measuring wall-clock runtime at different core counts, strain-resolution of intra-genus micro-diversity, and correspondence of relative read abundances to known mock compositions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Benchmark an amplicon ASV pipeline (dadasnake/DADA2) against ground-truth mock communities of bacteria/archaea (16S, e.g. ERR777696, PRJNA517390) and fungi (ITS2, PRJNA626434) by measuring wall-clock runtime at different core counts, strain-resolution of intra-genus micro-diversity, and correspondence of relative read abundances to known mock compositions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/ASV table or processed OTU table rather than raw fastq reads You need relative read abundances to serve as estimates of true taxon abundances — the mock community results show read abundance does not correlate with ground-truth taxon abundance You need to resolve strain-level micro-diversity where classification confidence matters — 1 of the 3 Fusarium strains was misclassified despite correct micro-diversity detection

skills.description: Use when you have OTUs built at a 97% percent sequence similarity threshold and need to quantify how poorly clustered they are using MSD and BLD metrics, either across 16S hypervariable regions or across taxonomic groups.
skills.name: 16s-otu-compactness-analysis
skills.search_text: 16s-otu-compactness-analysis Use when you have OTUs built at a 97% percent sequence similarity threshold and need to quantify how poorly clustered they are using MSD and BLD metrics, either across 16S hypervariable regions or across taxonomic groups. When the analysis goal is de novo OTU clustering itself — this skill re-measures compactness of already-clustered OTUs, it does not cluster sequences When input sequences are not OTUs built from 16S amplicon data at a percent sequence similarity threshold (e.g. shotgun metagenomic bins or protein families) When only pairwise PSD similarity is needed — this skill specifically evaluates PSD-based OTUs with the alternative MSD and BLD metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Re-measures the compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs that were clustered at 97% pairwise sequence dissimilarity (PSD) by computing Mean Sequence Dissimilarity (MSD) and Branch Length Distance (BLD) between each OTU's representative sequence and all remaining member sequences, both per-region (HMP V1V3 vs V3V5) and per-taxon. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Re-measures the compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs that were clustered at 97% pairwise sequence dissimilarity (PSD) by computing Mean Sequence Dissimilarity (MSD) and Branch Length Distance (BLD) between each OTU's representative sequence and all remaining member sequences, both per-region (HMP V1V3 vs V3V5) and per-taxon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is de novo OTU clustering itself — this skill re-measures compactness of already-clustered OTUs, it does not cluster sequences When input sequences are not OTUs built from 16S amplicon data at a percent sequence similarity threshold (e.g. shotgun metagenomic bins or protein families) When only pairwise PSD similarity is needed — this skill specifically evaluates PSD-based OTUs with the alternative MSD and BLD metrics

skills.description: Use when 16S rRNA amplicon reads have already been clustered into OTUs (e.g. QIIME, 97% PSD threshold) and you need to re-evaluate OTU compactness or quantify how strongly MSD and BLD dissimilarities correlate, at read level or aggregated per OTU.
skills.name: 16s-otu-dissimilarity-metric-comparison
skills.search_text: 16s-otu-dissimilarity-metric-comparison Use when 16S rRNA amplicon reads have already been clustered into OTUs (e.g. QIIME, 97% PSD threshold) and you need to re-evaluate OTU compactness or quantify how strongly MSD and BLD dissimilarities correlate, at read level or aggregated per OTU. Input is raw unclustered amplicon reads — OTUs must already exist (the article uses QIIME-based OTUs from the HMP computed with PSD at 97% sequence similarity) You need de novo phylogenetic placement or tree building — this skill only compares precomputed MSD/BLD dissimilarities, it does not compute phylogenies from scratch The analysis concerns non-16S marker genes — the article's claims (e.g. 80.5% of V3V5 OTUs with MSD > 0.03 from the representative) are specific to 16S rRNA hypervariable regions V1V3 and V3V5 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Compares three 16S rRNA dissimilarity metrics — percent sequence similarity (PSD), MSA-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD), and phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) — across HMP V1V3 and V3V5 OTU members to quantify how much evolutionary divergence the 97% similarity threshold and MSD hide relative to BLD. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Compares three 16S rRNA dissimilarity metrics — percent sequence similarity (PSD), MSA-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD), and phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) — across HMP V1V3 and V3V5 OTU members to quantify how much evolutionary divergence the 97% similarity threshold and MSD hide relative to BLD.

skills.description: Use when full-length 16S reference sequences must be converted into in-silico amplicons for commonly used sub-regions (e.g., V4, V1–V3, V3–V5) to assess how much taxonomic resolution short-read sub-region sequencing loses relative to the full gene.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-subregion-amplicon-filtering
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-subregion-amplicon-filtering Use when full-length 16S reference sequences must be converted into in-silico amplicons for commonly used sub-regions (e.g., V4, V1–V3, V3–V5) to assess how much taxonomic resolution short-read sub-region sequencing loses relative to the full gene. Input sequences are already primer-trimmed amplicon reads or a feature table rather than full-length 16S reference sequences with primer-binding sites — Cutadapt will find no amplicon and everything will be discarded. The goal is to exploit the full discriminatory potential of the ~1500 bp gene (e.g., full-length Nanopore/PacBio analysis); this skill deliberately restricts sequences to partial variable regions. skills.summary: In-silico trimming of full-length 16S rRNA reference sequences (non-redundant Greengenes v13.8.99 FASTA) into sub-region amplicons (V4, V1–V3, V3–V5, V6–V9, V1–V9) using Cutadapt with study PCR primer pairs at ≤3 mismatches, then no-'N' and ±2-SD length filtering, to compare taxonomic resolution of sub-regions vs. the full ~1500 bp gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already primer-trimmed amplicon reads or a feature table rather than full-length 16S reference sequences with primer-binding sites — Cutadapt will find no amplicon and everything will be discarded. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metagenomes are real (non-synthetic) samples without a known ground-truth community composition — OPAL abundance-error metrics (Bray-Curtis, RMSE, TP/FP) require truth profiles The goal is strain-level population genomics (StrainPhlAn) or functional profiling (HUMAnN) rather than species-level abundance quantification Communities are dominated by viral, eukaryotic, or under-characterized environmental taxa not captured by current uSGBs, where the article notes profiling remains incomplete

skills.description: Use when a feature table (BIOM) and per-feature values (e.g., predicted 16S rRNA copy number) must be combined into one abundance-weighted per-sample score for comparing environment classes such as animal-associated vs. free-living.
skills.name: abundance-weighted-community-metric-computation
skills.search_text: abundance-weighted-community-metric-computation Use when a feature table (BIOM) and per-feature values (e.g., predicted 16S rRNA copy number) must be combined into one abundance-weighted per-sample score for comparing environment classes such as animal-associated vs. free-living. The feature table is not closed-reference picked against Greengenes 13.8, so PICRUSt copy-number predictions cannot be joined to OTU IDs The analysis goal is sequence-variant level (e.g., Deblur exact sequences) rather than Greengenes reference OTU-level functional inference Samples lack environment ontology labels, so the free-living / plant-associated / animal-associated classes cannot be assigned http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-sample community-level metrics as abundance-weighted averages over OTU features, exemplified by the average 16S rRNA copy number (ACN) on the EMP 16S Release 1 closed-reference Greengenes 13.8 table normalized with PICRUSt, to distinguish animal-associated from free-living/plant-associated communities. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Computes per-sample community-level metrics as abundance-weighted averages over OTU features, exemplified by the average 16S rRNA copy number (ACN) on the EMP 16S Release 1 closed-reference Greengenes 13.8 table normalized with PICRUSt, to distinguish animal-associated from free-living/plant-associated communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table is not closed-reference picked against Greengenes 13.8, so PICRUSt copy-number predictions cannot be joined to OTU IDs The analysis goal is sequence-variant level (e.g., Deblur exact sequences) rather than Greengenes reference OTU-level functional inference Samples lack environment ontology labels, so the free-living / plant-associated / animal-associated classes cannot be assigned

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ metabarcoding reads (e.g. 16S or ITS2 amplicons) may carry 3'-end adapter contamination and must be cleaned before quality trimming, merging, and OTU clustering or taxonomic classification.
skills.name: adapter-contaminant-trimming
skills.search_text: adapter-contaminant-trimming Use when raw FASTQ metabarcoding reads (e.g. 16S or ITS2 amplicons) may carry 3'-end adapter contamination and must be cleaned before quality trimming, merging, and OTU clustering or taxonomic classification. Contamination can occur at any read position, not just the 3'-end — use a tool like TagDust, which removes contaminated reads entirely The goal is 5'-end trimming — Scythe does not allow adapters to overlap the 5'-end and should not be used for 5'-trimming Reads have already been quality-trimmed — quality-based trimming could remove bases helpful for identifying 3'-end adapter contaminants, so Scythe should precede it, not follow it http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Removes 3'-end adapter contaminants from raw metabarcoding FASTQ reads using Scythe, a Naive Bayesian adapter trimmer (v0.994 BETA), before quality trimming and OTU clustering. Scythe is quality-aware, so it can detect adapters even where poor-quality bases cause mismatches. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Removes 3'-end adapter contaminants from raw metabarcoding FASTQ reads using Scythe, a Naive Bayesian adapter trimmer (v0.994 BETA), before quality trimming and OTU clustering. Scythe is quality-aware, so it can detect adapters even where poor-quality bases cause mismatches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Contamination can occur at any read position, not just the 3'-end — use a tool like TagDust, which removes contaminated reads entirely The goal is 5'-end trimming — Scythe does not allow adapters to overlap the 5'-end and should not be used for 5'-trimming Reads have already been quality-trimmed — quality-based trimming could remove bases helpful for identifying 3'-end adapter contaminants, so Scythe should precede it, not follow it

skills.description: Use when single-end FASTQ data lacks a known adapter sequence and you need to auto-detect and export candidate adapter sequences (e.g. Illumina TruSeq) to a FASTA for trimming or inspection.
skills.name: adapter-fasta-file-generation
skills.search_text: adapter-fasta-file-generation Use when single-end FASTQ data lacks a known adapter sequence and you need to auto-detect and export candidate adapter sequences (e.g. Illumina TruSeq) to a FASTA for trimming or inspection. Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, per the fastp README An adapter sequence is already known and supplied — fastp then trims directly against the provided sequence and automatic detection is unnecessary Data are paired-end, where fastp primarily relies on overlap analysis of PE reads rather than single-end k-mer seed detection http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates a FASTA file of adapter sequences automatically detected by fastp's Algorithm 1, which computes 10-mer seed frequencies from the first 1M FASTQ reads and extends seeds via nucleotide trees. It enables adapter trimming on single-end data without requiring adapters as input. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Generates a FASTA file of adapter sequences automatically detected by fastp's Algorithm 1, which computes 10-mer seed frequencies from the first 1M FASTQ reads and extends seeds via nucleotide trees. It enables adapter trimming on single-end data without requiring adapters as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, per the fastp README An adapter sequence is already known and supplied — fastp then trims directly against the provided sequence and automatic detection is unnecessary Data are paired-end, where fastp primarily relies on overlap analysis of PE reads rather than single-end k-mer seed detection

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how much adapter sequence remains in filtered FASTQ output from tools like fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, AfterQC or SOAPnuke, or compare adapter-removal quality across tools on PE150 data.
skills.name: adapter-sequence-mismatch-tolerant-search
skills.search_text: adapter-sequence-mismatch-tolerant-search Use when you must quantify how much adapter sequence remains in filtered FASTQ output from tools like fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, AfterQC or SOAPnuke, or compare adapter-removal quality across tools on PE150 data. Input reads are raw unfiltered FASTQ — the skill measures adapter residue after filtering, not adapter content before trimming The goal is adapter removal itself rather than benchmarking how well already-produced filtered outputs were trimmed Data are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio) — use fastplong-style preprocessing instead of this short-read PE150 benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 Post-filtering adapter residue assessment: scan FASTQ reads from each preprocessing tool's output for known 33 bp adapter sequences while sweeping an allowed-mismatch tolerance (0 through ~5), quantifying residual adapter contamination to benchmark adapter-removal performance. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Post-filtering adapter residue assessment: scan FASTQ reads from each preprocessing tool's output for known 33 bp adapter sequences while sweeping an allowed-mismatch tolerance (0 through ~5), quantifying residual adapter contamination to benchmark adapter-removal performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are raw unfiltered FASTQ — the skill measures adapter residue after filtering, not adapter content before trimming The goal is adapter removal itself rather than benchmarking how well already-produced filtered outputs were trimmed Data are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio) — use fastplong-style preprocessing instead of this short-read PE150 benchmark

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. Illumina NA12878 SRR952827) must be cleaned of adapters and low-quality bases before alignment and variant calling, and a fast all-in-one preprocessor is preferred.
skills.name: adapter-trimming-configuration
skills.search_text: adapter-trimming-configuration Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. Illumina NA12878 SRR952827) must be cleaned of adapters and low-quality bases before alignment and variant calling, and a fast all-in-one preprocessor is preferred. Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, as fastp is designed for short reads Adapter sequences cannot be auto-detected or non-standard UMI/low-complexity handling is required without reviewing fastp's optional flags http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configure adapter trimming and quality filtering on paired-end Illumina FASTQ data using fastp, whose adapter sequences are auto-detected and whose default quality filtering (qualified_quality_phred 15, unqualified_percent_limit 40, length_required 15) runs in a single scan and is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic or Cutadapt. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Configure adapter trimming and quality filtering on paired-end Illumina FASTQ data using fastp, whose adapter sequences are auto-detected and whose default quality filtering (qualified_quality_phred 15, unqualified_percent_limit 40, length_required 15) runs in a single scan and is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic or Cutadapt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, as fastp is designed for short reads Adapter sequences cannot be auto-detected or non-standard UMI/low-complexity handling is required without reviewing fastp's optional flags

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample species/SGB relative-abundance profiles from a large metagenome cohort annotated with host metadata (lifestyle, age) and need prevalence-ranked taxa or enrichment of unidentified taxa (uSGBs) per category.
skills.name: age-category-stratified-taxa-prevalence
skills.search_text: age-category-stratified-taxa-prevalence Use when you have per-sample species/SGB relative-abundance profiles from a large metagenome cohort annotated with host metadata (lifestyle, age) and need prevalence-ranked taxa or enrichment of unidentified taxa (uSGBs) per category. Input is already an aggregated feature/abundance table without raw reads — MetaPhlAn 4 profiling from shotgun reads is the prerequisite step The goal is strain-level genomic or population-genetic analysis (use StrainPhlAn) rather than taxon prevalence across sample strata Samples come from environmental, nonhost-associated, or under-characterized habitats, where sequences are highly enriched for content not captured by current uSGBs http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes and stratifies taxon (SGB-level) prevalence — the fraction of samples in which each taxon is detected — across host categories such as lifestyle (westernized vs nonwesternized) and age (childhood vs adult), using MetaPhlAn 4 profiles of large human gut metagenome collections. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Computes and stratifies taxon (SGB-level) prevalence — the fraction of samples in which each taxon is detected — across host categories such as lifestyle (westernized vs nonwesternized) and age (childhood vs adult), using MetaPhlAn 4 profiles of large human gut metagenome collections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated feature/abundance table without raw reads — MetaPhlAn 4 profiling from shotgun reads is the prerequisite step The goal is strain-level genomic or population-genetic analysis (use StrainPhlAn) rather than taxon prevalence across sample strata Samples come from environmental, nonhost-associated, or under-characterized habitats, where sequences are highly enriched for content not captured by current uSGBs

skills.description: Use when long-read metagenomic reads map to a reference database but identity or coverage patterns suggest the sample genome is absent or diverged from the database, e.g. HMP7 Actinomyces meyeri or CAMI samples.
skills.name: alignment-identity-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: alignment-identity-distribution-analysis Use when long-read metagenomic reads map to a reference database but identity or coverage patterns suggest the sample genome is absent or diverged from the database, e.g. HMP7 Actinomyces meyeri or CAMI samples. Sample genomes or close relatives are confidently in the database and identities cluster at the expected ~0.88 mode, so no mismatch analysis is needed Sample has a high proportion of short reads, since reads below the minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations Precise base-to-base alignments are required; MetaMaps estimates approximate alignment identities (Poisson/binomial approximations) rather than computing explicit alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Uses MetaMaps' per-read mapping output (mapping locations, estimated alignment identities, and coverage per 1000 bp window) to detect database-sample mismatches, e.g. an in-sample genome whose closest reference is divergent, by visualizing uneven read-depth coverage along the reference and a shift in the alignment-identity distribution away from its expected mode (~0.88 for correct references; ~82% median identity signals mismatch on CAMI). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Uses MetaMaps' per-read mapping output (mapping locations, estimated alignment identities, and coverage per 1000 bp window) to detect database-sample mismatches, e.g. an in-sample genome whose closest reference is divergent, by visualizing uneven read-depth coverage along the reference and a shift in the alignment-identity distribution away from its expected mode (~0.88 for correct references; ~82% median identity signals mismatch on CAMI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample genomes or close relatives are confidently in the database and identities cluster at the expected ~0.88 mode, so no mismatch analysis is needed Sample has a high proportion of short reads, since reads below the minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations Precise base-to-base alignments are required; MetaMaps estimates approximate alignment identities (Poisson/binomial approximations) rather than computing explicit alignments

skills.description: Use when mapping long reads (minimum length ~1000 bp) to a large reference database (>12,000 RefSeq genomes) and you need fast, per-location approximate alignment identity estimates instead of exact base-to-base alignments.
skills.name: alignment-identity-estimation
skills.search_text: alignment-identity-estimation Use when mapping long reads (minimum length ~1000 bp) to a large reference database (>12,000 RefSeq genomes) and you need fast, per-location approximate alignment identity estimates instead of exact base-to-base alignments. Sample contains a high proportion of short reads, or reads below the 1000 bp minimum length, since minimizer sets become too small to reliably determine mapping locations You need exact base-to-base alignments rather than approximate boundaries and identity estimates (MashMap does not compute alignments explicitly) Sample comprises many non-characterized entities absent or highly divergent from the reference database, where database-sample incongruity dominates assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Estimate alignment identity between long metagenomic reads (PacBio/ONT) and reference database genomes using a winnowed-minhash (MinHash/Jaccard-based) approach inherited from MashMap, as used in MetaMaps' approximate mapping stage, retaining candidate locations with estimated identity of at least 80%. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Estimate alignment identity between long metagenomic reads (PacBio/ONT) and reference database genomes using a winnowed-minhash (MinHash/Jaccard-based) approach inherited from MashMap, as used in MetaMaps' approximate mapping stage, retaining candidate locations with estimated identity of at least 80%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample contains a high proportion of short reads, or reads below the 1000 bp minimum length, since minimizer sets become too small to reliably determine mapping locations You need exact base-to-base alignments rather than approximate boundaries and identity estimates (MashMap does not compute alignments explicitly) Sample comprises many non-characterized entities absent or highly divergent from the reference database, where database-sample incongruity dominates assignment

skills.description: Use when a denoised DADA2/Deblur feature table (.qza) and sample metadata are available and the goal is to test whether amplicon communities separate by metadata factors such as location or size fraction.
skills.name: alpha-beta-diversity-analysis
skills.search_text: alpha-beta-diversity-analysis Use when a denoised DADA2/Deblur feature table (.qza) and sample metadata are available and the goal is to test whether amplicon communities separate by metadata factors such as location or size fraction. Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been denoised into a feature table by DADA2 or Deblur Representative sequences have not yet had taxonomy assigned or the feature table has not been filtered when the filtered run's diversity outputs are the target The analysis goal is denoising, trimming, or taxonomy classification rather than community separation testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes taxonomic, alpha, and beta diversity analyses on a denoised feature table using QIIME 2's core-metrics workflow within the Tourmaline Snakemake pipeline, including UniFrac distance matrices, PCoA ordinations, and PERMANOVA group-significance tests. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Computes taxonomic, alpha, and beta diversity analyses on a denoised feature table using QIIME 2's core-metrics workflow within the Tourmaline Snakemake pipeline, including UniFrac distance matrices, PCoA ordinations, and PERMANOVA group-significance tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been denoised into a feature table by DADA2 or Deblur Representative sequences have not yet had taxonomy assigned or the feature table has not been filtered when the filtered run's diversity outputs are the target The analysis goal is denoising, trimming, or taxonomy classification rather than community separation testing

skills.description: Use when an OTU table (or curated vs raw versions) must be validated against independent per-site species richness/composition data, e.g. metabarcoding paired with botanical survey counts.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-correlation-against-field-survey
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-correlation-against-field-survey Use when an OTU table (or curated vs raw versions) must be validated against independent per-site species richness/composition data, e.g. metabarcoding paired with botanical survey counts. No paired independent inventory data exist for the sampled sites, so no ground-truth richness can be regressed against OTU richness The goal is identifying single rare species rather than biodiversity estimates — LULU curation and this validation are not suited to that Input is a mock community with known genetic content; the authors note mock communities never have the complexity of real soil samples and recommend separate validation approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Validates OTU tables against paired field-survey ground truth by regressing OTU-inferred site richness on per-site survey species richness (extracting R2, slope, intercept) and comparing beta-diversity, as done with 130 Danish soil sites and 564 surveyed plant species in the LULU paper. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Validates OTU tables against paired field-survey ground truth by regressing OTU-inferred site richness on per-site survey species richness (extracting R2, slope, intercept) and comparing beta-diversity, as done with 130 Danish soil sites and 564 surveyed plant species in the LULU paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired independent inventory data exist for the sampled sites, so no ground-truth richness can be regressed against OTU richness The goal is identifying single rare species rather than biodiversity estimates — LULU curation and this validation are not suited to that Input is a mock community with known genetic content; the authors note mock communities never have the complexity of real soil samples and recommend separate validation approaches

skills.description: Use when benchmark metrics for multiple profiler/reference-library pairings are available and you need to test whether quality traits (sensitivity, specificity, error score, alpha diversity deviation) are correlated across pairings.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-deviation-analysis
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-deviation-analysis Use when benchmark metrics for multiple profiler/reference-library pairings are available and you need to test whether quality traits (sensitivity, specificity, error score, alpha diversity deviation) are correlated across pairings. Input is raw sequencing reads or a single profiler's output rather than an already-computed per-pairing benchmark metrics table The analysis goal is per-sample taxonomic profiling rather than cross-pairing quality-metric correlation Only one profiler-library pairing is available, leaving too few points for a meaningful Spearman rank correlation http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Computes Spearman rank correlations between quality metrics (species-level sensitivity vs. specificity, error score vs. alpha diversity deviation) across 16S profiler-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes/SILVA/RefSeq/Kraken Standard) and renders paired scatterplots with per-pairing centroid diamonds, showing sensitivity and specificity are correlated traits (r = 0.85). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Computes Spearman rank correlations between quality metrics (species-level sensitivity vs. specificity, error score vs. alpha diversity deviation) across 16S profiler-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes/SILVA/RefSeq/Kraken Standard) and renders paired scatterplots with per-pairing centroid diamonds, showing sensitivity and specificity are correlated traits (r = 0.85).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or a single profiler's output rather than an already-computed per-pairing benchmark metrics table The analysis goal is per-sample taxonomic profiling rather than cross-pairing quality-metric correlation Only one profiler-library pairing is available, leaving too few points for a meaningful Spearman rank correlation

skills.description: Use when an amplicon feature table (BIOM or QIIME 2 format) plus a sample metadata mapping file must be tested for significant group differences in alpha-diversity indices, with boxplot figures as output.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-group-comparison
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-group-comparison Use when an amplicon feature table (BIOM or QIIME 2 format) plus a sample metadata mapping file must be tested for significant group differences in alpha-diversity indices, with boxplot figures as output. The question is about beta-diversity group separation, which requires distance matrices, ordination (PCoA/NMDS/CPCoA), and PERMANOVA (vegan adonis) rather than per-sample alpha tests Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an already-processed feature table; upstream amplicon pipeline steps must run first The goal is taxonomic composition or differential-feature (biomarker) testing rather than within-sample diversity comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Tests whether experimental groups differ in alpha-diversity indices computed from an amplicon feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2 format), using ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, or Kruskal-Wallis tests and visualizing per-sample values as boxplots. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Tests whether experimental groups differ in alpha-diversity indices computed from an amplicon feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2 format), using ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, or Kruskal-Wallis tests and visualizing per-sample values as boxplots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about beta-diversity group separation, which requires distance matrices, ordination (PCoA/NMDS/CPCoA), and PERMANOVA (vegan adonis) rather than per-sample alpha tests Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an already-processed feature table; upstream amplicon pipeline steps must run first The goal is taxonomic composition or differential-feature (biomarker) testing rather than within-sample diversity comparison

skills.description: Use when a Tourmaline/QIIME 2 run has produced diversity outputs (.qzv) and the question is whether one metadata group (e.g., size fraction) has higher observed features than another, and at what sampling depth richness saturates.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-group-significance-comparison
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-group-significance-comparison Use when a Tourmaline/QIIME 2 run has produced diversity outputs (.qzv) and the question is whether one metadata group (e.g., size fraction) has higher observed features than another, and at what sampling depth richness saturates. The run is still pre-diversity: no .qzv diversity outputs exist yet (denoising with DADA2/Deblur or taxonomy assignment has not completed). The comparison target is beta diversity (between-sample community structure) rather than within-sample richness. Input is already a per-sample feature table exported from QIIME 2 — the group-significance .qzv parsing step is unnecessary. Verify within-sample (alpha) diversity differences between sample groups in a Tourmaline/QIIME 2 amplicon run by parsing the observed-features group-significance .qzv and the alpha-rarefaction .qzv, then stratifying per-sample richness against metadata (e.g., 5.0-μm vs 0.22-μm size fractions) and checking rarefaction plateau depth (~350 sequences/sample in the Lake Erie 16S test run). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Verify within-sample (alpha) diversity differences between sample groups in a Tourmaline/QIIME 2 amplicon run by parsing the observed-features group-significance .qzv and the alpha-rarefaction .qzv, then stratifying per-sample richness against metadata (e.g., 5.0-μm vs 0.22-μm size fractions) and checking rarefaction plateau depth (~350 sequences/sample in the Lake Erie 16S test run).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The run is still pre-diversity: no .qzv diversity outputs exist yet (denoising with DADA2/Deblur or taxonomy assignment has not completed). The comparison target is beta diversity (between-sample community structure) rather than within-sample richness. Input is already a per-sample feature table exported from QIIME 2 — the group-significance .qzv parsing step is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when comparing within-sample diversity (richness/evenness) across categorical groups — e.g., 16S hypervariable regions V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9 — on a genus-level ASV count table.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-index-calculation
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-index-calculation Use when comparing within-sample diversity (richness/evenness) across categorical groups — e.g., 16S hypervariable regions V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9 — on a genus-level ASV count table. When the input is already a diversity summary table rather than a per-sample ASV/genus abundance matrix (nothing to estimate; proceed directly to statistical testing). When the analysis goal is between-sample compositional dissimilarity (beta diversity, e.g., NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities) rather than within-sample richness/evenness. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Estimate per-sample alpha diversity (Chao1 richness, Shannon entropy, and inverse Simpson dominance) on genus-level 16S rRNA ASV abundance tables in R using phyloseq and vegan, then test for differences between sample groups (e.g., hypervariable regions) with the Kruskal–Wallis test. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Estimate per-sample alpha diversity (Chao1 richness, Shannon entropy, and inverse Simpson dominance) on genus-level 16S rRNA ASV abundance tables in R using phyloseq and vegan, then test for differences between sample groups (e.g., hypervariable regions) with the Kruskal–Wallis test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a diversity summary table rather than a per-sample ASV/genus abundance matrix (nothing to estimate; proceed directly to statistical testing). When the analysis goal is between-sample compositional dissimilarity (beta diversity, e.g., NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities) rather than within-sample richness/evenness.

skills.description: Use when rarefied 16S amplicon count tables from mock-community profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) need Shannon/Simpson/richness deviation scores against a ground-truth library.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-index-computation
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-index-computation Use when rarefied 16S amplicon count tables from mock-community profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) need Shannon/Simpson/richness deviation scores against a ground-truth library. Input is raw 16S FASTQ rather than an already-profiled, rarefied count table — taxonomic profiling (PathoScope/Kraken 2/DADA2) must run first The goal is genus/species-level classification accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, error score) rather than alpha-diversity deviation analysis Beta-diversity or differential-abundance questions, which are outside this deviation-from-ground-truth alpha-diversity workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes species-level alpha diversity (Shannon, Simpson via vegan::diversity; richness via breakaway_nof1 with log transform) on rarefied 10,000-read count tables from 16S mock-community profilers and on 1,000,000-virtual-read ground-truth libraries, then quantifies per-pairing absolute deviations to rank profiler/reference-library accuracy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Computes species-level alpha diversity (Shannon, Simpson via vegan::diversity; richness via breakaway_nof1 with log transform) on rarefied 10,000-read count tables from 16S mock-community profilers and on 1,000,000-virtual-read ground-truth libraries, then quantifies per-pairing absolute deviations to rank profiler/reference-library accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S FASTQ rather than an already-profiled, rarefied count table — taxonomic profiling (PathoScope/Kraken 2/DADA2) must run first The goal is genus/species-level classification accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, error score) rather than alpha-diversity deviation analysis Beta-diversity or differential-abundance questions, which are outside this deviation-from-ground-truth alpha-diversity workflow

skills.description: Use when a normalized (rarefied) OTU/feature table with uniform per-sample depth (e.g. 10,000 reads) is available and alpha diversity indices plus rarefaction curves are needed for downstream diversity analysis and visualization.
skills.name: alpha-diversity-index-computation
skills.search_text: alpha-diversity-index-computation Use when a normalized (rarefied) OTU/feature table with uniform per-sample depth (e.g. 10,000 reads) is available and alpha diversity indices plus rarefaction curves are needed for downstream diversity analysis and visualization. skills.description: Use when you have a dereplicated amplicon FASTA (each entry labeled with its abundance, e.g. seqID_1000) and need high-resolution, input-order-resilient OTU clustering of datasets from thousands up to tera-scale (hundreds of millions of unique sequences).

skills.search_text: amplicon-otu-clustering Use when you have a dereplicated amplicon FASTA (each entry labeled with its abundance, e.g. seqID_1000) and need high-resolution, input-order-resilient OTU clustering of datasets from thousands up to tera-scale (hundreds of millions of unique sequences). The input FASTA is not dereplicated or lacks abundance annotations in the headers — swarm requires strict dereplication and per-entry occurrence counts and will not work properly You intend to mimic a 97% global similarity threshold by setting a large d value — this is an incorrect use of swarm; clusters are naturally larger than d and small d values (1-3) should be used The raw reads have not been pair-assembled (e.g. with vsearch) and trimmed of adaptors/primers (e.g. with cutadapt) — preprocessing must precede dereplication and clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 De novo amplicon clustering into fine-scale OTUs with swarm (v3), using the local linking threshold d (default d = 1) instead of an arbitrary global similarity threshold, on strictly dereplicated FASTA inputs with abundance annotations. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: De novo amplicon clustering into fine-scale OTUs with swarm (v3), using the local linking threshold d (default d = 1) instead of an arbitrary global similarity threshold, on strictly dereplicated FASTA inputs with abundance annotations.
