skills.search_text: asv-exact-partial-miss-categorization Use when you have ASVs/OTUs from a mock community amplicon dataset and a reference fasta of expected sequences, and need to count how many variants are exact matches, near-matches, or unexpected relative to the known mock composition. Input is an environmental/community sample with no known expected taxon list — there is no reference set to define 'exact' or 'miss' categories. You need taxonomic classification of unknown sequences — this skill only matches against a closed mock reference set, not a general reference database or classifier. Your goal is to assess classifier accuracy (e.g., BOLD API vs. naive Bayes) rather than denoising/clustering recovery of mock sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Categorize denoised or clustered representative sequences from a biological mock community as 'exact' (100% identity), 'partial' (97%-99% identity), or 'miss' (<97% identity) by aligning each variant to a set of expected mock reference sequences requiring at least 97% coverage. This quantifies how well DADA2, Deblur, or VSEARCH processing recovers known mock taxa versus spurious variants. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Categorize denoised or clustered representative sequences from a biological mock community as 'exact' (100% identity), 'partial' (97%-99% identity), or 'miss' (<97% identity) by aligning each variant to a set of expected mock reference sequences requiring at least 97% coverage. This quantifies how well DADA2, Deblur, or VSEARCH processing recovers known mock taxa versus spurious variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an environmental/community sample with no known expected taxon list — there is no reference set to define 'exact' or 'miss' categories. You need taxonomic classification of unknown sequences — this skill only matches against a closed mock reference set, not a general reference database or classifier. Your goal is to assess classifier accuracy (e.g., BOLD API vs. naive Bayes) rather than denoising/clustering recovery of mock sequences.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ reads (e.g., 2 x 300 bp Illumina MiSeq libraries such as V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) must be denoised into ASVs as an alternative to OTU binning.
skills.name: asv-feature-table-generation
skills.search_text: asv-feature-table-generation Use when raw paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ reads (e.g., 2 x 300 bp Illumina MiSeq libraries such as V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) must be denoised into ASVs as an alternative to OTU binning. Input is already a denoised ASV feature table (e.g., BIOM) or the goal is downstream diversity/taxonomy analysis rather than read denoising. Reads are full-length 16S rRNA sequences from third-generation platforms: the article notes Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments and that DADA2 identified more real variants, so it is the better choice there. The aim is strain- or species-level resolution beyond collapsed genus-level assignments; this skill ends at genus-level taxonomic collapsing via Greengenes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Generates bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 16S amplicon reads by quality-filtering with FastQC (Q30), denoising with the Deblur pipeline, and screening chimeras against QIIME 2's non-chimeric 16S rRNA database, producing a BIOM feature table for genus-level assignment. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Generates bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from 16S amplicon reads by quality-filtering with FastQC (Q30), denoising with the Deblur pipeline, and screening chimeras against QIIME 2's non-chimeric 16S rRNA database, producing a BIOM feature table for genus-level assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a denoised ASV feature table (e.g., BIOM) or the goal is downstream diversity/taxonomy analysis rather than read denoising. Reads are full-length 16S rRNA sequences from third-generation platforms: the article notes Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments and that DADA2 identified more real variants, so it is the better choice there. The aim is strain- or species-level resolution beyond collapsed genus-level assignments; this skill ends at genus-level taxonomic collapsing via Greengenes.

skills.description: Use when running PEMA on quality-filtered, dereplicated Illumina .fastq.gz amplicon reads (16S/18S/ITS/12S/COI) and the study objective calls for ASV inference rather than VSEARCH OTU clustering.
skills.name: asv-inference-with-swarm
skills.search_text: asv-inference-with-swarm Use when running PEMA on quality-filtered, dereplicated Illumina .fastq.gz amplicon reads (16S/18S/ITS/12S/COI) and the study objective calls for ASV inference rather than VSEARCH OTU clustering. The study objective requires OTU clusters — PEMA's VSEARCH (or CROP) OTU clustering path should be used instead, especially since whether to use ASVs instead of OTUs should be based on each study's objectives Raw reads have not yet been through PEMA Part 1 (adapter/primer trimming, BayesHammer error correction, PANDAseq assembly, obiuniq dereplication) — Swarm should run on pre-processed reads Input data are not paired-end Illumina .fastq/.fastq.gz amplicon reads accepted by PEMA http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Infer amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from pre-processed eDNA metabarcoding reads using Swarm v2 as implemented in PEMA, with cluster radius tuned per marker gene (e.g. d=3 for 16S, d=20 for ITS2). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Infer amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from pre-processed eDNA metabarcoding reads using Swarm v2 as implemented in PEMA, with cluster radius tuned per marker gene (e.g. d=3 for 16S, d=20 for ITS2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study objective requires OTU clusters — PEMA's VSEARCH (or CROP) OTU clustering path should be used instead, especially since whether to use ASVs instead of OTUs should be based on each study's objectives Raw reads have not yet been through PEMA Part 1 (adapter/primer trimming, BayesHammer error correction, PANDAseq assembly, obiuniq dereplication) — Swarm should run on pre-processed reads Input data are not paired-end Illumina .fastq/.fastq.gz amplicon reads accepted by PEMA

skills.description: Use when a FASTQ-derived ASV occurrence table (read counts per ASV, sample and PCR replicate) must be stringently filtered to remove false positives such as PCR errors, chimeras, low-frequency noise, tag-jump artifacts, and false negatives from non-reproducible detections.
skills.name: asv-occurrence-table-filtering
skills.search_text: asv-occurrence-table-filtering Use when a FASTQ-derived ASV occurrence table (read counts per ASV, sample and PCR replicate) must be stringently filtered to remove false positives such as PCR errors, chimeras, low-frequency noise, tag-jump artifacts, and false negatives from non-reproducible detections. When the input is already a filtered, validated ASV table — reapplying occurrence filters would discard legitimate low-abundance detections. When the goal is denoising or clustering of raw reads (Swarm, Unoise, Deblur, DADA2) rather than occurrence-level validation of ASVs using control samples. When no negative controls, mock samples or PCR replicates are available, since VTAM's cutoff optimization explicitly depends on these experimental design elements. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Apply VTAM's occurrence-level filters (FilterLNF, FilterPCRerror, FilterMinReplicateNumber, FilterRenkonen, FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop/FilterIndel) to an ASV × sample × replicate read-count table, using control-sample-optimized cutoffs (e.g. lfn_read_count_cutoff=60, lfn_sample_replicate_cutoff=0.002, lfn_variant_cutoff=0.006, pcr_error_var_prop=0.2 for the bat dataset) to remove PCR errors, low-frequency noise, non-reproducible occurrences, chimeras and pseudogenes while minimizing false po metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Apply VTAM's occurrence-level filters (FilterLNF, FilterPCRerror, FilterMinReplicateNumber, FilterRenkonen, FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop/FilterIndel) to an ASV × sample × replicate read-count table, using control-sample-optimized cutoffs (e.g. lfn_read_count_cutoff=60, lfn_sample_replicate_cutoff=0.002, lfn_variant_cutoff=0.006, pcr_error_var_prop=0.2 for the bat dataset) to remove PCR errors, low-frequency noise, non-reproducible occurrences, chimeras and pseudogenes while minimizing false po
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a filtered, validated ASV table — reapplying occurrence filters would discard legitimate low-abundance detections. When the goal is denoising or clustering of raw reads (Swarm, Unoise, Deblur, DADA2) rather than occurrence-level validation of ASVs using control samples. When no negative controls, mock samples or PCR replicates are available, since VTAM's cutoff optimization explicitly depends on these experimental design elements.

skills.description: Use when processing merged ASV occurrence tables from metabarcoding datasets (e.g. bat, fish, shark COI/16S) and you need per-dataset filtering cut-offs that minimize false positives and false negatives using control samples.
skills.name: asv-occurrence-threshold-tuning
skills.search_text: asv-occurrence-threshold-tuning Use when processing merged ASV occurrence tables from metabarcoding datasets (e.g. bat, fish, shark COI/16S) and you need per-dataset filtering cut-offs that minimize false positives and false negatives using control samples. Datasets lacking mock community samples or negative controls, since VTAM's optimize step derives thresholds explicitly from known occurrences in control samples Raw FASTQ input that has not yet passed through VTAM's merge, sortreads, and filter steps, which are prerequisites for building the ASV occurrence tables Datasets where a single global threshold is required across samples, since this skill produces per-dataset (and per-marker) optima rather than one universal cut-off http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Tunes VTAM's ASV occurrence filtering thresholds (lfn_sample_replicate_cutoff, pcr_error_var_prop, lfn_variant_cutoff, lfn_read_count_cutoff) per dataset by explicitly using mock, negative control, and replicate samples, yielding dataset-specific optima such as read count cut-offs of 60 (bat), 10 (fish), and 40 (shark). metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Tunes VTAM's ASV occurrence filtering thresholds (lfn_sample_replicate_cutoff, pcr_error_var_prop, lfn_variant_cutoff, lfn_read_count_cutoff) per dataset by explicitly using mock, negative control, and replicate samples, yielding dataset-specific optima such as read count cut-offs of 60 (bat), 10 (fish), and 40 (shark).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lacking mock community samples or negative controls, since VTAM's optimize step derives thresholds explicitly from known occurrences in control samples Raw FASTQ input that has not yet passed through VTAM's merge, sortreads, and filter steps, which are prerequisites for building the ASV occurrence tables Datasets where a single global threshold is required across samples, since this skill produces per-dataset (and per-marker) optima rather than one universal cut-off

skills.description: Use when preparing raw 16S rRNA ASV abundance tables (tsv count tables plus two-column sample-group metadata) for multi-tool differential abundance testing, so that DA results are not driven by rare taxa.
skills.name: asv-prevalence-filtering
skills.search_text: asv-prevalence-filtering Use when preparing raw 16S rRNA ASV abundance tables (tsv count tables plus two-column sample-group metadata) for multi-tool differential abundance testing, so that DA results are not driven by rare taxa. Input is already a prevalence-filtered or relative-abundance table (prevalence computed on transformed tables is meaningless; ANCOM pre-processing explicitly expects absolute abundance) The metadata has more than two sample groupings — the pipeline metadata format specifies 'maximum 2 groupings' The goal is advice on rarefying for other analyses such as diversity metrics, which the article explicitly states is beyond the scope of this work http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Pre-process raw 16S rRNA ASV count tables by removing ASVs observed in fewer than 10% of samples within each dataset, producing prevalence-filtered abundance tables used as inputs to differential abundance (DA) testing in the 38-dataset hackathon comparison. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Pre-process raw 16S rRNA ASV count tables by removing ASVs observed in fewer than 10% of samples within each dataset, producing prevalence-filtered abundance tables used as inputs to differential abundance (DA) testing in the 38-dataset hackathon comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a prevalence-filtered or relative-abundance table (prevalence computed on transformed tables is meaningless; ANCOM pre-processing explicitly expects absolute abundance) The metadata has more than two sample groupings — the pipeline metadata format specifies 'maximum 2 groupings' The goal is advice on rarefying for other analyses such as diversity metrics, which the article explicitly states is beyond the scope of this work

skills.description: Use when a per-sample-replicate ASV read-count table with ASV sequences is available and low-frequency ASV occurrences that closely match a much more abundant ASV must be removed as PCR errors before downstream replicate/abundance filtering.
skills.name: asv-read-count-proportion-analysis
skills.search_text: asv-read-count-proportion-analysis Use when a per-sample-replicate ASV read-count table with ASV sequences is available and low-frequency ASV occurrences that closely match a much more abundant ASV must be removed as PCR errors before downstream replicate/abundance filtering. The occurrence table has already been through FilterPCRerror (or a denoiser such as DADA2/Unoise applied to the same end), so re-filtering would double-remove occurrences ASV sequences are unavailable, so a 'closely matching more abundant ASV' cannot be identified and the proportion rule cannot be evaluated The goal is filtering tag-jumps, contamination, or chimeras — VTAM handles those with other filters (FilterChimera, control-based LFN filtering), not FilterPCRerror http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Applies the VTAM FilterPCRerror logic to an ASV occurrence table: discards occurrences of an ASV whose reads are a low proportion of a closely matching, far more abundant ASV, treating them as likely PCR/sequencing errors. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Applies the VTAM FilterPCRerror logic to an ASV occurrence table: discards occurrences of an ASV whose reads are a low proportion of a closely matching, far more abundant ASV, treating them as likely PCR/sequencing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The occurrence table has already been through FilterPCRerror (or a denoiser such as DADA2/Unoise applied to the same end), so re-filtering would double-remove occurrences ASV sequences are unavailable, so a 'closely matching more abundant ASV' cannot be identified and the proportion rule cannot be evaluated The goal is filtering tag-jumps, contamination, or chimeras — VTAM handles those with other filters (FilterChimera, control-based LFN filtering), not FilterPCRerror

skills.description: Use when a metabarcoding occurrence table contains technical replicates per sample and non-reproducible ASV occurrences (e.g. tag-jumps, contaminants) must be removed by requiring occurrence repeatability across replicates.
skills.name: asv-replicate-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: asv-replicate-reproducibility-assessment Use when a metabarcoding occurrence table contains technical replicates per sample and non-reproducible ASV occurrences (e.g. tag-jumps, contaminants) must be removed by requiring occurrence repeatability across replicates. The sequencing design has only one replicate per sample, so occurrence reproducibility across replicates cannot be evaluated The goal is to remove whole poorly reproducible replicates (VTAM FilterRenkonen) rather than individual non-reproducible ASV-sample occurrences The occurrence table has already been replicate-filtered and you would risk double-filtering the same occurrences Implements the VTAM FilterMinReplicateNumber logic: for each ASV-sample pair in a replicate-structured occurrence table (read counts Nijk per ASV i, sample j, replicate k), counts the distinct replicates with non-zero reads and discards occurrences not reproduced across at least a minimum number of technical replicates (benchmark threshold of 2). metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Implements the VTAM FilterMinReplicateNumber logic: for each ASV-sample pair in a replicate-structured occurrence table (read counts Nijk per ASV i, sample j, replicate k), counts the distinct replicates with non-zero reads and discards occurrences not reproduced across at least a minimum number of technical replicates (benchmark threshold of 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing design has only one replicate per sample, so occurrence reproducibility across replicates cannot be evaluated The goal is to remove whole poorly reproducible replicates (VTAM FilterRenkonen) rather than individual non-reproducible ASV-sample occurrences The occurrence table has already been replicate-filtered and you would risk double-filtering the same occurrences

skills.description: Use when comparing amplicon/ASV tables produced by multiple metabarcoding pipelines (e.g., VTAM vs DALU vs OBIbaR) to quantify whether filtering stringency changes per-sample richness and inter-sample Jaccard dissimilarity.
skills.name: asv-richness-alpha-diversity-calculation
skills.search_text: asv-richness-alpha-diversity-calculation Use when comparing amplicon/ASV tables produced by multiple metabarcoding pipelines (e.g., VTAM vs DALU vs OBIbaR) to quantify whether filtering stringency changes per-sample richness and inter-sample Jaccard dissimilarity. Input is already a diversity/t-test result table rather than a per-sample ASV count or final taxa table The comparison does not involve control-validated pipeline outputs (e.g., raw FASTQ without a per-pipeline ASV table from VTAM/DALU/OBIbaR filtering) Single-pipeline analyses with no alternative pipeline to contrast richness against http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-sample ASV richness (alpha-diversity) and Jaccard-based beta-diversity from per-pipeline final taxa tables (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR) to benchmark metabarcoding pipelines across read-count cut-offs using t-tests in R. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Computes per-sample ASV richness (alpha-diversity) and Jaccard-based beta-diversity from per-pipeline final taxa tables (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR) to benchmark metabarcoding pipelines across read-count cut-offs using t-tests in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a diversity/t-test result table rather than a per-sample ASV count or final taxa table The comparison does not involve control-validated pipeline outputs (e.g., raw FASTQ without a per-pipeline ASV table from VTAM/DALU/OBIbaR filtering) Single-pipeline analyses with no alternative pipeline to contrast richness against

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple Tourmaline/DADA2 runs that differ only in dada2 truncation lengths (e.g., 100/150/200/250 bp) and you need per-run ASV length distributions plus taxonomy-assigned read counts to choose optimal truncation parameters.
skills.name: asv-sequence-length-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: asv-sequence-length-distribution-analysis Use when comparing multiple Tourmaline/DADA2 runs that differ only in dada2 truncation lengths (e.g., 100/150/200/250 bp) and you need per-run ASV length distributions plus taxonomy-assigned read counts to choose optimal truncation parameters. Data has not been through the Tourmaline qaqc step — no demultiplexed QIIME 2 artifact exists yet to run repseqs on The goal is OTU clustering rather than DADA2 ASV inference — the sweep relies on asv_method: dada2pe truncation parameters The analysis targets single-end data — the sweep grid here uses dada2pe with paired forward and reverse truncation lengths http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts and aggregates representative sequence (ASV) length distributions and Eukaryota read-assignment counts across DADA2 truncation-length sweep runs (100–250 bp) produced by the Tourmaline workflow, enabling selection of truncation lengths that best capture target organism diversity in the 2018 Lake Erie 16S rRNA dataset. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Extracts and aggregates representative sequence (ASV) length distributions and Eukaryota read-assignment counts across DADA2 truncation-length sweep runs (100–250 bp) produced by the Tourmaline workflow, enabling selection of truncation lengths that best capture target organism diversity in the 2018 Lake Erie 16S rRNA dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been through the Tourmaline qaqc step — no demultiplexed QIIME 2 artifact exists yet to run repseqs on The goal is OTU clustering rather than DADA2 ASV inference — the sweep relies on asv_method: dada2pe truncation parameters The analysis targets single-end data — the sweep grid here uses dada2pe with paired forward and reverse truncation lengths

skills.description: Use when cross-validating taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Deblur/Greengenes genus-level ASV tables from different 16S hypervariable regions) against a labeled mock-community control and you need AUC with a 0.95 confidence interval to rank region performance.
skills.name: auc-confidence-interval-estimation
skills.search_text: auc-confidence-interval-estimation Use when cross-validating taxonomic classifiers (e.g., Deblur/Greengenes genus-level ASV tables from different 16S hypervariable regions) against a labeled mock-community control and you need AUC with a 0.95 confidence interval to rank region performance. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than a denoised genus-level ASV table — the regions must first be processed with Deblur and Greengenes-based assignment collapsed at genus level There is no labeled positive control (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock community) to define reference taxa, so ROC sensitivity/specificity cannot be cross-validated Sequencing is full-length third-generation (e.g., Nanopore) 16S rRNA, where hypervariable-region choice is not the discriminating variable

skills.description: Use when 16S amplicon reads (full-length V1–V9 or partial V1–V3) from stool samples must be resolved to Bacteroides species-level relative abundances and cross-checked against mWGS quantification.
skills.name: bacteroides-taxonomic-abundance-comparison
skills.search_text: bacteroides-taxonomic-abundance-comparison Use when 16S amplicon reads (full-length V1–V9 or partial V1–V3) from stool samples must be resolved to Bacteroides species-level relative abundances and cross-checked against mWGS quantification. skills.when_to_use_negative: Short-read sequencing of a single 16S variable region (e.g., V4) is the only data available and species-level resolution is required — the paper shows none of the partial regions recaptured full-gene diversity The goal is strain-level discrimination via intragenomic 16S copy variants — that requires the paper's SNP-phasing substitution-profile approach, not 99% OTU clustering Input is already a taxonomic abundance table rather than raw/dereplicated amplicon reads

Input is not paired-end Illumina .fastq.gz reads (e.g., already a feature table or single-end reads outside the pipeline's design scope) The 12S marker gene needs OTU clustering via VSEARCH — PEMA supports 12S only for ASV inference with Swarm, not VSEARCH OTUs A single fixed algorithm run with no intent to explore alternative tools or parameters is needed, so checkpoint-based partial re-execution adds no benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implement a multi-part metabarcoding pipeline as a BigDataScript (BDS) script so that checkpoint files enable partial re-execution and crash recovery, letting users swap algorithms or parameters for individual steps (e.g., OTU clustering vs. ASV inference) without rerunning the whole pipeline. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022

skills.description: Use when a statistical test (e.g., a linear mixed model with diet as fixed effect) has been run independently for many taxa or features, such as hundreds of SGBs, and raw p-values must be converted into BH-adjusted FDR values before declaring biomarkers.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when a statistical test (e.g., a linear mixed model with diet as fixed effect) has been run independently for many taxa or features, such as hundreds of SGBs, and raw p-values must be converted into BH-adjusted FDR values before declaring biomarkers. There is only a single hypothesis test, so no multiple-testing correction is needed. The analysis requires strict control of family-wise error rate (e.g., confirmatory claims) — BH controls expected false discoveries, not the probability of any false positive; a Bonferroni-style correction would be the wrong-tool counterpart to reach for instead. The p-values are not a valid test family (e.g., they come from different nested test stages or dependent subsets), which can distort BH calibration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to the per-taxon association p-values produced by high-dimensional testing (here, per-SGB linear mixed models of diet), so that a controlled set of significant biomarkers can be reported. In the source study this step gates which MetaPhlAn 4 SGBs are called high-fat-diet biomarkers at FDR < 0.2. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to the per-taxon association p-values produced by high-dimensional testing (here, per-SGB linear mixed models of diet), so that a controlled set of significant biomarkers can be reported. In the source study this step gates which MetaPhlAn 4 SGBs are called high-fat-diet biomarkers at FDR < 0.2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is only a single hypothesis test, so no multiple-testing correction is needed. The analysis requires strict control of family-wise error rate (e.g., confirmatory claims) — BH controls expected false discoveries, not the probability of any false positive; a Bonferroni-style correction would be the wrong-tool counterpart to reach for instead. The p-values are not a valid test family (e.g., they come from different nested test stages or dependent subsets), which can distort BH calibration.

skills.description: Use when a genus-level 16S rRNA abundance table (e.g., Greengenes-collapsed ASVs from QIIME 2) exists and the goal is to quantify and visualize compositional dissimilarity between sample groups via NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities.
skills.name: beta-diversity-analysis-of-16s-microbiome-data
skills.search_text: beta-diversity-analysis-of-16s-microbiome-data Use when a genus-level 16S rRNA abundance table (e.g., Greengenes-collapsed ASVs from QIIME 2) exists and the goal is to quantify and visualize compositional dissimilarity between sample groups via NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities. When the input is raw sequencing reads rather than a processed genus-level abundance table — upstream steps (FastQC quality filtering with Q30 cutoffs, Deblur denoising, chimera identification, Greengenes genus-level collapsing) must run first When the research question concerns within-sample richness or alpha diversity (e.g., Kruskal–Wallis comparisons of diversity indices or rarefaction curves) rather than between-sample compositional dissimilarity http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities on genus-level 16S rRNA ASV tables to test whether sample groups (e.g., hypervariable regions V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) differ compositionally and to visualize overlap or separation in ordination space. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities on genus-level 16S rRNA ASV tables to test whether sample groups (e.g., hypervariable regions V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) differ compositionally and to visualize overlap or separation in ordination space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw sequencing reads rather than a processed genus-level abundance table — upstream steps (FastQC quality filtering with Q30 cutoffs, Deblur denoising, chimera identification, Greengenes genus-level collapsing) must run first When the research question concerns within-sample richness or alpha diversity (e.g., Kruskal–Wallis comparisons of diversity indices or rarefaction curves) rather than between-sample compositional dissimilarity

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether OTU tables (e.g., from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP, DADA2 at multiple clustering levels) have realistic sample-to-sample composition, by comparing their beta-diversity to an independent field-survey reference value.
skills.name: beta-diversity-computation
skills.search_text: beta-diversity-computation Use when evaluating whether OTU tables (e.g., from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP, DADA2 at multiple clustering levels) have realistic sample-to-sample composition, by comparing their beta-diversity to an independent field-survey reference value. The goal is to identify or report on single rare species — the article notes LULU curation 'may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets' The data are not community abundance tables (OTU tables across multiple samples); beta-diversity comparison against survey ground truth is undefined without paired sample-level composition data Only alpha-diversity (per-site richness) is of interest — use the richness regression (R2, slope, intercept) workflow instead of beta-diversity Computes and compares beta-diversity (community composition turnover) for raw and LULU-curated OTU tables against ground-truth survey composition, as a validation metric for post-clustering curation of amplicon data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Computes and compares beta-diversity (community composition turnover) for raw and LULU-curated OTU tables against ground-truth survey composition, as a validation metric for post-clustering curation of amplicon data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify or report on single rare species — the article notes LULU curation 'may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets' The data are not community abundance tables (OTU tables across multiple samples); beta-diversity comparison against survey ground truth is undefined without paired sample-level composition data Only alpha-diversity (per-site richness) is of interest — use the richness regression (R2, slope, intercept) workflow instead of beta-diversity

skills.description: Use when a rarefied feature/OTU table (result/otutab_rare.txt), sample metadata with a Group column, and an OTU tree (result/otus.tree) are available and the goal is beta-diversity distance matrices, a PCoA plot, and pairwise group p-values.
skills.name: beta-diversity-distance-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: beta-diversity-distance-matrix-computation Use when a rarefied feature/OTU table (result/otutab_rare.txt), sample metadata with a Group column, and an OTU tree (result/otus.tree) are available and the goal is beta-diversity distance matrices, a PCoA plot, and pairwise group p-values. The feature table has not been rarefied/standardized to equal sampling depth — normalize for sequencing depth differences first (e.g., vegan resampling in EasyAmplicon) The analysis goal is alpha diversity or taxonomic composition rather than inter-sample dissimilarity and ordination UniFrac is required but no phylogenetic tree of representative sequences has been or can be built http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Compute inter-sample beta-diversity distance matrices (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, UniFrac) from a rarefied OTU/feature table using USEARCH, then ordinate the Bray-Curtis matrix via PCoA and test pairwise group differences as implemented in the EasyAmplicon pipeline. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: Compute inter-sample beta-diversity distance matrices (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, UniFrac) from a rarefied OTU/feature table using USEARCH, then ordinate the Bray-Curtis matrix via PCoA and test pairwise group differences as implemented in the EasyAmplicon pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has not been rarefied/standardized to equal sampling depth — normalize for sequencing depth differences first (e.g., vegan resampling in EasyAmplicon) The analysis goal is alpha diversity or taxonomic composition rather than inter-sample dissimilarity and ordination UniFrac is required but no phylogenetic tree of representative sequences has been or can be built

skills.description: Use when sample sets span multiple geographic sites and you need to test whether community composition turnover (beta-diversity) tracks geographic distance, e.g. isolation-by-distance in aquaculture or similar spatial metabarcoding designs.
skills.name: beta-diversity-geographic-correlation
skills.search_text: beta-diversity-geographic-correlation Use when sample sets span multiple geographic sites and you need to test whether community composition turnover (beta-diversity) tracks geographic distance, e.g. isolation-by-distance in aquaculture or similar spatial metabarcoding designs. When only inflow-water samples are available — the I-source samples showed no significant Mantel correlation (p > 0.05), so the isolation-by-distance signal is not expected there When beta-diversity is computed from eukaryotic (ITS) OTUs — the reported Mantel correlation was based on Bray-Curtis beta-diversity of prokaryotes only Tests whether Bray-Curtis beta-diversity (prokaryotic OTUs only) correlates with inter-farm geographic distance using a Mantel test, distinguishing water-source-specific patterns (inflow vs pond water). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Tests whether Bray-Curtis beta-diversity (prokaryotic OTUs only) correlates with inter-farm geographic distance using a Mantel test, distinguishing water-source-specific patterns (inflow vs pond water).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only inflow-water samples are available — the I-source samples showed no significant Mantel correlation (p > 0.05), so the isolation-by-distance signal is not expected there When beta-diversity is computed from eukaryotic (ITS) OTUs — the reported Mantel correlation was based on Bray-Curtis beta-diversity of prokaryotes only

skills.description: Use when amplicon feature tables (BIOM/QIIME 2) plus a sample metadata mapping file are available and the goal is to test whether experimental groups differ in community composition and visualize sample separation on ordination plots.
skills.name: beta-diversity-ordination-pcoa
skills.search_text: beta-diversity-ordination-pcoa Use when amplicon feature tables (BIOM/QIIME 2) plus a sample metadata mapping file are available and the goal is to test whether experimental groups differ in community composition and visualize sample separation on ordination plots. The question concerns within-sample (alpha) diversity only — use ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, or Kruskal-Wallis on alpha-diversity indices with boxplots instead Input is raw sequencing data that has not yet been reduced to a feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2) — run the upstream amplicon pipeline first The goal is functional potential prediction rather than community-composition comparison — PICRUSt2 applies to that task http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Computes beta-diversity distance matrices between samples (Bray-Curtis, UniFrac, Jaccard), ordinated them with PCoA/NMDS/CPCoA, and evaluates whether experimental groups differ using PERMANOVA, following the amplicon-analysis pipeline of Liu et al. 2020. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Computes beta-diversity distance matrices between samples (Bray-Curtis, UniFrac, Jaccard), ordinated them with PCoA/NMDS/CPCoA, and evaluates whether experimental groups differ using PERMANOVA, following the amplicon-analysis pipeline of Liu et al. 2020.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns within-sample (alpha) diversity only — use ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, or Kruskal-Wallis on alpha-diversity indices with boxplots instead Input is raw sequencing data that has not yet been reduced to a feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2) — run the upstream amplicon pipeline first The goal is functional potential prediction rather than community-composition comparison — PICRUSt2 applies to that task

skills.description: Use when a raw OTU/ASV count table from an eDNA amplicon study includes PCR replicate metadata, and contamination or sporadic detection must be removed before taxonomic grouping and downstream community analyses.
skills.name: binomial-occupancy-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: binomial-occupancy-probability-estimation Use when a raw OTU/ASV count table from an eDNA amplicon study includes PCR replicate metadata, and contamination or sporadic detection must be removed before taxonomic grouping and downstream community analyses. Input is already a quality-filtered feature/OTU table or lacks PCR replicate information needed for the binomial detection model Data are shotgun metagenomic or quantitative abundance data rather than multilocus amplicon presence/absence detections, where occupancy-based removal of negatives is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A site-occupancy decontamination filter for eDNA amplicon data that treats per-OTU detections across PCR replicates as independent binomial draws, estimates each OTU's occurrence probability, and drops OTUs estimated at <80% to remove contaminant/sporadic sequences. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: A site-occupancy decontamination filter for eDNA amplicon data that treats per-OTU detections across PCR replicates as independent binomial draws, estimates each OTU's occurrence probability, and drops OTUs estimated at <80% to remove contaminant/sporadic sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quality-filtered feature/OTU table or lacks PCR replicate information needed for the binomial detection model Data are shotgun metagenomic or quantitative abundance data rather than multilocus amplicon presence/absence detections, where occupancy-based removal of negatives is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when long reads (PacBio/ONT FASTQ) already have candidate approximate mappings from a minimizer-based stage and you need per-location posterior mapping qualities plus binomial-approximation alignment identities before EM-based composition estimation.
skills.name: binomial-probabilistic-alignment-scoring
skills.search_text: binomial-probabilistic-alignment-scoring Use when long reads (PacBio/ONT FASTQ) already have candidate approximate mappings from a minimizer-based stage and you need per-location posterior mapping qualities plus binomial-approximation alignment identities before EM-based composition estimation. Reads below the chosen minimum length: their minimizer sets are too small to reliably determine mapping locations, so the binomial scoring model has no reliable input Samples dominated by short reads — MetaMaps' minimizer-based approximate mapping and this scoring stage are specifically designed for long reads Exact base-level alignment identity is required — the binomial stage yields an approximate k-mer-based identity, not an explicit alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scores each candidate mapping location of a long read with MetaMaps' second-stage probabilistic model: the MinHash intersection size is modeled as Binomial(n = union size, p = (1-e)^k), where e is derived from the top hit's estimated alignment identity, yielding posterior mapping qualities that sum to 1 per read. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Scores each candidate mapping location of a long read with MetaMaps' second-stage probabilistic model: the MinHash intersection size is modeled as Binomial(n = union size, p = (1-e)^k), where e is derived from the top hit's estimated alignment identity, yielding posterior mapping qualities that sum to 1 per read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads below the chosen minimum length: their minimizer sets are too small to reliably determine mapping locations, so the binomial scoring model has no reliable input Samples dominated by short reads — MetaMaps' minimizer-based approximate mapping and this scoring stage are specifically designed for long reads Exact base-level alignment identity is required — the binomial stage yields an approximate k-mer-based identity, not an explicit alignment

skills.description: Use when you hold an OTU/taxon assignment table from a QC'd eDNA amplicon study and must reproduce or verify a reported taxonomic group count after agglomeration and marine-only filtering.
skills.name: biodiversity-count-verification
skills.search_text: biodiversity-count-verification Use when you hold an OTU/taxon assignment table from a QC'd eDNA amplicon study and must reproduce or verify a reported taxonomic group count after agglomeration and marine-only filtering. Input is raw sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ) that has not yet been quality-filtered and taxonomically assigned to OTUs — the skill operates downstream of bioinformatic QC. The analysis goal is species-level resolution of communities — the article notes the lower the taxonomy assignment, the lower the confidence, so species-level biodiversity tracking is not what this verification supports. The input table is already agglomerated to Family-or-higher rank — re-agglomeration would be redundant; only the terrestrial-filtering and count-verification steps would apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the curated biodiversity inventory from the Djurhuus et al. 2020 Monterey Bay eDNA time-series by agglomerating QC'd multilocus OTU assignments to Family-or-higher rank and filtering to marine taxa, yielding the reported totals of 663 taxonomic groups, 348 unique marine taxa, and 274 (78%) agglomerated at Family level. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Reproduces the curated biodiversity inventory from the Djurhuus et al. 2020 Monterey Bay eDNA time-series by agglomerating QC'd multilocus OTU assignments to Family-or-higher rank and filtering to marine taxa, yielding the reported totals of 663 taxonomic groups, 348 unique marine taxa, and 274 (78%) agglomerated at Family level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ) that has not yet been quality-filtered and taxonomically assigned to OTUs — the skill operates downstream of bioinformatic QC. The analysis goal is species-level resolution of communities — the article notes the lower the taxonomy assignment, the lower the confidence, so species-level biodiversity tracking is not what this verification supports. The input table is already agglomerated to Family-or-higher rank — re-agglomeration would be redundant; only the terrestrial-filtering and count-verification steps would apply.

skills.description: Use when a resolved eDNA metabarcoding species list needs independent validation against public occurrence records, e.g. checking whether taxa detected at a site (Vestamager) match national fauna databases.
skills.name: biodiversity-database-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: biodiversity-database-cross-referencing Use when a resolved eDNA metabarcoding species list needs independent validation against public occurrence records, e.g. checking whether taxa detected at a site (Vestamager) match national fauna databases. The taxon list has not yet been resolved to species level — unresolved OTUs cannot be meaningfully matched to faunistic records The sampling region lacks public occurrence database coverage (e.g. no Naturbasen/Fauna Europaea records), since absence of records may reflect database gaps rather than true absence The goal is community ecology comparison (e.g. clustering arthropod communities by plant species) rather than validation of detections against independent records Validates eDNA-derived arthropod taxon lists against independent biodiversity databases (Naturbasen/allearter, Fauna Europaea) by flagging each resolved species as present or absent at a specific locality and a broader region, then tallying concordance counts and percentages. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Validates eDNA-derived arthropod taxon lists against independent biodiversity databases (Naturbasen/allearter, Fauna Europaea) by flagging each resolved species as present or absent at a specific locality and a broader region, then tallying concordance counts and percentages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The taxon list has not yet been resolved to species level — unresolved OTUs cannot be meaningfully matched to faunistic records The sampling region lacks public occurrence database coverage (e.g. no Naturbasen/Fauna Europaea records), since absence of records may reflect database gaps rather than true absence The goal is community ecology comparison (e.g. clustering arthropod communities by plant species) rather than validation of detections against independent records

skills.description: Use when you have an OTU/ASV table from environmental samples paired with independent ground-truth species inventories (e.g., field surveys) and need to test whether a curation or filtering step improves α-diversity correspondence.
skills.name: biodiversity-metric-validation-against-field-survey
skills.search_text: biodiversity-metric-validation-against-field-survey Use when you have an OTU/ASV table from environmental samples paired with independent ground-truth species inventories (e.g., field surveys) and need to test whether a curation or filtering step improves α-diversity correspondence. No paired ground-truth inventory exists for the sampled sites — the R2 correspondence cannot be computed and the validation is meaningless You only need taxonomic composition or β-diversity assessment rather than α-diversity validation; the article notes rank-abundance tail-discard approaches may be adequate for composition but less so for α-diversity The survey and molecular data are not site-paired or sample-matched, so per-site richness regression is not defensible http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Validate molecular biodiversity estimates by regressing per-site OTU richness from metabarcoding tables against paired field-survey species richness, using R2 correspondence as the metric. Grounded in the Frøslev et al. 2017 LULU validation on 130 Danish sites of plant ITS2 soil metabarcoding paired with vascular plant survey data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Validate molecular biodiversity estimates by regressing per-site OTU richness from metabarcoding tables against paired field-survey species richness, using R2 correspondence as the metric. Grounded in the Frøslev et al. 2017 LULU validation on 130 Danish sites of plant ITS2 soil metabarcoding paired with vascular plant survey data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired ground-truth inventory exists for the sampled sites — the R2 correspondence cannot be computed and the validation is meaningless You only need taxonomic composition or β-diversity assessment rather than α-diversity validation; the article notes rank-abundance tail-discard approaches may be adequate for composition but less so for α-diversity The survey and molecular data are not site-paired or sample-matched, so per-site richness regression is not defensible

skills.description: Use when the analysis needs to pull EMP sample data into a BIOM table, join it with mapping-file metadata (e.g., EMPO levels), and subset/rarefy samples so that a classifier or diversity analysis operates on a clean, comparable feature table.
skills.name: biom-table-parsing-and-subsetting
skills.search_text: biom-table-parsing-and-subsetting Use when the analysis needs to pull EMP sample data into a BIOM table, join it with mapping-file metadata (e.g., EMPO levels), and subset/rarefy samples so that a classifier or diversity analysis operates on a clean, comparable feature table. The input is already a rarefied, chloroplast-filtered feature table aligned to metadata — re-filtering would discard data The analysis needs full-depth (non-rarefied) abundance information, since the 5,000-read rarefaction discards deeper samples' extra reads The target data are not in BIOM format and cannot be retrieved through redbiom/QIIME-compatible processing contexts (e.g., shotgun metagenomics stored in other formats) Load and subset BIOM feature tables and quality-filtered mapping files from the EMP 16S Release 1 catalogue (e.g., the ~25,000-sample Deblur table) using redbiom, Python/Pandas, and QIIME, applying count-based filters (rarefaction to 5,000 observations per sample, chloroplast exclusion) before downstream statistics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Load and subset BIOM feature tables and quality-filtered mapping files from the EMP 16S Release 1 catalogue (e.g., the ~25,000-sample Deblur table) using redbiom, Python/Pandas, and QIIME, applying count-based filters (rarefaction to 5,000 observations per sample, chloroplast exclusion) before downstream statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a rarefied, chloroplast-filtered feature table aligned to metadata — re-filtering would discard data The analysis needs full-depth (non-rarefied) abundance information, since the 5,000-read rarefaction discards deeper samples' extra reads The target data are not in BIOM format and cannot be retrieved through redbiom/QIIME-compatible processing contexts (e.g., shotgun metagenomics stored in other formats)

skills.description: Use when the input is an EMP/QIIME BIOM observation table plus a mapping file that must be loaded, subset by environment ontology labels, filterered (mc2, chloroplast), rarefied, or aggregated to taxonomic levels before statistics.
skills.name: biom-table-processing
skills.search_text: biom-table-processing Use when the input is an EMP/QIIME BIOM observation table plus a mapping file that must be loaded, subset by environment ontology labels, filterered (mc2, chloroplast), rarefied, or aggregated to taxonomic levels before statistics. The data is already a filtered, rarefied feature table with the specific analysis's sample subset selected — re-applying mc2/chloroplast/rarefaction filters would double-filter The analysis targets raw per-sample FASTQ/demultiplexed data rather than an already-built BIOM table; initial QIIME processing (demux, OTU picking) is a separate workflow step Shotgun metagenomic or metabolomics data, which the EMP pipeline handles with different SOPs rather than the 16S BIOM-table filters http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Load, filter, and transform BIOM-format feature tables and their mapping files from the EMP 16S Release 1 dataset using QIIME1/biom I/O and Python/Pandas, applying the release's quality filters (mc2 minimum sequence count of 2, chloroplast exclusion, rarefaction to 5,000 observations per sample) before computing richness, NODF nestedness, or PICRUSt-normalized copy-number statistics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Load, filter, and transform BIOM-format feature tables and their mapping files from the EMP 16S Release 1 dataset using QIIME1/biom I/O and Python/Pandas, applying the release's quality filters (mc2 minimum sequence count of 2, chloroplast exclusion, rarefaction to 5,000 observations per sample) before computing richness, NODF nestedness, or PICRUSt-normalized copy-number statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already a filtered, rarefied feature table with the specific analysis's sample subset selected — re-applying mc2/chloroplast/rarefaction filters would double-filter The analysis targets raw per-sample FASTQ/demultiplexed data rather than an already-built BIOM table; initial QIIME processing (demux, OTU picking) is a separate workflow step Shotgun metagenomic or metabolomics data, which the EMP pipeline handles with different SOPs rather than the 16S BIOM-table filters

skills.description: Use when a profiler's taxonomic assignment looks suspicious (e.g. 16S reads of a known mock community member mapped to an unexpected genus) and you need to verify, at the sequence level, whether a reference library entry is contaminated.
skills.name: blast-output-parsing
skills.search_text: blast-output-parsing Use when a profiler's taxonomic assignment looks suspicious (e.g. 16S reads of a known mock community member mapped to an unexpected genus) and you need to verify, at the sequence level, whether a reference library entry is contaminated. The goal is profiling reads against the reference library itself (use PathoScope 2.0 or Kraken 2), not auditing individual library entries for contamination Input is a 16S OTU/ASV feature table without any suspect sequence or reference entry to align The reference library has already been processed to remove contamination (the paper recommends using older, cleaned RefSeq libraries rather than re-auditing newer ones entry-by-entry) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Runs and parses pairwise BLAST alignments to quantify sequence-level contamination in reference databases, e.g. detecting an E. coli 16S rRNA contaminant embedded in a RefSeq T. flagellatus scaffold by extracting percent identity, alignment length, and bit score of the top HSP. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Runs and parses pairwise BLAST alignments to quantify sequence-level contamination in reference databases, e.g. detecting an E. coli 16S rRNA contaminant embedded in a RefSeq T. flagellatus scaffold by extracting percent identity, alignment length, and bit score of the top HSP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is profiling reads against the reference library itself (use PathoScope 2.0 or Kraken 2), not auditing individual library entries for contamination Input is a 16S OTU/ASV feature table without any suspect sequence or reference entry to align The reference library has already been processed to remove contamination (the paper recommends using older, cleaned RefSeq libraries rather than re-auditing newer ones entry-by-entry)

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode (primer-anchored ~200 bp or longer) query sequences via a top BLAST hit, or when benchmarking a classifier's false positive rate against the popular top BLAST hit approach.
skills.name: blast-percent-identity-assignment-criteria
skills.search_text: blast-percent-identity-assignment-criteria Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode (primer-anchored ~200 bp or longer) query sequences via a top BLAST hit, or when benchmarking a classifier's false positive rate against the popular top BLAST hit approach. When queries are likely absent from the reference database — the method implicitly assumes the query sequence is represented, and absent taxa produce confident misassignments (near-100% FPR) When a lower false positive rate matters more than speed — the RDP classifier with the CO1 Eukaryote v1 training set and a 0.60 genus-rank bootstrap cutoff reduces FPR to ~34% and is ~19x faster When assigning at the species rank with the current CO1Classifier releases — README cutoff tables provide no usable species-rank cutoff achieving 99% correct assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Applies the paper's 'good' top-BLAST-hit taxonomic assignment criterion for CO1 metabarcodes: run blastn (megablast task, evalue 1e-20) against a CO1 reference nucleotide database and accept an assignment only when percent identity >= 95% and alignment covers >= 85% of the query length. It is the baseline method the RDP CO1 classifier was benchmarked against. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Applies the paper's 'good' top-BLAST-hit taxonomic assignment criterion for CO1 metabarcodes: run blastn (megablast task, evalue 1e-20) against a CO1 reference nucleotide database and accept an assignment only when percent identity >= 95% and alignment covers >= 85% of the query length. It is the baseline method the RDP CO1 classifier was benchmarked against.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When queries are likely absent from the reference database — the method implicitly assumes the query sequence is represented, and absent taxa produce confident misassignments (near-100% FPR) When a lower false positive rate matters more than speed — the RDP classifier with the CO1 Eukaryote v1 training set and a 0.60 genus-rank bootstrap cutoff reduces FPR to ~34% and is ~19x faster When assigning at the species rank with the current CO1Classifier releases — README cutoff tables provide no usable species-rank cutoff achieving 99% correct assignments

skills.description: Use when CO1 metabarcode query fragments need taxonomic assignment by top BLAST hit, or when benchmarking assignment speed against the RDP classifier with explicit 'good' hit thresholds (identity >= 95%, coverage >= 85% of query).
skills.name: blast-top-hit-search-criteria
skills.search_text: blast-top-hit-search-criteria Use when CO1 metabarcode query fragments need taxonomic assignment by top BLAST hit, or when benchmarking assignment speed against the RDP classifier with explicit 'good' hit thresholds (identity >= 95%, coverage >= 85% of query). When you need probabilistic confidence scores (bootstrap support cutoffs at genus rank) rather than database similarity top hits — use the RDP classifier instead When the query sequences are not represented in the nucleotide reference database — the top BLAST hit method assumes the query sequence is actually present in the database When input is already a classified/feature table and the goal is summarization rather than raw sequence assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode query sequences via the top BLAST hit method against a locally installed copy of the NCBI nucleotide database, defining 'good' assignments as percent identity >= 95% with alignment spanning >= 85% of the query length, and recording sequences-per-minute throughput for speed benchmarking against the RDP classifier. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode query sequences via the top BLAST hit method against a locally installed copy of the NCBI nucleotide database, defining 'good' assignments as percent identity >= 95% with alignment spanning >= 85% of the query length, and recording sequences-per-minute throughput for speed benchmarking against the RDP classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need probabilistic confidence scores (bootstrap support cutoffs at genus rank) rather than database similarity top hits — use the RDP classifier instead When the query sequences are not represented in the nucleotide reference database — the top BLAST hit method assumes the query sequence is actually present in the database When input is already a classified/feature table and the goal is summarization rather than raw sequence assignment

skills.description: Use when clustering or comparing massive amplicon datasets (tera-scale FASTA inputs) where storing one byte per nucleotide or full sequence objects exhausts memory, and fast approximate membership testing between amplicons is needed.
skills.name: bloom-filter-hash-storage
skills.search_text: bloom-filter-hash-storage Use when clustering or comparing massive amplicon datasets (tera-scale FASTA inputs) where storing one byte per nucleotide or full sequence objects exhausts memory, and fast approximate membership testing between amplicons is needed. Input is raw FASTQ reads or non-dereplicated FASTA — swarm requires strict dereplication first, with each entry carrying an occurrence count The task requires exact all-vs-all sequence alignment output; the Bloom filter only supports approximate membership screening, not full similarity computation Amplicons contain ambiguity codes beyond A/C/G/T, which have no 2-bit encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A memory-reduction technique from swarm v3 that stores DNA amplicons as 2-bit packed sequences processed in fixed-length chunks, uses a fast Zobrist hash function to fingerprint them, and indexes the hash set in a Bloom filter to avoid storing full sequences — contributing to swarm v3's reduced memory footprint of up to 50%. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: A memory-reduction technique from swarm v3 that stores DNA amplicons as 2-bit packed sequences processed in fixed-length chunks, uses a fast Zobrist hash function to fingerprint them, and indexes the hash set in a Bloom filter to avoid storing full sequences — contributing to swarm v3's reduced memory footprint of up to 50%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads or non-dereplicated FASTA — swarm requires strict dereplication first, with each entry carrying an occurrence count The task requires exact all-vs-all sequence alignment output; the Bloom filter only supports approximate membership screening, not full similarity computation Amplicons contain ambiguity codes beyond A/C/G/T, which have no 2-bit encoding

skills.description: Use when building a reference database for taxonomic assignment of short COI metabarcoding reads (120–135 bp target fragment) where public curated barcoding sequences (BOLD) must be supplemented with non-target sequences to quantify/contain non-elasmobranch amplification.
skills.name: bold-c-oi-sequence-retrieval-replace
skills.search_text: bold-c-oi-sequence-retrieval-replace Use when building a reference database for taxonomic assignment of short COI metabarcoding reads (120–135 bp target fragment) where public curated barcoding sequences (BOLD) must be supplemented with non-target sequences to quantify/contain non-elasmobranch amplification. The target marker is not the 127 bp mitochondrial COI fragment amplified by the elasmobranch-specific primer pair (e.g. a longer fragment designed to resolve closely related Carcharhinus/Rhizoprionodon/Negaprion species, which the authors left to future work). A general-purpose public reference database release already covers the required taxa and no bespoke merging with non-target sequences is needed. The goal is assembling a reference database for non-elasmobranch eukaryotic groups; this skill is specific to elasmobranch COI plus ecoPCR-derived non-elasmobranch homologs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assembles a bespoke elasmobranch COI reference database for taxonomic assignment of 127-bp eDNA metabarcoding reads by retrieving all COI elasmobranch sequences from BOLD (boldsystems.org) with a custom R script and merging them with non-elasmobranch homologs extracted via ecoPCR in silico PCR. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assembles a bespoke elasmobranch COI reference database for taxonomic assignment of 127-bp eDNA metabarcoding reads by retrieving all COI elasmobranch sequences from BOLD (boldsystems.org) with a custom R script and merging them with non-elasmobranch homologs extracted via ecoPCR in silico PCR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target marker is not the 127 bp mitochondrial COI fragment amplified by the elasmobranch-specific primer pair (e.g. a longer fragment designed to resolve closely related Carcharhinus/Rhizoprionodon/Negaprion species, which the authors left to future work). A general-purpose public reference database release already covers the required taxa and no bespoke merging with non-target sequences is needed. The goal is assembling a reference database for non-elasmobranch eukaryotic groups; this skill is specific to elasmobranch COI plus ecoPCR-derived non-elasmobranch homologs.

skills.description: Use when deploying the RDP classifier on CO1 metabarcodes and you need defensible bootstrap support cutoffs per taxonomic rank and query fragment length (500 bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) before filtering assignments.
skills.name: bootstrap-support-cutoff-derivation
skills.search_text: bootstrap-support-cutoff-derivation Use when deploying the RDP classifier on CO1 metabarcodes and you need defensible bootstrap support cutoffs per taxonomic rank and query fragment length (500 bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) before filtering assignments. Input sequences are not expected to be represented in the reference set — the classifier is not meant to classify taxa absent from the training database, and leave-one-out estimates assume the query exists in the reference You need species-rank assignment: the genus-trained CO1 Eukaryote v1 set supports genus-level cutoffs, but species-rank cutoffs (NA for 99% correct) require the species-trained v2 set A cutoff matrix already exists for your exact training-set version and fragment lengths (e.g. README tables for v3 or v5.1.0) — reuse it instead of re-deriving Empirically derives rank- and fragment-length-specific minimum RDP classifier bootstrap support cutoffs that yield at least 99% correct taxonomic assignments, by leave-one-out testing of CO1 reference sets (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1) with repeated bootstrap subsampling of 8 bp words. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Empirically derives rank- and fragment-length-specific minimum RDP classifier bootstrap support cutoffs that yield at least 99% correct taxonomic assignments, by leave-one-out testing of CO1 reference sets (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1) with repeated bootstrap subsampling of 8 bp words.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are not expected to be represented in the reference set — the classifier is not meant to classify taxa absent from the training database, and leave-one-out estimates assume the query exists in the reference You need species-rank assignment: the genus-trained CO1 Eukaryote v1 set supports genus-level cutoffs, but species-rank cutoffs (NA for 99% correct) require the species-trained v2 set A cutoff matrix already exists for your exact training-set version and fragment lengths (e.g. README tables for v3 or v5.1.0) — reuse it instead of re-deriving

skills.description: Use when you need bootstrap support values or minimum cutoff thresholds (e.g. 70% for genus, 500 bp+ CO1) for RDP classifier taxonomic assignments of CO1 sequences, or when validating classifier accuracy across fragment lengths (50–500+ bp) and taxonomic ranks.
skills.name: bootstrap-support-estimation
skills.search_text: bootstrap-support-estimation Use when you need bootstrap support values or minimum cutoff thresholds (e.g. 70% for genus, 500 bp+ CO1) for RDP classifier taxonomic assignments of CO1 sequences, or when validating classifier accuracy across fragment lengths (50–500+ bp) and taxonomic ranks. Query taxa are not represented in the training database (e.g. singleton taxa excluded from leave-one-out testing) — classifier assignments and their bootstrap support are not meaningful Working with rDNA metabarcode markers (16S, ITS) whose accuracy shows distinctive stem-loop variation rather than the length-insensitive behavior of CO1 You need species-rank assignments — no bootstrap cutoff yields 99% correct species assignments (NA in Table 2); fall back to genus or more inclusive ranks http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Estimates confidence in RDP classifier taxonomic assignments of CO1 metabarcode sequences by randomly subsampling 8 bp words from each query and repeating classification 100 times, then deriving minimum bootstrap support cutoffs per rank and fragment length via leave-one-out testing. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Estimates confidence in RDP classifier taxonomic assignments of CO1 metabarcode sequences by randomly subsampling 8 bp words from each query and repeating classification 100 times, then deriving minimum bootstrap support cutoffs per rank and fragment length via leave-one-out testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query taxa are not represented in the training database (e.g. singleton taxa excluded from leave-one-out testing) — classifier assignments and their bootstrap support are not meaningful Working with rDNA metabarcode markers (16S, ITS) whose accuracy shows distinctive stem-loop variation rather than the length-insensitive behavior of CO1 You need species-rank assignments — no bootstrap cutoff yields 99% correct species assignments (NA in Table 2); fall back to genus or more inclusive ranks

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences with the RDP classifier and a bootstrap support threshold must be selected to match fragment length and target rank (e.g., genus vs species).
skills.name: bootstrap-support-threshold-application
skills.search_text: bootstrap-support-threshold-application Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences with the RDP classifier and a bootstrap support threshold must be selected to match fragment length and target rank (e.g., genus vs species). Query sequences are not represented in the reference/training set — high bootstrap support cannot be expected and false negatives will dominate Assignments at the species rank are required with the genus-trained CO1 Eukaryote v1 classifier — no genus-rank cutoff guarantees species-level accuracy (species is NA for 99% correct assignments) The taxonomic assignment method is top BLAST hit rather than the RDP classifier — bootstrap support cutoffs do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Applies rank- and fragment-length-specific RDP classifier bootstrap support cutoffs to control false positive rates in CO1 metabarcode taxonomic assignment. The article's Table 2 and the CO1Classifier README define minimum bootstrap proportions (e.g., 0.60 at genus rank for primer-anchored 200 bp fragments) that yield ~99% correct assignments. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Applies rank- and fragment-length-specific RDP classifier bootstrap support cutoffs to control false positive rates in CO1 metabarcode taxonomic assignment. The article's Table 2 and the CO1Classifier README define minimum bootstrap proportions (e.g., 0.60 at genus rank for primer-anchored 200 bp fragments) that yield ~99% correct assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query sequences are not represented in the reference/training set — high bootstrap support cannot be expected and false negatives will dominate Assignments at the species rank are required with the genus-trained CO1 Eukaryote v1 classifier — no genus-rank cutoff guarantees species-level accuracy (species is NA for 99% correct assignments) The taxonomic assignment method is top BLAST hit rather than the RDP classifier — bootstrap support cutoffs do not apply

skills.description: Use when comparing model performance between two feature sets (e.g., MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 taxonomic profiles) against a panel of markers and you need a robust, bootstrap-replicated estimate of AUC/R2 deltas.
skills.name: bootstrapped-cross-validation-performance-estimation
skills.search_text: bootstrapped-cross-validation-performance-estimation Use when comparing model performance between two feature sets (e.g., MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 taxonomic profiles) against a panel of markers and you need a robust, bootstrap-replicated estimate of AUC/R2 deltas. Input is already a single fitted model or a held-out test score and no comparison across feature sets is required — simple cross-validation suffices. The task is taxonomic profiling itself (generating SGB abundance tables from reads) rather than downstream model evaluation — use MetaPhlAn profiling, not this evaluation skill. Sample size is too small for repeated 80/20 splits to yield stable per-split AUC estimates (the anchor cohort here is n=1,001). http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Estimates and compares predictive performance of random forest classifiers/regressors (e.g., on MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 SGB abundance profiles) using 80/20 train–test splits repeated over 100 bootstrap iterations, reporting cross-validated AUC/R2 medians and per-marker deltas. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Estimates and compares predictive performance of random forest classifiers/regressors (e.g., on MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 SGB abundance profiles) using 80/20 train–test splits repeated over 100 bootstrap iterations, reporting cross-validated AUC/R2 medians and per-marker deltas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single fitted model or a held-out test score and no comparison across feature sets is required — simple cross-validation suffices. The task is taxonomic profiling itself (generating SGB abundance tables from reads) rather than downstream model evaluation — use MetaPhlAn profiling, not this evaluation skill. Sample size is too small for repeated 80/20 splits to yield stable per-split AUC estimates (the anchor cohort here is n=1,001).

skills.description: Use when you have HMP-style V1V3 or V3V5 16S OTUs with precomputed MSD and BLD dissimilarities between each representative sequence and its OTU members, and you need to test whether BLD reveals evolutionary divergence that MSD underestimates.
skills.name: branch-length-difference-interpretation
skills.search_text: branch-length-difference-interpretation Use when you have HMP-style V1V3 or V3V5 16S OTUs with precomputed MSD and BLD dissimilarities between each representative sequence and its OTU members, and you need to test whether BLD reveals evolutionary divergence that MSD underestimates. You have no phylogenetic tree or branch lengths — BLD cannot be computed and only percent/MSD dissimilarity is available, so the MSD-vs-BLD comparison is impossible. Your goal is OTU annotation or classification rather than assessing whether the 97% PSD-based clustering is evolutionarily compact. The OTUs were not built from percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) at a ~97% threshold, so the MSD/BLD-vs-0.03-threshold interpretation does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 A method for quantifying how phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) complements and corrects multiple sequence alignment-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD) when assessing 16S rRNA OTU compactness in HMP V1V3/V3V5 amplicon data, by correlating read-level and per-OTU-mean MSD/BLD pairs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: A method for quantifying how phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) complements and corrects multiple sequence alignment-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD) when assessing 16S rRNA OTU compactness in HMP V1V3/V3V5 amplicon data, by correlating read-level and per-OTU-mean MSD/BLD pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no phylogenetic tree or branch lengths — BLD cannot be computed and only percent/MSD dissimilarity is available, so the MSD-vs-BLD comparison is impossible. Your goal is OTU annotation or classification rather than assessing whether the 97% PSD-based clustering is evolutionarily compact. The OTUs were not built from percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) at a ~97% threshold, so the MSD/BLD-vs-0.03-threshold interpretation does not apply.

skills.description: Use when auditing 97%-threshold 16S OTUs (e.g., HMP V1V3/V3V5) for phylogenetic coherence by measuring BLD between a representative sequence and all other OTU members.
skills.name: branch-length-dissimilarity-quantification
skills.search_text: branch-length-dissimilarity-quantification Use when auditing 97%-threshold 16S OTUs (e.g., HMP V1V3/V3V5) for phylogenetic coherence by measuring BLD between a representative sequence and all other OTU members. OTUs are already defined by phylogenetic distance rather than percent sequence similarity, so re-measuring BLD compactness adds no new check No reference phylogeny or placement framework is available and only raw pairwise sequence similarity (PSD) is needed The analysis goal is taxonomic annotation of the representative rather than assessing OTU compactness http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Quantifies phylogenetic compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs by computing branch length distance (BLD) from each OTU's representative sequence to every member read on a maximum-likelihood tree, complementing alignment-based MSD. Used to show that OTUs clustered at 97% sequence similarity are often not compact under phylogenetic metrics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Quantifies phylogenetic compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs by computing branch length distance (BLD) from each OTU's representative sequence to every member read on a maximum-likelihood tree, complementing alignment-based MSD. Used to show that OTUs clustered at 97% sequence similarity are often not compact under phylogenetic metrics.

skills.search_text: chao1-richness-estimation Use when estimating total microbial richness (including unobserved taxa) from amplicon feature tables where Chao1's singleton/doubleton assumptions hold, and when choosing a denoiser that does not remove singletons. The feature table was produced by DADA2, which removes singletons — Chao1's singleton-dependent estimator cannot recover unobserved richness and will collapse toward observed features. Data are rarefied and the goal is maximum information retention — the study calculated alpha metrics on non-rarefied data (rarefied tables were only used for validation). The metric of interest is not singleton-dependent richness (e.g. Faith's phylogenetic diversity or entropy metrics), where the singleton-treatment constraint does not apply. Estimates unobserved microbial richness with the Chao1 metric, which depends directly on singleton counts. Because DADA2 discards singletons while DEBLUR retains them, Chao1 must be computed on singleton-preserving denoised feature tables. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-024-77864-y
skills.summary: Estimates unobserved microbial richness with the Chao1 metric, which depends directly on singleton counts. Because DADA2 discards singletons while DEBLUR retains them, Chao1 must be computed on singleton-preserving denoised feature tables.

skills.description: Use when building or modifying a multi-step pipeline where users may swap tools or tweak parameters (e.g., quality trimming, OTU clustering/ASV inference) and must avoid re-running upstream, already-completed stages.
