skills.search_text: checkpoint-based-partial-re-execution Use when building or modifying a multi-step pipeline where users may swap tools or tweak parameters (e.g., quality trimming, OTU clustering/ASV inference) and must avoid re-running upstream, already-completed stages. When a single monolithic run is acceptable and no tool/parameter exploration is planned — checkpoint bookkeeping adds overhead without benefit When the execution environment lacks BDS's ad hoc task parallelism (the partial re-execution relies on BDS checkpoint support, not a generic scheduler) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Implements partial re-execution of a metabarcoding pipeline by writing each stage of the PEMA workflow in BigDataScript (BDS) and relying on BDS roll-back checkpoint files, so that changing an algorithm or parameter for one step (e.g., OTU clustering vs. ASV inference) triggers re-execution of only the affected downstream steps instead of a full rerun. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Implements partial re-execution of a metabarcoding pipeline by writing each stage of the PEMA workflow in BigDataScript (BDS) and relying on BDS roll-back checkpoint files, so that changing an algorithm or parameter for one step (e.g., OTU clustering vs. ASV inference) triggers re-execution of only the affected downstream steps instead of a full rerun.

skills.description: Use when reproducing OTU counts from in-silico 16S sub-region amplicons (e.g., V4) across multiple identity thresholds (0.97/0.98/0.99) to benchmark how much diversity clustering recaptures relative to distinct full-length ~1500 bp sequences.
skills.name: chimera-detection-disabling-in-clustering
skills.search_text: chimera-detection-disabling-in-clustering Use when reproducing OTU counts from in-silico 16S sub-region amplicons (e.g., V4) across multiple identity thresholds (0.97/0.98/0.99) to benchmark how much diversity clustering recaptures relative to distinct full-length ~1500 bp sequences. Input is real sequencing reads with plausible PCR/sequencing chimeras — disabling uchime_denovo there would inflate OTU counts with artifact sequences; this skill applies only to in-silico amplicon benchmarks Input is already an OTU count table or a feature/ASV table rather than per-sub-region amplicon FASTA files Clustering in-silico 16S amplicons with USEARCH cluster_otus at 97%, 98%, and 99% identity thresholds while deliberately leaving chimera detection (uchime_denovo) disabled, so that OTU counts reflect pure sequence-diversity collapse rather than chimera-filtering artifacts. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1

skills.name: chimera-detection-in-16s-reads
skills.search_text: chimera-detection-in-16s-reads Use when raw 16S amplicon FASTQ reads (paired-end Illumina MiSeq, e.g. V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 pools) have been quality-filtered to Q30 and denoised with Deblur, and chimeric artifacts must be removed before genus-level taxonomic collapsing. Input is not 16S rRNA amplicon sequence data (e.g. shotgun metagenomic or ITS reads) — the QIIME 2 non-chimeric 16S rRNA reference and 99% threshold are calibrated for 16S amplicons Reads have not yet been quality-filtered (Q30) and denoised with Deblur — chimera screening is a downstream filter step, not a replacement for denoising http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Screens denoised 16S rRNA amplicon reads against the non-chimeric 16S rRNA database from QIIME 2, removing reads whose best hit similarity rate is less than 99%, so that downstream ASV-level (genus) taxonomic assignment with Deblur is not corrupted by chimeric sequences. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how divergent taxonomic class weights (e.g., cross-habitat EMPO 3 weights or uniform weights) inflate species-level classification error relative to source-habitat weights in QIIME 2.

When the sample's true source-habitat bespoke weights are already available and you simply want the best classification — use those directly rather than benchmarking cross-habitat degradation For samples from environments lacking sufficient characterization for bespoke weight assembly — the article recommends average weights from global microbial species distributions instead of uniform weights For highly unusual sample distributions (e.g., synthetic populations) — compile custom bespoke weights from existing samples rather than reusing habitat-level weights http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark how species-level naive Bayes classification error rates change when taxonomic class weights from a mismatched (cross-habitat) source are applied instead of bespoke habitat weights, and quantify degradation via linear regression of error rate on weight divergence. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6

skills.description: Use when evaluating a trained taxonomic classifier (e.g., RDP classifier with a CO1 training set) to determine how assignment accuracy changes with query fragment length and rank, or to pick bootstrap support cutoffs.

skills.search_text: classification-accuracy-tabulation Use when evaluating a trained taxonomic classifier (e.g., RDP classifier with a CO1 training set) to determine how assignment accuracy changes with query fragment length and rank, or to pick bootstrap support cutoffs. The query sequences are novel metabarcoding reads rather than training-set members with known taxonomy — leave-one-out testing is a benchmarking procedure, not an assignment pipeline. You need species-rank accuracy for fragments shorter than 500 bp where no cutoff achieves 99% correct assignments (NA in the cutoff matrix). The classifier training set contains only singleton taxa for the ranks of interest, since assignments are not meaningful for taxa unrepresented (or represented once) in the database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A leave-one-out benchmarking protocol that quantifies how RDP classifier taxonomic assignment accuracy for CO1 metabarcodes varies with sequence fragment length (500bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) and taxonomic rank, producing a table of correct-assignment proportions and minimum bootstrap support cutoffs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: A leave-one-out benchmarking protocol that quantifies how RDP classifier taxonomic assignment accuracy for CO1 metabarcodes varies with sequence fragment length (500bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) and taxonomic rank, producing a table of correct-assignment proportions and minimum bootstrap support cutoffs.

skills.search_text: classifier-database-version-benchmarking Use when comparing two releases of a classifier training set (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1 vs the 2013 Insecta Genbank-Genus set) to quantify taxonomic coverage and reference-sequence growth against published claims. skills.description: Use when an OTU/ASV table contains inflated richness from PCR/sequencing errors or intraspecific variation, and you need reference-free post-clustering curation that preserves rare but real OTUs.
skills.name: co-occurrence-based-error-detection
skills.search_text: co-occurrence-based-error-detection Use when an OTU/ASV table contains inflated richness from PCR/sequencing errors or intraspecific variation, and you need reference-free post-clustering curation that preserves rare but real OTUs. The goal is to identify single rare species in community data sets — LULU curation may not be suitable for this A reference-database-driven error correction is required — LULU is independent of a reference database and relies on co-occurrence rather than external taxonomic references The input is raw reads rather than an OTU table with a matching centroid sequence file and match list — the workflow requires an existing OTU table plus representative sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 The LULU algorithm identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs in an OTU table by evaluating co-occurrence patterns among samples, guided by pairwise sequence similarity from a match list, and merges flagged errors into more abundant 'parent' OTUs to produce a curated table with more realistic α-diversity estimates. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: The LULU algorithm identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs in an OTU table by evaluating co-occurrence patterns among samples, guided by pairwise sequence similarity from a match list, and merges flagged errors into more abundant 'parent' OTUs to produce a curated table with more realistic α-diversity estimates.

skills.description: Use when you have per-subnetwork edge lists (e.g. blue/grey seasonal subnetworks from a co-occurrence network) and need to rank taxa by connectivity to flag central hub taxa and their degree as a percentage of subnetwork taxa.
skills.name: co-occurrence-network-edge-weight-summation
skills.search_text: co-occurrence-network-edge-weight-summation Use when you have per-subnetwork edge lists (e.g. blue/grey seasonal subnetworks from a co-occurrence network) and need to rank taxa by connectivity to flag central hub taxa and their degree as a percentage of subnetwork taxa. Input is raw amplicon sequencing data (FASTQ) or an unclustered OTU/asv table — the skill operates on already-derived subnetwork edge lists, not on sequencing output The goal is to confirm direct predator–prey interactions — the paper notes co-occurrence may be 'a common response to an external driver' and requires hypothesis-based follow-up experiments Species-level hub identification is required — the paper warns that 'the lower the taxonomy assignment, the lower the confidence in that assignment becomes' (findings are at Family or higher rank) Ranks taxa in the blue (autumn) and grey (winter) subnetworks of the Monterey Bay 18-month eDNA community network by summed edge weights and node degree to identify the single most-connected hub taxon in each subnetwork. It reproduces the paper's reported hubs (Balaenopteridae, Rhodospirillaceae) and their connection counts as validation targets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1

skills.search_text: co1-reference-database-deployment Use when CO1 (cox1/COI) metabarcode amplicons need genus- or species-rank taxonomic assignment using a curated eukaryote reference set and the RDP classifier instead of top BLAST hit assignment. The query sequences are not CO1 (the training sets are built for eukaryote CO1 mtDNA; use SILVA, Greengenes, or UNITE for 16S/ITS data) A web portal is required — no portal exists yet for this RDP-based CO1 method; the CLI is the only route Species-rank assignment is needed with the CO1 Eukaryote v1 training set, for which no species-rank cutoff is available (NA) http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Deploy the pre-trained CO1 Eukaryote reference training sets from the terrimporter/CO1Classifier repository with the RDP classifier (v2.12/2.13) to assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences, and apply the correct length- and rank-specific bootstrap support cutoffs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Deploy the pre-trained CO1 Eukaryote reference training sets from the terrimporter/CO1Classifier repository with the RDP classifier (v2.12/2.13) to assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences, and apply the correct length- and rank-specific bootstrap support cutoffs.

skills.search_text: co1-reference-sequence-assembly Use when building a CO1 (cox1/COI) reference training set from NCBI GenBank for taxonomic classification of metabarcode reads, e.g. sampling taxa by phylum and filtering sequences by length, name completeness, and contamination. Input sequences are shorter than 500 bp or contain nucleotide ambiguities — the assembly filters these out, so they do not belong in the reference set The goal is classifying non-CO1 markers (e.g. prokaryote 16S rDNA or fungal ITS) — curated databases such as SILVA, Greengenes, or UNITE already exist for those markers A trained CO1 classifier already exists (e.g. the terrimporter/CO1Classifier releases) — download and use it rather than rebuilding the training set http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Assembles a CO1 mitochondrial DNA reference/training set for the RDP classifier by sampling taxa from the NCBI taxonomy database (emphasizing Arthropoda and Chordata), retrieving CO1 sequences from the NCBI nucleotide database, filtering by length and annotation quality, and formatting FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files for training. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Assembles a CO1 mitochondrial DNA reference/training set for the RDP classifier by sampling taxa from the NCBI taxonomy database (emphasizing Arthropoda and Chordata), retrieving CO1 sequences from the NCBI nucleotide database, filtering by length and annotation quality, and formatting FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files for training.

skills.description: Use when evaluating how CO1 metabarcode classification accuracy of the RDP classifier changes with fragment length (e.g., 500bp+ down to 50 bp) or taxonomic rank, to set bootstrap support cutoffs for short-read metabarcoding.
skills.name: co1-sequence-fragment-truncation
skills.search_text: co1-sequence-fragment-truncation Use when evaluating how CO1 metabarcode classification accuracy of the RDP classifier changes with fragment length (e.g., 500bp+ down to 50 bp) or taxonomic rank, to set bootstrap support cutoffs for short-read metabarcoding. The query sequences are full-length 500bp+ barcodes only and you need a production assignment rather than a length-benchmark — use a single classification run with the 70% genus-rank bootstrap cutoff instead. The benchmark targets rDNA metabarcode markers (e.g., 16S, ITS) rather than CO1 — the article notes rDNA markers show distinctive stem-loop variation in accuracy that this CO1-specific benchmark does not model. You need the newer 5-fold cross-validation cutoffs of the v5.1.0 release rather than reproducing the original v1 leave-one-out benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Truncates or subsamples CO1 reference sequences to metabarcode-scale fragment lengths (500bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) and runs leave-one-out testing with the RDP classifier v2.12 to benchmark how classification accuracy varies with fragment length and taxonomic rank. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Truncates or subsamples CO1 reference sequences to metabarcode-scale fragment lengths (500bp+, 400, 200, 100, 50 bp) and runs leave-one-out testing with the RDP classifier v2.12 to benchmark how classification accuracy varies with fragment length and taxonomic rank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query sequences are full-length 500bp+ barcodes only and you need a production assignment rather than a length-benchmark — use a single classification run with the 70% genus-rank bootstrap cutoff instead. skills.description: Use when long reads (e.g., HMP7 ONT/PacBio data) have been mapped with MetaMaps against a COG-annotated reference database and the goal is to rank functional categories (COG groups like S, K, E) by the number of reads overlapping annotated gene intervals.
skills.name: cog-functional-annotation-profiling
skills.search_text: cog-functional-annotation-profiling Use when long reads (e.g., HMP7 ONT/PacBio data) have been mapped with MetaMaps against a COG-annotated reference database and the goal is to rank functional categories (COG groups like S, K, E) by the number of reads overlapping annotated gene intervals. The sample has a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small for reliable mapping and remain unassigned Only taxonomic composition is needed (use the MetaMaps EM/WIMP classification output directly instead of gene-overlap profiling) The reference database lacks gene interval and COG/eggNOG-mapper annotation, so reads cannot be assigned to functional categories http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Profiles COG functional-category abundance from long-read metagenomic mappings by intersecting MetaMaps per-read mapping locations against eggNOG-mapper COG-annotated gene intervals in the reference database, then ranking categories by overlapping-read counts (e.g., HMP7: S > K > E). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Profiles COG functional-category abundance from long-read metagenomic mappings by intersecting MetaMaps per-read mapping locations against eggNOG-mapper COG-annotated gene intervals in the reference database, then ranking categories by overlapping-read counts (e.g., HMP7: S > K > E).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a CO1 classifier with metabarcoding-like queries: you need primer binding regions located on the CO1 barcoding region, or full-length 500 bp+ training sequences converted to primer-anchored 200 bp query fragments.

skills.search_text: coi-metabarcoding-primer-alignment Use when benchmarking a CO1 classifier with metabarcoding-like queries: you need primer binding regions located on the CO1 barcoding region, or full-length 500 bp+ training sequences converted to primer-anchored 200 bp query fragments. Query data are already real primer-trimmed amplicon reads — classify them directly rather than re-simulating fragments from full-length training sequences. Non-CO1 markers such as 16S rDNA (SILVA/Greengenes) or fungal ITS (UNITE): the Table S14 CO1 primer set and the X03240 D. yakuba reference do not apply. skills.description: Use when benchmarking a CO1 taxonomic classifier on fragments that mimic real Illumina metabarcode reads: you need primer-anchored 200 bp query sequences derived from full-length training-set FASTA records rather than arbitrary truncations.
skills.name: coi-primer-anchored-sequence-trimming
skills.search_text: coi-primer-anchored-sequence-trimming Use when benchmarking a CO1 taxonomic classifier on fragments that mimic real Illumina metabarcode reads: you need primer-anchored 200 bp query sequences derived from full-length training-set FASTA records rather than arbitrary truncations. Input consists of already-trimmed raw amplicon reads from a real sequencing run — this skill builds simulated query fragments from full-length training references, not processing live data Sequences are shorter than 500 bp or contain nucleotide ambiguities, since the CO1 training sets were filtered to 500bp+ ambiguity-free records The goal is actual taxonomic assignment of reads (use the trained RDP classifier directly) rather than constructing the benchmark fragment sets http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Simulates real metabarcode query reads by using CUTADAPT to trim CO1 training-set sequences at primer binding sites (≤10% primer mismatch allowed) and truncating retrieved sequences to 200 bp primer-anchored fragments. skills.description: Use when building or comparing COI (or other barcode-gene) reference databases for metabarcoding classification, when you need to quantify the effect of clustering radius or filtering on reference composition, or when merging BOLD- and GenBank-derived resources.
skills.name: coi-reference-database-curation
skills.search_text: coi-reference-database-curation Use when building or comparing COI (or other barcode-gene) reference databases for metabarcoding classification, when you need to quantify the effect of clustering radius or filtering on reference composition, or when merging BOLD- and GenBank-derived resources. The input is already a feature/ASV table and the goal is diversity metric computation or count transformation — this skill only covers reference database construction and comparison. The goal is to benchmark taxonomic classifiers (SINTAX, BLAST+LCA, Naive Bayes, BOLD API) on a fixed reference set rather than to build or curate the reference database itself. The marker gene is not COI or the target taxa are non-arthropod — the Family/Order completeness filters and BOLD arthropod retrieval steps here are COI/arthropod-specific. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 Curate arthropod COI reference databases by downloading BOLD (and GenBank-derived) records, filtering taxonomically incomplete sequences, dereplicating with LCA consensus taxonomy resolution, and clustering at defined identity radii (e.g., 99%) to quantify how clustering radius shapes database composition and taxonomic ambiguity. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Curate arthropod COI reference databases by downloading BOLD (and GenBank-derived) records, filtering taxonomically incomplete sequences, dereplicating with LCA consensus taxonomy resolution, and clustering at defined identity radii (e.g., 99%) to quantify how clustering radius shapes database composition and taxonomic ambiguity.
