skills.description: Use when the input is a Deblur exact-sequence BIOM observation table of EMP-style 90-bp V4 tag sequences and the goal is to recover unique sequences for exact-match searches against reference databases such as Greengenes or SILVA.
skills.name: deblur-observation-table-processing
skills.search_text: deblur-observation-table-processing Use when the input is a Deblur exact-sequence BIOM observation table of EMP-style 90-bp V4 tag sequences and the goal is to recover unique sequences for exact-match searches against reference databases such as Greengenes or SILVA. Input is an OTU-clustered table (closed- or open-reference picked against Greengenes 13.8/Silva 123) rather than Deblur exact sequences — exact 100%-identity matching is meaningless on consensus OTU IDs. Queries are not 90-bp V4 tag sequences (e.g., full-length amplicons or ITS sequences), since the skill's recapture metric is defined on Deblur V4 tags. The goal is approximate or partial sequence matching (identity < 1.0), which is outside the exact-sequence recapture design. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Loads a Deblur-generated exact-sequence BIOM observation table of 90-bp 16S V4 tag sequences, extracts the unique tag sequences, and (per the source task) aligns them against Greengenes 13.8 and SILVA 128 references with VSEARCH global alignment at 100% similarity to quantify reference recapture. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Loads a Deblur-generated exact-sequence BIOM observation table of 90-bp 16S V4 tag sequences, extracts the unique tag sequences, and (per the source task) aligns them against Greengenes 13.8 and SILVA 128 references with VSEARCH global alignment at 100% similarity to quantify reference recapture.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an OTU-clustered table (closed- or open-reference picked against Greengenes 13.8/Silva 123) rather than Deblur exact sequences — exact 100%-identity matching is meaningless on consensus OTU IDs. skills.description: Use when benchmarking 16S profiler/reference-library pairings on mock communities with known species composition, to rank methods by how closely their Shannon, Simpson, and breakaway_nof1 estimates match true alpha diversity.
skills.name: deviation-from-ground-truth-quantification
skills.search_text: deviation-from-ground-truth-quantification Use when benchmarking 16S profiler/reference-library pairings on mock communities with known species composition, to rank methods by how closely their Shannon, Simpson, and breakaway_nof1 estimates match true alpha diversity. Samples lack ground-truth composition (natural communities, not mock communities), so |estimated - true| deviations cannot be defined. Count tables are raw/unrarefied; diversity comparisons require equal sequencing depth (the workflow rarefies to 10,000 reads). Goal is genus-level rather than species-level accuracy assessment; the deviation reference values here are species-level. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies how far each 16S profiler/reference-library pairing deviates from mock-community ground truth by computing absolute deviations of Shannon, Simpson, and log breakaway_nof1 alpha-diversity estimates (on 10,000-read rarefied tables) from true values derived from 1,000,000-virtual-read ground-truth libraries. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Quantifies how far each 16S profiler/reference-library pairing deviates from mock-community ground truth by computing absolute deviations of Shannon, Simpson, and log breakaway_nof1 alpha-diversity estimates (on 10,000-read rarefied tables) from true values derived from 1,000,000-virtual-read ground-truth libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack ground-truth composition (natural communities, not mock communities), so |estimated - true| deviations cannot be defined. Count tables are raw/unrarefied; diversity comparisons require equal sequencing depth (the workflow rarefies to 10,000 reads). Goal is genus-level rather than species-level accuracy assessment; the deviation reference values here are species-level.

skills.description: Use when metagenomic taxonomic profiles (e.g. MetaPhlAn 4 SGB-level relative abundances) must be tested for differential abundance between two host conditions, such as high-fat vs normal-chow diet, while controlling for host covariates.
skills.name: diet-biomarker-identification-from-taxonomic-profiles
skills.search_text: diet-biomarker-identification-from-taxonomic-profiles Use when metagenomic taxonomic profiles (e.g. MetaPhlAn 4 SGB-level relative abundances) must be tested for differential abundance between two host conditions, such as high-fat vs normal-chow diet, while controlling for host covariates. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a taxonomic abundance table — profile first with MetaPhlAn 4 before biomarker testing The outcome of interest is functional potential rather than taxonomic abundance (use HUMAnN-style functional profiling instead) Environments dominated by sequences not captured by current uSGBs (e.g. environmental or nonhost-associated communities), where uSGB biomarker fractions will be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identify taxonomic biomarkers (SGBs) associated with a binary diet condition by fitting per-taxon linear mixed models on CLR-transformed MetaPhlAn 4 relative abundances, with covariate control and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and quantify the fraction of biomarkers that are uncharacterized species (uSGBs). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Identify taxonomic biomarkers (SGBs) associated with a binary diet condition by fitting per-taxon linear mixed models on CLR-transformed MetaPhlAn 4 relative abundances, with covariate control and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and quantify the fraction of biomarkers that are uncharacterized species (uSGBs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a taxonomic abundance table — profile first with MetaPhlAn 4 before biomarker testing The outcome of interest is functional potential rather than taxonomic abundance (use HUMAnN-style functional profiling instead) Environments dominated by sequences not captured by current uSGBs (e.g. environmental or nonhost-associated communities), where uSGB biomarker fractions will be unreliable

skills.description: Use when comparing absolute taxon abundances across experimental groups from compositional OTU/feature tables (samples × taxa counts) where unequal sampling fractions may bias relative-abundance-based tests.
skills.name: differential-abundance-bias-correction
skills.search_text: differential-abundance-bias-correction Use when comparing absolute taxon abundances across experimental groups from compositional OTU/feature tables (samples × taxa counts) where unequal sampling fractions may bias relative-abundance-based tests. Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The taxon of interest is a structural zero in a group (presence/absence test), since ANCOM-BC/BC2 are not designed to detect significant differences in taxa with structural zeros The goal is a multi-group or covariate-adjusted model beyond ANCOM-BC v1.0's discrete two-group/multi-group group.var support — use the newer ANCOMBC package functions instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies ANCOM-BC to estimate sample-specific sampling fractions via an E-M algorithm and correct the bias they induce in differential abundance analysis of microbiome count data, within a linear regression framework on the log scale. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Applies ANCOM-BC to estimate sample-specific sampling fractions via an E-M algorithm and correct the bias they induce in differential abundance analysis of microbiome count data, within a linear regression framework on the log scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The taxon of interest is a structural zero in a group (presence/absence test), since ANCOM-BC/BC2 are not designed to detect significant differences in taxa with structural zeros The goal is a multi-group or covariate-adjusted model beyond ANCOM-BC v1.0's discrete two-group/multi-group group.var support — use the newer ANCOMBC package functions instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating which microbiome DA method (e.g., ANCOM-BC, ANCOM, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, edgeR) controls FDR at a nominal level (e.g., 5%) while maintaining power, via simulation across balanced/unbalanced two-group designs.
skills.name: differential-abundance-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: differential-abundance-method-benchmarking Use when evaluating which microbiome DA method (e.g., ANCOM-BC, ANCOM, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, edgeR) controls FDR at a nominal level (e.g., 5%) while maintaining power, via simulation across balanced/unbalanced two-group designs. Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC itself does not control FDR well and benchmark conclusions may not generalize The proportion of differentially abundant taxa in the simulation is too large, which can cause slightly elevated FDR and confound the comparison The analysis goal is a single-dataset DA test rather than a method comparison — use the individual method (e.g., ANCOM-BC with two-group comparison) directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark differential abundance (DA) methods for microbiome compositional data by simulating data under a Poisson-Gamma model and comparing empirical False Discovery Rate (FDR) and power across designs, as done in the ANCOM-BC Nature Communications paper. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Benchmark differential abundance (DA) methods for microbiome compositional data by simulating data under a Poisson-Gamma model and comparing empirical False Discovery Rate (FDR) and power across designs, as done in the ANCOM-BC Nature Communications paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC itself does not control FDR well and benchmark conclusions may not generalize The proportion of differentially abundant taxa in the simulation is too large, which can cause slightly elevated FDR and confound the comparison The analysis goal is a single-dataset DA test rather than a method comparison — use the individual method (e.g., ANCOM-BC with two-group comparison) directly instead

skills.description: Use when comparing taxa between exactly two sample groups in 16S rRNA ASV/genera count tables, benchmarking which DA tools call significant features, or deciding whether to rarefy and prevalence-filter before DA testing.
skills.name: differential-abundance-testing-microbiome
skills.search_text: differential-abundance-testing-microbiome Use when comparing taxa between exactly two sample groups in 16S rRNA ASV/genera count tables, benchmarking which DA tools call significant features, or deciding whether to rarefy and prevalence-filter before DA testing. When the goal is diversity or ordination analysis rather than between-group DA testing — the authors state that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work'. When the metadata has more than two sample groupings — the pipeline metadata file supports a 'maximum 2 groupings'. When a single tool's output is sufficient for the biological claim — the paper found tools identify drastically different significant ASVs, so single-tool results are fragile. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Runs and interprets 14 differential abundance (DA) methods (ALDEx2 1.18.0, ANCOM-II, corncob 0.1.0, DESeq2 1.26.0, edgeR 3.28.1, LEfSe, Maaslin2 0.99.12, metagenomeSeq 1.28.2, limma voom, ANCOM, and rarefied/CLR test variants) on 16S rRNA ASV count tables with two sample groups, quantifying how many and which ASVs/genera each tool calls significant under common pre-processing choices. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Runs and interprets 14 differential abundance (DA) methods (ALDEx2 1.18.0, ANCOM-II, corncob 0.1.0, DESeq2 1.26.0, edgeR 3.28.1, LEfSe, Maaslin2 0.99.12, metagenomeSeq 1.28.2, limma voom, ANCOM, and rarefied/CLR test variants) on 16S rRNA ASV count tables with two sample groups, quantifying how many and which ASVs/genera each tool calls significant under common pre-processing choices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is diversity or ordination analysis rather than between-group DA testing — the authors state that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work'. When the metadata has more than two sample groupings — the pipeline metadata file supports a 'maximum 2 groupings'. When a single tool's output is sufficient for the biological claim — the paper found tools identify drastically different significant ASVs, so single-tool results are fragile.

skills.description: Use when simulated amplicon reads must be validated against real HiFi data by comparing per-genome error (edit distance) distributions and their shape (bimodal vs unimodal) across mock communities.
skills.name: distribution-shape-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: distribution-shape-comparison-across-datasets Use when simulated amplicon reads must be validated against real HiFi data by comparing per-genome error (edit distance) distributions and their shape (bimodal vs unimodal) across mock communities. Input is already a feature/ASV count table with no read-level sequences — edit distances cannot be computed Reads are short Illumina amplicon reads rather than PacBio HiFi long-read amplicon data; the error model and distributions being compared are HiFi-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates a microbiome HiFi sequencing simulator (MHASS) by comparing per-genome edit distance distributions of simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads against real sequencing data across three mock communities (Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, Phylotag/16S). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Validates a microbiome HiFi sequencing simulator (MHASS) by comparing per-genome edit distance distributions of simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads against real sequencing data across three mock communities (Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, Phylotag/16S).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/ASV count table with no read-level sequences — edit distances cannot be computed Reads are short Illumina amplicon reads rather than PacBio HiFi long-read amplicon data; the error model and distributions being compared are HiFi-specific

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 amplicon/metabarcode sequences (500 bp to 50 bp fragments) with the RDP classifier, or when selecting minimum bootstrap support cutoffs per taxonomic rank and sequence length.
skills.name: dna-barcode-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: dna-barcode-taxonomic-classification Use when assigning taxonomy to CO1 amplicon/metabarcode sequences (500 bp to 50 bp fragments) with the RDP classifier, or when selecting minimum bootstrap support cutoffs per taxonomic rank and sequence length. Query taxa are expected to be absent from the reference training set — the classifier cannot classify taxa not represented in the database and congeneric-sequence gaps cause false negatives, a particular concern in quarantine situations Species-rank assignment is required — the genus-ranked training sets (e.g., v1) report 'NA' cutoffs at species rank; use the species-ranked set (v2) or the species-level 95%-accuracy table instead Target marker is not CO1 — for prokaryote 16S or fungal ITS use SILVA, Greengenes, or UNITE reference sets rather than this CO1 training set http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Taxonomically classify animal CO1 metabarcode sequences using the RDP Naive Bayesian classifier with the CO1 Eukaryote training sets from the CO1Classifier repository, applying rank- and fragment-length-specific bootstrap support cutoffs to obtain at least 99% correct assignments. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Taxonomically classify animal CO1 metabarcode sequences using the RDP Naive Bayesian classifier with the CO1 Eukaryote training sets from the CO1Classifier repository, applying rank- and fragment-length-specific bootstrap support cutoffs to obtain at least 99% correct assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query taxa are expected to be absent from the reference training set — the classifier cannot classify taxa not represented in the database and congeneric-sequence gaps cause false negatives, a particular concern in quarantine situations Species-rank assignment is required — the genus-ranked training sets (e.g., v1) report 'NA' cutoffs at species rank; use the species-ranked set (v2) or the species-level 95%-accuracy table instead Target marker is not CO1 — for prokaryote 16S or fungal ITS use SILVA, Greengenes, or UNITE reference sets rather than this CO1 training set

skills.description: Use when ASV/MOTU tables from amplicon metabarcoding (e.g. DADA2 output for 16S rRNA or COI markers) need taxonomic assignment, arthropod-only filtering, and taxonomic richness or dominance summaries.
skills.name: dna-metabarcoding-taxonomic-assignment
skills.search_text: dna-metabarcoding-taxonomic-assignment Use when ASV/MOTU tables from amplicon metabarcoding (e.g. DADA2 output for 16S rRNA or COI markers) need taxonomic assignment, arthropod-only filtering, and taxonomic richness or dominance summaries. Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been denoised — run DADA2 MOTU inference first; this skill starts from the inferred MOTU table The analysis targets non-arthropod taxa or requires presence/absence occupancy modeling rather than taxonomic assignment and read-based richness/dominance summaries http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assigns taxonomy to DADA2-inferred eDNA MOTUs by matching amplicon sequences against curated arthropod reference databases for two markers (mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI), then aggregates assignments into species/family/order richness and per-taxon read-share metrics. It underpins the flower-eDNA result of at least 135 arthropod species in 67 families and 14 orders. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to DADA2-inferred eDNA MOTUs by matching amplicon sequences against curated arthropod reference databases for two markers (mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI), then aggregates assignments into species/family/order richness and per-taxon read-share metrics. It underpins the flower-eDNA result of at least 135 arthropod species in 67 families and 14 orders.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been denoised — run DADA2 MOTU inference first; this skill starts from the inferred MOTU table The analysis targets non-arthropod taxa or requires presence/absence occupancy modeling rather than taxonomic assignment and read-based richness/dominance summaries

skills.description: Use when you need wall-clock runtime benchmarks of a full amplicon workflow (e.g. ~96-sample 16S rRNA dataset) under different core counts (1 vs 8 cores) inside the Tourmaline Docker container.
skills.name: docker-containerized-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: docker-containerized-pipeline-execution Use when you need wall-clock runtime benchmarks of a full amplicon workflow (e.g. ~96-sample 16S rRNA dataset) under different core counts (1 vs 8 cores) inside the Tourmaline Docker container. Your goal is to change denoising or filtering parameters (e.g. DADA2 truncation lengths, repseq filters) rather than to measure runtime — use parameter-comparison runs instead. Your data is single-end or not Illumina amplicon data — Tourmaline 2 targets Illumina paired-end amplicon sequences. You need per-rule Snakemake customization beyond the three steps (qaqc, repseqs, taxonomy) exposed by tourmaline.sh. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Runs the Tourmaline amplicon workflow (QIIME 2 + Snakemake) inside its Docker container via tourmaline.sh, executing the qaqc, repseqs, and taxonomy steps with a specified core count and timing each step, as demonstrated on the 2018 Lake Erie 16S rRNA dataset (PRJNA679730). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Runs the Tourmaline amplicon workflow (QIIME 2 + Snakemake) inside its Docker container via tourmaline.sh, executing the qaqc, repseqs, and taxonomy steps with a specified core count and timing each step, as demonstrated on the 2018 Lake Erie 16S rRNA dataset (PRJNA679730).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to change denoising or filtering parameters (e.g. DADA2 truncation lengths, repseq filters) rather than to measure runtime — use parameter-comparison runs instead. Your data is single-end or not Illumina amplicon data — Tourmaline 2 targets Illumina paired-end amplicon sequences. You need per-rule Snakemake customization beyond the three steps (qaqc, repseqs, taxonomy) exposed by tourmaline.sh.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether dominance-type alpha diversity metrics (e.g., dominance, Gini, Simpson) respond monotonically to artificially imposed community unevenness, using synthetic ASV feature tables with known abundance ratios.
skills.name: dominance-metric-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: dominance-metric-sensitivity-analysis Use when you need to test whether dominance-type alpha diversity metrics (e.g., dominance, Gini, Simpson) respond monotonically to artificially imposed community unevenness, using synthetic ASV feature tables with known abundance ratios. The dataset is a real (empirical) microbiome feature table where phylogenetic metrics like Faith or unobserved-richness metrics like ACE can be computed — these are excluded here only because of technical limitations on synthetic data The goal is rarefaction-based comparison — this skill computes metrics on non-rarefied data, and rarefied validation would require a different (unpublished-location) dataset The input is raw sequence data (e.g., SRA FASTQ) rather than an already-denoised feature table — sample processing with DADA2/DEBLUR is a separate workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates the behavior of dominance-category alpha diversity metrics by recomputing them with QIIME2's diversity module on negative-binomial synthetic feature tables with controlled unevenness (ASV2/ASV1 ratios of 2x, 10x, and 100x against an average of 0.8x), demonstrating their sensitivity to community imbalance. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-024-77864-y
skills.summary: Validates the behavior of dominance-category alpha diversity metrics by recomputing them with QIIME2's diversity module on negative-binomial synthetic feature tables with controlled unevenness (ASV2/ASV1 ratios of 2x, 10x, and 100x against an average of 0.8x), demonstrating their sensitivity to community imbalance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a real (empirical) microbiome feature table where phylogenetic metrics like Faith or unobserved-richness metrics like ACE can be computed — these are excluded here only because of technical limitations on synthetic data The goal is rarefaction-based comparison — this skill computes metrics on non-rarefied data, and rarefied validation would require a different (unpublished-location) dataset The input is raw sequence data (e.g., SRA FASTQ) rather than an already-denoised feature table — sample processing with DADA2/DEBLUR is a separate workflow

skills.description: Use when computing accuracy-based error metrics (e.g., log NRMSE) between a profiler's taxonomic abundance table and a mock community's true composition, so that taxa absent in both are not treated as perfect matches.
skills.name: double-zero-exclusion-in-taxon-comparison
skills.search_text: double-zero-exclusion-in-taxon-comparison Use when computing accuracy-based error metrics (e.g., log NRMSE) between a profiler's taxonomic abundance table and a mock community's true composition, so that taxa absent in both are not treated as perfect matches. Input is already a filtered feature/error table with zero-count taxa removed — re-filtering is redundant Computing detection-based sensitivity/specificity at the sample level rather than accuracy-based error rates on per-taxon counts Comparing read-mapping quality or contamination screening rather than taxonomic abundance accuracy A data-preparation rule for accuracy-based comparison of measured vs. ground-truth mock community taxonomic abundance tables (from DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2): restrict each comparison to the union of expected and detected taxa and exclude double-zero pairs where both measured and true counts are zero before computing log NRMSE. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: A data-preparation rule for accuracy-based comparison of measured vs. ground-truth mock community taxonomic abundance tables (from DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2): restrict each comparison to the union of expected and detected taxa and exclude double-zero pairs where both measured and true counts are zero before computing log NRMSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature/error table with zero-count taxa removed — re-filtering is redundant Computing detection-based sensitivity/specificity at the sample level rather than accuracy-based error rates on per-taxon counts Comparing read-mapping quality or contamination screening rather than taxonomic abundance accuracy

skills.description: Use when simulating or preparing PacBio HiFi amplicon reads that must carry sample-identifying dual barcodes inside a single full-length read, e.g. building barcoded_templates.fasta from ASV sequences, primer sequences, and a barcode TSV.
skills.name: dual-barcode-sequence-design
skills.search_text: dual-barcode-sequence-design Use when simulating or preparing PacBio HiFi amplicon reads that must carry sample-identifying dual barcodes inside a single full-length read, e.g. building barcoded_templates.fasta from ASV sequences, primer sequences, and a barcode TSV. Input is already a FASTQ of sequencing reads — barcodes are then demultiplexed, not concatenated into templates The platform reads only one end of the molecule (e.g. single-indexed short-read libraries), where the dual-barcode 5'/3' layout does not apply You need to simulate only ASV abundance profiles without sequence-level templates (MHASS counts.tsv output), since no template concatenation is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Constructs PacBio HiFi amplicon sequencing templates in which each sample is tagged with a unique forward/reverse barcode pair arranged in the dual-barcoded layout A + forward barcode + forward primer + ASV + RC(reverse primer) + RC(reverse barcode) + A, so full-length HiFi reads span both barcodes and both primers. This mirrors the template-concatenation step used by MHASS to create realistic synthetic microbiome HiFi datasets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Constructs PacBio HiFi amplicon sequencing templates in which each sample is tagged with a unique forward/reverse barcode pair arranged in the dual-barcoded layout A + forward barcode + forward primer + ASV + RC(reverse primer) + RC(reverse barcode) + A, so full-length HiFi reads span both barcodes and both primers. This mirrors the template-concatenation step used by MHASS to create realistic synthetic microbiome HiFi datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a FASTQ of sequencing reads — barcodes are then demultiplexed, not concatenated into templates The platform reads only one end of the molecule (e.g. single-indexed short-read libraries), where the dual-barcode 5'/3' layout does not apply You need to simulate only ASV abundance profiles without sequence-level templates (MHASS counts.tsv output), since no template concatenation is required

skills.description: Use when a taxon-by-sample abundance time-series (e.g. 663 taxonomic groups across an 18-month Monterey Bay 2015–2016 eDNA index table) should be partitioned into co-fluctuating subnetworks/modules with seasonal membership.
skills.name: dynamic-tree-cut-module-detection
skills.search_text: dynamic-tree-cut-module-detection Use when a taxon-by-sample abundance time-series (e.g. 663 taxonomic groups across an 18-month Monterey Bay 2015–2016 eDNA index table) should be partitioned into co-fluctuating subnetworks/modules with seasonal membership. The abundance table has no temporal replication (single samples), so co-fluctuation modules and seasonal membership cannot be defined The goal is to claim direct predator–prey interactions from module connectivity — the article cautions that network connectivity does not necessarily indicate interaction and co-occurrence may reflect a common response to an external driver Species-level module interpretation is required — the article notes the lower the taxonomic assignment, the lower the confidence http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Detects taxon modules (subnetworks) in eDNA amplicon-index time-series by building a weighted correlation network (WGCNA, soft-thresholding power beta=22), converting correlations to topological-overlap dissimilarity, and cutting the hierarchical clustering dendrogram with the Dynamic Tree Cut algorithm. It is what allowed Djurhuus et al. to identify six seasonal taxon communities from 663 Monterey Bay taxonomic groups. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Detects taxon modules (subnetworks) in eDNA amplicon-index time-series by building a weighted correlation network (WGCNA, soft-thresholding power beta=22), converting correlations to topological-overlap dissimilarity, and cutting the hierarchical clustering dendrogram with the Dynamic Tree Cut algorithm. It is what allowed Djurhuus et al. to identify six seasonal taxon communities from 663 Monterey Bay taxonomic groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance table has no temporal replication (single samples), so co-fluctuation modules and seasonal membership cannot be defined The goal is to claim direct predator–prey interactions from module connectivity — the article cautions that network connectivity does not necessarily indicate interaction and co-occurrence may reflect a common response to an external driver Species-level module interpretation is required — the article notes the lower the taxonomic assignment, the lower the confidence

skills.description: Use when per-location eDNA MOTU richness and sequence read abundance counts are available and the goal is to test whether these biodiversity metrics differ significantly among categorical sampling sites with a Poisson GLM and post-hoc Tukey contrasts.
skills.name: ecological-diversity-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: ecological-diversity-hypothesis-testing Use when per-location eDNA MOTU richness and sequence read abundance counts are available and the goal is to test whether these biodiversity metrics differ significantly among categorical sampling sites with a Poisson GLM and post-hoc Tukey contrasts. Input is raw sequencing reads or a sample-by-MOTU matrix — aggregate first via the OBITools/sumaclust pipeline (99% clustering, single-read MOTU removal) before applying this skill. The response variable is proportional or normalized (e.g., relative percentages) rather than counts — the Poisson family with square-root-transformed abundances assumed here would be misspecified. You need quantitative biomass estimates per species — the paper states no experiment has verified the read-abundance-to-biomass relationship for elasmobranchs, so abundance contrasts describe relative reads, not biomass. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 R-based hypothesis-testing skill for eDNA metabarcoding outputs: a Poisson glm2 model with sampling location as a categorical factor tests whether MOTU richness and square-root-transformed sequence read abundances differ among locations, with multcomp post-hoc Tukey contrasts quantifying every pairwise difference. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: R-based hypothesis-testing skill for eDNA metabarcoding outputs: a Poisson glm2 model with sampling location as a categorical factor tests whether MOTU richness and square-root-transformed sequence read abundances differ among locations, with multcomp post-hoc Tukey contrasts quantifying every pairwise difference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or a sample-by-MOTU matrix — aggregate first via the OBITools/sumaclust pipeline (99% clustering, single-read MOTU removal) before applying this skill. The response variable is proportional or normalized (e.g., relative percentages) rather than counts — the Poisson family with square-root-transformed abundances assumed here would be misspecified. You need quantitative biomass estimates per species — the paper states no experiment has verified the read-abundance-to-biomass relationship for elasmobranchs, so abundance contrasts describe relative reads, not biomass.

skills.description: Use when you have a taxon-by-sample detection/abundance matrix (here: plant species x arthropod family) and need to build and render a bipartite interaction web that makes diversity differences across samples visually apparent.
skills.name: ecological-network-analysis-in-r
skills.search_text: ecological-network-analysis-in-r Use when you have a taxon-by-sample detection/abundance matrix (here: plant species x arthropod family) and need to build and render a bipartite interaction web that makes diversity differences across samples visually apparent. The data are not a bipartite sample-by-taxon matrix (e.g. raw metabarcoding reads, FASTQ files, or ASV tables that have not yet been aggregated to family level) The analysis goal is taxonomic composition or ordination (community clustering) rather than a two-level interaction-web visualization Construct and draw bipartite ecological networks in R using the bipartite package to visualize how eDNA-recovered taxa (e.g. 67 arthropod families) are distributed across sampling units (e.g. seven plant species), highlighting which units have the highest and lowest partner diversity. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Construct and draw bipartite ecological networks in R using the bipartite package to visualize how eDNA-recovered taxa (e.g. 67 arthropod families) are distributed across sampling units (e.g. seven plant species), highlighting which units have the highest and lowest partner diversity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not a bipartite sample-by-taxon matrix (e.g. raw metabarcoding reads, FASTQ files, or ASV tables that have not yet been aggregated to family level) The analysis goal is taxonomic composition or ordination (community clustering) rather than a two-level interaction-web visualization

skills.description: Use when you have subnetwork edge lists from a co-occurrence/community network (e.g., seasonal subnetworks from an eDNA time series) and need to identify and rank the most highly connected hub taxa with degree/percentage-of-subnetwork statistics.
skills.name: ecological-network-connectivity-analysis
skills.search_text: ecological-network-connectivity-analysis Use when you have subnetwork edge lists from a co-occurrence/community network (e.g., seasonal subnetworks from an eDNA time series) and need to identify and rank the most highly connected hub taxa with degree/percentage-of-subnetwork statistics. Input is a raw sequencing dataset (FASTQ/amplicon reads) rather than a derived subnetwork edge list — the repository README indicates it is for sequencing data analysis and quality filtering, which precedes network construction The goal is species-level taxonomic assignment or life-history inference — the paper notes species-level assignments carry lower confidence and eDNA cannot identify life history stages You need to demonstrate direct predator–prey interaction — the paper states that whether co-occurrence reflects direct predator–prey relationships or a common response to an external driver is unclear http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks hub taxa by connectivity (edge-weight sums and node degree) within seasonally clustered subnetworks of an eDNA community network, identifying the most central taxon in each subnetwork. Used to quantify, e.g., Balaenopteridae as the hub of the blue (autumn) subnetwork and Rhodospirillaceae as the hub of the grey (winter) subnetwork. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Ranks hub taxa by connectivity (edge-weight sums and node degree) within seasonally clustered subnetworks of an eDNA community network, identifying the most central taxon in each subnetwork. Used to quantify, e.g., Balaenopteridae as the hub of the blue (autumn) subnetwork and Rhodospirillaceae as the hub of the grey (winter) subnetwork.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw sequencing dataset (FASTQ/amplicon reads) rather than a derived subnetwork edge list — the repository README indicates it is for sequencing data analysis and quality filtering, which precedes network construction The goal is species-level taxonomic assignment or life-history inference — the paper notes species-level assignments carry lower confidence and eDNA cannot identify life history stages You need to demonstrate direct predator–prey interaction — the paper states that whether co-occurrence reflects direct predator–prey relationships or a common response to an external driver is unclear

skills.description: Use when you have an ecotag-style per-sample MOTU read-count table and need to apply a conservative singleton-removal filter before reporting taxon richness per sampling location or region.
skills.name: ecotaxonomic-assignment-table-processing
skills.search_text: ecotaxonomic-assignment-table-processing Use when you have an ecotag-style per-sample MOTU read-count table and need to apply a conservative singleton-removal filter before reporting taxon richness per sampling location or region. Input is raw sequencing reads that have not yet been aligned, length-filtered (120-135 bp), dereplicated, and chimera-removed — this skill operates on the post-clustering ecotag table, not FASTQ. The goal is a permissive richness estimate including rare reads — removing all single-read MOTUs is by design a conservative control and will discard low-support detections. MOTUs were clustered at a similarity threshold other than 99% with sumaclust — richness counts will not be comparable to the paper's reported figures. Filters an ecotag taxonomic assignment table produced from sumaclust MOTU clustering (99% similarity threshold) by removing all single-read (singleton) MOTUs, then computes per-location and per-region elasmobranch MOTU richness. This is the paper's conservative control against contamination and sequencing-error false positives. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Filters an ecotag taxonomic assignment table produced from sumaclust MOTU clustering (99% similarity threshold) by removing all single-read (singleton) MOTUs, then computes per-location and per-region elasmobranch MOTU richness. This is the paper's conservative control against contamination and sequencing-error false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads that have not yet been aligned, length-filtered (120-135 bp), dereplicated, and chimera-removed — this skill operates on the post-clustering ecotag table, not FASTQ. skills.description: Use when benchmarking a HiFi amplicon simulator (e.g., MHASS) by checking whether per-genome nearest-reference edit distance distributions of simulated reads mirror real-data distributions for mock communities like Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, or Phylotag/16S.
skills.name: edit-distance-distribution-computation
skills.search_text: edit-distance-distribution-computation Use when benchmarking a HiFi amplicon simulator (e.g., MHASS) by checking whether per-genome nearest-reference edit distance distributions of simulated reads mirror real-data distributions for mock communities like Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, or Phylotag/16S. Input is already a per-read edit distance table or distribution summary — skip to the comparison step instead of recomputing distances The goal is taxonomic assignment or ASV clustering of reads rather than benchmarking simulator error profiles No reference ASV FASTA exists for the mock community, so nearest-reference distances cannot be defined Computes per-genome distributions of minimum (Levenshtein) edit distances between simulated or real PacBio HiFi amplicon reads and their candidate reference ASV sequences, enabling direct comparison of error profiles between MHASS-simulated and real sequencing data across mock communities. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Computes per-genome distributions of minimum (Levenshtein) edit distances between simulated or real PacBio HiFi amplicon reads and their candidate reference ASV sequences, enabling direct comparison of error profiles between MHASS-simulated and real sequencing data across mock communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-read edit distance table or distribution summary — skip to the comparison step instead of recomputing distances The goal is taxonomic assignment or ASV clustering of reads rather than benchmarking simulator error profiles No reference ASV FASTA exists for the mock community, so nearest-reference distances cannot be defined

skills.search_text: edna-amplicon-read-processing Use when a FASTQ/annotated read set from paired-end Illumina amplicon sequencing (post-alignment, demultiplexing and length filtering) must be collapsed to unique representative sequences prior to chimera detection and MOTU clustering. Input reads have not yet been aligned, demultiplexed, or length-filtered — dereplicating raw or unfiltered reads would collapse artefactual variants prematurely The data is already a MOTU table or feature table — dereplication operates on raw sequence reads, not abundance matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Dereplication of quality- and length-filtered eDNA amplicon reads using obiuniq from the OBITools suite, collapsing identical sequences into single records with aggregated per-sample abundance annotations before chimera removal and MOTU clustering. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Dereplication of quality- and length-filtered eDNA amplicon reads using obiuniq from the OBITools suite, collapsing identical sequences into single records with aggregated per-sample abundance annotations before chimera removal and MOTU clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been aligned, demultiplexed, or length-filtered — dereplicating raw or unfiltered reads would collapse artefactual variants prematurely The data is already a MOTU table or feature table — dereplication operates on raw sequence reads, not abundance matrices

skills.description: Use when you have an eDNA metabarcoding community matrix (COI or 16S OTU/ASV table) plus sample metadata with host/source identity (e.g. plant species) and site coordinates, and want to test whether communities separate by that identity.
skills.name: edna-metabarcoding-community-profiling
skills.search_text: edna-metabarcoding-community-profiling Use when you have an eDNA metabarcoding community matrix (COI or 16S OTU/ASV table) plus sample metadata with host/source identity (e.g. plant species) and site coordinates, and want to test whether communities separate by that identity. Input is raw sequencing reads or FASTQ data rather than an already-derived OTU/ASV community matrix — bioinformatic processing must precede this ordination step The question concerns taxonomic richness or diversity of the flower eDNA rather than whether community composition separates by sample group (the article notes richness could be even higher and the experiment was not exhaustive) http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 Profile arthropod community composition from flower eDNA metabarcoding data (COI and 16S rRNA OTU/ASV matrices) and test whether communities cluster by plant species, e.g. via redundancy analysis (vegan::rda) with site latitude/longitude as conditioning variables, as in Thomsen & Sigsgaard (2019). metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or FASTQ data rather than an already-derived OTU/ASV community matrix — bioinformatic processing must precede this ordination step The question concerns taxonomic richness or diversity of the flower eDNA rather than whether community composition separates by sample group (the article notes richness could be even higher and the experiment was not exhaustive)

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina .fastq.gz metabarcoding reads for 16S/18S/12S rRNA, ITS, or COI marker genes need processing from quality control through OTU clustering/ASV inference to taxonomy assignment in a single containerized run.
skills.name: edna-metabarcoding-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: edna-metabarcoding-pipeline-execution Use when raw paired-end Illumina .fastq.gz metabarcoding reads for 16S/18S/12S rRNA, ITS, or COI marker genes need processing from quality control through OTU clustering/ASV inference to taxonomy assignment in a single containerized run. Input is already an OTU/ASV feature table or processed amplicon data — PEMA starts from raw paired-end .fastq.gz reads Reads are not paired-end Illumina amplicon data for one of the supported marker genes (16S/18S/12S rRNA, ITS, COI) A targeted single-tool benchmark (e.g., only Swarm d=3 vs VSEARCH clustering) is needed without a full pipeline re-run — use PEMA's checkpoint/partial execution instead of a fresh full run http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Execute the PEMA containerized pipeline end-to-end on Illumina .fastq.gz amplicon reads (16S/18S rRNA, ITS, COI, and since v.2.1.4 12S rRNA), producing an OTU- or ASV-table with taxonomies and per-sample abundances plus downstream phyloseq ecological analysis. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Execute the PEMA containerized pipeline end-to-end on Illumina .fastq.gz amplicon reads (16S/18S rRNA, ITS, COI, and since v.2.1.4 12S rRNA), producing an OTU- or ASV-table with taxonomies and per-sample abundances plus downstream phyloseq ecological analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an OTU/ASV feature table or processed amplicon data — PEMA starts from raw paired-end .fastq.gz reads Reads are not paired-end Illumina amplicon data for one of the supported marker genes (16S/18S/12S rRNA, ITS, COI) A targeted single-tool benchmark (e.g., only Swarm d=3 vs VSEARCH clustering) is needed without a full pipeline re-run — use PEMA's checkpoint/partial execution instead of a fresh full run

skills.description: Use when a metabarcoding pipeline has produced dereplicated amplicon sequences (e.g. after obiuniq on quality- and length-filtered paired-end reads) and chimeras must be removed before MOTU clustering.
skills.name: edna-metabarcoding-pipeline-preprocessing
skills.search_text: edna-metabarcoding-pipeline-preprocessing Use when a metabarcoding pipeline has produced dereplicated amplicon sequences (e.g. after obiuniq on quality- and length-filtered paired-end reads) and chimeras must be removed before MOTU clustering. Input is raw paired-end FASTQ that has not yet been aligned, quality-filtered, length-filtered and dereplicated — uchime-denovo in this pipeline operates on dereplicated reads, not raw reads A curated reference-based chimera detection strategy is required (uchime-denovo is de novo and does not use a reference database) Input is already a MOTU table or post-clustering representative sequences — chimera filtering belongs upstream of sumaclust clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 De novo chimera removal step for eDNA metabarcoding amplicon reads: chimeric sequences are detected and discarded using the uchime-denovo algorithm implemented in vsearch, operating on dereplicated reads without a reference database, before MOTU delimitation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: De novo chimera removal step for eDNA metabarcoding amplicon reads: chimeric sequences are detected and discarded using the uchime-denovo algorithm implemented in vsearch, operating on dereplicated reads without a reference database, before MOTU delimitation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw paired-end FASTQ that has not yet been aligned, quality-filtered, length-filtered and dereplicated — uchime-denovo in this pipeline operates on dereplicated reads, not raw reads A curated reference-based chimera detection strategy is required (uchime-denovo is de novo and does not use a reference database) Input is already a MOTU table or post-clustering representative sequences — chimera filtering belongs upstream of sumaclust clustering
