skills.description: Use when you have a per-sample eDNA MOTU detection table (e.g. sumaclust 99% MOTUs) grouped by location and need to determine whether richness is saturated or under-sampled.
skills.name: edna-sampling-effort-assessment
skills.search_text: edna-sampling-effort-assessment Use when you have a per-sample eDNA MOTU detection table (e.g. sumaclust 99% MOTUs) grouped by location and need to determine whether richness is saturated or under-sampled. The input is already a curated presence/absence site-by-species matrix for which saturation has already been assessed — re-running curves adds no information The goal is taxonomic assignment or read-based abundance modelling (e.g. the paper's generalized linear model of MOTU richness and square-root-transformed read abundances) rather than sampling-effort/saturation assessment Samples cannot be resolved to individual sampling units per location (e.g. only pooled or per-library reads are available), since sample-based accumulation curves require per-sample detection data Assess whether sample-based eDNA metabarcoding captured total species diversity by computing species accumulation curves per sampling location from a MOTU-by-sample table and inspecting them for a plateau. This tells the analyst whether increased sampling effort would still add new MOTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assess whether sample-based eDNA metabarcoding captured total species diversity by computing species accumulation curves per sampling location from a MOTU-by-sample table and inspecting them for a plateau. This tells the analyst whether increased sampling effort would still add new MOTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated presence/absence site-by-species matrix for which saturation has already been assessed — re-running curves adds no information The goal is taxonomic assignment or read-based abundance modelling (e.g. the paper's generalized linear model of MOTU richness and square-root-transformed read abundances) rather than sampling-effort/saturation assessment Samples cannot be resolved to individual sampling units per location (e.g. only pooled or per-library reads are available), since sample-based accumulation curves require per-sample detection data

skills.description: Use when you have a per-locus taxa x time-point read-proportion table from eDNA metabarcoding (e.g. an 8-time-point Monterey Bay seawater series) and need a 0-1 relative abundance index per taxon that is robust to primer bias and consistent across multiple genetic loci.
skills.name: edna-timeseries-data-processing
skills.search_text: edna-timeseries-data-processing Use when you have a per-locus taxa x time-point read-proportion table from eDNA metabarcoding (e.g. an 8-time-point Monterey Bay seawater series) and need a 0-1 relative abundance index per taxon that is robust to primer bias and consistent across multiple genetic loci. Input is raw sequencing reads or FASTQ data rather than a per-locus read-proportion table; upstream metabarcoding processing must be done first Data comes from a single locus and a single sample (no time series), since the within-taxon 0-1 scaling is defined across a time series of read proportions The goal is absolute quantification of organismal abundance; the index only captures relative changes because amplification bias obscures the relationship between organismal and amplicon abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the ensemble eDNA abundance index from a multilocus metabarcoding time-series: per-locus read proportions are scaled 0-1 within each taxon and averaged across loci to approximate relative changes in taxon abundance despite constant per-taxon amplification bias. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Reconstructs the ensemble eDNA abundance index from a multilocus metabarcoding time-series: per-locus read proportions are scaled 0-1 within each taxon and averaged across loci to approximate relative changes in taxon abundance despite constant per-taxon amplification bias.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or FASTQ data rather than a per-locus read-proportion table; upstream metabarcoding processing must be done first Data comes from a single locus and a single sample (no time series), since the within-taxon 0-1 scaling is defined across a time series of read proportions The goal is absolute quantification of organismal abundance; the index only captures relative changes because amplification bias obscures the relationship between organismal and amplicon abundance

skills.description: Use when ANCOM-BC (or similar DA) output includes mean.difference and se per taxon and you need to report effect sizes with CIs, e.g., reproducing Fig. 6a-style phylum-level plots stratified by infants vs adults.
skills.name: effect-size-confidence-interval-visualization
skills.search_text: effect-size-confidence-interval-visualization Use when ANCOM-BC (or similar DA) output includes mean.difference and se per taxon and you need to report effect sizes with CIs, e.g., reproducing Fig. 6a-style phylum-level plots stratified by infants vs adults. Data are already relative abundances and you only want normalized relative-abundance summaries — ANCOM-BC mean differences are on the log absolute-abundance scale after sampling-fraction correction, not relative abundances Very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group) — the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases The goal is a p-value-only summary without effect sizes — use the res table directly rather than this visualization step http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Plots ANCOM-BC estimated mean differences of log absolute abundance between experimental groups (e.g., US vs Malawi/Venezuela gut microbiota) with their confidence intervals per taxon, highlighting differentially abundant taxa at q.val < 0.05 so effect sizes are visible alongside significance. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Plots ANCOM-BC estimated mean differences of log absolute abundance between experimental groups (e.g., US vs Malawi/Venezuela gut microbiota) with their confidence intervals per taxon, highlighting differentially abundant taxa at q.val < 0.05 so effect sizes are visible alongside significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already relative abundances and you only want normalized relative-abundance summaries — ANCOM-BC mean differences are on the log absolute-abundance scale after sampling-fraction correction, not relative abundances Very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group) — the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases The goal is a p-value-only summary without effect sizes — use the res table directly rather than this visualization step

skills.description: Use when you have a MOTU table with per-sample read counts and taxonomic assignments (ecotag output from sumaclust-delimited MOTUs) and need post-singleton-removal richness counts per location or region for a taxon subset such as elasmobranchs.
skills.name: elasmobranch-motu-richness-tabulation
skills.search_text: elasmobranch-motu-richness-tabulation Use when you have a MOTU table with per-sample read counts and taxonomic assignments (ecotag output from sumaclust-delimited MOTUs) and need post-singleton-removal richness counts per location or region for a taxon subset such as elasmobranchs. Input is raw FASTQ reads — singleton removal operates on a dereplicated, clustered, taxonomically assigned MOTU table, not on reads. The analysis goal is species-level identification of closely related taxa (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) — the 127 bp COI fragment leaves some MOTUs 100% identical to multiple BOLD species, so richness counts cannot be equated with species counts. Quantitative biomass/abundance estimation is desired — read abundance is not a validated proxy for elasmobranch community biomass. Input is already a richness table or the MOTUs have not been clustered and assigned (e.g. chimeras not yet removed via vsearch uchime-denovo). http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Tabulates elasmobranch MOTU richness per sampling location and region from an ecotag taxonomic assignment table after removing single-read (singleton) MOTUs, as a conservative contamination/sequencing-error control. Produces location-level counts (e.g. Bahamas 11, Jamaica 2, Belize 1, Chesterfield 11, New Caledonia North 14, Noumea 5) and region-level totals (12 Caribbean, 16 New Caledonia, 9 shared, 22 overall). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Tabulates elasmobranch MOTU richness per sampling location and region from an ecotag taxonomic assignment table after removing single-read (singleton) MOTUs, as a conservative contamination/sequencing-error control. Produces location-level counts (e.g. Bahamas 11, Jamaica 2, Belize 1, Chesterfield 11, New Caledonia North 14, Noumea 5) and region-level totals (12 Caribbean, 16 New Caledonia, 9 shared, 22 overall).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads — singleton removal operates on a dereplicated, clustered, taxonomically assigned MOTU table, not on reads. The analysis goal is species-level identification of closely related taxa (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) — the 127 bp COI fragment leaves some MOTUs 100% identical to multiple BOLD species, so richness counts cannot be equated with species counts. Quantitative biomass/abundance estimation is desired — read abundance is not a validated proxy for elasmobranch community biomass. Input is already a richness table or the MOTUs have not been clustered and assigned (e.g. chimeras not yet removed via vsearch uchime-denovo).

skills.description: Use when assigning 127-bp COI eDNA metabarcoding reads (amplified with Fields et al. elasmobranch-specific primers) to shark/ray taxa and no suitable combined elasmobranch+non-target reference database exists yet.
skills.name: elasmobranch-reference-database-construction
skills.search_text: elasmobranch-reference-database-construction Use when assigning 127-bp COI eDNA metabarcoding reads (amplified with Fields et al. elasmobranch-specific primers) to shark/ray taxa and no suitable combined elasmobranch+non-target reference database exists yet. The taxonomic assignment target is not short COI eDNA reads from elasmobranch-specific primers (e.g. full-length COI barcodes or other marker genes) — retrieve or reuse a marker-appropriate reference database instead. The published combined database at github.com/metabarpark/Reference-databases already matches your primer pair and target fragment; downloading it is preferable to rebuilding. You need to resolve closely related species (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) — the 127-bp fragment leaves some MOTUs 100% identical to multiple species in BOLD, so this database cannot separate them; longer-amplicon primers would be required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Assembles a bespoke COI reference database for taxonomic assignment of short (127-bp) elasmobranch eDNA reads by merging all BOLD elasmobranch COI sequences (retrieved via custom R script) with ecoPCR-derived non-elasmobranch sequences from EMBL-EBI release R117, for use with OBITools' ecotag. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assembles a bespoke COI reference database for taxonomic assignment of short (127-bp) elasmobranch eDNA reads by merging all BOLD elasmobranch COI sequences (retrieved via custom R script) with ecoPCR-derived non-elasmobranch sequences from EMBL-EBI release R117, for use with OBITools' ecotag.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The taxonomic assignment target is not short COI eDNA reads from elasmobranch-specific primers (e.g. full-length COI barcodes or other marker genes) — retrieve or reuse a marker-appropriate reference database instead. The published combined database at github.com/metabarpark/Reference-databases already matches your primer pair and target fragment; downloading it is preferable to rebuilding. You need to resolve closely related species (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) — the 127-bp fragment leaves some MOTUs 100% identical to multiple species in BOLD, so this database cannot separate them; longer-amplicon primers would be required.

skills.description: Use when performing differential abundance testing on compositional microbiome count data (OTU/feature tables) where bias from differing sampling fractions across samples must be estimated and corrected, as in ANCOM-BC.
skills.name: em-algorithm-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: em-algorithm-parameter-estimation Use when performing differential abundance testing on compositional microbiome count data (OTU/feature tables) where bias from differing sampling fractions across samples must be estimated and corrected, as in ANCOM-BC. Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The group variable is continuous — ANCOM-BC v1.0 only supports a discrete group.var The goal is testing mean relative abundance rather than mean absolute abundance, which is not equivalent for compositional data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fits the ANCOM-BC log-linear model of absolute abundance with a sample-specific sampling-fraction offset via an E-M algorithm, iteratively estimating bias until convergence (tol.EM) or a maximum number of iterations (max.iterNum), yielding bias-corrected mean differences, standard errors, W statistics, and p-values per taxon. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Fits the ANCOM-BC log-linear model of absolute abundance with a sample-specific sampling-fraction offset via an E-M algorithm, iteratively estimating bias until convergence (tol.EM) or a maximum number of iterations (max.iterNum), yielding bias-corrected mean differences, standard errors, W statistics, and p-values per taxon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The group variable is continuous — ANCOM-BC v1.0 only supports a discrete group.var The goal is testing mean relative abundance rather than mean absolute abundance, which is not equivalent for compositional data

skills.description: Use when long reads (PacBio/ONT) have already been approximately mapped and scored by MetaMaps and you need an overall sample composition estimate plus disambiguation of reads with multiple candidate mapping locations.
skills.name: em-based-composition-estimation
skills.search_text: em-based-composition-estimation Use when long reads (PacBio/ONT) have already been approximately mapped and scored by MetaMaps and you need an overall sample composition estimate plus disambiguation of reads with multiple candidate mapping locations. Sample contains a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and end up unassigned The sample comprises many non-characterized entities absent from the reference database — database-sample incongruity (e.g. HMP7/CAMI mismatches) undermines composition estimation Input is raw reads without prior MetaMaps approximate mapping and probabilistic scoring — this EM stage requires mapping-quality-based probabilities as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 MetaMaps' second analysis stage: probabilistic per-read mapping scores from a >12,000-genome RefSeq database are iteratively reweighted via the EM algorithm to estimate sample composition and resolve each read to a maximum-likelihood genome, giving strain-level (definedGenomes) resolution. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: MetaMaps' second analysis stage: probabilistic per-read mapping scores from a >12,000-genome RefSeq database are iteratively reweighted via the EM algorithm to estimate sample composition and resolve each read to a maximum-likelihood genome, giving strain-level (definedGenomes) resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample contains a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and end up unassigned The sample comprises many non-characterized entities absent from the reference database — database-sample incongruity (e.g. HMP7/CAMI mismatches) undermines composition estimation Input is raw reads without prior MetaMaps approximate mapping and probabilistic scoring — this EM stage requires mapping-quality-based probabilities as input

skills.description: Use when you have long-read metagenomic data (FASTQ) and need simultaneous per-read taxonomic assignment and sample composition estimation, especially at strain level against a RefSeq-style database.
skills.name: em-based-sample-composition-inference
skills.search_text: em-based-sample-composition-inference Use when you have long-read metagenomic data (FASTQ) and need simultaneous per-read taxonomic assignment and sample composition estimation, especially at strain level against a RefSeq-style database. Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length threshold get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities — database-sample incongruity (novel strains/species absent from the reference) is an explicit unresolved limitation Real-time/streaming analysis workflows — MetaMaps lacks streaming support needed for live clinical or sequencing-control applications http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Estimate taxonomic composition of a long-read (PacBio/ONT) metagenomic sample by scoring approximate mapping locations probabilistically and running an EM algorithm over per-read assignments, as implemented in MetaMaps. This disambiguates reads mapping to closely related strains and corrects for unmapped reads. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Estimate taxonomic composition of a long-read (PacBio/ONT) metagenomic sample by scoring approximate mapping locations probabilistically and running an EM algorithm over per-read assignments, as implemented in MetaMaps. This disambiguates reads mapping to closely related strains and corrects for unmapped reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length threshold get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities — database-sample incongruity (novel strains/species absent from the reference) is an explicit unresolved limitation Real-time/streaming analysis workflows — MetaMaps lacks streaming support needed for live clinical or sequencing-control applications

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential abundance methods on simulated compositional data where ground-truth DA taxa are known, to check which methods control FDR at a nominal level (e.g., 5%) while retaining power.
skills.name: empirical-fdr-estimation-across-simulation-replicates
skills.search_text: empirical-fdr-estimation-across-simulation-replicates Use when benchmarking differential abundance methods on simulated compositional data where ground-truth DA taxa are known, to check which methods control FDR at a nominal level (e.g., 5%) while retaining power. The data are real observational data with no known ground truth of DA taxa — empirical FDR/power cannot be computed without simulation Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where the paper notes ANCOM-BC may not control FDR The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is very large, which can yield slightly elevated FDR even for well-controlled methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimate empirical False Discovery Rate and statistical power for differential abundance methods by running each method on many simulated microbiome datasets (e.g., 100 Poisson-Gamma replicates) under known ground truth and comparing declared DA taxa to truly DA taxa. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Estimate empirical False Discovery Rate and statistical power for differential abundance methods by running each method on many simulated microbiome datasets (e.g., 100 Poisson-Gamma replicates) under known ground truth and comparing declared DA taxa to truly DA taxa.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real observational data with no known ground truth of DA taxa — empirical FDR/power cannot be computed without simulation Sample sizes are very small (e.g., n = 5 per group), where the paper notes ANCOM-BC may not control FDR The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is very large, which can yield slightly elevated FDR even for well-controlled methods

skills.description: Use when a correlation matrix over many taxa × environmental variable pairs from a eDNA time-series must be tested for significance, and the multiple-comparison burden requires an empirical permutation null rather than parametric p-values.
skills.name: empirical-p-value-density-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-p-value-density-estimation Use when a correlation matrix over many taxa × environmental variable pairs from a eDNA time-series must be tested for significance, and the multiple-comparison burden requires an empirical permutation null rather than parametric p-values. When testing a single or very small number of pre-specified associations, where no multiple-comparison correction or permutation null density is needed. When the input is raw sequencing reads or a quality-filtering problem (the repository README scopes the repo to sequencing data analysis, quality filtering, and bioinformatics); this skill operates downstream on the proportional-abundance table. When taxon detection counts must be interpreted absolutely — the article notes primer biases, inhibitors, and variable template abundances affect which taxa are detected, so tau thresholds should not be read as absolute abundance relationships. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Builds a permutation null density of pairwise Kendall tau correlations over an 18-month Monterey Bay eDNA proportional-abundance time-series (663 taxonomic groups plus environmental variables), then derives empirical p-values and a Benjamani-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction that yields a corrected significance threshold of tau = 0.70. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Builds a permutation null density of pairwise Kendall tau correlations over an 18-month Monterey Bay eDNA proportional-abundance time-series (663 taxonomic groups plus environmental variables), then derives empirical p-values and a Benjamani-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction that yields a corrected significance threshold of tau = 0.70.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing a single or very small number of pre-specified associations, where no multiple-comparison correction or permutation null density is needed. When the input is raw sequencing reads or a quality-filtering problem (the repository README scopes the repo to sequencing data analysis, quality filtering, and bioinformatics); this skill operates downstream on the proportional-abundance table. When taxon detection counts must be interpreted absolutely — the article notes primer biases, inhibitors, and variable template abundances affect which taxa are detected, so tau thresholds should not be read as absolute abundance relationships.

skills.description: Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon data whose subread pass counts should reflect a real instrument run, or when real run data has sparse/noisy per-read pass counts and a lognormal fit (mu, sigma, np-min, np-max) is needed as the sampling source.
skills.name: empirical-pass-number-distribution-extraction
skills.search_text: empirical-pass-number-distribution-extraction Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon data whose subread pass counts should reflect a real instrument run, or when real run data has sparse/noisy per-read pass counts and a lognormal fit (mu, sigma, np-min, np-max) is needed as the sampling source. The pass-number distribution of the target run is already faithfully represented by PBSIM3's default single-pass-per-run behavior and per-pass variation is irrelevant to the downstream benchmark The input is already a simulated dataset or a feature/ASV table with no underlying per-read pass counts to tabulate http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extract per-read number-of-passes (np) distributions from real PacBio HiFi sequencing runs (e.g., the ATCC 16S Sequel II System 2.0 release) and supply them, or a fitted lognormal surrogate, to MHASS so PBSIM3 can generate reads with realistic pass counts. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Extract per-read number-of-passes (np) distributions from real PacBio HiFi sequencing runs (e.g., the ATCC 16S Sequel II System 2.0 release) and supply them, or a fitted lognormal surrogate, to MHASS so PBSIM3 can generate reads with realistic pass counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pass-number distribution of the target run is already faithfully represented by PBSIM3's default single-pass-per-run behavior and per-pass variation is irrelevant to the downstream benchmark The input is already a simulated dataset or a feature/ASV table with no underlying per-read pass counts to tabulate

skills.description: Use when a sample set carries an environment/habitat metadata category (e.g., EMPO 3) and bespoke, habitat-specific taxonomic weights must be generated per environment rather than globally.
skills.name: empo-habitat-stratification
skills.search_text: empo-habitat-stratification Use when a sample set carries an environment/habitat metadata category (e.g., EMPO 3) and bespoke, habitat-specific taxonomic weights must be generated per environment rather than globally. When no environment/habitat metadata category is available for the samples, or the sample type lacks sufficient characterization for bespoke weight assembly — use average weights estimated from global microbial species distributions instead of uniform weights For highly unusual sample distributions (e.g., synthetic populations) where compiling custom bespoke weights from existing samples is required rather than habitat-level stratification When ready-made weights already exist for the primer/database/habitat combination — use the readytowear inventory instead of re-running clawback http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Stratifies fetched Qiita samples by their EMPO 3 habitat metadata category so that per-habitat taxonomic weights can be assembled with q2-clawback, yielding habitat-specific (e.g., 14 EMPO 3 habitat type) weights for q2-feature-classifier. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: Stratifies fetched Qiita samples by their EMPO 3 habitat metadata category so that per-habitat taxonomic weights can be assembled with q2-clawback, yielding habitat-specific (e.g., 14 EMPO 3 habitat type) weights for q2-feature-classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no environment/habitat metadata category is available for the samples, or the sample type lacks sufficient characterization for bespoke weight assembly — use average weights estimated from global microbial species distributions instead of uniform weights For highly unusual sample distributions (e.g., synthetic populations) where compiling custom bespoke weights from existing samples is required rather than habitat-level stratification When ready-made weights already exist for the primer/database/habitat combination — use the readytowear inventory instead of re-running clawback

skills.description: Use when EMP 16S Release 1 samples need environment-category labels (EMPO level 2 or level 3) derived from the quality-filtered mapping file, e.g. to train or evaluate a classifier on community composition.
skills.name: empo-metadata-label-mapping
skills.search_text: empo-metadata-label-mapping Use when EMP 16S Release 1 samples need environment-category labels (EMPO level 2 or level 3) derived from the quality-filtered mapping file, e.g. to train or evaluate a classifier on community composition. The mapping file already contains the target environment labels and you only need community data (skip straight to feature-table rarefaction) You are working with samples outside EMP 16S Release 1 that lack EMPO annotations — labels cannot be derived from metadata that does not carry EMPO terms You need taxonomy-based label assignment (e.g. Greengenes OTU taxonomy) rather than sample environment metadata http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps EMP sample metadata to EMPO (Earth Microbiome Project Ontology) environment labels at coarse (level 2: animal-associated, plant-associated, saline, non-saline free-living) and fine (level 3) scales, providing the class labels needed for environment classification from community composition. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Maps EMP sample metadata to EMPO (Earth Microbiome Project Ontology) environment labels at coarse (level 2: animal-associated, plant-associated, saline, non-saline free-living) and fine (level 3) scales, providing the class labels needed for environment classification from community composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mapping file already contains the target environment labels and you only need community data (skip straight to feature-table rarefaction) You are working with samples outside EMP 16S Release 1 that lack EMPO annotations — labels cannot be derived from metadata that does not carry EMPO terms You need taxonomy-based label assignment (e.g. Greengenes OTU taxonomy) rather than sample environment metadata

skills.description: Use when assembling CO1 (or other gene) reference sequence sets from NCBI for a defined taxon list, and the query must capture all gene-name spellings and taxonomic rank constraints so that no reference records are missed.
skills.name: entrez-search-term-construction
skills.search_text: entrez-search-term-construction Use when assembling CO1 (or other gene) reference sequence sets from NCBI for a defined taxon list, and the query must capture all gene-name spellings and taxonomic rank constraints so that no reference records are missed. Queries against curated databases such as BOLD, SILVA, or UNITE, where Entrez field tags like [gene] and [keyword] do not apply Retrieval of short metabarcode query reads or existing training sets (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1/v2 from github.com/terrimporter/CO1Classifier) — these are consumed, not re-mined with Entrez terms http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Constructs compound NCBI Entrez queries that combine CO1 gene synonyms (cox1[gene] OR coxI[gene] OR CO1[gene] OR COI[gene]) with formatted Linnean taxon lists to retrieve barcode reference sequences from the NCBI nucleotide and taxonomy databases. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Constructs compound NCBI Entrez queries that combine CO1 gene synonyms (cox1[gene] OR coxI[gene] OR CO1[gene] OR COI[gene]) with formatted Linnean taxon lists to retrieve barcode reference sequences from the NCBI nucleotide and taxonomy databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Queries against curated databases such as BOLD, SILVA, or UNITE, where Entrez field tags like [gene] and [keyword] do not apply Retrieval of short metabarcode query reads or existing training sets (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1/v2 from github.com/terrimporter/CO1Classifier) — these are consumed, not re-mined with Entrez terms

skills.description: Use when sample metadata carries environment ontology labels that must be mapped to coarse habitat classes before comparing community-level metrics (e.g., weighted ACN, alpha/beta diversity) across animal-associated vs free-living or plant-associated EMP samples.
skills.name: environment-ontology-stratification
skills.search_text: environment-ontology-stratification Use when sample metadata carries environment ontology labels that must be mapped to coarse habitat classes before comparing community-level metrics (e.g., weighted ACN, alpha/beta diversity) across animal-associated vs free-living or plant-associated EMP samples. Samples lack environment ontology labels in the mapping file, so they cannot be assigned to a habitat class Input is shotgun metagenomic or other non-16S-V4 data not processed against Greengenes 13.8 closed-reference, where PICRUSt copy-number normalization is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Stratifies EMP samples into environment classes (free-living, plant-associated, animal-associated) using environment ontology metadata labels, enabling environment-stratified comparisons such as abundance-weighted average 16S rRNA copy number (ACN) via PICRUSt on Greengenes 13.8 closed-reference tables. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Stratifies EMP samples into environment classes (free-living, plant-associated, animal-associated) using environment ontology metadata labels, enabling environment-stratified comparisons such as abundance-weighted average 16S rRNA copy number (ACN) via PICRUSt on Greengenes 13.8 closed-reference tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack environment ontology labels in the mapping file, so they cannot be assigned to a habitat class Input is shotgun metagenomic or other non-16S-V4 data not processed against Greengenes 13.8 closed-reference, where PICRUSt copy-number normalization is not applicable

skills.description: Use when asked to locate the pH or temperature value at which microbial richness peaks in non-host-associated EMP samples, or to compare Laplace vs. Gaussian fits of richness along an environmental gradient.
skills.name: environmental-gradient-binning
skills.search_text: environmental-gradient-binning Use when asked to locate the pH or temperature value at which microbial richness peaks in non-host-associated EMP samples, or to compare Laplace vs. Gaussian fits of richness along an environmental gradient. The question concerns taxonomic composition or abundance (e.g., counting genera in samples with pH > 8) rather than locating a richness maximum along a continuous environmental gradient. Samples are host-associated or lack pH/temperature metadata, leaving too few samples to bin into 100/120 equal-width bins. The input is clustered-reference OTU data (e.g., closed-reference against Greengenes 13.8) instead of the exact-sequence Deblur table the gradient analysis was built on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Bins environmental metadata gradients (e.g., pH into 100 bins, temperature into 120 bins) from EMP 16S Release 1 Deblur data and fits two-sided exponential (Laplace) and Gaussian curves to per-bin 99th-percentile observed richness to locate the gradient peaks. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Bins environmental metadata gradients (e.g., pH into 100 bins, temperature into 120 bins) from EMP 16S Release 1 Deblur data and fits two-sided exponential (Laplace) and Gaussian curves to per-bin 99th-percentile observed richness to locate the gradient peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns taxonomic composition or abundance (e.g., counting genera in samples with pH > 8) rather than locating a richness maximum along a continuous environmental gradient. Samples are host-associated or lack pH/temperature metadata, leaving too few samples to bin into 100/120 equal-width bins. The input is clustered-reference OTU data (e.g., closed-reference against Greengenes 13.8) instead of the exact-sequence Deblur table the gradient analysis was built on.

skills.description: Use when a fitted linear mixed-effects model (e.g. metric ~ pairing + (1|sample)) needs post hoc pairwise comparisons between categorical factor levels, such as profiler-library pairings across 136 mock community samples.
skills.name: estimated-marginal-means-computation
skills.search_text: estimated-marginal-means-computation Use when a fitted linear mixed-effects model (e.g. metric ~ pairing + (1|sample)) needs post hoc pairwise comparisons between categorical factor levels, such as profiler-library pairings across 136 mock community samples. The input is raw per-sample metric data with no fitted mixed-effects model — fit the lmer() model first; EMMs cannot be computed without a model object The comparison involves only two groups or pre-specified orthogonal contrasts where Tukey's all-pairwise adjustment is unnecessary and overly conservative http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Compute estimated marginal means (EMMs) for each profiler/reference-library pairing from fitted linear mixed-effects models, then derive Tukey-adjusted pairwise contrasts, replicating the per-metric comparison tables (Supplementary Tables S2-S7) of the 16S benchmarking study. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Compute estimated marginal means (EMMs) for each profiler/reference-library pairing from fitted linear mixed-effects models, then derive Tukey-adjusted pairwise contrasts, replicating the per-metric comparison tables (Supplementary Tables S2-S7) of the 16S benchmarking study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw per-sample metric data with no fitted mixed-effects model — fit the lmer() model first; EMMs cannot be computed without a model object The comparison involves only two groups or pre-specified orthogonal contrasts where Tukey's all-pairwise adjustment is unnecessary and overly conservative

skills.description: Use when an ITS2 metabarcoding study reports eukaryotic OTU totals, known-species identifications, and kingdom/functional-group percentages that must be compiled into a structured, validated summary table.
skills.name: eukaryotic-otu-summary-extraction
skills.search_text: eukaryotic-otu-summary-extraction Use when an ITS2 metabarcoding study reports eukaryotic OTU totals, known-species identifications, and kingdom/functional-group percentages that must be compiled into a structured, validated summary table. Input is already a computed feature/OTU table (e.g. a BIOM file or abundance matrix) rather than reported summary statistics to be extracted The study reports prokaryotic (16S) OTU summaries only, with no eukaryotic/ITS kingdom or functional-group breakdown The percentages in the source are exact (not '~' rounded), so the article's tolerance-based validation would not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2814 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Extracts and structures reported eukaryotic (ITS2) OTU summary statistics — total OTUs, known-species counts, kingdom-level distribution (Fungi/Plantae/Animalia), and fungal functional-group proportions — into a machine-readable profile table (CSV) for reproducible reporting of metabarcoding results. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Extracts and structures reported eukaryotic (ITS2) OTU summary statistics — total OTUs, known-species counts, kingdom-level distribution (Fungi/Plantae/Animalia), and fungal functional-group proportions — into a machine-readable profile table (CSV) for reproducible reporting of metabarcoding results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed feature/OTU table (e.g. a BIOM file or abundance matrix) rather than reported summary statistics to be extracted The study reports prokaryotic (16S) OTU summaries only, with no eukaryotic/ITS kingdom or functional-group breakdown The percentages in the source are exact (not '~' rounded), so the article's tolerance-based validation would not apply

skills.description: Use when testing a metagenomic classifier's robustness to large out-of-database contaminant genomes, by quantifying precision/recall of leaving reads unclassified rather than misassigning them.
skills.name: eukaryotic-read-unclassification-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: eukaryotic-read-unclassification-precision-recall-evaluation Use when testing a metagenomic classifier's robustness to large out-of-database contaminant genomes, by quantifying precision/recall of leaving reads unclassified rather than misassigning them. The sample is expected to contain only organisms whose genomes or close relatives are in the database — use standard species-level assignment accuracy evaluation instead Input is dominated by short reads; the article notes MetaMaps is not well suited to samples with a high proportion of short reads The goal is abundance/composition estimation (r2 of EM-frequency estimates) rather than robustness to contaminant genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Evaluates whether a long-read metagenomic classifier correctly leaves out-of-database eukaryotic reads unclassified, using simulated contamination sets (e.g., yellow fever mosquito and Toxoplasma gondii reads in MetaMaps experiment e2) to compute precision and recall of non-classification at species, genus, and family levels. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a long-read metagenomic classifier correctly leaves out-of-database eukaryotic reads unclassified, using simulated contamination sets (e.g., yellow fever mosquito and Toxoplasma gondii reads in MetaMaps experiment e2) to compute precision and recall of non-classification at species, genus, and family levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is expected to contain only organisms whose genomes or close relatives are in the database — use standard species-level assignment accuracy evaluation instead Input is dominated by short reads; the article notes MetaMaps is not well suited to samples with a high proportion of short reads The goal is abundance/composition estimation (r2 of EM-frequency estimates) rather than robustness to contaminant genomes

skills.description: Use when representative sequences (e.g. from a DADA2 paired-end run on 16S rRNA data) need taxonomic assignment against PR2 and you must record Eukaryota-assigned read counts to judge which parameters capture target eukaryotic diversity.
skills.name: eukaryotic-taxonomy-read-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: eukaryotic-taxonomy-read-abundance-quantification Use when representative sequences (e.g. from a DADA2 paired-end run on 16S rRNA data) need taxonomic assignment against PR2 and you must record Eukaryota-assigned read counts to judge which parameters capture target eukaryotic diversity. Input is already a feature/taxonomy table or a downstream diversity result — taxonomy assignment requires representative sequences from a repseqs run The analysis targets bacteria/archaea reads only and no eukaryotic (Eukaryota) abundance metric is needed — PR2 is a eukaryotic reference database Single-end Deblur denoising is required (Deblur is single-end), while this skill's workflow uses DADA2 paired-end truncation settings http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantify how many reads in an amplicon run are assigned to Eukaryota by running the Tourmaline taxonomy step on DADA2 representative sequences against a eukaryotic reference database (database_name: PR2), enabling comparison of eukaryotic read capture across parameter settings such as DADA2 truncation lengths. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Quantify how many reads in an amplicon run are assigned to Eukaryota by running the Tourmaline taxonomy step on DADA2 representative sequences against a eukaryotic reference database (database_name: PR2), enabling comparison of eukaryotic read capture across parameter settings such as DADA2 truncation lengths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/taxonomy table or a downstream diversity result — taxonomy assignment requires representative sequences from a repseqs run The analysis targets bacteria/archaea reads only and no eukaryotic (Eukaryota) abundance metric is needed — PR2 is a eukaryotic reference database Single-end Deblur denoising is required (Deblur is single-end), while this skill's workflow uses DADA2 paired-end truncation settings

skills.description: Use when replicate eDNA samples can be grouped (e.g., flower replicates per plant species) and you must judge from accumulation curves whether richness has plateaued or more sampling would recover additional taxa.
skills.name: exact-method-rarefaction
skills.search_text: exact-method-rarefaction Use when replicate eDNA samples can be grouped (e.g., flower replicates per plant species) and you must judge from accumulation curves whether richness has plateaued or more sampling would recover additional taxa. The question concerns which arthropod taxa are present or how communities cluster by plant species, not whether sampling effort is sufficient Samples cannot be grouped into replicate sets per plant species (e.g., singletons or heterogeneous environmental samples), so accumulation curves would be uninterpretable Sample-based species accumulation (rarefaction) using vegan::specaccum with method='exact' on arthropod eDNA OTU/ASV tables grouped per plant species, to test whether arthropod richness recovered from flower eDNA saturates with sampling effort. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Sample-based species accumulation (rarefaction) using vegan::specaccum with method='exact' on arthropod eDNA OTU/ASV tables grouped per plant species, to test whether arthropod richness recovered from flower eDNA saturates with sampling effort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns which arthropod taxa are present or how communities cluster by plant species, not whether sampling effort is sufficient Samples cannot be grouped into replicate sets per plant species (e.g., singletons or heterogeneous environmental samples), so accumulation curves would be uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when comparing the runtime performance of competing FASTQ preprocessing tools (e.g. UMI extraction by fastp, umis, UMI-tools) on an identical input file, and you need reproducible wall-clock timings and throughput numbers.
skills.name: execution-time-profiling
skills.search_text: execution-time-profiling Use when comparing the runtime performance of competing FASTQ preprocessing tools (e.g. UMI extraction by fastp, umis, UMI-tools) on an identical input file, and you need reproducible wall-clock timings and throughput numbers. The input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — fastp targets short reads and fastplong should be considered instead. The goal is correctness/functional comparison of preprocessing results rather than speed benchmarking. The FASTQ has no UMI or the UMI is not at a fixed position in read1, so the tools cannot be configured for an equivalent task. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark wall-clock execution time of FASTQ preprocessing tools on the same input to quantify speed differences — here, fastp vs umis vs UMI-tools for UMI extraction on 4 Gb Illumina PE150 data, where fastp is ~2.7x faster than umis and ~6.1x faster than UMI-tools. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock execution time of FASTQ preprocessing tools on the same input to quantify speed differences — here, fastp vs umis vs UMI-tools for UMI extraction on 4 Gb Illumina PE150 data, where fastp is ~2.7x faster than umis and ~6.1x faster than UMI-tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — fastp targets short reads and fastplong should be considered instead. The goal is correctness/functional comparison of preprocessing results rather than speed benchmarking. The FASTQ has no UMI or the UMI is not at a fixed position in read1, so the tools cannot be configured for an equivalent task.

skills.description: Use when an artificial 'mock' community amplicon dataset with a known expected taxonomic composition is available and you need to measure how faithfully rRNA classifiers recover that composition.
skills.name: expected-vs-recovered-abundance-comparison
skills.search_text: expected-vs-recovered-abundance-comparison Use when an artificial 'mock' community amplicon dataset with a known expected taxonomic composition is available and you need to measure how faithfully rRNA classifiers recover that composition. Input is real environmental/clinical data with no known expected taxonomic composition — there is no ground truth to compare abundances against The goal is OTU-based (closed-reference clustering) rather than taxonomy-based abundance recovery — MAPseq's hierarchical OTU mapping is a separate analysis path Reads are non-rRNA sequences; MAPseq is designed for ribosomal RNA sequence classification only http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarking skill that classifies an artificial mock rRNA community dataset with MAPseq and competing tools, aggregates per-tool classified read counts into species/genus/family abundance profiles, and compares recovered vs expected abundances to quantify classification accuracy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that classifies an artificial mock rRNA community dataset with MAPseq and competing tools, aggregates per-tool classified read counts into species/genus/family abundance profiles, and compares recovered vs expected abundances to quantify classification accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real environmental/clinical data with no known expected taxonomic composition — there is no ground truth to compare abundances against The goal is OTU-based (closed-reference clustering) rather than taxonomy-based abundance recovery — MAPseq's hierarchical OTU mapping is a separate analysis path Reads are non-rRNA sequences; MAPseq is designed for ribosomal RNA sequence classification only

skills.description: Use when comparing rRNA amplicon classifiers on reads of known identity, to reproduce MAPseq-style F½-score rankings against genus-level and 98%-identity hOTU placement targets.

skills.search_text: false-positive-rate-quantification Decision support for choosing between top BLAST hit and RDP classifier taxonomic assignment of CO1 metabarcodes, or for benchmarking any assignment method's false positive rate on sequences with known ground-truth taxa. The goal is to assign taxonomy to unknown environmental sequences rather than to benchmark false positive rates on sequences with known ground truth. Sequences are full-length (500 bp+) CO1 barcodes — the RDP classifier is ~19x faster and Table 2 cutoffs differ (70% bootstrap at genus rank for 500 bp+ rather than 60% for 200 bp). skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to short (120–135 bp) COI eDNA amplicon reads from elasmobranch samples and no ready-made reference covering both target elasmobranchs and non-target homologs exists.
skills.name: fasta-reference-database-curation
skills.search_text: fasta-reference-database-curation Use when assigning taxonomy to short (120–135 bp) COI eDNA amplicon reads from elasmobranch samples and no ready-made reference covering both target elasmobranchs and non-target homologs exists. The marker is not the 127 bp COI fragment amplified by the elasmobranch-specific primer pair — an in silico PCR-extracted database matched to a different primer pair or locus is inappropriate. Species-level resolution among closely related elasmobranchs (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) is required; some MOTUs are 100% identical to multiple BOLD species, and the authors note longer-fragment primers would be needed. A published release comparable in sequence content and taxonomic coverage (github.com/metabarpark/Reference-databases) already satisfies the need — reuse it rather than rebuilding. Assembles a bespoke elasmobranch COI reference FASTA by merging BOLD-derived elasmobranch sequences (containing the 127 bp target fragment) with ecoPCR-extracted non-elasmobranch homologs, for use with ecotag taxonomic assignment in eDNA metabarcoding. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assembles a bespoke elasmobranch COI reference FASTA by merging BOLD-derived elasmobranch sequences (containing the 127 bp target fragment) with ecoPCR-extracted non-elasmobranch homologs, for use with ecotag taxonomic assignment in eDNA metabarcoding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The marker is not the 127 bp COI fragment amplified by the elasmobranch-specific primer pair — an in silico PCR-extracted database matched to a different primer pair or locus is inappropriate. Species-level resolution among closely related elasmobranchs (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) is required; some MOTUs are 100% identical to multiple BOLD species, and the authors note longer-fragment primers would be needed. A published release comparable in sequence content and taxonomic coverage (github.com/metabarpark/Reference-databases) already satisfies the need — reuse it rather than rebuilding.

skills.description: Use when trimming Illumina short-read FASTQ data without knowing the adapter sequence, and you need to recover or reimplement fastp's seed-and-nucleotide-tree adapter detection.
skills.name: fastq-adapter-sequence-auto-detection
skills.search_text: fastq-adapter-sequence-auto-detection Use when trimming Illumina short-read FASTQ data without knowing the adapter sequence, and you need to recover or reimplement fastp's seed-and-nucleotide-tree adapter detection. Processing long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the README directs those inputs to fastplong instead of fastp Adapter sequences are already known and provided as input — fastp's auto-detection is specifically for when you don't have to input the adapter sequences Data quality/composition makes high-frequency 10-mers reflect genomic content rather than adapter (e.g. low-diversity libraries with low-complexity seeds not filtered out) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Reconstructs fastp's automatic adapter-detection algorithm (Algorithm 1): adapter seeds are found as high-frequency 10-mers in the first 1M reads of a single-end FASTQ file, then extended via nucleotide-tree traversal into complete adapter sequences without requiring adapter input. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560

skills.description: Use when processing paired-end Illumina FASTQ data (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) and you need duplication-rate evaluation or to replicate fastp's key1/key2 array-based duplication estimation.
skills.name: fastq-paired-end-data-handling
skills.search_text: fastq-paired-end-data-handling Use when processing paired-end Illumina FASTQ data (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) and you need duplication-rate evaluation or to replicate fastp's key1/key2 array-based duplication estimation. Input is single-end FASTQ — the key1/key2 scheme requires both mates of each pair Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, since fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina NovaSeq, MGI) Reads carry UMI sequences — deduplication should be UMI-aware rather than based on identical base pairs alone http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, where key1 is derived from the first 12 bp of read1 as an offset into a 2^24-entry duplication array D and key2 from the first 32 bp of read2 as a 64-bit integer incrementing a counting array C. This differs from FASTQC's hash-table approach and yields an estimate of the PE duplication rate. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, where key1 is derived from the first 12 bp of read1 as an offset into a 2^24-entry duplication array D and key2 from the first 32 bp of read2 as a 64-bit integer incrementing a counting array C. This differs from FASTQC's hash-table approach and yields an estimate of the PE duplication rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end FASTQ — the key1/key2 scheme requires both mates of each pair Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead, since fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina NovaSeq, MGI) Reads carry UMI sequences — deduplication should be UMI-aware rather than based on identical base pairs alone

skills.description: Use when paired-end amplicon reads have been merged per sample (e.g. temp/Sample1.merged.fq) and a uniform filtering pass (primer strip + max expected error) must be applied across all samples in one vsearch call before OTU/ASV analysis.
skills.name: fastq-sequence-concatenation
skills.search_text: fastq-sequence-concatenation Use when paired-end amplicon reads have been merged per sample (e.g. temp/Sample1.merged.fq) and a uniform filtering pass (primer strip + max expected error) must be applied across all samples in one vsearch call before OTU/ASV analysis. Input is per-sample FASTQ that has not yet been merged and relabeled with sample-ID prefixes — merging (--fastq_mergepairs) must come first so headers carry sample provenance. Input is already a pooled/concatenated FASTQ awaiting only OTU clustering, dereplication, or chimera removal — this concatenation step belongs strictly in the preprocessing stage before primer trimming. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is per-sample FASTQ that has not yet been merged and relabeled with sample-ID prefixes — merging (--fastq_mergepairs) must come first so headers carry sample provenance. skills.description: Use when building or auditing a CO1 (or other gene) reference set from GenBank for a taxon of interest, e.g., to measure which genera or species have full-length species-rank barcodes and identify coverage gaps.
skills.name: genbank-nucleotide-sequence-retrieval
skills.search_text: genbank-nucleotide-sequence-retrieval Use when building or auditing a CO1 (or other gene) reference set from GenBank for a taxon of interest, e.g., to measure which genera or species have full-length species-rank barcodes and identify coverage gaps. The query sequences are not intended for taxonomic assignment or reference-set building — e.g., you already have a curated training set like CO1 Eukaryote v1/v2 or the RDP_COI releases and only need to classify queries via the RDP classifier You need a community-curated reference database equivalent to SILVA/Greengenes/UNITE for CO1 — none exists, and ad hoc GenBank mining will not substitute for targeted barcoding of local biota Records lack complete binomial species names or contain sp./nr./aff./cf. designations — these should be excluded rather than retrieved, per the paper's taxon-list rules http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Retrieves and curates GenBank CO1 reference sequences for a taxonomic group by querying the NCBI taxonomy database to build a formatted taxon list, then querying the NCBI nucleotide database with an Entrez CO1 gene term and filtering records by sequence length and taxonomic rank. It underpins construction of CO1 reference sets (e.g., the CO1 Eukaryote v1 training set) and quantification of database coverage gaps. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Retrieves and curates GenBank CO1 reference sequences for a taxonomic group by querying the NCBI taxonomy database to build a formatted taxon list, then querying the NCBI nucleotide database with an Entrez CO1 gene term and filtering records by sequence length and taxonomic rank. It underpins construction of CO1 reference sets (e.g., the CO1 Eukaryote v1 training set) and quantification of database coverage gaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query sequences are not intended for taxonomic assignment or reference-set building — e.g., you already have a curated training set like CO1 Eukaryote v1/v2 or the RDP_COI releases and only need to classify queries via the RDP classifier You need a community-curated reference database equivalent to SILVA/Greengenes/UNITE for CO1 — none exists, and ad hoc GenBank mining will not substitute for targeted barcoding of local biota Records lack complete binomial species names or contain sp./nr./aff./cf. designations — these should be excluded rather than retrieved, per the paper's taxon-list rules

skills.description: Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon datasets and you need to turn genome-level abundance/molarity inputs into realistic per-sample ASV count matrices with metaSPARSim-style negative binomial variability.
skills.name: genome-molarity-to-asv-abundance-mapping
skills.search_text: genome-molarity-to-asv-abundance-mapping Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon datasets and you need to turn genome-level abundance/molarity inputs into realistic per-sample ASV count matrices with metaSPARSim-style negative binomial variability. Input is already an ASV feature/count table — no genome-to-amplicon molarity mapping is needed or available Simulating Illumina short-read or single-end amplicon data — MHASS targets PacBio HiFi amplicon sequencing with dual barcoding and pass-number (np) distributions You only need technical read-level simulation (PBSIM error model, barcoding) without genome-aware biological abundance variability http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 MHASS's genome-aware abundance simulation step converts user-supplied genome molarity values into per-sample ASV abundance matrices by fitting a negative binomial model with metaSPARSim's R1 preset parameters to model between-sample variability for each ASV. Negative sampled variability estimates are emulated as NA (converted to 0 by metaSPARSim), yielding identical replicate abundances before technical sampling. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: MHASS's genome-aware abundance simulation step converts user-supplied genome molarity values into per-sample ASV abundance matrices by fitting a negative binomial model with metaSPARSim's R1 preset parameters to model between-sample variability for each ASV. Negative sampled variability estimates are emulated as NA (converted to 0 by metaSPARSim), yielding identical replicate abundances before technical sampling.

Input genomes are already quality-controlled or represent a small curated isolate set where CheckM thresholds add no value The goal is profiling metagenomes against an existing MetaPhlAn 4 database rather than reconstructing the SGB database itself Working with viral or eukaryotic genomes, which the paper notes are not extensively incorporated 'due to their unique genomic architectures and quality control requirements relative to bacterial and archaeal genomes' http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quality-filter an integrated catalog of reference and metagenome-assembled genomes with CheckM before dereplication, retaining only genomes with completeness >50% and contamination <5%. skills.search_text: genus-level-asv-taxonomic-classification Use when raw 16S rRNA FASTQ data from sputum or mock-community samples must be denoised to ASVs, assigned taxonomy at genus level, and cross-validated for sensitivity/specificity against a ZymoBIOMICS standard control. The goal is full-length 16S rRNA taxonomic resolution — the study explicitly does not compare against full-length third-generation sequencing and recommends it as future work. Species-level or strain-level identification is required — taxonomic assignments here are collapsed at the genus level only. Estimating absolute sensitivity/specificity on complex communities — the ZymoBIOMICS mock control contains only 10 species, which limits sensitivity/specificity estimates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Classifies 16S rRNA amplicons from respiratory (sputum) samples into bacterial ASVs collapsed at genus level using Deblur denoising and Greengenes taxonomy, then benchmarks classification accuracy against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community via ROC/AUC to identify the best-performing hypervariable region. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Classifies 16S rRNA amplicons from respiratory (sputum) samples into bacterial ASVs collapsed at genus level using Deblur denoising and Greengenes taxonomy, then benchmarks classification accuracy against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community via ROC/AUC to identify the best-performing hypervariable region.

skills.name: ground-truth-profile-comparison
skills.search_text: ground-truth-profile-comparison Use when profiling synthetic/mock metagenomes whose per-genome (SGB) abundance compositions are known, and you need to quantify detection and quantification accuracy of a profiler such as MetaPhlAn 4 with per-SGB F1 scores. The input is real (non-synthetic) metagenome data with no known ground-truth composition — F1 against expected SGBs cannot be computed You already have a per-sample relative abundance table and no reference genome compositions to compare against The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic detection/quantification accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Scores a taxonomic profiler's species-level output against known ground-truth genome compositions by computing per-SGB F1 scores that combine detection (presence/absence) and quantification (relative-abundance agreement). This is the evaluation strategy MetaPhlAn 4 used to demonstrate that uSGBs are detected as accurately as kSGBs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Scores a taxonomic profiler's species-level output against known ground-truth genome compositions by computing per-SGB F1 scores that combine detection (presence/absence) and quantification (relative-abundance agreement). This is the evaluation strategy MetaPhlAn 4 used to demonstrate that uSGBs are detected as accurately as kSGBs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real (non-synthetic) metagenome data with no known ground-truth composition — F1 against expected SGBs cannot be computed You already have a per-sample relative abundance table and no reference genome compositions to compare against The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic detection/quantification accuracy

skills.description: Use when estimating or replicating fastp's paired-end duplication rate from FASTQ data, implementing key1/key2 array-based duplication counting, or assessing how hash collisions bias duplication metrics versus FASTQC.
skills.name: hash-collision-error-assessment
skills.search_text: hash-collision-error-assessment Use when estimating or replicating fastp's paired-end duplication rate from FASTQ data, implementing key1/key2 array-based duplication counting, or assessing how hash collisions bias duplication metrics versus FASTQC. Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — fastp/this key scheme targets short reads; use fastplong instead Goal is FASTQC-style hash-table duplication profiling rather than fastp's array-based key1/key2 evaluation Single-end-only deduplication workflow where the paired-end key1/key2 scheme does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, in which key1 (first 12 bp of read1, offset into a 2^24-entry array D) and key2 (first 32 bp of read2, packed into a 64-bit integer) replace FASTQC's hash-table approach, and quantifies the hash-collision error (~0.01% of reads) inherent to fixed-size counting arrays. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, in which key1 (first 12 bp of read1, offset into a 2^24-entry array D) and key2 (first 32 bp of read2, packed into a 64-bit integer) replace FASTQC's hash-table approach, and quantifies the hash-collision error (~0.01% of reads) inherent to fixed-size counting arrays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — fastp/this key scheme targets short reads; use fastplong instead Goal is FASTQC-style hash-table duplication profiling rather than fastp's array-based key1/key2 evaluation Single-end-only deduplication workflow where the paired-end key1/key2 scheme does not apply

skills.description: Use when an OTU table (e.g. 2425 OTUs over 130 sites from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2, uncurated or LULU-curated) must be transformed into Hellinger-standardized abundance or binary presence/absence form before computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity for β-diversity or Mantel correlation analyses.
skills.name: hellinger-abundance-transformation
skills.search_text: hellinger-abundance-transformation Use when an OTU table (e.g. 2425 OTUs over 130 sites from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2, uncurated or LULU-curated) must be transformed into Hellinger-standardized abundance or binary presence/absence form before computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity for β-diversity or Mantel correlation analyses. Input is already a transformed or relative-abundance table — re-transforming would distort the Bray-Curtis dissimilarities The goal is α-diversity estimation rather than composition/turnover: the paper notes current approaches retaining composition metrics are 'much less so for α-diversity', and Hellinger/Bray-Curtis is a β-diversity tool The aim is to identify individual rare species, since LULU-style curation and dissimilarity-level analyses are not suitable for that purpose Converts OTU abundance tables (samples as columns, OTUs as rows, per the LULU format) into Hellinger-transformed relative-abundance matrices — and paired binary presence/absence matrices — so that Bray-Curtis dissimilarity among the 130 Danish field sites can be computed and compared against plant survey ground truth via Mantel tests. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Converts OTU abundance tables (samples as columns, OTUs as rows, per the LULU format) into Hellinger-transformed relative-abundance matrices — and paired binary presence/absence matrices — so that Bray-Curtis dissimilarity among the 130 Danish field sites can be computed and compared against plant survey ground truth via Mantel tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a transformed or relative-abundance table — re-transforming would distort the Bray-Curtis dissimilarities The goal is α-diversity estimation rather than composition/turnover: the paper notes current approaches retaining composition metrics are 'much less so for α-diversity', and Hellinger/Bray-Curtis is a β-diversity tool The aim is to identify individual rare species, since LULU-style curation and dissimilarity-level analyses are not suitable for that purpose

skills.description: Use when you have a plant-species (or site) x arthropod-OTU count table from eDNA metabarcoding and need to visualise/quantify whether community composition clusters by sample grouping via average-linkage dendrograms.
skills.name: hierarchical-average-linkage-clustering
skills.search_text: hierarchical-average-linkage-clustering Use when you have a plant-species (or site) x arthropod-OTU count table from eDNA metabarcoding and need to visualise/quantify whether community composition clusters by sample grouping via average-linkage dendrograms. The question concerns gradient-based relationships with environmental predictors better handled by ordination/RDA (the article used RDA separately for that purpose). The count table is dominated by high-abundance taxa you do not want down-weighted and a presence/absence or untransformed metric is preferred; Raup-Crick on cube-root-transformed counts is tuned to incidence-driven metabarcoding data. Data are continuous trait measurements rather than community count data, where Raup-Crick dissimilarity is undefined or inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Cluster arthropod eDNA community samples (e.g. flower samples by plant species) using Raup-Crick dissimilarity and UPGMA (average-linkage) hierarchical clustering, rendered as a pheatmap dendrogram, to test whether communities segregate by plant species. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Cluster arthropod eDNA community samples (e.g. flower samples by plant species) using Raup-Crick dissimilarity and UPGMA (average-linkage) hierarchical clustering, rendered as a pheatmap dendrogram, to test whether communities segregate by plant species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns gradient-based relationships with environmental predictors better handled by ordination/RDA (the article used RDA separately for that purpose). The count table is dominated by high-abundance taxa you do not want down-weighted and a presence/absence or untransformed metric is preferred; Raup-Crick on cube-root-transformed counts is tuned to incidence-driven metabarcoding data. Data are continuous trait measurements rather than community count data, where Raup-Crick dissimilarity is undefined or inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify runtime and memory requirements of a multi-sample amplicon workflow (e.g. >27,000 samples, billions of reads) on a bounded cluster allocation such as 50 cores.
