Input is already a demultiplexed, denoised sequence table or MOTU/ASV abundance matrix rather than raw FASTQ reads The amplicon targets nuclear loci or non-mitochondrial markers for which the 16S/COI-specific error models and 5 bp merge-overlap assumptions of this workflow were built Denoises raw paired-end Illumina amplicon reads (mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI) into error-corrected MOTU count tables using the DADA2 R package, as applied to flower eDNA metabarcoding of terrestrial arthropods. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Denoises raw paired-end Illumina amplicon reads (mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI) into error-corrected MOTU count tables using the DADA2 R package, as applied to flower eDNA metabarcoding of terrestrial arthropods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a demultiplexed, denoised sequence table or MOTU/ASV abundance matrix rather than raw FASTQ reads The amplicon targets nuclear loci or non-mitochondrial markers for which the 16S/COI-specific error models and 5 bp merge-overlap assumptions of this workflow were built

skills.description: Use when raw metagenomic sequencing reads (FASTQ) from microbiome samples must be converted into per-sample taxonomic abundance profiles and functional gene-family/KO tables for downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: marker-gene-taxonomic-profiling
skills.search_text: marker-gene-taxonomic-profiling Use when raw metagenomic sequencing reads (FASTQ) from microbiome samples must be converted into per-sample taxonomic abundance profiles and functional gene-family/KO tables for downstream statistical analysis. Input is amplicon (e.g. 16S) data — the article recommends a separate amplicon analysis pipeline (QIIME 2-based) rather than this metagenomic workflow Input is already a taxonomic or KO feature table — proceed directly to the article's statistical/visualization methods instead of re-profiling Data are metatranscriptome, metaproteome, or metabolome — the article notes these 'have not been widely accepted due to their high cost and the complex experimental and analysis methods required' http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A reproducible metagenomic profiling pipeline from the Liu et al. 2020 Protein & Cell practical guide that converts raw metagenomic FASTQ reads into taxonomic abundance tables (via marker-gene and k-mer profilers) and KEGG orthology (KO) functional tables, using the step-by-step scripts from the YongxinLiu/Liu2020ProteinCell repository. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: A reproducible metagenomic profiling pipeline from the Liu et al. 2020 Protein & Cell practical guide that converts raw metagenomic FASTQ reads into taxonomic abundance tables (via marker-gene and k-mer profilers) and KEGG orthology (KO) functional tables, using the step-by-step scripts from the YongxinLiu/Liu2020ProteinCell repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is amplicon (e.g. 16S) data — the article recommends a separate amplicon analysis pipeline (QIIME 2-based) rather than this metagenomic workflow Input is already a taxonomic or KO feature table — proceed directly to the article's statistical/visualization methods instead of re-profiling Data are metatranscriptome, metaproteome, or metabolome — the article notes these 'have not been widely accepted due to their high cost and the complex experimental and analysis methods required'

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to (M)OTUs/ASVs from eDNA metabarcoding of 16S/18S rRNA, ITS, or COI marker genes in PEMA, and when deciding between alignment-based and phylogeny-based assignment for 16S rRNA.
skills.name: marker-gene-taxonomy-assignment-configuration
skills.search_text: marker-gene-taxonomy-assignment-configuration Use when assigning taxonomy to (M)OTUs/ASVs from eDNA metabarcoding of 16S/18S rRNA, ITS, or COI marker genes in PEMA, and when deciding between alignment-based and phylogeny-based assignment for 16S rRNA. The data are shotgun metagenomes rather than amplicon (marker-gene) reads — PEMA is designed for metabarcoding amplicon analysis of 16S/18S rRNA, 12S rRNA, ITS, and COI. A taxonomy table already exists and only downstream ecological analysis (e.g., phyloseq) is needed. The target marker gene has no OTU route in PEMA — e.g., COI supports only Swarm ASV inference, and 12S rRNA (added in v.2.1.4) has no VSEARCH OTU option. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Configure taxonomy assignment within PEMA by pairing each marker gene (16S/18S rRNA, ITS, COI) with its alignment-based classifier and reference database, and optionally invoking the phylogeny-based route for 16S rRNA using a Silva-derived reference tree. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Configure taxonomy assignment within PEMA by pairing each marker gene (16S/18S rRNA, ITS, COI) with its alignment-based classifier and reference database, and optionally invoking the phylogeny-based route for 16S rRNA using a Silva-derived reference tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are shotgun metagenomes rather than amplicon (marker-gene) reads — PEMA is designed for metabarcoding amplicon analysis of 16S/18S rRNA, 12S rRNA, ITS, and COI. A taxonomy table already exists and only downstream ecological analysis (e.g., phyloseq) is needed. The target marker gene has no OTU route in PEMA — e.g., COI supports only Swarm ASV inference, and 12S rRNA (added in v.2.1.4) has no VSEARCH OTU option.

skills.description: Use when a genome catalog of hundreds of thousands of reference genomes and/or MAGs must be reduced to species-level clusters (SGBs) prior to pangenome construction and species-unique marker extraction.
skills.name: mash-genome-dereplication
skills.search_text: mash-genome-dereplication Use when a genome catalog of hundreds of thousands of reference genomes and/or MAGs must be reduced to species-level clusters (SGBs) prior to pangenome construction and species-unique marker extraction. Input genomes have not passed quality control (completeness >50%, contamination <5%) — clustering unfiltered genomes will inflate SGB counts with fragmented or contaminated MAGs Goal is below-species (strain-level) clustering — 5% identity is a species-level cut point, not a strain dereplication threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Dereplicates large catalogs of prokaryotic reference genomes and MAGs into species-level genome bins (SGBs) using Mash MinHash sketches at a 5% sequence-similarity threshold, the clustering step underlying the MetaPhlAn 4 marker database. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Dereplicates large catalogs of prokaryotic reference genomes and MAGs into species-level genome bins (SGBs) using Mash MinHash sketches at a 5% sequence-similarity threshold, the clustering step underlying the MetaPhlAn 4 marker database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes have not passed quality control (completeness >50%, contamination <5%) — clustering unfiltered genomes will inflate SGB counts with fragmented or contaminated MAGs Goal is below-species (strain-level) clustering — 5% identity is a species-level cut point, not a strain dereplication threshold

skills.description: Use when you have an OTU table plus a FASTA file of OTU representative sequences and need to curate the table with LULU, which cannot run without a precomputed match list.
skills.name: matchlist-generation-from-otu-sequences
skills.search_text: matchlist-generation-from-otu-sequences Use when you have an OTU table plus a FASTA file of OTU representative sequences and need to curate the table with LULU, which cannot run without a precomputed match list. You only need curated biodiversity metrics and already possess a valid match list — regenerating it is unnecessary The OTU ids in the sequence FASTA do not match the OTU table row names — fix the ids first, since LULU requires matching identifiers You are running dbotu3 in its intended one-step clustering mode, which does not use a LULU-style match list input http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Produces a three-column match list (query OTU id, matching OTU id, percent similarity) by all-against-all pairwise comparison of OTU representative sequences, as the mandatory second input required by the LULU post-clustering curation algorithm. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Produces a three-column match list (query OTU id, matching OTU id, percent similarity) by all-against-all pairwise comparison of OTU representative sequences, as the mandatory second input required by the LULU post-clustering curation algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need curated biodiversity metrics and already possess a valid match list — regenerating it is unnecessary The OTU ids in the sequence FASTA do not match the OTU table row names — fix the ids first, since LULU requires matching identifiers You are running dbotu3 in its intended one-step clustering mode, which does not use a LULU-style match list input

skills.description: Use when long reads have probabilistic mapping scores to multiple candidate (possibly strain-level) reference genomes and each read must be resolved to a single taxon while jointly estimating sample composition.
skills.name: maximum-likelihood-read-assignment
skills.search_text: maximum-likelihood-read-assignment Use when long reads have probabilistic mapping scores to multiple candidate (possibly strain-level) reference genomes and each read must be resolved to a single taxon while jointly estimating sample composition. Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length produce minimizer sets too small for reliable mapping and remain unassigned Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities not represented in the RefSeq database, where database-sample mismatch dominates When only raw k-mer-based taxonomic labels without positional/mapping-quality information are sufficient — this skill is specific to mapping-based long-read assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Resolve ambiguous long-read mapping locations by assigning each read to its maximum-likelihood genome under an EM-estimated sample composition, as implemented in MetaMaps' classify step. This step simultaneously disambiguates reads shared between closely related RefSeq genomes and yields per-read taxonomic assignments plus composition estimates. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Resolve ambiguous long-read mapping locations by assigning each read to its maximum-likelihood genome under an EM-estimated sample composition, as implemented in MetaMaps' classify step. This step simultaneously disambiguates reads shared between closely related RefSeq genomes and yields per-read taxonomic assignments plus composition estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length produce minimizer sets too small for reliable mapping and remain unassigned Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities not represented in the RefSeq database, where database-sample mismatch dominates When only raw k-mer-based taxonomic labels without positional/mapping-quality information are sufficient — this skill is specific to mapping-based long-read assignment

skills.description: Use when a default-mode MetaMaps run against the >12,000-genome miniSeq+H/RefSeq database needs ~262 GB RAM but the target machine offers far less (e.g. 28 GB or 16 GB), and a small runtime penalty is acceptable.
skills.name: memory-constrained-execution-tuning
skills.search_text: memory-constrained-execution-tuning Use when a default-mode MetaMaps run against the >12,000-genome miniSeq+H/RefSeq database needs ~262 GB RAM but the target machine offers far less (e.g. 28 GB or 16 GB), and a small runtime penalty is acceptable. The machine has enough RAM (~262 GB) for default-mode mapping, since memory-efficient mode only adds 1.2-1.4x runtime overhead without memory-pressure benefits The sample contains a high proportion of short reads or reads below the minimum length requirement, which MetaMaps handles poorly regardless of memory mode Real-time/streaming analysis is required — MetaMaps has no streaming-data support, and this skill addresses memory capping, not latency http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run MetaMaps' mapping step in memory-efficient mode using the --maxmemory parameter to cap peak RAM (e.g. 28 GB or 16 GB) when a default-mode run against the >12,000-genome RefSeq database (~262 GB RAM) exceeds available machine memory, accepting a modest 1.2-1.4x runtime increase with virtually no loss of assignment accuracy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Run MetaMaps' mapping step in memory-efficient mode using the --maxmemory parameter to cap peak RAM (e.g. 28 GB or 16 GB) when a default-mode run against the >12,000-genome RefSeq database (~262 GB RAM) exceeds available machine memory, accepting a modest 1.2-1.4x runtime increase with virtually no loss of assignment accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The machine has enough RAM (~262 GB) for default-mode mapping, since memory-efficient mode only adds 1.2-1.4x runtime overhead without memory-pressure benefits The sample contains a high proportion of short reads or reads below the minimum length requirement, which MetaMaps handles poorly regardless of memory mode Real-time/streaming analysis is required — MetaMaps has no streaming-data support, and this skill addresses memory capping, not latency

skills.description: Use when a clustering pipeline for amplicon FASTA inputs is expected to exceed available RAM (tera-scale datasets), and you must verify that 2-bit packed representations actually deliver the documented memory reduction.
skills.name: memory-footprint-benchmarking
skills.search_text: memory-footprint-benchmarking Use when a clustering pipeline for amplicon FASTA inputs is expected to exceed available RAM (tera-scale datasets), and you must verify that 2-bit packed representations actually deliver the documented memory reduction. The input FASTA entries lack the required abundance suffixes (e.g. _1000), since swarm requires each entry to carry an occurrence count to work properly The question is clustering quality or OTU delineation rather than memory/compression measurement (e.g. choosing the local threshold d) Comparing wall-clock speed across versions without controlling for the documented ~15% slowdown at d >= 2 on some datasets (e.g. 18SV9) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Measures and validates the RAM savings obtained from swarm v3's compressed sequence representation (2-bit nucleotide packing with Zobrist hashing and a Bloom filter) by benchmarking memory footprint against the one-byte-per-nucleotide baseline and the ~0.6x input-FASTA rule of thumb. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: Measures and validates the RAM savings obtained from swarm v3's compressed sequence representation (2-bit nucleotide packing with Zobrist hashing and a Bloom filter) by benchmarking memory footprint against the one-byte-per-nucleotide baseline and the ~0.6x input-FASTA rule of thumb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input FASTA entries lack the required abundance suffixes (e.g. _1000), since swarm requires each entry to carry an occurrence count to work properly The question is clustering quality or OTU delineation rather than memory/compression measurement (e.g. choosing the local threshold d) Comparing wall-clock speed across versions without controlling for the documented ~15% slowdown at d >= 2 on some datasets (e.g. 18SV9)

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end amplicon reads from a biological mock community (with a known expected reference fasta) are available and you need to compare how denoising vs clustering pipelines recover expected, partial, and missed sequences.
skills.name: metabarcoding-benchmark-table-assembly
skills.search_text: metabarcoding-benchmark-table-assembly Use when raw paired-end amplicon reads from a biological mock community (with a known expected reference fasta) are available and you need to compare how denoising vs clustering pipelines recover expected, partial, and missed sequences. Input is already a feature table with no representative sequences or expected mock reference fasta available for alignment The study has no biological mock community, so exact/partial/miss recovery cannot be evaluated against known expected sequences The goal is taxonomic classification accuracy (classifier benchmarking) rather than sequence-recovery comparison between denoising and clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark amplicon denoising (DADA2, Deblur) against VSEARCH clustering by recovering a mock community's expected sequences, aligning every representative sequence back to the expected mock references, and assembling a per-library table of exact/partial/miss counts to quantify ASV recovery differences. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Benchmark amplicon denoising (DADA2, Deblur) against VSEARCH clustering by recovering a mock community's expected sequences, aligning every representative sequence back to the expected mock references, and assembling a per-library table of exact/partial/miss counts to quantify ASV recovery differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table with no representative sequences or expected mock reference fasta available for alignment The study has no biological mock community, so exact/partial/miss recovery cannot be evaluated against known expected sequences The goal is taxonomic classification accuracy (classifier benchmarking) rather than sequence-recovery comparison between denoising and clustering

skills.description: Use when a MOTU table built with sumaclust (99% similarity) contains single-read MOTUs and the goal is a conservative contamination/false-positive control before computing elasmobranch (or other taxon) richness per sampling location or region.
skills.name: metabarcoding-contamination-control
skills.search_text: metabarcoding-contamination-control Use when a MOTU table built with sumaclust (99% similarity) contains single-read MOTUs and the goal is a conservative contamination/false-positive control before computing elasmobranch (or other taxon) richness per sampling location or region. The input is raw FASTQ reads — singleton removal operates on dereplicated, clustered MOTU tables, not reads; quality/length filtering happens earlier with illuminapairedend, obigrep length filtering (120–135 bp), and vsearch chimera removal The analysis aims to detect genuinely rare, low-abundance taxa where single-read evidence must be retained — the paper explicitly accepts losing such signals as the price of a conservative control MOTUs were not clustered with sumaclust and assigned with ecotag — the singleton definition (MOTU supported by exactly one read) depends on that per-MOTU read-count structure A conservative metabarcoding quality-control skill that removes all single-read (singleton) MOTUs from an ecotag taxonomic assignment table to control contamination and sequencing-error false positives, then recounts per-location and per-region MOTU richness on the filtered set. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: A conservative metabarcoding quality-control skill that removes all single-read (singleton) MOTUs from an ecotag taxonomic assignment table to control contamination and sequencing-error false positives, then recounts per-location and per-region MOTU richness on the filtered set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ reads — singleton removal operates on dereplicated, clustered MOTU tables, not reads; quality/length filtering happens earlier with illuminapairedend, obigrep length filtering (120–135 bp), and vsearch chimera removal The analysis aims to detect genuinely rare, low-abundance taxa where single-read evidence must be retained — the paper explicitly accepts losing such signals as the price of a conservative control MOTUs were not clustered with sumaclust and assigned with ecotag — the singleton definition (MOTU supported by exactly one read) depends on that per-MOTU read-count structure

Input is already a machine-readable OTU/ASV feature table or BIOM file — count extraction from figures/Venn segments would be redundant and lossy The study reports abundance (read counts) rather than delimited species/OTU occurrence counts — Venn-segment reproduction does not recover abundances Exact farm/sample metadata are withheld and cannot be mapped to segments — note this study states 'The exact location of these farms cannot be disclosed based on the farmer demand' http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs species occurrence counts from a metabarcoding study by extracting reported Venn-diagram segment counts (inflow I-source vs pond P-source water samples across three trout farm locations B, N, G) and assembling them into a tidy occurrence-count table whose totals reconcile to the article's reported species counts. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a machine-readable OTU/ASV feature table or BIOM file — count extraction from figures/Venn segments would be redundant and lossy The study reports abundance (read counts) rather than delimited species/OTU occurrence counts — Venn-segment reproduction does not recover abundances Exact farm/sample metadata are withheld and cannot be mapped to segments — note this study states 'The exact location of these farms cannot be disclosed based on the farmer demand'

skills.description: Use when a practitioner needs to reproduce or extend the assessment of how denoising vs. clustering pipeline choices and sequence filtering regimes alter per-sample alpha diversity (Hill Numbers 0/1/2) in amplicon data.
skills.name: metabarcoding-diversity-figure-reproduction
skills.search_text: metabarcoding-diversity-figure-reproduction Use when a practitioner needs to reproduce or extend the assessment of how denoising vs. clustering pipeline choices and sequence filtering regimes alter per-sample alpha diversity (Hill Numbers 0/1/2) in amplicon data. When the goal is to select a single best metabarcoding pipeline — the paper states its aim is not to present a single best pathway, only to illustrate how processes are affected by program or parameter choices When the input is already a rarefied, filtered feature table with diversity values computed — this skill reproduces the full pipeline from raw reads through denoising, filtering, and rarefaction When data are not COI amplicon libraries (e.g., 16S/ITS) with reference databases like UNITE, Greengenes, or SILVA, since host/mock COI removal and the mock-guided 'miss' subtraction are COI-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reproduces the O'Rourke et al. (2020) 'tidybug' analysis showing that Hill-number alpha diversity of bat guano COI metabarcoding data remains sensitive to the choice of denoising program (DADA2, Deblur, VSEARCH) and filtering regime, even after rarefaction to 5,000 reads per sample. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Reproduces the O'Rourke et al. (2020) 'tidybug' analysis showing that Hill-number alpha diversity of bat guano COI metabarcoding data remains sensitive to the choice of denoising program (DADA2, Deblur, VSEARCH) and filtering regime, even after rarefaction to 5,000 reads per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to select a single best metabarcoding pipeline — the paper states its aim is not to present a single best pathway, only to illustrate how processes are affected by program or parameter choices When the input is already a rarefied, filtered feature table with diversity values computed — this skill reproduces the full pipeline from raw reads through denoising, filtering, and rarefaction When data are not COI amplicon libraries (e.g., 16S/ITS) with reference databases like UNITE, Greengenes, or SILVA, since host/mock COI removal and the mock-guided 'miss' subtraction are COI-specific

skills.description: Use when metabarcoding ASV tables from different filtering pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU/OBIbaR) are available and you suspect unfiltered false positives (tag-jumps, contaminants) inflating per-sample richness or deflating inter-sample dissimilarity.

skills.search_text: metabarcoding-false-positive-diagnosis Use when metabarcoding ASV tables from different filtering pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU/OBIbaR) are available and you suspect unfiltered false positives (tag-jumps, contaminants) inflating per-sample richness or deflating inter-sample dissimilarity. Only one pipeline's ASV table exists — the comparison-based diagnosis requires matched tables from at least two pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU/OBIbaR) over the same samples The goal is to run or configure VTAM's own filtering steps (FilterLNF, FilterMinReplicateNumber, etc.) rather than to diagnose false positives in already-filtered output tables Input is raw FASTQ data rather than per-pipeline final taxa tables — pipeline processing must precede this diversity-based diagnosis http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Diagnoses metabarcoding false positives by comparing per-sample ASV richness (alpha-diversity) and Jaccard-based beta-diversity across filtering pipelines (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR), then tracing inflated richness in suspect samples (e.g. unfiltered tag-jumps in five marine fish samples) back to their origin. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Diagnoses metabarcoding false positives by comparing per-sample ASV richness (alpha-diversity) and Jaccard-based beta-diversity across filtering pipelines (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR), then tracing inflated richness in suspect samples (e.g. unfiltered tag-jumps in five marine fish samples) back to their origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one pipeline's ASV table exists — the comparison-based diagnosis requires matched tables from at least two pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU/OBIbaR) over the same samples The goal is to run or configure VTAM's own filtering steps (FilterLNF, FilterMinReplicateNumber, etc.) rather than to diagnose false positives in already-filtered output tables Input is raw FASTQ data rather than per-pipeline final taxa tables — pipeline processing must precede this diversity-based diagnosis

skills.search_text: metabarcoding-read-count-normalization Use when you have an ASV occurrence table with read counts Nijk (ASV i, sample j, replicate k) from HTS amplicon data plus negative controls, and you need to remove low-frequency noise occurrences before downstream replicate-consistency or taxonomic-assignment steps. When the occurrence-level noise to remove is a sequencing/PCR error closely matching a high-read ASV — that is the job of FilterPCRerror, not the LFN cutoffs When occurrences have not yet been produced by the upstream VTAM filter step (filter, sortreads, merge) — LFN cutoffs operate on ASV occurrence tables, not raw FASTQ When filtering should be driven by per-taxon abundance patterns across control samples — that is handled by VTAM's optimize/make_known_occurrences parameter optimization, not the LFN cutoffs http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies VTAM's FilterLNF (Filter Low Frequency Noise) logic, which removes low-frequency-noise occurrences from an ASV-by-sample-replicate read-count table using three cutoffs (absolute reads, within-sample-replicate relative abundance, and within-ASV relative abundance) to eliminate false positives such as tag-jump and low-level contamination that denoisers like DADA2 or Unoise cannot address. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Applies VTAM's FilterLNF (Filter Low Frequency Noise) logic, which removes low-frequency-noise occurrences from an ASV-by-sample-replicate read-count table using three cutoffs (absolute reads, within-sample-replicate relative abundance, and within-ASV relative abundance) to eliminate false positives such as tag-jump and low-level contamination that denoisers like DADA2 or Unoise cannot address.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the occurrence-level noise to remove is a sequencing/PCR error closely matching a high-read ASV — that is the job of FilterPCRerror, not the LFN cutoffs When occurrences have not yet been produced by the upstream VTAM filter step (filter, sortreads, merge) — LFN cutoffs operate on ASV occurrence tables, not raw FASTQ When filtering should be driven by per-taxon abundance patterns across control samples — that is handled by VTAM's optimize/make_known_occurrences parameter optimization, not the LFN cutoffs

skills.description: Use when you have MOTU representative sequences from a metabarcoding run (e.g. sumaclust 99% clusters, single-read MOTUs removed) and need to assign taxonomy against a curated reference database such as the BOLD-derived elasmobranch COI database.
skills.name: metabarcoding-taxonomic-assignment
skills.search_text: metabarcoding-taxonomic-assignment Use when you have MOTU representative sequences from a metabarcoding run (e.g. sumaclust 99% clusters, single-read MOTUs removed) and need to assign taxonomy against a curated reference database such as the BOLD-derived elasmobranch COI database. When reads have not yet been clustered into MOTUs — run the upstream pipeline (illuminapairedend >40 quality, obigrep 120–135 bp length filter, obiuniq, vsearch uchime-denovo, sumaclust 99%) first. When the target marker/region needs resolution of closely related species pairs (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) and a longer COI fragment would be available — the 127 bp fragment is 100% identical across such species in BOLD, so ecotag cannot unambiguously separate them. When no suitable reference database exists for the taxon of interest — the study notes a bespoke database (BOLD COI sequences + ecoPCR in silico PCR non-targets) was required for assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Assigns a most-specific consistent taxon to each MOTU representative sequence (from 99%-similarity sumaclust clustering) using the OBITools ecotag algorithm against a BOLD-derived COI reference database. This converts clustered amplicon sequences into a per-MOTU taxonomy table, but the short 127 bp COI fragment may yield ambiguous one-to-many species matches. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assigns a most-specific consistent taxon to each MOTU representative sequence (from 99%-similarity sumaclust clustering) using the OBITools ecotag algorithm against a BOLD-derived COI reference database. This converts clustered amplicon sequences into a per-MOTU taxonomy table, but the short 127 bp COI fragment may yield ambiguous one-to-many species matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads have not yet been clustered into MOTUs — run the upstream pipeline (illuminapairedend >40 quality, obigrep 120–135 bp length filter, obiuniq, vsearch uchime-denovo, sumaclust 99%) first. When the target marker/region needs resolution of closely related species pairs (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) and a longer COI fragment would be available — the 127 bp fragment is 100% identical across such species in BOLD, so ecotag cannot unambiguously separate them. When no suitable reference database exists for the taxon of interest — the study notes a bespoke database (BOLD COI sequences + ecoPCR in silico PCR non-targets) was required for assignment.

skills.search_text: metagenomic-abundance-profile-visualization Use when MetaMaps per-read mappings (classification_results.EM) from long reads (e.g., HMP7) must be intersected with annotated gene intervals and aggregated into a ranked abundance profile such as COG category counts. Sample has a high proportion of short reads — MetaMaps does not handle short reads well and sub-minimum-length reads end up unassigned Input is already a quantified abundance or feature table rather than raw long reads needing taxonomic/functional assignment Only overall sample composition is needed at taxon level — the classification_results.EM.WIMP output already provides Absolute/EMFrequency/PotFrequency without gene-level intersection http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Build and rank abundance profiles (e.g., per-COG functional category counts) from MetaMaps per-read mapping output on long-read metagenomic data, then check the ranking against the published ordering such as Supplementary Fig. 2 (S > K > E). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Build and rank abundance profiles (e.g., per-COG functional category counts) from MetaMaps per-read mapping output on long-read metagenomic data, then check the ranking against the published ordering such as Supplementary Fig. 2 (S > K > E).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample has a high proportion of short reads — MetaMaps does not handle short reads well and sub-minimum-length reads end up unassigned Input is already a quantified abundance or feature table rather than raw long reads needing taxonomic/functional assignment Only overall sample composition is needed at taxon level — the classification_results.EM.WIMP output already provides Absolute/EMFrequency/PotFrequency without gene-level intersection

skills.description: Use when long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned per-read to taxa and converted into strain- or species-level sample composition estimates against a reference database such as miniSeq+H/RefSeq.
skills.name: metagenomic-composition-estimation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-composition-estimation Use when long-read (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned per-read to taxa and converted into strain- or species-level sample composition estimates against a reference database such as miniSeq+H/RefSeq. The sample has a high proportion of short reads — reads below the chosen minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned The sample comprises many non-characterized (novel) entities absent from the reference database — database-sample incongruity detection is limited and remains an open problem Real-time/streaming analysis is required (e.g. clinical applications with live sequencing control) — MetaMaps does not support streaming data http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Estimate taxonomic sample composition from long-read (PacBio/ONT) metagenomic data by combining minimizer-based approximate mapping with probabilistic mapping-quality scoring and EM-based estimation of overall sample composition, as implemented in MetaMaps. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Estimate taxonomic sample composition from long-read (PacBio/ONT) metagenomic data by combining minimizer-based approximate mapping with probabilistic mapping-quality scoring and EM-based estimation of overall sample composition, as implemented in MetaMaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample has a high proportion of short reads — reads below the chosen minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned The sample comprises many non-characterized (novel) entities absent from the reference database — database-sample incongruity detection is limited and remains an open problem Real-time/streaming analysis is required (e.g. clinical applications with live sequencing control) — MetaMaps does not support streaming data

skills.description: Use when MetaPhlAn 4 profiles detect a target species (including taxonomically unidentified SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and you need a strain phylogeny or strain-sharing/transmission analysis from marker alignments.
skills.name: metagenomic-marker-consensus-sequencing
skills.search_text: metagenomic-marker-consensus-sequencing Use when MetaPhlAn 4 profiles detect a target species (including taxonomically unidentified SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and you need a strain phylogeny or strain-sharing/transmission analysis from marker alignments. The target taxon has high-quality reference isolate genomes available, so a reference-based phylogeny (e.g., PhyloPhlAn) is preferable to marker consensus reconstruction Only a few samples contain the clade, so per-sample marker coverage is too sparse for reliable consensus sequence reconstruction The question is species-level abundance profiling rather than strain-level population genomics — plain MetaPhlAn 4 profiling suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Build per-sample consensus sequences from clade-specific marker-gene alignments so that strain-level phylogenies can be reconstructed for species lacking reference isolates (e.g., uncharacterized SGBs profiled by MetaPhlAn 4) using StrainPhlAn. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Build per-sample consensus sequences from clade-specific marker-gene alignments so that strain-level phylogenies can be reconstructed for species lacking reference isolates (e.g., uncharacterized SGBs profiled by MetaPhlAn 4) using StrainPhlAn.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target taxon has high-quality reference isolate genomes available, so a reference-based phylogeny (e.g., PhyloPhlAn) is preferable to marker consensus reconstruction Only a few samples contain the clade, so per-sample marker coverage is too sparse for reliable consensus sequence reconstruction The question is species-level abundance profiling rather than strain-level population genomics — plain MetaPhlAn 4 profiling suffices

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a reference marker-gene database from a large genome catalog (isolates plus MAGs), e.g. deriving SGBs and unique markers underlying MetaPhlAn 4-style taxonomic profiling.
skills.name: metagenomic-marker-database-construction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-marker-database-construction Use when building or reproducing a reference marker-gene database from a large genome catalog (isolates plus MAGs), e.g. deriving SGBs and unique markers underlying MetaPhlAn 4-style taxonomic profiling. Input is already a marker database or abundance table — this skill constructs the reference from genomes, not profiles metagenomes The goal is profiling samples with MetaPhlAn rather than rebuilding the SGB/marker reference underlying it Genomes fail the quality gate (completeness <=50% or contamination >=5% by CheckM) and would be excluded from the catalog Incorporating viral or eukaryotic microbial sequences — the article notes current methods do not extensively incorporate them due to unique genomic architectures and QC requirements http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs the MetaPhlAn 4 marker-gene database by quality-filtering an integrated catalog of ~1.01M reference genomes and MAGs, dereplicating them into species-level genome bins (SGBs), and extracting species-unique markers from SGB pangenomes. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs the MetaPhlAn 4 marker-gene database by quality-filtering an integrated catalog of ~1.01M reference genomes and MAGs, dereplicating them into species-level genome bins (SGBs), and extracting species-unique markers from SGB pangenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a marker database or abundance table — this skill constructs the reference from genomes, not profiles metagenomes The goal is profiling samples with MetaPhlAn rather than rebuilding the SGB/marker reference underlying it Genomes fail the quality gate (completeness <=50% or contamination >=5% by CheckM) and would be excluded from the catalog Incorporating viral or eukaryotic microbial sequences — the article notes current methods do not extensively incorporate them due to unique genomic architectures and QC requirements

skills.description: Reference for applying Kraken 2 to classify 16S amplicon reads from mock community samples at species/genus level and comparing its accuracy against 16S-specific pipelines over matched reference libraries.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification-kraken2
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification-kraken2 Reference for applying Kraken 2 to classify 16S amplicon reads from mock community samples at species/genus level and comparing its accuracy against 16S-specific pipelines over matched reference libraries. Input data is not 16S amplicon sequencing data but general shotgun metagenomic reads, or the goal is OTU clustering rather than read-level taxonomic classification Only a 16S-native toolchain (e.g. DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur) is in scope and no read-mapping comparison is intended Reference library choice must follow the current RefSeq database without contamination processing — the authors recommend using older RefSeq libraries until newer versions are corrected http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarking skill for taxonomically profiling 16S amplicon sequencing reads from mock communities with Kraken 2 read-mapping against SILVA, Greengenes, Kraken Standard, and RefSeq reference libraries, so results can be compared per sample against 16S-native profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur) and PathoScope 2. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for taxonomically profiling 16S amplicon sequencing reads from mock communities with Kraken 2 read-mapping against SILVA, Greengenes, Kraken Standard, and RefSeq reference libraries, so results can be compared per sample against 16S-native profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur) and PathoScope 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not 16S amplicon sequencing data but general shotgun metagenomic reads, or the goal is OTU clustering rather than read-level taxonomic classification Only a 16S-native toolchain (e.g. DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur) is in scope and no read-mapping comparison is intended Reference library choice must follow the current RefSeq database without contamination processing — the authors recommend using older RefSeq libraries until newer versions are corrected

skills.description: Use when raw metagenomic sequencing FASTQ files must be converted into clean, host-free reads before taxonomic or functional profiling, or when reproducing the Liu 2020 metagenomic pipeline.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-quality-control Use when raw metagenomic sequencing FASTQ files must be converted into clean, host-free reads before taxonomic or functional profiling, or when reproducing the Liu 2020 metagenomic pipeline. Input is already a cleaned, non-host read set or an assembled contig set rather than raw metagenomic FASTQ The analysis goal is 16S/amplicon processing (the review recommends a separate amplicon pipeline, e.g., QIIME 2, for that data type) Downstream feature tables (taxonomic profiles or KEGG orthology tables) already exist and only profiling or statistics are needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quality-control step of the metagenomic pipeline recommended by Liu et al. 2020: raw metagenomic FASTQ reads are adapter/quality trimmed with Trimmomatic and host-aligned reads are removed with Bowtie 2, chained together by KneadData, to yield clean non-host reads for downstream taxonomic (MetaPhlAn2, Kraken2) and functional (HUMAnN2) profiling. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Quality-control step of the metagenomic pipeline recommended by Liu et al. 2020: raw metagenomic FASTQ reads are adapter/quality trimmed with Trimmomatic and host-aligned reads are removed with Bowtie 2, chained together by KneadData, to yield clean non-host reads for downstream taxonomic (MetaPhlAn2, Kraken2) and functional (HUMAnN2) profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned, non-host read set or an assembled contig set rather than raw metagenomic FASTQ The analysis goal is 16S/amplicon processing (the review recommends a separate amplicon pipeline, e.g., QIIME 2, for that data type) Downstream feature tables (taxonomic profiles or KEGG orthology tables) already exist and only profiling or statistics are needed

skills.description: Use when a microbiome analysis plan or pipeline audit must name the recommended tool per metagenomic or amplicon phase (quality control, assembly, binning, classification, annotation) as catalogued in the Bharti & Grimm -practice review.
skills.name: metagenomic-workflow-curation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-workflow-curation Use when a microbiome analysis plan or pipeline audit must name the recommended tool per metagenomic or amplicon phase (quality control, assembly, binning, classification, annotation) as catalogued in the Bharti & Grimm -practice review. The goal is to execute the pipelines on raw paired-end *.fastq.gz reads rather than curate the tool map - run amplicon_analysis.sh / metagenomics_analysis.sh directly instead Input is already a curated tool map (best_practice_tools_map.csv exists) and the task is downstream statistical or visualization analysis (e.g., phyloseq), not tool selection The data are non-microbiome libraries (e.g., ChIP-Seq, RNA-Seq, BS-Seq): FastQC itself is generic, but the review's phase-to-tool catalogue covers only 16S rRNA and shotgun/long-read metagenomics http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Curates the Bharti & Grimm (2019) best-practice microbiome workflows (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz155) into a phase-by-phase tool-selection map (best_practice_tools_map.csv), so future agents know which tool (e.g., Trimmomatic/Sickle/BBMap for metagenomic quality control) to apply at each 16S rRNA or shotgun-metagenomics step. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: Curates the Bharti & Grimm (2019) best-practice microbiome workflows (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz155) into a phase-by-phase tool-selection map (best_practice_tools_map.csv), so future agents know which tool (e.g., Trimmomatic/Sickle/BBMap for metagenomic quality control) to apply at each 16S rRNA or shotgun-metagenomics step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to execute the pipelines on raw paired-end *.fastq.gz reads rather than curate the tool map - run amplicon_analysis.sh / metagenomics_analysis.sh directly instead Input is already a curated tool map (best_practice_tools_map.csv exists) and the task is downstream statistical or visualization analysis (e.g., phyloseq), not tool selection The data are non-microbiome libraries (e.g., ChIP-Seq, RNA-Seq, BS-Seq): FastQC itself is generic, but the review's phase-to-tool catalogue covers only 16S rRNA and shotgun/long-read metagenomics

skills.description: Use when a QIIME 2/Tourmaline run has produced alpha-diversity outputs (observed_features_group_significance.qzv, alpha_rarefaction.qzv) and you need to compare richness across a metadata grouping or find the rarefaction plateau depth.
skills.name: microbial-community-richness-analysis
skills.search_text: microbial-community-richness-analysis Use when a QIIME 2/Tourmaline run has produced alpha-diversity outputs (observed_features_group_significance.qzv, alpha_rarefaction.qzv) and you need to compare richness across a metadata grouping or find the rarefaction plateau depth. The input is already a feature table or per-sample richness vector rather than a QIIME 2 .qzv visualization — extract values directly instead of re-parsing. The question concerns beta diversity (between-sample community structure) rather than within-sample richness; Tourmaline's alpha and beta diversity analyses are separate outputs. Rarefaction curves have not plateaued within the configured alpha_max_depth (e.g. curves still rising at 500 sequences/sample), so the observed-features comparison would be depth-confounded. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Compares within-sample alpha diversity (observed features) between sample groups and identifies the sequencing depth at which richness saturates, by parsing QIIME 2 alpha-diversity visualizations produced by the Tourmaline workflow. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Compares within-sample alpha diversity (observed features) between sample groups and identifies the sequencing depth at which richness saturates, by parsing QIIME 2 alpha-diversity visualizations produced by the Tourmaline workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table or per-sample richness vector rather than a QIIME 2 .qzv visualization — extract values directly instead of re-parsing. The question concerns beta diversity (between-sample community structure) rather than within-sample richness; Tourmaline's alpha and beta diversity analyses are separate outputs. Rarefaction curves have not plateaued within the configured alpha_max_depth (e.g. curves still rising at 500 sequences/sample), so the observed-features comparison would be depth-confounded.

skills.description: Use when an OTU/species abundance table with taxonomic assignments and sample metadata needs relative-abundance normalization, group-wise mean/SEM summarization, and significance testing between sample groups.
skills.name: microbial-taxa-relative-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: microbial-taxa-relative-abundance-quantification Use when an OTU/species abundance table with taxonomic assignments and sample metadata needs relative-abundance normalization, group-wise mean/SEM summarization, and significance testing between sample groups. Input is raw FASTQ rather than a classified OTU abundance table — run the SILVAngs pipeline (BBmerge, BBduk, cd-hit-est, BLASTn) first Goal is alpha/beta diversity or Mantel-test analysis rather than taxon-level abundance comparison (use the Simpson/Bray-Curtis workflow instead) ITS/eukaryotic data classified with the Warcup V2 'Classify Sequences' tool at 90% similarity — this skill targets the 16S SILVAngs BLASTn-based prokaryotic table http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute per-taxon relative abundances from a SILVAngs-derived 16S OTU table (cd-hit-est clustered, BLASTn-classified against SILVA SSU ref 132), aggregate mean abundance and SEM per sample group (e.g. inflow- vs pond-water), and test species-level differences with two-sample t-tests in XLSTAT 2017. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Compute per-taxon relative abundances from a SILVAngs-derived 16S OTU table (cd-hit-est clustered, BLASTn-classified against SILVA SSU ref 132), aggregate mean abundance and SEM per sample group (e.g. inflow- vs pond-water), and test species-level differences with two-sample t-tests in XLSTAT 2017.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ rather than a classified OTU abundance table — run the SILVAngs pipeline (BBmerge, BBduk, cd-hit-est, BLASTn) first Goal is alpha/beta diversity or Mantel-test analysis rather than taxon-level abundance comparison (use the Simpson/Bray-Curtis workflow instead) ITS/eukaryotic data classified with the Warcup V2 'Classify Sequences' tool at 90% similarity — this skill targets the 16S SILVAngs BLASTn-based prokaryotic table

skills.description: Use when you have final ASV abundance tables from a DADA2/dadasnake amplicon run (e.g. mock communities ERR777696 or PRJNA626434) and a known expected taxon composition, and need to test whether relative read abundances reflect true taxon proportions.
skills.name: microbial-taxonomy-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: microbial-taxonomy-abundance-analysis Use when you have final ASV abundance tables from a DADA2/dadasnake amplicon run (e.g. mock communities ERR777696 or PRJNA626434) and a known expected taxon composition, and need to test whether relative read abundances reflect true taxon proportions. Input is still raw FASTQ reads — primer removal, quality filtering and trimming, and chimera removal must first run through dadasnake's DADA2-based steps before this skill applies The community has no known expected (ground-truth) composition, so no observed-vs-expected comparison can be quantified The goal is functional prediction (e.g. PICRUSt2 pathway inference) rather than taxonomic abundance assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aggregates dadasnake/DADA2 ASV read counts to taxonomically assigned taxa, normalizes them to relative read abundances, and compares them against known ground-truth mock community compositions to quantify how faithfully read abundances reflect true taxon abundances. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Aggregates dadasnake/DADA2 ASV read counts to taxonomically assigned taxa, normalizes them to relative read abundances, and compares them against known ground-truth mock community compositions to quantify how faithfully read abundances reflect true taxon abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ reads — primer removal, quality filtering and trimming, and chimera removal must first run through dadasnake's DADA2-based steps before this skill applies The community has no known expected (ground-truth) composition, so no observed-vs-expected comparison can be quantified The goal is functional prediction (e.g. PICRUSt2 pathway inference) rather than taxonomic abundance assessment

skills.description: Use when you have aggregated alpha diversity tables (alpha-out_dataset-name.tsv or alpha_aggregated.tsv) with sample metadata and need to compare metric distributions between microbiome projects, e.g. reproducing Fig. 4 for the 471_swedish and 514_imp_project cohorts.
skills.name: microbiome-alpha-diversity-boxplot-visualization
skills.search_text: microbiome-alpha-diversity-boxplot-visualization Use when you have aggregated alpha diversity tables (alpha-out_dataset-name.tsv or alpha_aggregated.tsv) with sample metadata and need to compare metric distributions between microbiome projects, e.g. reproducing Fig. 4 for the 471_swedish and 514_imp_project cohorts. Input is raw sequencing data (SRA runs) that still needs downloading with sra-tools and QIIME2 processing/denoising — metric values must already exist in the aggregated TSV tables The goal is beta diversity (between-sample) analysis rather than within-sample alpha diversity metric comparison Projects lacking associated metadata must be excluded rather than plotted, per the paper's filter steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates per-project boxplots of recommended alpha diversity metrics (Shannon, Observed features, Berger-Parker) from the aggregated QIIME2 alpha diversity tables, reproducing Fig. 4-style comparisons across human gut microbiome projects. It complements the correlation analysis by making richness, entropy and dominance differences between cohorts visually explicit. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-024-77864-y
skills.summary: Generates per-project boxplots of recommended alpha diversity metrics (Shannon, Observed features, Berger-Parker) from the aggregated QIIME2 alpha diversity tables, reproducing Fig. 4-style comparisons across human gut microbiome projects. It complements the correlation analysis by making richness, entropy and dominance differences between cohorts visually explicit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (SRA runs) that still needs downloading with sra-tools and QIIME2 processing/denoising — metric values must already exist in the aggregated TSV tables The goal is beta diversity (between-sample) analysis rather than within-sample alpha diversity metric comparison Projects lacking associated metadata must be excluded rather than plotted, per the paper's filter steps

skills.description: Use when you have a DADA2-denoised QIIME 2 feature table from a Tourmaline run with sample metadata (e.g. 5.0-um vs 0.22-um size fractions) and must verify which taxa dominate each fraction before publishing or reusing the findings.
skills.name: microbiome-community-composition-validation
skills.search_text: microbiome-community-composition-validation Use when you have a DADA2-denoised QIIME 2 feature table from a Tourmaline run with sample metadata (e.g. 5.0-um vs 0.22-um size fractions) and must verify which taxa dominate each fraction before publishing or reusing the findings. Input is not yet a feature table (e.g. raw FASTQ has not been denoised with DADA2 in the qaqc/repseqs/taxonomy steps) The analysis goal is differential composition testing or beta diversity rather than reproducing/verifying reported dominance patterns The run was filtered (taxonomy, length, abundance, prevalence) or used Deblur rather than the unfiltered DADA2-PE run the findings were reported from http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reproduce and verify family-level taxonomic dominance patterns in size-fractionated 16S rRNA amplicon data by collapsing Tourmaline/QIIME 2 ASV tables at family level (collapse_taxalevel: 7) and comparing relative abundances per size fraction against expected findings. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Reproduce and verify family-level taxonomic dominance patterns in size-fractionated 16S rRNA amplicon data by collapsing Tourmaline/QIIME 2 ASV tables at family level (collapse_taxalevel: 7) and comparing relative abundances per size fraction against expected findings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not yet a feature table (e.g. raw FASTQ has not been denoised with DADA2 in the qaqc/repseqs/taxonomy steps) The analysis goal is differential composition testing or beta diversity rather than reproducing/verifying reported dominance patterns The run was filtered (taxonomy, length, abundance, prevalence) or used Deblur rather than the unfiltered DADA2-PE run the findings were reported from

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered 16S rRNA amplicon reads have been processed into OTU (97% identity, mothur) or ASV (DADA2 denoising) tables with taxonomy assignments, and taxonomic composition visualizations are required.
skills.name: microbiome-community-visualization-phyloseq
skills.search_text: microbiome-community-visualization-phyloseq Use when quality-filtered 16S rRNA amplicon reads have been processed into OTU (97% identity, mothur) or ASV (DADA2 denoising) tables with taxonomy assignments, and taxonomic composition visualizations are required. Input is shotgun metagenomic data, which belongs to the separate metagenomics_analysis.sh workflow rather than the amplicon visualization path Input is raw unprocessed reads with no OTU/ASV taxonomy tables yet — run mothur_workflow.sh and dada2_workflow.sh first Data is already a rendered figure or pre-summarized community profile requiring no further Phyloseq processing http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A skill for summarizing and visualizing 16S rRNA amplicon community profiles by rendering taxonomic composition figures from OTU (mothur) and ASV (DADA2) outputs using the R libraries Phyloseq, ggplot2, and argparser, as part of the best-practice amplicon workflow. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: A skill for summarizing and visualizing 16S rRNA amplicon community profiles by rendering taxonomic composition figures from OTU (mothur) and ASV (DADA2) outputs using the R libraries Phyloseq, ggplot2, and argparser, as part of the best-practice amplicon workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is shotgun metagenomic data, which belongs to the separate metagenomics_analysis.sh workflow rather than the amplicon visualization path Input is raw unprocessed reads with no OTU/ASV taxonomy tables yet — run mothur_workflow.sh and dada2_workflow.sh first Data is already a rendered figure or pre-summarized community profile requiring no further Phyloseq processing

skills.description: Use when evaluating which DA method controls FDR at a nominal level (e.g. 5%) while maintaining power on compositional microbiome count data, or when reproducing simulation-based method comparisons across balanced and unbalanced group designs.
skills.name: microbiome-compositional-data-analysis
skills.search_text: microbiome-compositional-data-analysis Use when evaluating which DA method controls FDR at a nominal level (e.g. 5%) while maintaining power on compositional microbiome count data, or when reproducing simulation-based method comparisons across balanced and unbalanced group designs. Input is an already-analyzed real dataset rather than simulated data — this skill is a simulation benchmark for method comparison, not a DA analysis of observed data Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not control FDR The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is very large, which can slightly elevate FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark differential abundance (DA) methods for compositional microbiome data by simulating data under a Poisson-Gamma model, running ANCOM-BC (and competitors ANCOM, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, edgeR) on each replicate, and comparing empirical FDR and power across two-group designs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Benchmark differential abundance (DA) methods for compositional microbiome data by simulating data under a Poisson-Gamma model, running ANCOM-BC (and competitors ANCOM, metagenomeSeq, DESeq2, edgeR) on each replicate, and comparing empirical FDR and power across two-group designs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-analyzed real dataset rather than simulated data — this skill is a simulation benchmark for method comparison, not a DA analysis of observed data Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not control FDR The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is very large, which can slightly elevate FDR

skills.description: Use when raw OTU/feature count tables need normalization prior to ordination, BSS, or differential abundance analysis, and competing normalization methods must be ranked on a dataset such as the global gut microbiota data.
skills.name: microbiome-count-normalization
skills.search_text: microbiome-count-normalization Use when raw OTU/feature count tables need normalization prior to ordination, BSS, or differential abundance analysis, and competing normalization methods must be ranked on a dataset such as the global gut microbiota data. The input is already normalized relative abundances or the analysis goal does not involve comparing normalization methods on count data Sample sizes per group are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large, where the method may show slightly elevated FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies and compares microbiome count normalization methods (ANCOM-BC, CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, TSS) on a preprocessed feature table so that cross-sample and cross-group comparisons of absolute abundance are debiased for sampling-fraction differences. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Applies and compares microbiome count normalization methods (ANCOM-BC, CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, TSS) on a preprocessed feature table so that cross-sample and cross-group comparisons of absolute abundance are debiased for sampling-fraction differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already normalized relative abundances or the analysis goal does not involve comparing normalization methods on count data Sample sizes per group are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large, where the method may show slightly elevated FDR

skills.description: Use when you have per-tool significant ASV outputs for many two-group 16S datasets and want to test whether the numbers of significant features correlate with effect size, sample size, sequencing depth, or sparsity, with vs without prevalence filtering.
skills.name: microbiome-dataset-characteristic-computation
skills.search_text: microbiome-dataset-characteristic-computation Use when you have per-tool significant ASV outputs for many two-group 16S datasets and want to test whether the numbers of significant features correlate with effect size, sample size, sequencing depth, or sparsity, with vs without prevalence filtering. You have not yet run the DA tools: this skill consumes per-tool significant ASV outputs, not raw ASV tables — run run_all_tools.sh first Your question is tool-to-tool agreement (consistency/intersect of significant features), not correlation of significance counts with dataset characteristics Datasets lack two sample groups, so a PERMANOVA effect size on Aitchison distance between test groups cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assembles per-dataset characteristics (Aitchison PERMANOVA effect size, sample size, read depth, richness, sparsity) for 16S rRNA gene datasets and correlates them against each differential abundance tool's percent of significant ASVs using Spearman rank correlation, under unfiltered and 10% prevalence-filtered conditions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Assembles per-dataset characteristics (Aitchison PERMANOVA effect size, sample size, read depth, richness, sparsity) for 16S rRNA gene datasets and correlates them against each differential abundance tool's percent of significant ASVs using Spearman rank correlation, under unfiltered and 10% prevalence-filtered conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet run the DA tools: this skill consumes per-tool significant ASV outputs, not raw ASV tables — run run_all_tools.sh first Your question is tool-to-tool agreement (consistency/intersect of significant features), not correlation of significance counts with dataset characteristics Datasets lack two sample groups, so a PERMANOVA effect size on Aitchison distance between test groups cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when analyzing microbiome OTU/feature count tables to identify taxa differentially abundant across experimental groups (e.g., nationality, age strata, bmi_group) while accounting for compositionality and unequal sampling fractions.
skills.name: microbiome-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: microbiome-differential-abundance-analysis Use when analyzing microbiome OTU/feature count tables to identify taxa differentially abundant across experimental groups (e.g., nationality, age strata, bmi_group) while accounting for compositionality and unequal sampling fractions. Very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group) — ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases When the proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large, FDR may be slightly elevated — consider alternatives or interpret q.vals cautiously Testing hypotheses about mean relative abundance rather than absolute abundance — the method targets absolute abundance via sampling-fraction correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Performs bias-corrected differential abundance (DA) analysis of microbiome compositional data using ANCOM-BC, which estimates sample-specific sampling fractions and includes them as an offset in a log-scale linear regression to test absolute abundance differences between groups. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Performs bias-corrected differential abundance (DA) analysis of microbiome compositional data using ANCOM-BC, which estimates sample-specific sampling fractions and includes them as an offset in a log-scale linear regression to test absolute abundance differences between groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group) — ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases When the proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large, FDR may be slightly elevated — consider alternatives or interpret q.vals cautiously Testing hypotheses about mean relative abundance rather than absolute abundance — the method targets absolute abundance via sampling-fraction correction

skills.description: Use when you have significant-ASV result tables from several DA tools (e.g., 14 tools) run on the same datasets and need to quantify overlap, consensus, or tool clustering, including effects of prevalence filtering.
skills.name: microbiome-differential-abundance-results-aggregation
skills.search_text: microbiome-differential-abundance-results-aggregation Use when you have significant-ASV result tables from several DA tools (e.g., 14 tools) run on the same datasets and need to quantify overlap, consensus, or tool clustering, including effects of prevalence filtering. You are estimating false-positive rates on randomized/simulated data rather than aggregating real significant-ASV calls (the paper handles this with separate run_all_FP_datasets_filt.sh / run_all_FP_datasets_unfilt.sh scripts) You are assessing cross-study consistency of genera across datasets from the same environment (e.g., the diarrhea or obesity consistency analyses), which uses a different random-expectation comparison rather than tool-vs-tool Jaccard distances You only ran a single DA tool per dataset, so there is no cross-tool overlap to aggregate http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aggregates significant-ASV calls from multiple differential abundance (DA) tools across 16S rRNA datasets to quantify cross-tool overlap and clustering, using tool-vs-tool Jaccard distances and PCoA ordination, and to measure how prevalence filtering (e.g., -F 0.1) changes agreement. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Aggregates significant-ASV calls from multiple differential abundance (DA) tools across 16S rRNA datasets to quantify cross-tool overlap and clustering, using tool-vs-tool Jaccard distances and PCoA ordination, and to measure how prevalence filtering (e.g., -F 0.1) changes agreement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are estimating false-positive rates on randomized/simulated data rather than aggregating real significant-ASV calls (the paper handles this with separate run_all_FP_datasets_filt.sh / run_all_FP_datasets_unfilt.sh scripts) You are assessing cross-study consistency of genera across datasets from the same environment (e.g., the diarrhea or obesity consistency analyses), which uses a different random-expectation comparison rather than tool-vs-tool Jaccard distances You only ran a single DA tool per dataset, so there is no cross-tool overlap to aggregate

skills.description: Use when a genus-level ASV abundance table is grouped by experimental condition or amplified region and you must test whether alpha diversity (richness/evenness) differs significantly across groups.
skills.name: microbiome-diversity-statistics
skills.search_text: microbiome-diversity-statistics Use when a genus-level ASV abundance table is grouped by experimental condition or amplified region and you must test whether alpha diversity (richness/evenness) differs significantly across groups. The input is raw FASTQ reads or an uncollapsed ASV table — this skill requires a genus-level, Greengenes-collapsed abundance table after Deblur denoising The analysis goal is beta diversity / compositional dissimilarity (e.g., NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities), which is a separate analysis in this study Groups are expected to be normally distributed and homoscedastic, where a parametric ANOVA rather than Kruskal–Wallis would be appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Compares alpha diversity (Shannon, inverse Simpson, Chao1) across 16S rRNA hypervariable-region groups (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) using the Kruskal–Wallis test in R, to determine which region combination yields the highest richness and evenness in respiratory samples. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Compares alpha diversity (Shannon, inverse Simpson, Chao1) across 16S rRNA hypervariable-region groups (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) using the Kruskal–Wallis test in R, to determine which region combination yields the highest richness and evenness in respiratory samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ reads or an uncollapsed ASV table — this skill requires a genus-level, Greengenes-collapsed abundance table after Deblur denoising The analysis goal is beta diversity / compositional dissimilarity (e.g., NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities), which is a separate analysis in this study Groups are expected to be normally distributed and homoscedastic, where a parametric ANOVA rather than Kruskal–Wallis would be appropriate

skills.description: Use when an EMP 16S Release 1 BIOM table and mapping file must be analyzed per environment type — e.g., computing NODF nestedness separately for non-saline, saline, animal, and plant subsets of a 2,000-sample subset rather than only globally.
skills.name: microbiome-environment-stratification
skills.search_text: microbiome-environment-stratification Use when an EMP 16S Release 1 BIOM table and mapping file must be analyzed per environment type — e.g., computing NODF nestedness separately for non-saline, saline, animal, and plant subsets of a 2,000-sample subset rather than only globally. The analysis question requires abundance-based or beta-diversity comparison (e.g., weighted UniFrac) rather than presence-absence nestedness — this skill binarizes the abundance table and discards count information. The mapping file lacks environment-category metadata, so the non-saline/saline/animal/plant strata cannot be defined. The goal is functional (e.g., metabolomic) rather than taxonomic composition stratification of EMP samples. Stratifies EMP 16S Release 1 samples by environment category (non-saline, saline, animal, plant) and computes taxonomic nestedness (NODF) within each stratum against an equiprobable-rows/fixed-columns null model, showing communities are significantly nested (NODF = 0.841 ± 0.018) with phyla gained but not lost as richness increases. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Stratifies EMP 16S Release 1 samples by environment category (non-saline, saline, animal, plant) and computes taxonomic nestedness (NODF) within each stratum against an equiprobable-rows/fixed-columns null model, showing communities are significantly nested (NODF = 0.841 ± 0.018) with phyla gained but not lost as richness increases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis question requires abundance-based or beta-diversity comparison (e.g., weighted UniFrac) rather than presence-absence nestedness — this skill binarizes the abundance table and discards count information. The mapping file lacks environment-category metadata, so the non-saline/saline/animal/plant strata cannot be defined. The goal is functional (e.g., metabolomic) rather than taxonomic composition stratification of EMP samples.

skills.description: Use when an amplicon feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2 format) and a sample metadata mapping file are loaded and you must determine whether experimental groups differ in alpha- or beta-diversity and which features are biomarkers of each group.
skills.name: microbiome-feature-table-analysis
skills.search_text: microbiome-feature-table-analysis Use when an amplicon feature table (BIOM/QIIME 2 format) and a sample metadata mapping file are loaded and you must determine whether experimental groups differ in alpha- or beta-diversity and which features are biomarkers of each group. Input is still raw sequencing reads that have not been denoised into a feature table (run the amplicon pipeline first before diversity statistics) The goal is functional metagenome prediction rather than diversity/composition statistics (PICRUSt2 predicts metagenomes from amplicon data) Tree and annotation visualization is the sole goal (table2itol generates iTOL annotation files, not diversity tests) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Statistical and visualization analysis of microbiome amplicon feature tables: computing alpha/beta diversity, testing group differences (ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, PERMANOVA), ordinating samples (PCoA, NMDS, CPCoA), and assembling comparison figures and tables. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Statistical and visualization analysis of microbiome amplicon feature tables: computing alpha/beta diversity, testing group differences (ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, PERMANOVA), ordinating samples (PCoA, NMDS, CPCoA), and assembling comparison figures and tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw sequencing reads that have not been denoised into a feature table (run the amplicon pipeline first before diversity statistics) The goal is functional metagenome prediction rather than diversity/composition statistics (PICRUSt2 predicts metagenomes from amplicon data) Tree and annotation visualization is the sole goal (table2itol generates iTOL annotation files, not diversity tests)

skills.description: Use when a feature table (Deblur or OTU BIOM) with uneven per-sample sequence counts feeds into cross-sample statistics (e.g., random forest classification of EMPO environment labels), and per-sample depths must be equalized to 5,000 observations first.
skills.name: microbiome-feature-table-rarefaction
skills.search_text: microbiome-feature-table-rarefaction Use when a feature table (Deblur or OTU BIOM) with uneven per-sample sequence counts feeds into cross-sample statistics (e.g., random forest classification of EMPO environment labels), and per-sample depths must be equalized to 5,000 observations first. The goal is prevalence/abundance feature filtering (e.g., mc2 — minimum sequence count in an OTU of 2) rather than per-sample depth normalization; these are distinct filtering steps. The input is a closed-reference OTU table against a different reference (Greengenes 13.8 / Silva 123) at a different processing context — the 5,000-observation depth was specified for the Deblur tag-sequences table. The analysis requires total unfiltered abundance per sample (e.g., exact read-count reporting) rather than depth-normalized comparisons. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Normalizes 16S amplicon feature tables (e.g., the Deblur BIOM tables from EMP 16S Release 1) to equal sequencing depth — 5,000 observations per sample — before downstream statistics, and excludes contaminant lineages such as chloroplast sequences. This is the depth-standardization step used in the EMP meta-analysis to make cross-study community comparisons and machine-learning classification comparable. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Normalizes 16S amplicon feature tables (e.g., the Deblur BIOM tables from EMP 16S Release 1) to equal sequencing depth — 5,000 observations per sample — before downstream statistics, and excludes contaminant lineages such as chloroplast sequences. This is the depth-standardization step used in the EMP meta-analysis to make cross-study community comparisons and machine-learning classification comparable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is prevalence/abundance feature filtering (e.g., mc2 — minimum sequence count in an OTU of 2) rather than per-sample depth normalization; these are distinct filtering steps. The input is a closed-reference OTU table against a different reference (Greengenes 13.8 / Silva 123) at a different processing context — the 5,000-observation depth was specified for the Deblur tag-sequences table. The analysis requires total unfiltered abundance per sample (e.g., exact read-count reporting) rather than depth-normalized comparisons.
