skills.description: Use when metagenomic shotgun samples have been profiled with MetaPhlAn 4 and you must link taxonomic abundances (e.g. SGB4777) to host markers like HEI, aMED, uPDI or ASCVD risk via prediction metrics.
skills.name: microbiome-host-phenotype-association-analysis
skills.search_text: microbiome-host-phenotype-association-analysis Use when metagenomic shotgun samples have been profiled with MetaPhlAn 4 and you must link taxonomic abundances (e.g. SGB4777) to host markers like HEI, aMED, uPDI or ASCVD risk via prediction metrics. Input is raw shotgun reads not yet profiled at species level — first generate relative abundances with MetaPhlAn 4 before linking to host markers Markers are of a single continuous type with no classification target and no baseline profile — the AUC-based benchmarking against MetaPhlAn 3 has no anchor Study is an environmental or nonhost-associated community — the article notes such communities remain highly enriched for sequences not captured by current uSGBs, undermining host-phenotype association power http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Relates MetaPhlAn 4 taxonomic profiles (SGB/uSGB relative abundances) to host nutritional and cardiometabolic markers by cross-validated random forest prediction and partial Spearman correlation, benchmarking MetaPhlAn 4 against MetaPhlAn 3 baselines. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Relates MetaPhlAn 4 taxonomic profiles (SGB/uSGB relative abundances) to host nutritional and cardiometabolic markers by cross-validated random forest prediction and partial Spearman correlation, benchmarking MetaPhlAn 4 against MetaPhlAn 3 baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw shotgun reads not yet profiled at species level — first generate relative abundances with MetaPhlAn 4 before linking to host markers Markers are of a single continuous type with no classification target and no baseline profile — the AUC-based benchmarking against MetaPhlAn 3 has no anchor Study is an environmental or nonhost-associated community — the article notes such communities remain highly enriched for sequences not captured by current uSGBs, undermining host-phenotype association power

skills.description: Use when preparing 16S rRNA gene ASV/OTU count tables for differential abundance tools that require rarefied input, or when reproducing the rarefaction-vs-no-rarefaction arm of a DA method comparison.
skills.name: microbiome-library-size-normalization
skills.search_text: microbiome-library-size-normalization Use when preparing 16S rRNA gene ASV/OTU count tables for differential abundance tools that require rarefied input, or when reproducing the rarefaction-vs-no-rarefaction arm of a DA method comparison. The downstream DA tool is configured to take un-rarefied count data — Table 1 specifies only LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare) took rarefied count tables as input You are deciding whether to rarefy prior to computing diversity metrics — the paper states that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work' The count table has already been rarefied to equal library size (re-rarefying adds no information) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Rarefies (subsamples) a 16S rRNA ASV count table to a common per-sample library size so that differential abundance tools configured for rarefied input (e.g., LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare) in the 14-tool comparison) receive equal-depth count data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Rarefies (subsamples) a 16S rRNA ASV count table to a common per-sample library size so that differential abundance tools configured for rarefied input (e.g., LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare) in the 14-tool comparison) receive equal-depth count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream DA tool is configured to take un-rarefied count data — Table 1 specifies only LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare) took rarefied count tables as input You are deciding whether to rarefy prior to computing diversity metrics — the paper states that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work' The count table has already been rarefied to equal library size (re-rarefying adds no information)

skills.description: Use when per-dataset alpha diversity metric tables from QIIME2's diversity module must be merged with metadata into one table, or when metric conclusions must be re-validated under a second condition such as rarefaction.
skills.name: microbiome-metric-aggregation-and-comparison
skills.search_text: microbiome-metric-aggregation-and-comparison Use when per-dataset alpha diversity metric tables from QIIME2's diversity module must be merged with metadata into one table, or when metric conclusions must be re-validated under a second condition such as rarefaction. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than computed alpha diversity tables — the reads must first be denoised (DEBLUR) and metrics calculated via QIIME2's diversity module The analysis goal is taxonomic beta diversity or differential abundance rather than alpha diversity metric behavior across the Richness, Dominance, Phylogenetics, and Information categories Projects lack associated metadata, since projects without metadata were excluded from the aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregate per-dataset QIIME2 alpha diversity metric tables (alpha-out_dataset-name.tsv) with sample metadata into a combined per-sample table, then compare metric values across conditions (e.g., rarefied vs non-rarefied) to validate metric behavior. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-024-77864-y
skills.summary: Aggregate per-dataset QIIME2 alpha diversity metric tables (alpha-out_dataset-name.tsv) with sample metadata into a combined per-sample table, then compare metric values across conditions (e.g., rarefied vs non-rarefied) to validate metric behavior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than computed alpha diversity tables — the reads must first be denoised (DEBLUR) and metrics calculated via QIIME2's diversity module The analysis goal is taxonomic beta diversity or differential abundance rather than alpha diversity metric behavior across the Richness, Dominance, Phylogenetics, and Information categories Projects lack associated metadata, since projects without metadata were excluded from the aggregation

skills.description: Use when amplicon ASV abundance tables (e.g., Deblur-derived, genus-level) must be cross-validated against a mock community standard such as ZymoBIOMICS to quantify classifier sensitivity/specificity via ROC/AUC.
skills.name: microbiome-mock-control-validation
skills.search_text: microbiome-mock-control-validation Use when amplicon ASV abundance tables (e.g., Deblur-derived, genus-level) must be cross-validated against a mock community standard such as ZymoBIOMICS to quantify classifier sensitivity/specificity via ROC/AUC. The dataset has no positive-control mock community (e.g., no ZymoBIOMICS standard sequenced alongside samples), so cross-validation labels cannot be defined. Sequences come from third-generation full-length 16S rRNA platforms (e.g., Nanopore) rather than the Illumina MiSeq 300 bp-limited short-amplicon setting the region-pair comparison addresses. Input is already a validated classifier output or ROC table; no re-computation of region-level AUCs is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates a 16S rRNA microbiota classifier against a positive-control mock community by computing pair-wise ROC curves and AUC per hypervariable region, as done with the ZymoBIOMICS standard to determine which region pair has the highest sensitivity and specificity for respiratory taxa. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Validates a 16S rRNA microbiota classifier against a positive-control mock community by computing pair-wise ROC curves and AUC per hypervariable region, as done with the ZymoBIOMICS standard to determine which region pair has the highest sensitivity and specificity for respiratory taxa.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no positive-control mock community (e.g., no ZymoBIOMICS standard sequenced alongside samples), so cross-validation labels cannot be defined. Sequences come from third-generation full-length 16S rRNA platforms (e.g., Nanopore) rather than the Illumina MiSeq 300 bp-limited short-amplicon setting the region-pair comparison addresses. Input is already a validated classifier output or ROC table; no re-computation of region-level AUCs is needed.

skills.description: Use when building or auditing a 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomics pipeline and you need to know which concrete tool (e.g. Trimmomatic, MEGAHIT, MetaBAT, Kraken2, Prokka, mothur, DADA2) the -practice literature assigns to each phase.
skills.name: microbiome-pipeline-phase-tool-mapping
skills.search_text: microbiome-pipeline-phase-tool-mapping Use when building or auditing a 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomics pipeline and you need to know which concrete tool (e.g. Trimmomatic, MEGAHIT, MetaBAT, Kraken2, Prokka, mothur, DADA2) the -practice literature assigns to each phase. You already have a validated pipeline and only need runtime execution instructions rather than tool selection per phase The task concerns long-read metagenomics tool choices not explicitly covered by the short-read tool catalogue surfaced here Input is a processed feature table or abundance matrix where phase-level tool selection is no longer relevant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Constructs a phase-by-phase catalogue of the best-practice tools recommended by the Bharti & Grimm (2019) microbiome review, mapping each metagenomic and amplicon analysis phase (quality control, assembly, binning, read classification, annotation, visualization) to the specific named software and its role. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: Constructs a phase-by-phase catalogue of the best-practice tools recommended by the Bharti & Grimm (2019) microbiome review, mapping each metagenomic and amplicon analysis phase (quality control, assembly, binning, read classification, annotation, visualization) to the specific named software and its role.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a validated pipeline and only need runtime execution instructions rather than tool selection per phase The task concerns long-read metagenomics tool choices not explicitly covered by the short-read tool catalogue surfaced here Input is a processed feature table or abundance matrix where phase-level tool selection is no longer relevant

skills.description: Use when genus-level collapsed ASV abundance tables (e.g., Greengenes-assigned, QIIME 2-produced) must be grouped by 16S hypervariable region to assess compositional dissimilarity in ordination space between region combinations.
skills.name: microbiome-sample-grouping-by-hypervariable-region
skills.search_text: microbiome-sample-grouping-by-hypervariable-region Use when genus-level collapsed ASV abundance tables (e.g., Greengenes-assigned, QIIME 2-produced) must be grouped by 16S hypervariable region to assess compositional dissimilarity in ordination space between region combinations. Input is raw reads or ASVs not yet collapsed at the genus level with Greengenes assignments — collapse taxonomy upstream first The goal is comparison against full-length 16S rRNA sequencing, which the article explicitly did not perform The abundance table is not compositional microbiome count data (Bray–Curtis on genus-level relative abundances is the assumption here) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Groups sputum microbiome samples by 16S rRNA hypervariable region combination (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) and tests whether they differ compositionally via NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities, as used in the López-Aladid et al. 2023 Scientific Reports study of respiratory samples. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Groups sputum microbiome samples by 16S rRNA hypervariable region combination (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) and tests whether they differ compositionally via NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities, as used in the López-Aladid et al. 2023 Scientific Reports study of respiratory samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or ASVs not yet collapsed at the genus level with Greengenes assignments — collapse taxonomy upstream first The goal is comparison against full-length 16S rRNA sequencing, which the article explicitly did not perform The abundance table is not compositional microbiome count data (Bray–Curtis on genus-level relative abundances is the assumption here)

skills.description: Use when a denoised QIIME 2 feature table and metadata columns (e.g., location, size fraction) are available and the goal is to determine if 16S communities are significantly distinguished by those grouping factors.
skills.name: microbiome-sample-metadata-stratification
skills.search_text: microbiome-sample-metadata-stratification Use when a denoised QIIME 2 feature table and metadata columns (e.g., location, size fraction) are available and the goal is to determine if 16S communities are significantly distinguished by those grouping factors. The run artifacts are raw FASTQ reads rather than denoised QIIME 2 artifacts (.qza) — the qaqc/repseqs steps of Tourmaline must run first. Samples lack a categorical metadata column with at least two groups (e.g., no location or size-fraction labels), so PERMANOVA grouping is impossible. The goal is representative-sequence filtering (taxonomy, length, abundance, prevalence, or ID) rather than testing community separation by metadata groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Tests whether microbiome communities (e.g., Lake Erie 16S rRNA amplicon samples) separate by sample metadata groups — such as sampling location (Open Water vs. Western Boundary) and size fraction (0.22-μm vs. 5.0-μm) — using UniFrac beta diversity, PCoA/Emperor ordination, and PERMANOVA in QIIME 2 within the Tourmaline workflow. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Tests whether microbiome communities (e.g., Lake Erie 16S rRNA amplicon samples) separate by sample metadata groups — such as sampling location (Open Water vs. Western Boundary) and size fraction (0.22-μm vs. 5.0-μm) — using UniFrac beta diversity, PCoA/Emperor ordination, and PERMANOVA in QIIME 2 within the Tourmaline workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The run artifacts are raw FASTQ reads rather than denoised QIIME 2 artifacts (.qza) — the qaqc/repseqs steps of Tourmaline must run first. Samples lack a categorical metadata column with at least two groups (e.g., no location or size-fraction labels), so PERMANOVA grouping is impossible. The goal is representative-sequence filtering (taxonomy, length, abundance, prevalence, or ID) rather than testing community separation by metadata groups.

skills.description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ files (e.g., 33 sputum samples sequenced on Illumina MiSeq) must be quality-filtered, denoised, and reduced to per-sample sequence counts, per-region ASV totals, and genus-level taxonomy counts.
skills.name: microbiome-sequence-count-tabulation
skills.search_text: microbiome-sequence-count-tabulation Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ files (e.g., 33 sputum samples sequenced on Illumina MiSeq) must be quality-filtered, denoised, and reduced to per-sample sequence counts, per-region ASV totals, and genus-level taxonomy counts. Input is already a denoised feature/ASV table or a collapsed genus-level abundance table — this skill regenerates counts from raw FASTQ, so it would duplicate completed preprocessing. The data are full-length 16S rRNA reads from third-generation platforms (e.g., Nanopore) — the pipeline is tuned to Illumina MiSeq's 300 bp length limit and paired-end Deblur. The goal is functional profiling or strain-level resolution — Greengenes is collapsed at genus level and the article explicitly did not compare against full-length sequencing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A reproducible workflow for tabulating post-QC sequence depth, ASV counts, and collapsed taxonomy counts from 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of sputum samples across hypervariable region combinations (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9). It standardizes the numbers a future agent needs to sanity-check a microbiome preprocessing run. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: A reproducible workflow for tabulating post-QC sequence depth, ASV counts, and collapsed taxonomy counts from 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of sputum samples across hypervariable region combinations (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9). It standardizes the numbers a future agent needs to sanity-check a microbiome preprocessing run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a denoised feature/ASV table or a collapsed genus-level abundance table — this skill regenerates counts from raw FASTQ, so it would duplicate completed preprocessing. The data are full-length 16S rRNA reads from third-generation platforms (e.g., Nanopore) — the pipeline is tuned to Illumina MiSeq's 300 bp length limit and paired-end Deblur. The goal is functional profiling or strain-level resolution — Greengenes is collapsed at genus level and the article explicitly did not compare against full-length sequencing.

skills.description: Use when a study needs controlled synthetic OTU/count data — e.g., known sampling fractions, 500–1000 taxa, unbalanced microbial load — to test bias correction, normalization residuals, or CPU-time scaling of DA methods.
skills.name: microbiome-simulation-data-generation
skills.search_text: microbiome-simulation-data-generation Use when a study needs controlled synthetic OTU/count data — e.g., known sampling fractions, 500–1000 taxa, unbalanced microbial load — to test bias correction, normalization residuals, or CPU-time scaling of DA methods. The input is already an observed feature table from a real experiment — use feature_table_pre_process + ANCOM_BC directly rather than simulating data The goal is DA inference on real data with confidence intervals and FDR control, not method benchmarking — simulation is unnecessary overhead The study design requires very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group), where the article notes ANCOM-BC does not control FDR, making benchmark conclusions unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generates synthetic microbiome OTU count tables (e.g., 500 or 1000 taxa, unbalanced microbial load with balanced library size) using the simulation scripts archived in the ANCOM-BC-Code-Archive, in R with dplyr and nloptr, to benchmark normalization and differential-abundance methods such as ANCOM-BC against CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, and TSS. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Generates synthetic microbiome OTU count tables (e.g., 500 or 1000 taxa, unbalanced microbial load with balanced library size) using the simulation scripts archived in the ANCOM-BC-Code-Archive, in R with dplyr and nloptr, to benchmark normalization and differential-abundance methods such as ANCOM-BC against CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, and TSS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an observed feature table from a real experiment — use feature_table_pre_process + ANCOM_BC directly rather than simulating data The goal is DA inference on real data with confidence intervals and FDR control, not method benchmarking — simulation is unnecessary overhead The study design requires very small sample sizes (e.g., n = 5 per group), where the article notes ANCOM-BC does not control FDR, making benchmark conclusions unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-processed taxa-by-sample absolute abundance table plus group assignments and need to estimate/correct the sampling-fraction bias (delta) via the ANCOM-BC E-M mixture model before testing taxon differential abundance.
skills.name: microbiome-taxa-abundance-difference-modeling
skills.search_text: microbiome-taxa-abundance-difference-modeling Use when you have a pre-processed taxa-by-sample absolute abundance table plus group assignments and need to estimate/correct the sampling-fraction bias (delta) via the ANCOM-BC E-M mixture model before testing taxon differential abundance. Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group): ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases The taxon is a structural zero in a group — entries must be masked; ANCOM-BC is not designed to detect log-scale abundance differences for structural-zero taxa group.var is continuous — ANCOM-BC v1.0 only supports discrete group.var http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs the E-M algorithm inside ANCOM-BC that estimates the sampling-fraction bias term delta — the mean difference of log (natural log) sampling fractions between groups — in a linear regression framework on the log scale, so that differential abundance of taxa in absolute abundance is bias-corrected. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs the E-M algorithm inside ANCOM-BC that estimates the sampling-fraction bias term delta — the mean difference of log (natural log) sampling fractions between groups — in a linear regression framework on the log scale, so that differential abundance of taxa in absolute abundance is bias-corrected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group): ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled in such cases The taxon is a structural zero in a group — entries must be masked; ANCOM-BC is not designed to detect log-scale abundance differences for structural-zero taxa group.var is continuous — ANCOM-BC v1.0 only supports discrete group.var

skills.description: Use when mapping long PacBio/ONT metagenomic reads against a large reference database (e.g. >12,000 RefSeq genomes) and you need fast candidate mapping locations to feed downstream probabilistic scoring, rather than base-level alignments.
skills.name: minimizer-based-approximate-mapping
skills.search_text: minimizer-based-approximate-mapping Use when mapping long PacBio/ONT metagenomic reads against a large reference database (e.g. >12,000 RefSeq genomes) and you need fast candidate mapping locations to feed downstream probabilistic scoring, rather than base-level alignments. Sample contains a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned Base-level exact alignments are required, since MashMap 'does not compute the alignments explicitly' and MetaMaps outputs only approximate mapping locations Real-time/streaming analysis is needed — MetaMaps lacks support for streaming data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generate candidate mapping locations for each long metagenomic read using a minimizer-based approximate mapping strategy (MashMap) instead of exact alignment, so that a comprehensive RefSeq database can be mapped rapidly on commodity hardware. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Generate candidate mapping locations for each long metagenomic read using a minimizer-based approximate mapping strategy (MashMap) instead of exact alignment, so that a comprehensive RefSeq database can be mapped rapidly on commodity hardware.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample contains a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and remain unassigned Base-level exact alignments are required, since MashMap 'does not compute the alignments explicitly' and MetaMaps outputs only approximate mapping locations Real-time/streaming analysis is needed — MetaMaps lacks support for streaming data

skills.description: Use when PacBio/ONT long reads (minimum length 1000 bp) must be mapped to a comprehensive reference database and approximate candidate mapping locations with estimated alignment identities are needed before probabilistic scoring.
skills.name: minimizer-index-construction
skills.search_text: minimizer-index-construction Use when PacBio/ONT long reads (minimum length 1000 bp) must be mapped to a comprehensive reference database and approximate candidate mapping locations with estimated alignment identities are needed before probabilistic scoring. Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length (1000 bp) yield minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and end up unassigned When exact base-to-base alignments are required — MashMap/MetaMaps estimate identity from k-mer Jaccard similarity and do not compute alignments explicitly When candidate mapping locations are already available (e.g. from a prior mapping run feeding metamaps classify) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generates candidate mapping locations for long reads against a large reference database (e.g. >12,000 RefSeq genomes) by indexing reference minimizers and intersecting them with read minimizers via a winnowed-minhash (MashMap-based) strategy, the first stage of MetaMaps' two-stage procedure. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Generates candidate mapping locations for long reads against a large reference database (e.g. >12,000 RefSeq genomes) by indexing reference minimizers and intersecting them with read minimizers via a winnowed-minhash (MashMap-based) strategy, the first stage of MetaMaps' two-stage procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the minimum length (1000 bp) yield minimizer sets too small to reliably determine mapping locations and end up unassigned When exact base-to-base alignments are required — MashMap/MetaMaps estimate identity from k-mer Jaccard similarity and do not compute alignments explicitly When candidate mapping locations are already available (e.g. from a prior mapping run feeding metamaps classify)

skills.description: Use when metabarcoding ASV/variant tables from replicated samples include mock community and negative control samples, and you need to score filtering pipelines by sensitivity and precision against expected (ground-truth) occurrences.
skills.name: mock-and-negative-control-occurrence-classification
skills.search_text: mock-and-negative-control-occurrence-classification Use when metabarcoding ASV/variant tables from replicated samples include mock community and negative control samples, and you need to score filtering pipelines by sensitivity and precision against expected (ground-truth) occurrences. The dataset lacks mock community samples or negative controls, since TP/FP classification cannot be established without expected-composition and blank samples You only have an already-filtered ASV table without replicate or control-sample metadata, so occurrence reproducibility and false-positive status cannot be assessed The goal is raw denoising/clustering quality of a single-sample study rather than cross-pipeline benchmarking of filtering against controls Classifies ASV/variant occurrences in metabarcoding samples as true or false positives using known-composition mock community samples and negative controls, then computes sensitivity TP/(TP+FN) and precision TP/(TP+FP) to benchmark filtering pipelines such as VTAM, DALU, and OBIbaR. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Classifies ASV/variant occurrences in metabarcoding samples as true or false positives using known-composition mock community samples and negative controls, then computes sensitivity TP/(TP+FN) and precision TP/(TP+FP) to benchmark filtering pipelines such as VTAM, DALU, and OBIbaR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks mock community samples or negative controls, since TP/FP classification cannot be established without expected-composition and blank samples You only have an already-filtered ASV table without replicate or control-sample metadata, so occurrence reproducibility and false-positive status cannot be assessed The goal is raw denoising/clustering quality of a single-sample study rather than cross-pipeline benchmarking of filtering against controls

skills.description: Use when a denoised (DADA2/Deblur) or clustered (VSEARCH 99%/97%/95%) mock-community ASV/OTU feature table still contains unexpected 'miss' variants (e.g., partial and miss ASVs) that must be removed before diversity analyses.
skills.name: mock-community-abundance-filtering
skills.search_text: mock-community-abundance-filtering Use when a denoised (DADA2/Deblur) or clustered (VSEARCH 99%/97%/95%) mock-community ASV/OTU feature table still contains unexpected 'miss' variants (e.g., partial and miss ASVs) that must be removed before diversity analyses. Input is already a fully filtered feature table in which all unexpected mock ASVs are absent — re-applying the subtraction would remove real reads The dataset contains no mock community, so no empirically derived per-library maximum for 'miss' variants can be computed You are filtering the COI reference database rather than a feature table — the paper's database filters (remove gaps, keep >100 bp, require Family/Order taxonomy) apply there instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Applies the tidybug paper's standard low-abundance filter (drop single-sample ASVs, keep ≥5,000-read samples) plus an extra per-library subtraction filter, using empirically derived maxima of unexpected 'miss' mock ASVs, to remove spurious sequence variants from mock-community COI feature tables. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Applies the tidybug paper's standard low-abundance filter (drop single-sample ASVs, keep ≥5,000-read samples) plus an extra per-library subtraction filter, using empirically derived maxima of unexpected 'miss' mock ASVs, to remove spurious sequence variants from mock-community COI feature tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fully filtered feature table in which all unexpected mock ASVs are absent — re-applying the subtraction would remove real reads The dataset contains no mock community, so no empirically derived per-library maximum for 'miss' variants can be computed You are filtering the COI reference database rather than a feature table — the paper's database filters (remove gaps, keep >100 bp, require Family/Order taxonomy) apply there instead

skills.description: Use when a metabarcoding pipeline needs quantitative performance validation on a mock community with known taxonomic composition, e.g., comparing ASV inference (Swarm v2) vs OTU clustering (VSEARCH) precision/recall.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation Use when a metabarcoding pipeline needs quantitative performance validation on a mock community with known taxonomic composition, e.g., comparing ASV inference (Swarm v2) vs OTU clustering (VSEARCH) precision/recall. The dataset is a real environmental community with unknown composition — precision/recall against ground truth cannot be computed Input is already an OTU/ASV table; this skill operates from raw .fastq.gz reads through the full pre-processing and inference chain http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_2814 Benchmark an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline (e.g., PEMA) against a known-composition 16S rRNA mock community (Gohl et al., 20 bacterial species) by computing precision, recall, and F1 at genus level for alternative clustering/ASV-inference conditions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Benchmark an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline (e.g., PEMA) against a known-composition 16S rRNA mock community (Gohl et al., 20 bacterial species) by computing precision, recall, and F1 at genus level for alternative clustering/ASV-inference conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a real environmental community with unknown composition — precision/recall against ground truth cannot be computed Input is already an OTU/ASV table; this skill operates from raw .fastq.gz reads through the full pre-processing and inference chain

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic profilers or reference libraries on 16S mock community sequencing data, to quantify genus-/species-level abundance error or alpha-diversity deviation against known ground-truth composition.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing taxonomic profilers or reference libraries on 16S mock community sequencing data, to quantify genus-/species-level abundance error or alpha-diversity deviation against known ground-truth composition. Input is real environmental/clinical microbiome data with no known ground-truth composition — accuracy-based NRMSE against expected taxa cannot be computed The goal is ASV/OTU inference or read processing itself rather than comparative benchmarking of profiler/library pairs Evaluation targets higher taxonomic levels (phylum/class) — the paper specifically analyzes genus- and species-level performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks 16S amplicon taxonomic profiling pipelines (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) paired with reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, RefSeq 2018/2020, Kraken 2 Standard) against synthetic mock communities using accuracy-based (log NRMSE) and diversity-deviation (Shannon, Simpson, breakaway_nof1) metrics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks 16S amplicon taxonomic profiling pipelines (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) paired with reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, RefSeq 2018/2020, Kraken 2 Standard) against synthetic mock communities using accuracy-based (log NRMSE) and diversity-deviation (Shannon, Simpson, breakaway_nof1) metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real environmental/clinical microbiome data with no known ground-truth composition — accuracy-based NRMSE against expected taxa cannot be computed The goal is ASV/OTU inference or read processing itself rather than comparative benchmarking of profiler/library pairs Evaluation targets higher taxonomic levels (phylum/class) — the paper specifically analyzes genus- and species-level performance

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an rRNA amplicon classification tool recovers known taxon abundances, using an artificial mock community dataset with a known expected taxonomic composition as ground truth.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an rRNA amplicon classification tool recovers known taxon abundances, using an artificial mock community dataset with a known expected taxonomic composition as ground truth. Input data is a real environmental or clinical community with no known expected composition — there is no ground truth to compare recovered abundances against, so abundance-recovery accuracy cannot be computed The goal is speed or resource benchmarking only; while MAPseq reports 'up to one hundred times faster', this workflow is designed for abundance-recovery accuracy, not runtime profiling Input is already a summarized abundance/OTU table — classification and per-read confidence estimation are unnecessary and the benchmarking must start from raw classified reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3300 Benchmark a taxonomy/OTU classification tool by classifying an artificial mock rRNA community with known expected composition and comparing recovered abundances against expected values at species, genus, and family levels. In the MAPseq article this workflow demonstrated MAPseq recovers expected mock community abundances better than competing tools. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Benchmark a taxonomy/OTU classification tool by classifying an artificial mock rRNA community with known expected composition and comparing recovered abundances against expected values at species, genus, and family levels. In the MAPseq article this workflow demonstrated MAPseq recovers expected mock community abundances better than competing tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is a real environmental or clinical community with no known expected composition — there is no ground truth to compare recovered abundances against, so abundance-recovery accuracy cannot be computed The goal is speed or resource benchmarking only; while MAPseq reports 'up to one hundred times faster', this workflow is designed for abundance-recovery accuracy, not runtime profiling Input is already a summarized abundance/OTU table — classification and per-read confidence estimation are unnecessary and the benchmarking must start from raw classified reads

skills.description: Use when benchmarking 16S amplicon taxonomic profilers on synthetic mock communities and you need comparable per-sample taxon abundance counts matrices per profiler–reference-library pairing as the substrate for genus- and species-level accuracy evaluation.
skills.name: mock-community-counts-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: mock-community-counts-matrix-generation Use when benchmarking 16S amplicon taxonomic profilers on synthetic mock communities and you need comparable per-sample taxon abundance counts matrices per profiler–reference-library pairing as the substrate for genus- and species-level accuracy evaluation. Input data are not synthetic mock communities with known composition — the skill's counts matrices feed accuracy/sensitivity/specificity evaluation that requires a reference 'ground truth' A feature/counts table already exists and only downstream genus- or species-level accuracy scoring is needed The analysis targets shotgun metagenomic (whole-genome) data rather than PCR-amplified 16S rRNA gene amplicons http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reproduces per-sample taxon-by-sample counts matrices for the 11 pipeline/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2 DADA2-plugin, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 crossed with SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, and RefSeq 2018/2020) applied to the 136 publicly available mock community 16S amplicon samples from Lluch, Kozich, Fouhy, and Karstens, as benchmarked by Odom et al. 2023. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Reproduces per-sample taxon-by-sample counts matrices for the 11 pipeline/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2 DADA2-plugin, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 crossed with SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, and RefSeq 2018/2020) applied to the 136 publicly available mock community 16S amplicon samples from Lluch, Kozich, Fouhy, and Karstens, as benchmarked by Odom et al. 2023.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not synthetic mock communities with known composition — the skill's counts matrices feed accuracy/sensitivity/specificity evaluation that requires a reference 'ground truth' A feature/counts table already exists and only downstream genus- or species-level accuracy scoring is needed The analysis targets shotgun metagenomic (whole-genome) data rather than PCR-amplified 16S rRNA gene amplicons

skills.description: Use when you have raw paired-end mock community reads and need to compare how representative-sequence inference methods (denoising vs OTU clustering) and filtering stringency affect erroneous-sequence rates.
skills.name: mock-community-error-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: mock-community-error-rate-quantification Use when you have raw paired-end mock community reads and need to compare how representative-sequence inference methods (denoising vs OTU clustering) and filtering stringency affect erroneous-sequence rates. Input is already a feature table of classified taxa rather than raw mock community reads — this skill requires re-running representative-sequence inference from the raw data. The biological dataset has no known expected community composition, so 'unexpected' sequences cannot be defined by comparison to references. Your goal is taxonomic classifier accuracy (e.g. BOLD API vs BLAST+LCA comparison) rather than denoising/clustering error assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies unexpected (erroneous) ASVs in a mock community metabarcoding dataset by aligning representative sequences from each denoising or clustering program (DADA2, Deblur, VSEARCH) against the known expected mock references, then computing per-condition error rates under escalating low-abundance filtering. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Quantifies unexpected (erroneous) ASVs in a mock community metabarcoding dataset by aligning representative sequences from each denoising or clustering program (DADA2, Deblur, VSEARCH) against the known expected mock references, then computing per-condition error rates under escalating low-abundance filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table of classified taxa rather than raw mock community reads — this skill requires re-running representative-sequence inference from the raw data. The biological dataset has no known expected community composition, so 'unexpected' sequences cannot be defined by comparison to references. Your goal is taxonomic classifier accuracy (e.g. BOLD API vs BLAST+LCA comparison) rather than denoising/clustering error assessment.

skills.description: Use when per-sample benchmark metrics (sensitivity, specificity, log NRMSE, alpha diversity deviations) exist for multiple profiler-library pairings on the same mock community samples and you must determine which pairings significantly outperform others.
skills.name: mock-community-profiler-performance-statistics
skills.search_text: mock-community-profiler-performance-statistics Use when per-sample benchmark metrics (sensitivity, specificity, log NRMSE, alpha diversity deviations) exist for multiple profiler-library pairings on the same mock community samples and you must determine which pairings significantly outperform others. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than computed per-sample benchmark metrics — pipeline profiling (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) must be run first Samples lack a ground-truth mock community composition, so sensitivity, specificity, and NRMSE cannot be computed against expected abundances There is only a single profiler-library pairing, since pairwise contrasts with Tukey correction require multiple pairings http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Statistical skill for benchmarking 16S profiler/reference-library pairings using linear mixed-effects models with Tukey-corrected post hoc comparisons, as used to rank DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, and Kraken 2 on 136 publicly available mock community samples. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Statistical skill for benchmarking 16S profiler/reference-library pairings using linear mixed-effects models with Tukey-corrected post hoc comparisons, as used to rank DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, and Kraken 2 on 136 publicly available mock community samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than computed per-sample benchmark metrics — pipeline profiling (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) must be run first Samples lack a ground-truth mock community composition, so sensitivity, specificity, and NRMSE cannot be computed against expected abundances There is only a single profiler-library pairing, since pairwise contrasts with Tukey correction require multiple pairings

skills.description: Use when finished DADA2 ASV tables from depth-subsampled mock community sequencing runs (e.g. ERR777696 downsampled from 100 to 1,600,000 read pairs; PRJNA626434 from 100 to 40,000 reads) are available and the goal is to evaluate how observed richness scales with sequencing depth.
skills.name: mock-community-richness-quantification
skills.search_text: mock-community-richness-quantification Use when finished DADA2 ASV tables from depth-subsampled mock community sequencing runs (e.g. ERR777696 downsampled from 100 to 1,600,000 read pairs; PRJNA626434 from 100 to 40,000 reads) are available and the goal is to evaluate how observed richness scales with sequencing depth. Input is still raw FASTQ data rather than finished DADA2 ASV tables — run the dadasnake pipeline (DADA2 denoising, chimera removal, final_table_filtering) first. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of sequences rather than richness/rarefaction behaviour assessment. The dataset is not subsampled across sequencing depths, so there is no depth series over which rarefaction flattening can be quantified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies observed ASV richness across sequencing-depth subsamples of mock community datasets and assesses whether rarefaction curves derived from finished DADA2 ASV tables faithfully reflect richness gain with additional sequencing depth. Surfaces the flattening artefact that makes DADA2-based richness estimates and rarefaction curves require caution. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Quantifies observed ASV richness across sequencing-depth subsamples of mock community datasets and assesses whether rarefaction curves derived from finished DADA2 ASV tables faithfully reflect richness gain with additional sequencing depth. Surfaces the flattening artefact that makes DADA2-based richness estimates and rarefaction curves require caution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ data rather than finished DADA2 ASV tables — run the dadasnake pipeline (DADA2 denoising, chimera removal, final_table_filtering) first. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of sequences rather than richness/rarefaction behaviour assessment. The dataset is not subsampled across sequencing depths, so there is no depth series over which rarefaction flattening can be quantified.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) or reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq) on 16S mock community data with known composition.
skills.name: mock-community-sensitivity-calculation
skills.search_text: mock-community-sensitivity-calculation Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) or reference libraries (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq) on 16S mock community data with known composition.
