skills.summary: Computes genus- and species-level taxon detection sensitivity and read assignment specificity by comparing profiler/library outputs against mock community ground truth, enabling benchmarking of 16S amplicon classification pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data comes from real (non-mock) microbiome samples with no ground-truth composition table — sensitivity/specificity against ground truth cannot be computed Analysis goal is producing taxonomy assignments rather than benchmarking profiler accuracy — use the classification pipelines directly instead Input is already the aggregated per-sample metric table — proceed to aggregation/tabulation rather than recomputing per-taxon detection

skills.description: Use when validating that simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads reproduce per-genome error profiles observed in real mock-community sequencing runs, e.g. before benchmarking ASV clustering or taxonomic assignment pipelines.
skills.name: mock-community-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mock-community-simulation-benchmarking Use when validating that simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads reproduce per-genome error profiles observed in real mock-community sequencing runs, e.g. before benchmarking ASV clustering or taxonomic assignment pipelines. Input is already a feature/ASV count table rather than raw simulated reads — error-profile comparison requires per-read sequences Reads are short-read (e.g. Illumina) rather than PacBio HiFi amplicon data, since MHASS models empirically derived HiFi pass-number and error distributions The goal is downstream benchmarking of ASV clustering or taxonomic assignment on an already-validated simulator rather than validation of the simulator's error model itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark a microbiome HiFi amplicon simulator by comparing per-genome edit distance distributions of simulated PacBio HiFi reads against real sequencing data from mock communities (Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, Phylotag/16S). This validates that simulated read error profiles mirror empirical ones before using the simulator for downstream benchmarking. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Benchmark a microbiome HiFi amplicon simulator by comparing per-genome edit distance distributions of simulated PacBio HiFi reads against real sequencing data from mock communities (Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, Phylotag/16S). This validates that simulated read error profiles mirror empirical ones before using the simulator for downstream benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/ASV count table rather than raw simulated reads — error-profile comparison requires per-read sequences Reads are short-read (e.g. Illumina) rather than PacBio HiFi amplicon data, since MHASS models empirically derived HiFi pass-number and error distributions The goal is downstream benchmarking of ASV clustering or taxonomic assignment on an already-validated simulator rather than validation of the simulator's error model itself

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a COI metabarcoding pipeline against a mock community of known composition (e.g. Bista et al.) to measure species recovery and genus-level F1-scores.
skills.name: mock-community-species-recovery-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-species-recovery-evaluation Use when benchmarking a COI metabarcoding pipeline against a mock community of known composition (e.g. Bista et al.) to measure species recovery and genus-level F1-scores. Analysis targets 16S/18S rRNA or ITS markers where OTU clustering via VSEARCH (not COI ASV inference via Swarm) is the appropriate PEMA route Input data are already a taxonomy-assigned ASV/MOTU table rather than raw .fastq.gz reads The sample is a real environmental community rather than a mock community with a known species inventory, so no ground-truth recovery rate can be computed Evaluates an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline (PEMA) on a COI mock community (Bista et al. dataset) by running the full read-preprocessing, ASV-inference (Swarm v2, d=10), and taxonomy-assignment (RDPClassifier + MIDORI) workflow and quantifying how many of the known mock community species are recovered. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Evaluates an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline (PEMA) on a COI mock community (Bista et al. dataset) by running the full read-preprocessing, ASV-inference (Swarm v2, d=10), and taxonomy-assignment (RDPClassifier + MIDORI) workflow and quantifying how many of the known mock community species are recovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis targets 16S/18S rRNA or ITS markers where OTU clustering via VSEARCH (not COI ASV inference via Swarm) is the appropriate PEMA route Input data are already a taxonomy-assigned ASV/MOTU table rather than raw .fastq.gz reads The sample is a real environmental community rather than a mock community with a known species inventory, so no ground-truth recovery rate can be computed

skills.description: Use when amplicon ASV tables from one or more 16S hypervariable regions are available alongside a ZymoBIOMICS mock community control, and the goal is to quantify which region(s) classify taxa with the sensitivity/specificity.
skills.name: mock-community-taxa-comparison
skills.search_text: mock-community-taxa-comparison Use when amplicon ASV tables from one or more 16S hypervariable regions are available alongside a ZymoBIOMICS mock community control, and the goal is to quantify which region(s) classify taxa with the sensitivity/specificity. Samples lack a mock community standard control, so no reference taxa exist for ROC cross-validation The question is compositional profiling (e.g. alpha diversity or NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities) rather than classification accuracy against a positive control http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Cross-validates the accuracy of 16S rRNA hypervariable-region taxonomic classification by comparing mock community (ZymoBIOMICS) standard control taxa against sample taxa, using ROC/AUC to rank region combinations by sensitivity and specificity. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Cross-validates the accuracy of 16S rRNA hypervariable-region taxonomic classification by comparing mock community (ZymoBIOMICS) standard control taxa against sample taxa, using ROC/AUC to rank region combinations by sensitivity and specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack a mock community standard control, so no reference taxa exist for ROC cross-validation The question is compositional profiling (e.g. alpha diversity or NMDS of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities) rather than classification accuracy against a positive control

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark that a DADA2-based amplicon pipeline correctly recovers known community richness (e.g. exactly 59 prokaryotic ASVs) and genus composition from a mock community fastq dataset.
skills.name: mock-community-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: mock-community-taxonomic-classification Use when you need to benchmark that a DADA2-based amplicon pipeline correctly recovers known community richness (e.g. exactly 59 prokaryotic ASVs) and genus composition from a mock community fastq dataset. Your input is already an ASV/feature table or has been taxonomically classified — this skill processes raw paired fastq reads from primer-trimming through classification. You lack a ground-truth mock community composition — without the 59-species reference there is no benchmark to compare recovered richness and genera against. Your data are single-end or non-16S fungal ITS amplicons requiring a different dadasnake configuration (e.g. UNITE instead of SILVA 138). http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates an amplicon-processing pipeline (dadasnake/DADA2) by running the 16S rRNA mock community ERR777696 (59 prokaryotic species: 10 archaea, 49 bacteria) through primer removal, DADA2 denoising/merging, and mothur taxonomy assignment against SILVA 138, then comparing recovered ASVs to the known ground-truth composition. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Validates an amplicon-processing pipeline (dadasnake/DADA2) by running the 16S rRNA mock community ERR777696 (59 prokaryotic species: 10 archaea, 49 bacteria) through primer removal, DADA2 denoising/merging, and mothur taxonomy assignment against SILVA 138, then comparing recovered ASVs to the known ground-truth composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already an ASV/feature table or has been taxonomically classified — this skill processes raw paired fastq reads from primer-trimming through classification. You lack a ground-truth mock community composition — without the 59-species reference there is no benchmark to compare recovered richness and genera against. Your data are single-end or non-16S fungal ITS amplicons requiring a different dadasnake configuration (e.g. UNITE instead of SILVA 138).

skills.description: Use when starting from deposited raw paired-end NextSeq FASTQ files of COI and 16S amplicons and the goal is a denoised, chimera-filtered MOTU abundance table with per-marker MOTU totals.
skills.name: motu-count-table-generation
skills.search_text: motu-count-table-generation Use when starting from deposited raw paired-end NextSeq FASTQ files of COI and 16S amplicons and the goal is a denoised, chimera-filtered MOTU abundance table with per-marker MOTU totals. Input is already a denoised feature/MOTU table or OTU count matrix — no FASTQ denoising is needed Amplicons are non-mitochondrial markers (e.g. ITS, 18S) with very different read lengths and error profiles than the COI/16S setup described here Only single-end reads are available — the mergePairs step requiring a 5 bp forward/reverse overlap cannot be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generates marker-specific MOTU (metabarcoding OTU) count tables from raw paired-end Illumina amplicon reads by running the DADA2 pipeline (filterAndTrim, learnErrors/dada, mergePairs, removeBimeraDenovo) separately per mitochondrial marker, producing a motu_count_table.tsv with per-sample MOTU abundances for COI and 16S amplicons. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Generates marker-specific MOTU (metabarcoding OTU) count tables from raw paired-end Illumina amplicon reads by running the DADA2 pipeline (filterAndTrim, learnErrors/dada, mergePairs, removeBimeraDenovo) separately per mitochondrial marker, producing a motu_count_table.tsv with per-sample MOTU abundances for COI and 16S amplicons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a denoised feature/MOTU table or OTU count matrix — no FASTQ denoising is needed Amplicons are non-mitochondrial markers (e.g. ITS, 18S) with very different read lengths and error profiles than the COI/16S setup described here Only single-end reads are available — the mergePairs step requiring a 5 bp forward/reverse overlap cannot be applied

skills.description: Use when a filtered DADA2 MOTU table (detections in >=2 PCR replicates) with taxonomic assignments must be reduced to total arthropod reads per marker and richness counts at species, family, and order ranks.
skills.name: motu-read-count-summarization
skills.search_text: motu-read-count-summarization Use when a filtered DADA2 MOTU table (detections in >=2 PCR replicates) with taxonomic assignments must be reduced to total arthropod reads per marker and richness counts at species, family, and order ranks. The MOTU table has not been filtered to at least two PCR replicates — richness and read totals will not reproduce the reported values Taxonomy assignments have not been made under the 99-100% identity rule, so MOTUs cannot be aggregated to species rank The question concerns community clustering by plant species rather than read totals and richness summarization http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Summarizes a DADA2-inferred, replicate-filtered MOTU table into per-marker arthropod read totals and taxonomic richness counts (species/family/order), plus per-species read-share fractions to quantify community dominance. This reproduces the headline numbers of a flower eDNA metabarcoding study. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Summarizes a DADA2-inferred, replicate-filtered MOTU table into per-marker arthropod read totals and taxonomic richness counts (species/family/order), plus per-species read-share fractions to quantify community dominance. This reproduces the headline numbers of a flower eDNA metabarcoding study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MOTU table has not been filtered to at least two PCR replicates — richness and read totals will not reproduce the reported values Taxonomy assignments have not been made under the 99-100% identity rule, so MOTUs cannot be aggregated to species rank The question concerns community clustering by plant species rather than read totals and richness summarization

skills.description: Use when processed (dereplicated, chimera-removed) amplicon reads must be grouped into MOTUs at a fixed similarity threshold to obtain representative sequences for taxonomic assignment.
skills.name: motu-representative-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: motu-representative-sequence-extraction Use when processed (dereplicated, chimera-removed) amplicon reads must be grouped into MOTUs at a fixed similarity threshold to obtain representative sequences for taxonomic assignment. Input reads still contain chimeras or have not been dereplicated — the article applies this clustering only after uchime-denovo chimera removal and obiuniq dereplication. The goal is OTU clustering at coarser resolution for general eukaryotic metabarcoding — this skill fixes a constant 99% threshold tuned to a 127 bp elasmobranch COI fragment. Input is already a MOTU/feature table — representative sequences have already been extracted and clustering should not be re-run. Delimits Molecular Operational Taxonomic Units (MOTUs) from chimera-filtered, dereplicated eDNA reads using sumaclust at a constant 99% sequence similarity threshold, and extracts the representative sequence and read count for each MOTU as input to downstream taxonomic assignment. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Delimits Molecular Operational Taxonomic Units (MOTUs) from chimera-filtered, dereplicated eDNA reads using sumaclust at a constant 99% sequence similarity threshold, and extracts the representative sequence and read count for each MOTU as input to downstream taxonomic assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads still contain chimeras or have not been dereplicated — the article applies this clustering only after uchime-denovo chimera removal and obiuniq dereplication. The goal is OTU clustering at coarser resolution for general eukaryotic metabarcoding — this skill fixes a constant 99% threshold tuned to a 127 bp elasmobranch COI fragment. Input is already a MOTU/feature table — representative sequences have already been extracted and clustering should not be re-run.

skills.description: Use when a sumaclust-delimited, ecotag-annotated MOTU table (per-sample read counts) must be cleaned of single-read MOTUs prior to per-location or per-region richness estimates for elasmobranch or other metabarcoding taxa.
skills.name: motu-single-read-filtering
skills.search_text: motu-single-read-filtering Use when a sumaclust-delimited, ecotag-annotated MOTU table (per-sample read counts) must be cleaned of single-read MOTUs prior to per-location or per-region richness estimates for elasmobranch or other metabarcoding taxa. Input is raw reads that have not yet been aligned, length-filtered (120–135 bp), dereplicated and clustered into MOTUs — the filter is defined on clustered MOTU tables, not FASTQ. The analysis goal is to retain rare-taxa signal or estimate detection prevalence of very low-abundance taxa; singleton removal deliberately discards such evidence. MOTU clustering used a similarity threshold other than 99% or a tool other than the OBITools/sumaclust pipeline, since per-location richness figures are only reproducible under this exact workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Conservative decontamination step that removes every MOTU supported by only a single read from an OBITools ecotag taxonomic-assignment table before computing elasmobranch MOTU richness, guarding against contamination- and sequencing-error false positives in 99% sumaclust clustering results. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Conservative decontamination step that removes every MOTU supported by only a single read from an OBITools ecotag taxonomic-assignment table before computing elasmobranch MOTU richness, guarding against contamination- and sequencing-error false positives in 99% sumaclust clustering results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads that have not yet been aligned, length-filtered (120–135 bp), dereplicated and clustered into MOTUs — the filter is defined on clustered MOTU tables, not FASTQ. The analysis goal is to retain rare-taxa signal or estimate detection prevalence of very low-abundance taxa; singleton removal deliberately discards such evidence. MOTU clustering used a similarity threshold other than 99% or a tool other than the OBITools/sumaclust pipeline, since per-location richness figures are only reproducible under this exact workflow.

skills.description: Use when auditing compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTUs clustered at 97% PSD) by re-measuring each member's distance from the representative with alignment-based (MSD) and tree-based (BLD) metrics.
skills.name: msd-computation-from-placement-msa
skills.search_text: msd-computation-from-placement-msa Use when auditing compactness of 16S rRNA OTUs (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTUs clustered at 97% PSD) by re-measuring each member's distance from the representative with alignment-based (MSD) and tree-based (BLD) metrics. The goal is to define OTUs de novo by percent sequence similarity (PSD) clustering at 97% — this skill audits existing OTUs rather than building them Input sequences lack OTU grouping or a designated representative sequence, so no representative-vs-member comparison can be defined A different dissimilarity metric (e.g. PSD) is explicitly requested, which this skill does not compute http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes maximum sequence dissimilarity (MSD) — and phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) — between each HMP OTU's representative sequence and every remaining member read, using a placement-induced multiple sequence alignment and an ML tree per OTU. It quantifies how far OTU members diverge from the single annotated representative. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Computes maximum sequence dissimilarity (MSD) — and phylogenetic branch length distance (BLD) — between each HMP OTU's representative sequence and every remaining member read, using a placement-induced multiple sequence alignment and an ML tree per OTU. It quantifies how far OTU members diverge from the single annotated representative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to define OTUs de novo by percent sequence similarity (PSD) clustering at 97% — this skill audits existing OTUs rather than building them Input sequences lack OTU grouping or a designated representative sequence, so no representative-vs-member comparison can be defined A different dissimilarity metric (e.g. PSD) is explicitly requested, which this skill does not compute

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTU analyses that need OTUs stratified by member-vs-representative MSD (threshold 0.03) and per-stratum annotation disagreement percentages.
skills.name: msd-stratified-otu-filtering
skills.search_text: msd-stratified-otu-filtering Use when reproducing or extending HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTU analyses that need OTUs stratified by member-vs-representative MSD (threshold 0.03) and per-stratum annotation disagreement percentages. The analysis goal is OTU clustering itself or choosing a clustering threshold — this skill only evaluates annotation stability of already-clustered OTUs. Input is a feature table or already-annotated BIOM file rather than raw OTU representative/member sequences, since member-level reclassification is required. Phylogenetic metrics other than MSD (e.g. BLD) are the stratification variable — the targets here (0.03 MSD) are specific to mean sequence dissimilarity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A skill for quantifying annotation instability of 97%-similarity OTUs: each OTU's member sequences are independently classified (RDP Classifier / Greengenes) and compared to the representative's annotation, then OTUs are stratified by member-vs-representative MSD (e.g. >= 0.03) to show how disagreement rates change in highly divergent OTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: A skill for quantifying annotation instability of 97%-similarity OTUs: each OTU's member sequences are independently classified (RDP Classifier / Greengenes) and compared to the representative's annotation, then OTUs are stratified by member-vs-representative MSD (e.g. >= 0.03) to show how disagreement rates change in highly divergent OTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is OTU clustering itself or choosing a clustering threshold — this skill only evaluates annotation stability of already-clustered OTUs. Input is a feature table or already-annotated BIOM file rather than raw OTU representative/member sequences, since member-level reclassification is required. Phylogenetic metrics other than MSD (e.g. BLD) are the stratification variable — the targets here (0.03 MSD) are specific to mean sequence dissimilarity.

skills.description: Use when full-length 16S reads (e.g., PacBio CCS ~1500 bp) are available for an organism whose reference genome contains multiple intragenomic 16S copies, and you need to check that observed per-position substitution frequencies match copy-stoichiometry predictions.
skills.name: multi-copy-gene-stoichiometry-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-copy-gene-stoichiometry-comparison Use when full-length 16S reads (e.g., PacBio CCS ~1500 bp) are available for an organism whose reference genome contains multiple intragenomic 16S copies, and you need to check that observed per-position substitution frequencies match copy-stoichiometry predictions. The question depends on insertions or deletions between 16S copies — indels are deliberately excluded here because PacBio CCS deletion errors coincide with homopolymer runs Only short-read data covering a single 16S variable region (e.g., V4) are available; such regions cannot recapture full-gene diversity or intragenomic copy profiles The organism's genome contains a single 16S copy, so no intragenomic stoichiometric prediction can be built http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that long-read (PacBio CCS) or short-read sequencing of a multi-copy gene reproduces the substitution profile predicted from the stoichiometry of all gene copies in a reference genome, using E. coli K-12 MG1655's seven 16S copies as the benchmark. Restricting analysis to substitutions (ignoring indels) avoids platform-specific PacBio CCS deletion errors. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Validates that long-read (PacBio CCS) or short-read sequencing of a multi-copy gene reproduces the substitution profile predicted from the stoichiometry of all gene copies in a reference genome, using E. coli K-12 MG1655's seven 16S copies as the benchmark. Restricting analysis to substitutions (ignoring indels) avoids platform-specific PacBio CCS deletion errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question depends on insertions or deletions between 16S copies — indels are deliberately excluded here because PacBio CCS deletion errors coincide with homopolymer runs Only short-read data covering a single 16S variable region (e.g., V4) are available; such regions cannot recapture full-gene diversity or intragenomic copy profiles The organism's genome contains a single 16S copy, so no intragenomic stoichiometric prediction can be built

skills.description: Use when the goal is to rerun several metabarcoding pipelines (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR) on the same public datasets under identical conditions and reproduce published runtime/memory or precision comparisons.
skills.name: multi-dataset-reproducible-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-reproducible-analysis Use when the goal is to rerun several metabarcoding pipelines (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR) on the same public datasets under identical conditions and reproduce published runtime/memory or precision comparisons. You only need to run a single pipeline (e.g. VTAM alone) on your own data — use the VTAM package directly instead of the benchmark harness Your goal is a methodological evaluation of filtering performance (sensitivity/precision) rather than reproducing the runtime and memory benchmark on the shared datasets Your datasets or hardware differ substantially from the three published datasets (bat, fish, shark) and the 8-CPU/32-GB reference desktop, making published timing values non-comparable Reproduce a published multi-pipeline metabarcoding benchmark by running the VTAM, DALU, and OBIbaR workflows via the Snakemake/Singularity-based vtam_benchmark repository on shared bat, fish, and shark datasets, then compare runtime and memory across pipelines. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Reproduce a published multi-pipeline metabarcoding benchmark by running the VTAM, DALU, and OBIbaR workflows via the Snakemake/Singularity-based vtam_benchmark repository on shared bat, fish, and shark datasets, then compare runtime and memory across pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to run a single pipeline (e.g. VTAM alone) on your own data — use the VTAM package directly instead of the benchmark harness Your goal is a methodological evaluation of filtering performance (sensitivity/precision) rather than reproducing the runtime and memory benchmark on the shared datasets Your datasets or hardware differ substantially from the three published datasets (bat, fish, shark) and the 8-CPU/32-GB reference desktop, making published timing values non-comparable

skills.description: Use when you need to apply several DA tools to the same ASV count table + two-column metadata grouping under identical filtering/rarefaction settings, and compare per-tool significant ASV calls.
skills.name: multi-tool-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: multi-tool-pipeline-execution Use when you need to apply several DA tools to the same ASV count table + two-column metadata grouping under identical filtering/rarefaction settings, and compare per-tool significant ASV calls. You want to use the maintained ANCOMBC R package (ancom/ancombc functions) instead of the archived, unmaintained standalone ANCOM scripts in FrederickHuangLin/ANCOM-Code-Archive Your metadata has more than 2 sample groupings — the two-column metadata file allows maximum 2 groupings You need results for a single tool only; running run_all_tools.sh incurs the overhead of all 14 tools (~20 min per dataset on a modern single-core CPU) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Runs 14 differential abundance tools (ALDEx2, ANCOM, ANCOM-II, DESeq2, edgeR, LEfSe, corncob, metagenomeSeq, limma voom, etc.) uniformly across 16S rRNA ASV tables using the Dockerized bash pipeline from nearinj/Comparison_of_DA_microbiome_methods, so tool outputs are directly comparable across datasets and pre-processing conditions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Runs 14 differential abundance tools (ALDEx2, ANCOM, ANCOM-II, DESeq2, edgeR, LEfSe, corncob, metagenomeSeq, limma voom, etc.) uniformly across 16S rRNA ASV tables using the Dockerized bash pipeline from nearinj/Comparison_of_DA_microbiome_methods, so tool outputs are directly comparable across datasets and pre-processing conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to use the maintained ANCOMBC R package (ancom/ancombc functions) instead of the archived, unmaintained standalone ANCOM scripts in FrederickHuangLin/ANCOM-Code-Archive Your metadata has more than 2 sample groupings — the two-column metadata file allows maximum 2 groupings You need results for a single tool only; running run_all_tools.sh incurs the overhead of all 14 tools (~20 min per dataset on a modern single-core CPU)

skills.description: Use when you have taxa x time-point read-proportion tables from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing and need relative abundance changes comparable across loci despite amplification bias.
skills.name: multilocus-ensemble-index-computation
skills.search_text: multilocus-ensemble-index-computation Use when you have taxa x time-point read-proportion tables from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing and need relative abundance changes comparable across loci despite amplification bias. The input is already a normalized feature table or relative abundance matrix rather than per-locus raw read proportions — re-scaling would double-normalize A taxon is detected at only one locus — no ensemble averaging is possible, and the per-locus index alone is the output You need absolute organismal abundance estimates; amplification bias from template–primer interaction means amplicon abundance is only proportional, not quantitative Computes a within-taxon, within-locus relative abundance index (0–1) from eDNA amplicon read-proportion tables and, when a taxon is detected at multiple genetic loci, averages its per-locus indices into an ensemble index. This mitigates primer/amplification bias that obscures the relationship between organismal and amplicon abundance in metabarcoding time-series. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Computes a within-taxon, within-locus relative abundance index (0–1) from eDNA amplicon read-proportion tables and, when a taxon is detected at multiple genetic loci, averages its per-locus indices into an ensemble index. This mitigates primer/amplification bias that obscures the relationship between organismal and amplicon abundance in metabarcoding time-series.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized feature table or relative abundance matrix rather than per-locus raw read proportions — re-scaling would double-normalize A taxon is detected at only one locus — no ensemble averaging is possible, and the per-locus index alone is the output You need absolute organismal abundance estimates; amplification bias from template–primer interaction means amplicon abundance is only proportional, not quantitative

skills.description: Use when arthropod eDNA richness from grouped flower-sample replicates (per plant species, per marker) must be rarefied and plotted as multi-panel accumulation curves to assess sampling sufficiency.
skills.name: multimarker-richness-visualization
skills.search_text: multimarker-richness-visualization Use when arthropod eDNA richness from grouped flower-sample replicates (per plant species, per marker) must be rarefied and plotted as multi-panel accumulation curves to assess sampling sufficiency. The question is community composition/clustering of arthropods by plant species rather than richness saturation with sampling effort Samples are not grouped flower-sample replicates of individual plant species (e.g., single pooled samples or non-flower eDNA sources), so per-species accumulation cannot be computed Only a single taxonomic level or single marker is of interest and no multi-panel COI/16S comparison is needed — a simpler rarefaction call suffices Computes and plots sample-based species accumulation curves (exact-method rarefaction) per plant species from COI and 16S eDNA metabarcoding OTU/ASV tables, at species and family taxonomic levels, to judge whether recovered arthropod richness saturates with flower sampling effort. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Computes and plots sample-based species accumulation curves (exact-method rarefaction) per plant species from COI and 16S eDNA metabarcoding OTU/ASV tables, at species and family taxonomic levels, to judge whether recovered arthropod richness saturates with flower sampling effort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is community composition/clustering of arthropods by plant species rather than richness saturation with sampling effort Samples are not grouped flower-sample replicates of individual plant species (e.g., single pooled samples or non-flower eDNA sources), so per-species accumulation cannot be computed Only a single taxonomic level or single marker is of interest and no multi-panel COI/16S comparison is needed — a simpler rarefaction call suffices

skills.description: Use when you need a reference alignment of a large full-length 16S rRNA set (e.g., RDP sequences) to serve as the substrate for aligning OTU fragments and computing MSD or BLD between representative and member sequences.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-estimation
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-estimation Use when you need a reference alignment of a large full-length 16S rRNA set (e.g., RDP sequences) to serve as the substrate for aligning OTU fragments and computing MSD or BLD between representative and member sequences. Input sequences are short 16S amplicon fragments (e.g., V1–V3 or V3–V5 regions) rather than full-length 16S — these are aligned against an existing reference alignment, not used to build one. The analysis only requires percent sequence similarity (PSD) OTU clustering at 97% and does not need phylogenetically-aware MSD/BLD distances from an alignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Estimate a single reference multiple sequence alignment of high-quality full-length 16S rRNA sequences (here, from the RDP database) using PASTA, so that downstream OTU fragments can be aligned and MSD/BLD dissimilarities computed against a consistent alignment substrate. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Estimate a single reference multiple sequence alignment of high-quality full-length 16S rRNA sequences (here, from the RDP database) using PASTA, so that downstream OTU fragments can be aligned and MSD/BLD dissimilarities computed against a consistent alignment substrate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are short 16S amplicon fragments (e.g., V1–V3 or V3–V5 regions) rather than full-length 16S — these are aligned against an existing reference alignment, not used to build one. The analysis only requires percent sequence similarity (PSD) OTU clustering at 97% and does not need phylogenetically-aware MSD/BLD distances from an alignment.

skills.description: Use when a tool release claims speed or memory improvements and you need to quantify speedup factors, memory ratios, and output equivalence across single-core and multi-core runs on identical input data.
skills.name: multithreaded-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: multithreaded-performance-comparison Use when a tool release claims speed or memory improvements and you need to quantify speedup factors, memory ratios, and output equivalence across single-core and multi-core runs on identical input data. The input FASTA is not strictly dereplicated — swarm 3.0 makes strict dereplication mandatory, so raw or under-dereplicated reads will break the benchmark The scientific question is about clustering quality or biological OTU composition rather than runtime and memory performance You intend to use large d values (d >= 2 or 3) or the fastidious option, since the benchmark targets default d = 1 behaviour and fastidious can significantly increase memory footprint http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Benchmark a new tool version against its predecessor by measuring wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory under fixed thread counts (e.g. 1 vs 16 cores), while verifying that outputs remain identical. Applied to swarm v3 vs v2 on large dereplicated SSU-rRNA amplicon FASTA datasets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: Benchmark a new tool version against its predecessor by measuring wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory under fixed thread counts (e.g. 1 vs 16 cores), while verifying that outputs remain identical. Applied to swarm v3 vs v2 on large dereplicated SSU-rRNA amplicon FASTA datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input FASTA is not strictly dereplicated — swarm 3.0 makes strict dereplication mandatory, so raw or under-dereplicated reads will break the benchmark The scientific question is about clustering quality or biological OTU composition rather than runtime and memory performance You intend to use large d values (d >= 2 or 3) or the fastidious option, since the benchmark targets default d = 1 behaviour and fastidious can significantly increase memory footprint

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina FASTQ metabarcoding reads (16S V3-V4 or ITS2) contain 3'-end adapter contaminants and quality-based trimming would erase the low-quality bases needed to identify those contaminants; run Scythe before quality trimming.
skills.name: naive-bayes-contamination-classification
skills.search_text: naive-bayes-contamination-classification Use when raw Illumina FASTQ metabarcoding reads (16S V3-V4 or ITS2) contain 3'-end adapter contaminants and quality-based trimming would erase the low-quality bases needed to identify those contaminants; run Scythe before quality trimming. Contamination can occur at any read position (not just the 3'-end): the README recommends TagDust for reads with contamination in any position, since Scythe only checks 3'-end contaminants and cannot trim 5'-end adapters The goal is to discard contaminated reads entirely: Scythe trims off contaminating sequence and keeps the remaining read, unlike TagDust which removes whole reads Input is already quality-trimmed: quality-based trimming may have removed the low-quality bases Scythe relies on to identify 3'-end adapters, so it should run before, not after, quality trimming http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Adapter trimming of metabarcoding FASTQ reads using Scythe v0.994, a Naive Bayesian classifier that removes 3'-end adapter contaminants while tolerating mismatches caused by poor base quality. In the trout-farm metabarcoding study it cleaned 1,054,909 16S reads and 2,193,552 ITS2 reads before OTU clustering. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Adapter trimming of metabarcoding FASTQ reads using Scythe v0.994, a Naive Bayesian classifier that removes 3'-end adapter contaminants while tolerating mismatches caused by poor base quality. In the trout-farm metabarcoding study it cleaned 1,054,909 16S reads and 2,193,552 ITS2 reads before OTU clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Contamination can occur at any read position (not just the 3'-end): the README recommends TagDust for reads with contamination in any position, since Scythe only checks 3'-end contaminants and cannot trim 5'-end adapters The goal is to discard contaminated reads entirely: Scythe trims off contaminating sequence and keeps the remaining read, unlike TagDust which removes whole reads Input is already quality-trimmed: quality-based trimming may have removed the low-quality bases Scythe relies on to identify 3'-end adapters, so it should run before, not after, quality trimming

skills.description: Use when generating synthetic microbiome count/abundance matrices that need realistic between-sample biological variability per ASV, e.g. simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon data from genome molarity values.
skills.name: negative-binomial-count-modeling
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-count-modeling Use when generating synthetic microbiome count/abundance matrices that need realistic between-sample biological variability per ASV, e.g. simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon data from genome molarity values. You already have an observed ASV count table and want downstream analysis rather than simulation of abundances. You need to simulate read-level technical error (PBSIM3 subread accuracy, difference-ratio substitution:insertion:deletion) — that is a separate MHASS step, not the abundance-variability model. The target ASVs have abundance levels where the fitted squared CV would be negative and you require nonzero variability — the NA-to-zero emulation intentionally yields zero biological variability for those ASVs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 MHASS's genome-aware abundance simulation fits a negative binomial model using metaSPARSim's R1 preset to predict each ASV's between-sample squared coefficient of variation from its expected abundance, with NA dispersion estimates emulated as zero variability. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: MHASS's genome-aware abundance simulation fits a negative binomial model using metaSPARSim's R1 preset to predict each ASV's between-sample squared coefficient of variation from its expected abundance, with NA dispersion estimates emulated as zero variability.

skills.name: nrmse-log-transform-aggregation
skills.search_text: nrmse-log-transform-aggregation Use when benchmarking 16S amplicon taxonomic profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) against mock communities with known composition and you need accuracy-based, log-scaled error rates at genus or species level. Input is already a diversity- or detection-based benchmark result (sensitivity/specificity) rather than count-level abundance data needing nRMSE computation Taxonomic abundance tables cannot be mapped to a shared ground truth (no mock community composition available), since nRMSE requires expected vs. measured counts for the union of expected and detected taxa http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute the Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (nRMSE) between measured and true mock-community read counts for each 16S profiler/reference-library pair, log-transform the values, and aggregate into genus- and species-level means (e.g., Kraken 2 + Standard species mean = 3.77; QIIME 2 + Greengenes genus mean = 5.36) to reproduce the Figure 2E-F accuracy benchmarks. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Compute the Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (nRMSE) between measured and true mock-community read counts for each 16S profiler/reference-library pair, log-transform the values, and aggregate into genus- and species-level means (e.g., Kraken 2 + Standard species mean = 3.77; QIIME 2 + Greengenes genus mean = 5.36) to reproduce the Figure 2E-F accuracy benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a diversity- or detection-based benchmark result (sensitivity/specificity) rather than count-level abundance data needing nRMSE computation Taxonomic abundance tables cannot be mapped to a shared ground truth (no mock community composition available), since nRMSE requires expected vs. measured counts for the union of expected and detected taxa

skills.description: Use when full-length 16S PacBio reads have been assigned to a 99%-identity OTU and the goal is to resolve strain-level intragenomic 16S copy variants via per-position substitution frequencies rather than indels.
skills.name: nucleotide-substitution-profiling
skills.search_text: nucleotide-substitution-profiling Use when full-length 16S PacBio reads have been assigned to a 99%-identity OTU and the goal is to resolve strain-level intragenomic 16S copy variants via per-position substitution frequencies rather than indels. The analysis target is insertion/deletion variation between 16S copies — PacBio CCS deletion errors coincident with homopolymer runs make indel calls unreliable; only substitutions are resolved Reads have not been clustered at the 99% identity OTU threshold, so inter-genomic (between-strain) variation would be confounded with intragenomic copy variation The data are short reads of a single 16S variable region (e.g., V4), which cannot recapture the diversity of the full ~1500 bp gene http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Profiles single-nucleotide substitution frequencies across full-length (~1500 bp) PacBio 16S amplicon reads to detect intragenomic variation between 16S gene copies within a genome, deliberately excluding insertions/deletions because systematic PacBio CCS deletion errors make indel calls unreliable. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Profiles single-nucleotide substitution frequencies across full-length (~1500 bp) PacBio 16S amplicon reads to detect intragenomic variation between 16S gene copies within a genome, deliberately excluding insertions/deletions because systematic PacBio CCS deletion errors make indel calls unreliable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is insertion/deletion variation between 16S copies — PacBio CCS deletion errors coincident with homopolymer runs make indel calls unreliable; only substitutions are resolved Reads have not been clustered at the 99% identity OTU threshold, so inter-genomic (between-strain) variation would be confounded with intragenomic copy variation The data are short reads of a single 16S variable region (e.g., V4), which cannot recapture the diversity of the full ~1500 bp gene

skills.description: Use when single-end FASTQ data needs adapter trimming but no adapter sequence is provided, and you must reproduce or re-implement fastp's seed-and-nucleotide-tree adapter detection (Algorithm 1).
skills.name: nucleotide-tree-adapter-extension
skills.search_text: nucleotide-tree-adapter-extension Use when single-end FASTQ data needs adapter trimming but no adapter sequence is provided, and you must reproduce or re-implement fastp's seed-and-nucleotide-tree adapter detection (Algorithm 1). Adapter sequences are already known and supplied on the command line, so automatic detection adds no value Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead of fastp Detection relies on read frequency statistics, so very small input files (< the sampling depth at which adapter k-mers reach frequency >0.0001) may yield no reliable seeds http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs fastp's automatic adapter-detection algorithm: high-frequency k-mer seeds from the first 1M FASTQ reads are extended forward and backward using nucleotide trees with a >90% dominant-child rule to recover full adapter sequences without user-supplied adapter input. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Reconstructs fastp's automatic adapter-detection algorithm: high-frequency k-mer seeds from the first 1M FASTQ reads are extended forward and backward using nucleotide trees with a >90% dominant-child rule to recover full adapter sequences without user-supplied adapter input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Adapter sequences are already known and supplied on the command line, so automatic detection adds no value Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — use fastplong instead of fastp Detection relies on read frequency statistics, so very small input files (< the sampling depth at which adapter k-mers reach frequency >0.0001) may yield no reliable seeds

skills.description: Use when an observed metric (e.g., NODF nestedness of a presence-absence matrix) must be tested against chance: build null matrices via constrained randomization, then derive z-scores and permutation p-values from many permutations.
skills.name: null-model-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: null-model-permutation-testing Use when an observed metric (e.g., NODF nestedness of a presence-absence matrix) must be tested against chance: build null matrices via constrained randomization, then derive z-scores and permutation p-values from many permutations. The input is already a randomized/null matrix or you only need to recompute a p-value from an existing null distribution The analysis goal is differential abundance or diversity estimation (e.g., alpha/beta diversity, SourceTracker2 source-sinking) rather than testing whether an observed matrix pattern exceeds a null model http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Computes permutation-based null distributions of an ecological statistic (here, NODF nestedness on binary presence-absence matrices of EMP 16S samples) to produce z-scores and p-values that test whether observed community structure exceeds chance. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Computes permutation-based null distributions of an ecological statistic (here, NODF nestedness on binary presence-absence matrices of EMP 16S samples) to produce z-scores and p-values that test whether observed community structure exceeds chance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a randomized/null matrix or you only need to recompute a p-value from an existing null distribution The analysis goal is differential abundance or diversity estimation (e.g., alpha/beta diversity, SourceTracker2 source-sinking) rather than testing whether an observed matrix pattern exceeds a null model

skills.description: Use when processing eDNA metabarcoding FASTQ data (e.g. elasmobranch COI amplicons) through OBITools and need to reproduce per-MOTU richness after removing single-read MOTUs.
skills.name: obitools-command-line-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: obitools-command-line-workflow-execution Use when processing eDNA metabarcoding FASTQ data (e.g. elasmobranch COI amplicons) through OBITools and need to reproduce per-MOTU richness after removing single-read MOTUs. Input is already a denoised, chimera-checked MOTU table — skip the OBITools read-processing steps and go straight to singleton filtering and richness counting Data are 12S or 16S shark metabarcoding data whose expected fragment length is not the 120–135 bp COI window this pipeline's obigrep filter enforces http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute the OBITools metabarcoding command-line pipeline used by Bakke et al. (2017) to go from raw Illumina MiSeq reads to ecotag-assigned MOTUs, then apply the paper's conservative singleton-removal filter (obigrep) before counting elasmobranch MOTU richness per location and region. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Execute the OBITools metabarcoding command-line pipeline used by Bakke et al. (2017) to go from raw Illumina MiSeq reads to ecotag-assigned MOTUs, then apply the paper's conservative singleton-removal filter (obigrep) before counting elasmobranch MOTU richness per location and region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a denoised, chimera-checked MOTU table — skip the OBITools read-processing steps and go straight to singleton filtering and richness counting Data are 12S or 16S shark metabarcoding data whose expected fragment length is not the 120–135 bp COI window this pipeline's obigrep filter enforces

skills.description: Use when MOTU representative sequences (e.g. from sumaclust 99% clustering) need taxonomic assignment against a curated COI reference database to label each MOTU with the most specific consistent taxon.
skills.name: obitools-ecotag-workflow
skills.search_text: obitools-ecotag-workflow Use when MOTU representative sequences (e.g. from sumaclust 99% clustering) need taxonomic assignment against a curated COI reference database to label each MOTU with the most specific consistent taxon. Input is raw reads or aligned reads that have not yet been dereplicated, chimera-filtered (uchime-denovo in vsearch), and clustered into MOTUs at 99% similarity — run the upstream OBITools pipeline first. The reference database does not cover the target group, or the 127 bp COI fragment is expected to be 100% identical among closely related species (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) and unambiguous species-level resolution is required. A longer marker or alternative primers are needed to separate closely related species; the article states this resolution requires new primers amplifying a longer fragment, not ecotag. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Assigns MOTU representative sequences to taxa using the OBITools ecotag algorithm against a bespoke COI reference database (BOLD-derived elasmobranch sequences plus in silico PCR non-elasmobranch sequences), producing a per-MOTU taxonomic assignment table. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assigns MOTU representative sequences to taxa using the OBITools ecotag algorithm against a bespoke COI reference database (BOLD-derived elasmobranch sequences plus in silico PCR non-elasmobranch sequences), producing a per-MOTU taxonomic assignment table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or aligned reads that have not yet been dereplicated, chimera-filtered (uchime-denovo in vsearch), and clustered into MOTUs at 99% similarity — run the upstream OBITools pipeline first. The reference database does not cover the target group, or the 127 bp COI fragment is expected to be 100% identical among closely related species (e.g. Carcharhinus, Rhizoprionodon, Negaprion) and unambiguous species-level resolution is required. A longer marker or alternative primers are needed to separate closely related species; the article states this resolution requires new primers amplifying a longer fragment, not ecotag.

skills.description: Use when you have an OBITools-annotated FASTQ of filtered, aligned eDNA reads (e.g. 120–135 bp COI fragments) and need to collapse identical sequences into representative records with aggregated sample-level abundance counts prior to chimera detection or clustering.
skills.name: obitools-sequence-dereplication
skills.search_text: obitools-sequence-dereplication Use when you have an OBITools-annotated FASTQ of filtered, aligned eDNA reads (e.g. 120–135 bp COI fragments) and need to collapse identical sequences into representative records with aggregated sample-level abundance counts prior to chimera detection or clustering. Input is already a dereplicated representative-sequence file or a MOTU table (e.g. sumaclust output) — re-running obiuniq would not add information. Input reads have not yet been length-filtered or demultiplexed (per the article's pipeline, dereplication follows illuminapairedend alignment, ngsfilter demultiplexing and obigrep 120–135 bp filtering). The goal is chimera removal — that is performed separately with the vsearch uchime-denovo algorithm on the dereplicated file, not by obiuniq. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Dereplicate filtered, demultiplexed eDNA metabarcoding reads (post-illuminapairedend alignment, ngsfilter demultiplexing and obigrep 120–135 bp length filtering) by collapsing identical sequences into single records with the OBITools obiuniq tool, aggregating per-sample read counts into the count annotation before chimera removal and MOTU clustering. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Dereplicate filtered, demultiplexed eDNA metabarcoding reads (post-illuminapairedend alignment, ngsfilter demultiplexing and obigrep 120–135 bp length filtering) by collapsing identical sequences into single records with the OBITools obiuniq tool, aggregating per-sample read counts into the count annotation before chimera removal and MOTU clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a dereplicated representative-sequence file or a MOTU table (e.g. sumaclust output) — re-running obiuniq would not add information. Input reads have not yet been length-filtered or demultiplexed (per the article's pipeline, dereplication follows illuminapairedend alignment, ngsfilter demultiplexing and obigrep 120–135 bp filtering). The goal is chimera removal — that is performed separately with the vsearch uchime-denovo algorithm on the dereplicated file, not by obiuniq.

skills.description: Use when a sample-by-OTU/ASV community matrix has a categorical grouping factor (e.g. plant species identity) plus site covariates (lat/long) and the goal is to visualize and permutation-test whether communities cluster by that factor.
skills.name: ordination-biplot-visualization
skills.search_text: ordination-biplot-visualization Use when a sample-by-OTU/ASV community matrix has a categorical grouping factor (e.g. plant species identity) plus site covariates (lat/long) and the goal is to visualize and permutation-test whether communities cluster by that factor. The community data have no grouping factor or the grouping is confounded with site coordinates such that Condition(lat, lon) would remove the effect of interest The input is raw sequencing reads or a per-sample taxon table without metadata linking samples to plant species and coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 Reproduce constrained ordination (partial RDA via vegan::rda) of flower eDNA arthropod community matrices, testing whether communities separate by plant species while conditioning on latitude/longitude of sampling sites, and render a species-colored site-score biplot. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Reproduce constrained ordination (partial RDA via vegan::rda) of flower eDNA arthropod community matrices, testing whether communities separate by plant species while conditioning on latitude/longitude of sampling sites, and render a species-colored site-score biplot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The community data have no grouping factor or the grouping is confounded with site coordinates such that Condition(lat, lon) would remove the effect of interest The input is raw sequencing reads or a per-sample taxon table without metadata linking samples to plant species and coordinates

skills.description: Use when genus-level ASV abundance tables must be compared across sample groups (e.g., 16S hypervariable regions) by beta diversity: build a Bray–Curtis dissimilarity matrix, ordinate with NMDS, and diagnose the solution's stress and group separation/overlap.
skills.name: ordination-stress-diagnostics
skills.search_text: ordination-stress-diagnostics Use when genus-level ASV abundance tables must be compared across sample groups (e.g., 16S hypervariable regions) by beta diversity: build a Bray–Curtis dissimilarity matrix, ordinate with NMDS, and diagnose the solution's stress and group separation/overlap. Input is raw FASTQ reads or uncollapsed ASV tables — taxonomy must first be assigned with Greengenes and collapsed at the genus level before Bray–Curtis ordination. Input tables come from different hypervariable regions than V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 or from non-16S data where the region-group overlap interpretation does not apply. The goal is alpha-diversity comparison (Kruskal–Wallis test on richness/diversity indices) rather than between-sample compositional dissimilarity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities over genus-level 16S ASV counts (Greengenes-collapsed) to visualize which hypervariable region combinations (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) overlap in ordination space, with stress and permutational fit statistics (R2 = 0.44, pAdonis < 0.001) as diagnostics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Reproduces NMDS ordination of Bray–Curtis dissimilarities over genus-level 16S ASV counts (Greengenes-collapsed) to visualize which hypervariable region combinations (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9) overlap in ordination space, with stress and permutational fit statistics (R2 = 0.44, pAdonis < 0.001) as diagnostics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads or uncollapsed ASV tables — taxonomy must first be assigned with Greengenes and collapsed at the genus level before Bray–Curtis ordination. Input tables come from different hypervariable regions than V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 or from non-16S data where the region-group overlap interpretation does not apply. The goal is alpha-diversity comparison (Kruskal–Wallis test on richness/diversity indices) rather than between-sample compositional dissimilarity.

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered amplicon reads (e.g., temp/filtered.fa) need to be mapped to a reference OTU database at 97% identity to produce a valid tab-delimited OTU count table.
skills.name: otu-abundance-table-construction
skills.search_text: otu-abundance-table-construction Use when quality-filtered amplicon reads (e.g., temp/filtered.fa) need to be mapped to a reference OTU database at 97% identity to produce a valid tab-delimited OTU count table. Input is already a feature/OTU table — this skill maps raw filtered reads to a reference, it does not transform existing count matrices. The goal is de novo OTU clustering rather than reference-based mapping of reads to a pre-built database such as Greengenes 97% OTUs. Sequences are amino acid or require local alignment — VSEARCH does not support amino acid sequences or local alignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Construct a sample-by-OTU abundance table by globally aligning quality-filtered amplicon reads against a reference OTU database (e.g., Greengenes 97% OTUs) with VSEARCH --usearch_global at a 97% identity threshold, then validate the resulting matrix with usearch -otutab_stats. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: Construct a sample-by-OTU abundance table by globally aligning quality-filtered amplicon reads against a reference OTU database (e.g., Greengenes 97% OTUs) with VSEARCH --usearch_global at a 97% identity threshold, then validate the resulting matrix with usearch -otutab_stats.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/OTU table — this skill maps raw filtered reads to a reference, it does not transform existing count matrices. The goal is de novo OTU clustering rather than reference-based mapping of reads to a pre-built database such as Greengenes 97% OTUs. Sequences are amino acid or require local alignment — VSEARCH does not support amino acid sequences or local alignments.

skills.description: Use when OTUs were built by clustering 16S sequences (e.g. HMP V3V5/V1V3 FASTAs at 97% similarity) with a single representative sequence, and you need to measure how representative-sequence annotation propagates (or fails) across OTU members.
skills.name: otu-annotation-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: otu-annotation-consistency-analysis Use when OTUs were built by clustering 16S sequences (e.g. HMP V3V5/V1V3 FASTAs at 97% similarity) with a single representative sequence, and you need to measure how representative-sequence annotation propagates (or fails) across OTU members. Input is already a feature table or BIOM file with pre-assigned taxonomy rather than raw OTU member/representative FASTA sequences The analysis goal is OTU clustering itself (choosing PSD/MSD/BLD thresholds) rather than auditing annotation consistency of existing 97%-similarity OTUs Sequences come from de novo phylogenetic placement methods (e.g. SEPP/pplacer) instead of representative-sequence-based OTU annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies how often member sequences within an HMP-derived OTU receive an RDP Classifier (Greengenes) annotation that differs from the OTU's representative sequence, stratified by 16S region (V3V5, V1V3) and by sequence divergence (average MSD >= 0.03). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Quantifies how often member sequences within an HMP-derived OTU receive an RDP Classifier (Greengenes) annotation that differs from the OTU's representative sequence, stratified by 16S region (V3V5, V1V3) and by sequence divergence (average MSD >= 0.03).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or BIOM file with pre-assigned taxonomy rather than raw OTU member/representative FASTA sequences The analysis goal is OTU clustering itself (choosing PSD/MSD/BLD thresholds) rather than auditing annotation consistency of existing 97%-similarity OTUs Sequences come from de novo phylogenetic placement methods (e.g. SEPP/pplacer) instead of representative-sequence-based OTU annotation

skills.description: Use when the input is an amplicon (16S rDNA) OTU/ASV abundance table from QIIME 2 or BIOM/TSV format and the analysis goal requires importing it into a functional-prediction or amplicon analysis pipeline.
skills.name: otu-asv-table-import
skills.search_text: otu-asv-table-import Use when the input is an amplicon (16S rDNA) OTU/ASV abundance table from QIIME 2 or BIOM/TSV format and the analysis goal requires importing it into a functional-prediction or amplicon analysis pipeline. The data are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than 16S rDNA amplicon-derived OTU/ASV tables — use a metagenomic analysis pipeline instead of amplicon-based import. The table is already loaded in the target tool's native format and sample/feature identifiers are consistent — re-importing adds no information. The goal is only tree/annotation visualization of existing results (e.g., generating iTOL annotations with table2itol), which consumes spreadsheet tables rather than QIIME 2/BIOM feature tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Import an OTU/ASV abundance table (QIIME 2 feature table, BIOM/TSV) together with its representative 16S rDNA sequences so downstream functional prediction (e.g., PICRUSt2 KEGG pathway inference) and other amplicon analyses can operate on it. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Import an OTU/ASV abundance table (QIIME 2 feature table, BIOM/TSV) together with its representative 16S rDNA sequences so downstream functional prediction (e.g., PICRUSt2 KEGG pathway inference) and other amplicon analyses can operate on it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than 16S rDNA amplicon-derived OTU/ASV tables — use a metagenomic analysis pipeline instead of amplicon-based import. The table is already loaded in the target tool's native format and sample/feature identifiers are consistent — re-importing adds no information. The goal is only tree/annotation visualization of existing results (e.g., generating iTOL annotations with table2itol), which consumes spreadsheet tables rather than QIIME 2/BIOM feature tables.

skills.description: Use when input is a length/quality-filtered amplicon FASTA (e.g. temp/filtered.fa) and the goal is to collapse redundant reads into representative OTU_ or ASV_ sequences before building an OTU table.
skills.name: otu-clustering-97-percent-similarity
skills.search_text: otu-clustering-97-percent-similarity Use when input is a length/quality-filtered amplicon FASTA (e.g. temp/filtered.fa) and the goal is to collapse redundant reads into representative OTU_ or ASV_ sequences before building an OTU table. Input is already a representative-sequence file (temp/otus.fa) or an OTU table — downstream steps like chimera_ref filtering or OTU table construction are the appropriate skills instead Sequences have not been dereplicated with a minimum abundance threshold (minuniquesize/minsize 10) — clustering raw filtered reads with singletons inflates spurious OTUs and noise The goal is closed-reference picking against a curated database rather than de novo clustering/denoising from the sample data itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reduces redundancy in filtered amplicon reads and selects representative OTU/ASV sequences by dereplication followed by 97% de novo OTU clustering (usearch -cluster_otus) or ASV denoising (usearch -unoise3), producing the representative-sequence file temp/otus.fa in the EasyAmplicon pipeline. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: Reduces redundancy in filtered amplicon reads and selects representative OTU/ASV sequences by dereplication followed by 97% de novo OTU clustering (usearch -cluster_otus) or ASV denoising (usearch -unoise3), producing the representative-sequence file temp/otus.fa in the EasyAmplicon pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a representative-sequence file (temp/otus.fa) or an OTU table — downstream steps like chimera_ref filtering or OTU table construction are the appropriate skills instead Sequences have not been dereplicated with a minimum abundance threshold (minuniquesize/minsize 10) — clustering raw filtered reads with singletons inflates spurious OTUs and noise The goal is closed-reference picking against a curated database rather than de novo clustering/denoising from the sample data itself

skills.description: Use when demultiplexed, quality-filtered rRNA amplicon or shotgun reads (FASTA) must be classified against a reference taxonomy and hierarchical OTU clusters simultaneously, with confidence values per level, to build OTU count tables or compare OTU consistency across sequencing runs.
skills.name: otu-hierarchical-mapping
skills.search_text: otu-hierarchical-mapping Use when demultiplexed, quality-filtered rRNA amplicon or shotgun reads (FASTA) must be classified against a reference taxonomy and hierarchical OTU clusters simultaneously, with confidence values per level, to build OTU count tables or compare OTU consistency across sequencing runs. Input reads are not demultiplexed and quality filtered — MAPseq expects cleaned FASTA input and is not a demultiplexing or QC tool You need de novo OTU clustering with no suitable full-length rRNA reference set — MAPseq is a reference-based classifier mapping reads to precomputed OTU clusters and known taxonomies You need organism-level (species) OTU identifications where reference coverage is sparse — low reference coverage can drive confidence (and hence assigned labels) down, e.g. the authors dropped the LTP taxonomy due to low coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Assign rRNA sequence reads to a reference taxonomy and to hierarchical operational taxonomic unit (OTU) clusters in a single MAPseq run, with per-level confidence estimates, to obtain taxonomy classifications and OTU mappings suitable for cross-run reproducibility analyses of amplicon datasets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Assign rRNA sequence reads to a reference taxonomy and to hierarchical operational taxonomic unit (OTU) clusters in a single MAPseq run, with per-level confidence estimates, to obtain taxonomy classifications and OTU mappings suitable for cross-run reproducibility analyses of amplicon datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not demultiplexed and quality filtered — MAPseq expects cleaned FASTA input and is not a demultiplexing or QC tool You need de novo OTU clustering with no suitable full-length rRNA reference set — MAPseq is a reference-based classifier mapping reads to precomputed OTU clusters and known taxonomies You need organism-level (species) OTU identifications where reference coverage is sparse — low reference coverage can drive confidence (and hence assigned labels) down, e.g. the authors dropped the LTP taxonomy due to low coverage

skills.description: Use when you need to test how the choice of reference OTU database (e.g. UCLUST-derived ab initio clusters vs. the default hOTU reference) affects MAPseq OTU mapping consistency between runs.
skills.name: otu-reference-construction-with-uclust
skills.search_text: otu-reference-construction-with-uclust Use when you need to test how the choice of reference OTU database (e.g. UCLUST-derived ab initio clusters vs. the default hOTU reference) affects MAPseq OTU mapping consistency between runs. The analysis goal is taxonomy classification only, not hierarchical OTU mapping — MAPseq provides both, but this skill specifically evaluates OTU reference consistency Input is already a count/feature table; this skill operates upstream on raw demultiplexed reads and reference sequence sets You need the maximum between-run consistency rather than an ab initio reference — the default hOTU reference showed higher medians (correlation and Jaccard) than the UCLUST-derived one http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Builds an ab initio reference OTU set from reference rRNA sequences using UCLUST at the paper's OTU identity thresholds, then swaps it into the MAPseq OTU mapping workflow in place of the default pre-clustered hOTU reference to quantify how the reference choice affects between-run consistency of OTU mapping. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Builds an ab initio reference OTU set from reference rRNA sequences using UCLUST at the paper's OTU identity thresholds, then swaps it into the MAPseq OTU mapping workflow in place of the default pre-clustered hOTU reference to quantify how the reference choice affects between-run consistency of OTU mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is taxonomy classification only, not hierarchical OTU mapping — MAPseq provides both, but this skill specifically evaluates OTU reference consistency Input is already a count/feature table; this skill operates upstream on raw demultiplexed reads and reference sequence sets You need the maximum between-run consistency rather than an ab initio reference — the default hOTU reference showed higher medians (correlation and Jaccard) than the UCLUST-derived one

skills.description: Use when OTU member sequences are short amplicon fragments (e.g., HMP V1V3 or V3V5 reads) that must be aligned to a fixed reference alignment before computing MSD between representative and member sequences.
skills.name: otu-sequence-fragment-insertion
skills.search_text: otu-sequence-fragment-insertion Use when OTU member sequences are short amplicon fragments (e.g., HMP V1V3 or V3V5 reads) that must be aligned to a fixed reference alignment before computing MSD between representative and member sequences. Sequences are full-length and a de novo multiple sequence alignment per OTU is feasible/required The analysis goal is percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) from pairwise alignments rather than MSA-based dissimilarity (MSD) No pre-existing reference alignment backbone is available and one has not been generated (e.g., via PASTA) http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Places fragmentary 16S rRNA OTU member sequences (HMP V1V3 and V3V5 amplicon reads) phylogenetically into an existing PASTA-generated 16S reference alignment using SEPP-based UPP 2.0, yielding one reference-aligned FASTA MSA per OTU for downstream MSA-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD) computation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Places fragmentary 16S rRNA OTU member sequences (HMP V1V3 and V3V5 amplicon reads) phylogenetically into an existing PASTA-generated 16S reference alignment using SEPP-based UPP 2.0, yielding one reference-aligned FASTA MSA per OTU for downstream MSA-based sequence dissimilarity (MSD) computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are full-length and a de novo multiple sequence alignment per OTU is feasible/required The analysis goal is percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) from pairwise alignments rather than MSA-based dissimilarity (MSD) No pre-existing reference alignment backbone is available and one has not been generated (e.g., via PASTA)

skills.description: Use when raw OTU count tables from eDNA metabarcoding (with PCR replicate detection data per sample) must be decontaminated before taxonomic grouping and downstream community analysis.
skills.name: otu-site-occupancy-filtering
skills.search_text: otu-site-occupancy-filtering Use when raw OTU count tables from eDNA metabarcoding (with PCR replicate detection data per sample) must be decontaminated before taxonomic grouping and downstream community analysis. Input is already a decontaminated/filtered feature or OTU table with no replicate-level detection information Only single-detection (non-replicated) samples are available, so per-OTU occurrence probability cannot be estimated from replicate detections The goal is taxonomic assignment rather than pre-grouping contamination removal; this filter operates as a quality-control step before taxonomic grouping http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A contamination/negative-removal quality-control step for eDNA amplicon OTU tables in R: per-OTU occurrence probability is estimated from PCR replicate detections under a site-occupancy (binomial) framework, and OTUs with <80% estimated occurrence probability are dropped before taxonomic grouping. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: A contamination/negative-removal quality-control step for eDNA amplicon OTU tables in R: per-OTU occurrence probability is estimated from PCR replicate detections under a site-occupancy (binomial) framework, and OTUs with <80% estimated occurrence probability are dropped before taxonomic grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a decontaminated/filtered feature or OTU table with no replicate-level detection information Only single-detection (non-replicated) samples are available, so per-OTU occurrence probability cannot be estimated from replicate detections The goal is taxonomic assignment rather than pre-grouping contamination removal; this filter operates as a quality-control step before taxonomic grouping

skills.description: Reference for validating OTU tables against ground-truth species inventories when OTUs must be labeled taxonomically (GenBank ITS2) and compared per-site to field survey lists to quantify recaptured, unregistered, redundant, and lost species.
skills.name: otu-species-reference-assignment
skills.search_text: otu-species-reference-assignment Reference for validating OTU tables against ground-truth species inventories when OTUs must be labeled taxonomically (GenBank ITS2) and compared per-site to field survey lists to quantify recaptured, unregistered, redundant, and lost species. The target organism group or locus has poor GenBank ITS2 coverage — assignment quality will be dominated by missing references rather than curation effects There is no independent ground-truth species inventory (e.g. field survey list) to compare OTU-derived inventories against Goal is single rare species identification — the article notes LULU curation 'may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species' http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Assigns OTUs from amplicon tables to species using public reference databases (GenBank ITS2) and classifies each assignment as an imperfect reference match, recaptured species, unregistered species, redundant species, or lost recaptured species relative to field-survey species lists. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Assigns OTUs from amplicon tables to species using public reference databases (GenBank ITS2) and classifies each assignment as an imperfect reference match, recaptured species, unregistered species, redundant species, or lost recaptured species relative to field-survey species lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target organism group or locus has poor GenBank ITS2 coverage — assignment quality will be dominated by missing references rather than curation effects There is no independent ground-truth species inventory (e.g. field survey list) to compare OTU-derived inventories against Goal is single rare species identification — the article notes LULU curation 'may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species'

skills.description: Use when an OTU/ASV table from any clustering method (VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP, DADA2) shows inflated richness or taxonomic redundancy (e.g., many OTUs mapping to single-species genera like Fagus) and needs curation before α-diversity, redundancy, or beta-diversity analyses.
skills.name: otu-table-curation
