skills.search_text: otu-table-curation Use when an OTU/ASV table from any clustering method (VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP, DADA2) shows inflated richness or taxonomic redundancy (e.g., many OTUs mapping to single-species genera like Fagus) and needs curation before α-diversity, redundancy, or beta-diversity analyses. The goal is to detect or retain single rare species: the article states LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species, and the 'cost of curation' is a small loss of real rare, low-abundance species. No representative OTU sequences are available to build a match list, or samples/OTUs are too few for meaningful co-occurrence patterns across a multi-sample data set. The table is already curated (e.g., a previously LULU-curated table), where a second pass would further collapse real diversity without new information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Post-clustering curation of amplicon OTU tables using the LULU algorithm, which identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs via sequence similarity plus co-occurrence patterns and merges them into more abundant 'parent' OTUs to yield more realistic biodiversity metrics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Post-clustering curation of amplicon OTU tables using the LULU algorithm, which identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs via sequence similarity plus co-occurrence patterns and merges them into more abundant 'parent' OTUs to yield more realistic biodiversity metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect or retain single rare species: the article states LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species, and the 'cost of curation' is a small loss of real rare, low-abundance species. No representative OTU sequences are available to build a match list, or samples/OTUs are too few for meaningful co-occurrence patterns across a multi-sample data set. The table is already curated (e.g., a previously LULU-curated table), where a second pass would further collapse real diversity without new information.

skills.description: Use when you have OTU tables for environmental samples ordered along a salinity gradient (e.g., river, lagoon, open sea 16S rRNA data) and need to test habitat differentiation via PERMANOVA and check the decreasing-OTU-with-salinity trend.
skills.name: otu-table-salinity-gradient-trend-analysis
skills.search_text: otu-table-salinity-gradient-trend-analysis Use when you have OTU tables for environmental samples ordered along a salinity gradient (e.g., river, lagoon, open sea 16S rRNA data) and need to test habitat differentiation via PERMANOVA and check the decreasing-OTU-with-salinity trend. The dataset has no environmental gradient metadata (e.g., a mock community study) — PERMANOVA habitat differentiation and OTU-vs-salinity trends are meaningless without habitat/salinity labels. You need OTU clustering via VSEARCH for the 12S rRNA marker gene — PEMA's table (and thus this downstream workflow as configured) does not support that combination. The input is a single-pipeline feature table with no cross-pipeline comparison intended — the PERMANOVA comparison step specifically requires PEMA, LotuS, and DADA2 outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Downstream ecological analysis of metabarcoding OTU tables (from PEMA, LotuS, DADA2, mothur, QIIME 2) along a river–lagoon–open sea salinity gradient, using the phyloseq and vegan R packages to compute community compositions, run PERMANOVA for habitat differentiation, and tabulate per-sample OTU numbers against salinity. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Downstream ecological analysis of metabarcoding OTU tables (from PEMA, LotuS, DADA2, mothur, QIIME 2) along a river–lagoon–open sea salinity gradient, using the phyloseq and vegan R packages to compute community compositions, run PERMANOVA for habitat differentiation, and tabulate per-sample OTU numbers against salinity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no environmental gradient metadata (e.g., a mock community study) — PERMANOVA habitat differentiation and OTU-vs-salinity trends are meaningless without habitat/salinity labels. You need OTU clustering via VSEARCH for the 12S rRNA marker gene — PEMA's table (and thus this downstream workflow as configured) does not support that combination. The input is a single-pipeline feature table with no cross-pipeline comparison intended — the PERMANOVA comparison step specifically requires PEMA, LotuS, and DADA2 outputs.

skills.description: Use when you have an initial OTU table (e.g., from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2) and want to remove single-read OTUs as a baseline noise-removal step, or to benchmark it against co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation such as LULU.
skills.name: otu-table-singleton-filtering
skills.search_text: otu-table-singleton-filtering Use when you have an initial OTU table (e.g., from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2) and want to remove single-read OTUs as a baseline noise-removal step, or to benchmark it against co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation such as LULU. When the goal is reliable α-diversity: the article shows singleton removal retains far less improvement (mean R2 gain 0.03) than LULU curation (0.27), and discarding the low-abundance tail drops rare but real OTUs. When the input is already a curated OTU table (e.g., LULU-curated) — additional singleton removal is redundant since curation merges errors while preserving total read counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Filters singleton OTUs (total read count of one) from an OTU table as a traditional noise-removal strategy, then evaluates whether the resulting richness better corresponds with independent ground-truth (e.g., plant survey richness). In the Frøslev et al. validation, singleton removal yielded only marginal gains (mean R2 improvement 0.03) versus LULU post-clustering curation (0.27). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Filters singleton OTUs (total read count of one) from an OTU table as a traditional noise-removal strategy, then evaluates whether the resulting richness better corresponds with independent ground-truth (e.g., plant survey richness). In the Frøslev et al. validation, singleton removal yielded only marginal gains (mean R2 improvement 0.03) versus LULU post-clustering curation (0.27).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is reliable α-diversity: the article shows singleton removal retains far less improvement (mean R2 gain 0.03) than LULU curation (0.27), and discarding the low-abundance tail drops rare but real OTUs. When the input is already a curated OTU table (e.g., LULU-curated) — additional singleton removal is redundant since curation merges errors while preserving total read counts.

skills.description: Use when 16S amplicon reads (e.g. V3-V4 FASTQ from MiSeq, already adapter- and quality-trimmed) must be clustered into OTUs and classified taxonomically against SILVA SSU ref release 132 to build an abundance table for downstream diversity or differential-abundance tests.
skills.name: otu-taxonomic-classification-mapping
skills.search_text: otu-taxonomic-classification-mapping Use when 16S amplicon reads (e.g. V3-V4 FASTQ from MiSeq, already adapter- and quality-trimmed) must be clustered into OTUs and classified taxonomically against SILVA SSU ref release 132 to build an abundance table for downstream diversity or differential-abundance tests. Input is ITS/eukaryotic amplicon data — the paper classifies ITS consensus sequences with the 'Classify Sequences' tool using the Warcup V2 training data set (90% similarity, minimum overlap 75 bp), not the SILVAngs/BLASTn 16S route. Input is already a classified OTU/feature table — only the downstream relative-abundance and statistical testing steps apply. Raw unprocessed reads that still contain 3'-end adapters and low-quality tails — run Scythe before quality-based trimming first, since quality trimming could remove bases helpful for identifying adapter contaminants. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Cluster quality-trimmed 16S rRNA amplicon reads into OTUs and assign taxonomy by aligning each read against the SILVA SSU reference database, as done in the trout-farm metabarcoding study via the SILVAngs pipeline (SINA alignment, cd-hit-est clustering, local BLASTn classification). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Cluster quality-trimmed 16S rRNA amplicon reads into OTUs and assign taxonomy by aligning each read against the SILVA SSU reference database, as done in the trout-farm metabarcoding study via the SILVAngs pipeline (SINA alignment, cd-hit-est clustering, local BLASTn classification).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is ITS/eukaryotic amplicon data — the paper classifies ITS consensus sequences with the 'Classify Sequences' tool using the Warcup V2 training data set (90% similarity, minimum overlap 75 bp), not the SILVAngs/BLASTn 16S route. Input is already a classified OTU/feature table — only the downstream relative-abundance and statistical testing steps apply. Raw unprocessed reads that still contain 3'-end adapters and low-quality tails — run Scythe before quality-based trimming first, since quality trimming could remove bases helpful for identifying adapter contaminants.

skills.description: Use when you have PacBio CCS reads of full-length (~1500 bp) 16S amplicons plus reference 16S sequences, and you need per-read error or per-position substitution profiles (e.g., CCS pass-number error curves, homopolymer-deletion mapping, or 16S SNP detection).
skills.name: pacbio-ccs-read-alignment
skills.search_text: pacbio-ccs-read-alignment Use when you have PacBio CCS reads of full-length (~1500 bp) 16S amplicons plus reference 16S sequences, and you need per-read error or per-position substitution profiles (e.g., CCS pass-number error curves, homopolymer-deletion mapping, or 16S SNP detection). The input is short-read sequence data from a 16S variable region (e.g., V4) rather than full-length PacBio CCS reads — the paper shows variable regions cannot match full-gene taxonomic accuracy The goal is to resolve insertions/deletions between intragenomic 16S copies — PacBio CCS indel errors are systematic, so the paper's SNP-calling approach ignores indels entirely An isolate has fewer than 200 aligned reads to its most-abundant sequence — the paper's coverage filter excludes such isolates from SNP calling http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Align PacBio CCS full-length 16S amplicon reads to reference 16S gene sequences (mock community references or the most-abundant per-isolate sequence) with Cross_match using the paper's parameters (minscore 750, penalty -9, masklevel 0), then parse the alignments to quantify substitutions, insertions, and deletions for error profiling or intragenomic SNP calling. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Align PacBio CCS full-length 16S amplicon reads to reference 16S gene sequences (mock community references or the most-abundant per-isolate sequence) with Cross_match using the paper's parameters (minscore 750, penalty -9, masklevel 0), then parse the alignments to quantify substitutions, insertions, and deletions for error profiling or intragenomic SNP calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read sequence data from a 16S variable region (e.g., V4) rather than full-length PacBio CCS reads — the paper shows variable regions cannot match full-gene taxonomic accuracy The goal is to resolve insertions/deletions between intragenomic 16S copies — PacBio CCS indel errors are systematic, so the paper's SNP-calling approach ignores indels entirely An isolate has fewer than 200 aligned reads to its most-abundant sequence — the paper's coverage filter excludes such isolates from SNP calling

skills.description: Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon subreads whose number of passes (np) must match a real sequencing run's distribution, since PBSIM3 supports only one pass number per invocation.
skills.name: pacbio-hifi-pass-number-sampling
skills.search_text: pacbio-hifi-pass-number-sampling Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon subreads whose number of passes (np) must match a real sequencing run's distribution, since PBSIM3 supports only one pass number per invocation. The simulation target is not PacBio HiFi amplicon data (e.g., ONT reads or short-read data), where PBSIM3 pass-number modeling is irrelevant. A single fixed pass number is acceptable for all simulated reads, in which case a plain PBSIM3 run suffices without distribution sampling. No empirical HiFi data or fitted lognormal parameters are available to define the number-of-passes distribution (an np source must exist). http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Samples per-read polymerase pass numbers from empirical distributions extracted from real PacBio HiFi runs (e.g., the ATCC 16S Sequel II System 2.0 dataset) or from fitted lognormal distributions, and invokes PBSIM3 separately for each distinct pass number in parallel so simulated subreads/CCS reads carry realistic np values despite PBSIM3's single-pass-per-run limitation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Samples per-read polymerase pass numbers from empirical distributions extracted from real PacBio HiFi runs (e.g., the ATCC 16S Sequel II System 2.0 dataset) or from fitted lognormal distributions, and invokes PBSIM3 separately for each distinct pass number in parallel so simulated subreads/CCS reads carry realistic np values despite PBSIM3's single-pass-per-run limitation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The simulation target is not PacBio HiFi amplicon data (e.g., ONT reads or short-read data), where PBSIM3 pass-number modeling is irrelevant. A single fixed pass number is acceptable for all simulated reads, in which case a plain PBSIM3 run suffices without distribution sampling. No empirical HiFi data or fitted lognormal parameters are available to define the number-of-passes distribution (an np source must exist).

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ files (e.g. Illumina MiSeq V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 libraries) must be quality-filtered, denoised into ASVs, and de-chimerized before genus-level taxonomic assignment.
skills.name: paired-end-amplicon-read-preprocessing
skills.search_text: paired-end-amplicon-read-preprocessing Use when raw paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ files (e.g. Illumina MiSeq V1–V2/V3–V4/V5–V7/V7–V9 libraries) must be quality-filtered, denoised into ASVs, and de-chimerized before genus-level taxonomic assignment. Input is already a denoised ASV feature table or BIOM file — re-running Deblur would be redundant Reads are full-length 16S rRNA sequences from third-generation/Nanopore platforms, since Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments and this workflow was tuned for 2 x 300 bp MiSeq data The goal is to maximize the number of recovered real variants — the article's discussion notes DADA2 identified more real variants and output sequences than other methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A quality-control and denoising workflow for paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (2 x 300 bp MiSeq) that uses FastQC for Q30-based quality assessment, the Deblur pipeline to infer amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from short fragments, and QIIME 2's non-chimeric 16S database for chimera removal, yielding a denoised ASV feature table for genus-level taxonomy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: A quality-control and denoising workflow for paired-end 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (2 x 300 bp MiSeq) that uses FastQC for Q30-based quality assessment, the Deblur pipeline to infer amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from short fragments, and QIIME 2's non-chimeric 16S database for chimera removal, yielding a denoised ASV feature table for genus-level taxonomy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a denoised ASV feature table or BIOM file — re-running Deblur would be redundant Reads are full-length 16S rRNA sequences from third-generation/Nanopore platforms, since Deblur is recommended for shorter bp fragments and this workflow was tuned for 2 x 300 bp MiSeq data The goal is to maximize the number of recovered real variants — the article's discussion notes DADA2 identified more real variants and output sequences than other methods

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end, demultiplexed 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ files (e.g. V4 region Sample_1.fastq/Sample_2.fastq) must be turned into OTU or ASV community profiles with taxonomic assignments and plots.
skills.name: paired-end-amplicon-read-workflow-scripting
skills.search_text: paired-end-amplicon-read-workflow-scripting Use when raw paired-end, demultiplexed 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ files (e.g. V4 region Sample_1.fastq/Sample_2.fastq) must be turned into OTU or ASV community profiles with taxonomic assignments and plots. Input is shotgun metagenomic data — use the review's metagenomics workflow (metagenomics_analysis.sh) with assemblers and binning instead of OTU/ASV clustering. Input is already an OTU/ASV abundance table — this skill processes raw reads, not feature tables. Reads are single-end or not demultiplexed — the workflow requires paired-end, demultiplexed reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A best-practice 16S rRNA amplicon analysis skill that quality-filters raw paired-end reads and branches them into an OTU-based path (mothur, 97% identity threshold) or an ASV-based path (DADA2 denoising), followed by taxonomy profiling and phyloseq/ggplot2 visualization. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: A best-practice 16S rRNA amplicon analysis skill that quality-filters raw paired-end reads and branches them into an OTU-based path (mothur, 97% identity threshold) or an ASV-based path (DADA2 denoising), followed by taxonomy profiling and phyloseq/ggplot2 visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is shotgun metagenomic data — use the review's metagenomics workflow (metagenomics_analysis.sh) with assemblers and binning instead of OTU/ASV clustering. Input is already an OTU/ASV abundance table — this skill processes raw reads, not feature tables. Reads are single-end or not demultiplexed — the workflow requires paired-end, demultiplexed reads.

skills.description: Use when you need to estimate or reproduce the duplication rate of paired-end FASTQ data (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) and want the memory-efficient key/array method fastp uses rather than a hash-table approach.
skills.name: paired-end-duplication-rate-evaluation
skills.search_text: paired-end-duplication-rate-evaluation Use when you need to estimate or reproduce the duplication rate of paired-end FASTQ data (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) and want the memory-efficient key/array method fastp uses rather than a hash-table approach. Data is long reads from Nanopore/PacBio/Cyclone — the README directs such data to fastplong, not fastp Only single-end FASTQ data is available — the key1/key2 scheme requires paired read1/read2 files You need exact duplicate detection of full sequences rather than the sampled 12 bp/32 bp key approximation http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, which computes key1 from the first 12 bp of read1 and key2 from the first 32 bp of read2 (a 64-bit packed integer) and uses flagging/counting arrays instead of FASTQC-style hash tables to estimate the PE duplication rate. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Reconstructs fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, which computes key1 from the first 12 bp of read1 and key2 from the first 32 bp of read2 (a 64-bit packed integer) and uses flagging/counting arrays instead of FASTQC-style hash tables to estimate the PE duplication rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is long reads from Nanopore/PacBio/Cyclone — the README directs such data to fastplong, not fastp Only single-end FASTQ data is available — the key1/key2 scheme requires paired read1/read2 files You need exact duplicate detection of full sequences rather than the sampled 12 bp/32 bp key approximation

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ (e.g. NextSeq PE150, NovaSeq) needs quality control, adapter removal, and filtering before downstream analysis, and speed or a single-pass all-in-one tool matters.
skills.name: paired-end-fastq-quality-control
skills.search_text: paired-end-fastq-quality-control Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ (e.g. NextSeq PE150, NovaSeq) needs quality control, adapter removal, and filtering before downstream analysis, and speed or a single-pass all-in-one tool matters. Input is long-read data from Nanopore, PacBio, or Cyclone devices — use fastplong instead, as fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina, MGI) The task requires comparing residual adapter content across tools with a custom mismatch-tolerance sweep (e.g. scanning 33 bp adapter sequences with 0-5 allowed mismatches), which needs an external Python scanning step beyond fastp's reports http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 All-in-one FASTQ quality control and preprocessing for paired-end (and single-end) Illumina short reads using fastp, which performs quality profiling, adapter trimming, quality filtering, per-read sliding-window cutting, and optional polyG/polyX trimming in a single scan of the data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: All-in-one FASTQ quality control and preprocessing for paired-end (and single-end) Illumina short reads using fastp, which performs quality profiling, adapter trimming, quality filtering, per-read sliding-window cutting, and optional polyG/polyX trimming in a single scan of the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data from Nanopore, PacBio, or Cyclone devices — use fastplong instead, as fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina, MGI) The task requires comparing residual adapter content across tools with a custom mismatch-tolerance sweep (e.g. scanning 33 bp adapter sequences with 0-5 allowed mismatches), which needs an external Python scanning step beyond fastp's reports

skills.description: Use when assessing duplication levels of high-depth (e.g. ~10000x cfDNA) paired-end Illumina FASTQ data, or when deciding whether a tool's duplication metric accounts for read1/read2 pairing.
skills.name: paired-end-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: paired-end-overlap-analysis Use when assessing duplication levels of high-depth (e.g. ~10000x cfDNA) paired-end Illumina FASTQ data, or when deciding whether a tool's duplication metric accounts for read1/read2 pairing. Input is true single-end data — the pairing-aware analysis and the PE-vs-SE contrast have no meaning Low-depth sequencing data where duplication rates are negligible and the PE overestimation effect is immaterial Long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) data — fastp is designed for short reads; fastplong is the recommended tool instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A benchmarking skill for evaluating duplication rates in high-depth paired-end FASTQ data, contrasting FASTQC's per-mate (single-end) duplication estimates with fastp's paired-end-aware duplication evaluation to expose PE overestimation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for evaluating duplication rates in high-depth paired-end FASTQ data, contrasting FASTQC's per-mate (single-end) duplication estimates with fastp's paired-end-aware duplication evaluation to expose PE overestimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is true single-end data — the pairing-aware analysis and the PE-vs-SE contrast have no meaning Low-depth sequencing data where duplication rates are negligible and the PE overestimation effect is immaterial Long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) data — fastp is designed for short reads; fastplong is the recommended tool instead

skills.description: Use when starting from per-sample paired-end gzipped FASTQ amplicon reads (e.g. Sample1_1.fq.gz/Sample1_2.fq.gz) and you need merged, primer-trimmed, quality-filtered amplicons before dereplication and OTU/ASV inference.
skills.name: paired-end-read-merging
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-merging Use when starting from per-sample paired-end gzipped FASTQ amplicon reads (e.g. Sample1_1.fq.gz/Sample1_2.fq.gz) and you need merged, primer-trimmed, quality-filtered amplicons before dereplication and OTU/ASV inference. Input is already a merged, dereplicated FASTA/feature table — merging and primer stripping have already been performed Long-read PacBio/Nanopore amplicon data (EasyAmplicon 2 handles these with a different sub-pipeline) Reads whose primer/amplicon lengths differ from the 29 bp/18 bp trim used here — trim lengths must be adjusted to the actual primer set http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Merges Illumina paired-end amplicon reads (e.g. seq/Sample1_1.fq.gz + seq/Sample1_2.fq.gz) into single sequences with VSEARCH's --fastq_mergepairs in EasyAmplicon, then strips primers (29 bp left / 18 bp right) and quality-filters by expected error to produce clean amplicon FASTA (temp/filtered.fa). metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: Merges Illumina paired-end amplicon reads (e.g. seq/Sample1_1.fq.gz + seq/Sample1_2.fq.gz) into single sequences with VSEARCH's --fastq_mergepairs in EasyAmplicon, then strips primers (29 bp left / 18 bp right) and quality-filters by expected error to produce clean amplicon FASTA (temp/filtered.fa).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a merged, dereplicated FASTA/feature table — merging and primer stripping have already been performed Long-read PacBio/Nanopore amplicon data (EasyAmplicon 2 handles these with a different sub-pipeline) Reads whose primer/amplicon lengths differ from the 29 bp/18 bp trim used here — trim lengths must be adjusted to the actual primer set

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads have been demultiplexed into per-sample files and must be merged and quality-filtered before OTU clustering or ASV denoising.
skills.name: paired-end-read-merging
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-merging Use when raw paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads have been demultiplexed into per-sample files and must be merged and quality-filtered before OTU clustering or ASV denoising. Input reads are single-end, so there is no overlap to merge Data are shotgun metagenomic rather than amplicon reads; metagenomic analysis follows the paper's separate metagenomic pipeline Input is already a merged sequence set or an existing OTU/ASV feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Merge quality-filtered paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads into single consensus sequences as a prerequisite step for OTU/ASV inference in the amplicon analysis pipeline recommended by Liu et al. 2020. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Merge quality-filtered paired-end amplicon FASTQ reads into single consensus sequences as a prerequisite step for OTU/ASV inference in the amplicon analysis pipeline recommended by Liu et al. 2020.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are single-end, so there is no overlap to merge Data are shotgun metagenomic rather than amplicon reads; metagenomic analysis follows the paper's separate metagenomic pipeline Input is already a merged sequence set or an existing OTU/ASV feature table

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end amplicon FASTQs (e.g., dual-indexed 181 bp COI reads from SRA PRJNA518082 Libraries A-D) still carry primer sequences and must be trimmed before denoising or OTU clustering.
skills.name: paired-end-read-primer-trimming
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-primer-trimming Use when raw paired-end amplicon FASTQs (e.g., dual-indexed 181 bp COI reads from SRA PRJNA518082 Libraries A-D) still carry primer sequences and must be trimmed before denoising or OTU clustering. Input reads have already been primer-trimmed during demultiplexing or a prior preprocessing run — re-trimming risks removing biological bases from the 181 bp COI fragment Data are shotgun metagenomic or otherwise non-amplicon reads with no expected primer motifs at read ends A feature table or denoised ASV artifact is already available — trimming applies only to raw read data upstream of DADA2/Deblur/VSEARCH http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Removes primer sequences from raw demultiplexed paired-end amplicon reads (e.g., dual-indexed 181 bp COI fragments) with Cutadapt inside a QIIME 2 workflow, so that downstream denoising (DADA2, Deblur) or VSEARCH clustering operates only on biological sequence. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Removes primer sequences from raw demultiplexed paired-end amplicon reads (e.g., dual-indexed 181 bp COI fragments) with Cutadapt inside a QIIME 2 workflow, so that downstream denoising (DADA2, Deblur) or VSEARCH clustering operates only on biological sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have already been primer-trimmed during demultiplexing or a prior preprocessing run — re-trimming risks removing biological bases from the 181 bp COI fragment Data are shotgun metagenomic or otherwise non-amplicon reads with no expected primer motifs at read ends A feature table or denoised ASV artifact is already available — trimming applies only to raw read data upstream of DADA2/Deblur/VSEARCH

skills.description: Use when you have paired-end FASTQ files (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) that must be mapped to a reference genome (hg19) and compared on alignment quality metrics across preprocessing variants.
skills.name: paired-end-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: paired-end-short-read-alignment Use when you have paired-end FASTQ files (e.g. in.R1.fq.gz/in.R2.fq.gz) that must be mapped to a reference genome (hg19) and compared on alignment quality metrics across preprocessing variants. Input reads are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) rather than short Illumina/MGI-style paired-end reads — use a long-read preprocessing and alignment workflow instead. You need only FASTQ quality control/preprocessing (QC curves, Q20/Q30, adapter content) and not genome mapping — a preprocessor like fastp alone suffices. Only a single-end dataset with no preprocessing-tool comparison is involved and no mismatch/clip/single-read-map metrics are required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Align gzip-compressed paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. NS_PE150 data, preprocessed by tools such as fastp) to a reference genome like hg19 using BWA-MEM, then evaluate alignment quality with Samtools to compare preprocessing tools by mismatched bases, clipped reads, and single-read maps. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Align gzip-compressed paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. NS_PE150 data, preprocessed by tools such as fastp) to a reference genome like hg19 using BWA-MEM, then evaluate alignment quality with Samtools to compare preprocessing tools by mismatched bases, clipped reads, and single-read maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) rather than short Illumina/MGI-style paired-end reads — use a long-read preprocessing and alignment workflow instead. You need only FASTQ quality control/preprocessing (QC curves, Q20/Q30, adapter content) and not genome mapping — a preprocessor like fastp alone suffices. Only a single-end dataset with no preprocessing-tool comparison is involved and no mismatch/clip/single-read-map metrics are required.

skills.description: Use when comparing classification error rates of two weighting schemes (e.g., uniform vs bespoke taxonomic weights) evaluated on the same test sequence variants and you need a paired significance test per taxon plus a per-phylum error-rate table.
skills.name: paired-t-test-error-comparison
skills.search_text: paired-t-test-error-comparison Use when comparing classification error rates of two weighting schemes (e.g., uniform vs bespoke taxonomic weights) evaluated on the same test sequence variants and you need a paired significance test per taxon plus a per-phylum error-rate table. When the two weighting schemes were evaluated on different test sequence variants or different habitats — the pairing that the t-test assumes would be broken When sample weights cannot be assembled for the habitat of interest (natural sample types lacking sufficient characterization for bespoke weight assembly); average weights or another comparison is more appropriate When the question is genus- or phylum-level error rather than species-level, since the reported improvements are specific to species-level classification http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistical comparison of species-level classification error rates between uniform and bespoke (habitat-specific) taxonomic weights, using paired t-tests averaged across the 14 EMPO 3 habitats, as done for the Proteobacteria/Firmicutes results in Supplementary Fig. 5 of the q2-clawback paper. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: Statistical comparison of species-level classification error rates between uniform and bespoke (habitat-specific) taxonomic weights, using paired t-tests averaged across the 14 EMPO 3 habitats, as done for the Proteobacteria/Firmicutes results in Supplementary Fig. 5 of the q2-clawback paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two weighting schemes were evaluated on different test sequence variants or different habitats — the pairing that the t-test assumes would be broken When sample weights cannot be assembled for the habitat of interest (natural sample types lacking sufficient characterization for bespoke weight assembly); average weights or another comparison is more appropriate When the question is genus- or phylum-level error rather than species-level, since the reported improvements are specific to species-level classification

skills.description: Use when two classification conditions (e.g., species-level with bespoke weights vs. genus-level with uniform weights) have been evaluated on the same matched test samples and you must test whether per-sample error rates or Bray-Curtis dissimilarities differ significantly.
skills.name: paired-t-test-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: paired-t-test-statistical-testing Use when two classification conditions (e.g., species-level with bespoke weights vs. genus-level with uniform weights) have been evaluated on the same matched test samples and you must test whether per-sample error rates or Bray-Curtis dissimilarities differ significantly. The two error-rate vectors come from different, unmatched test samples — pairing is required for ttest_rel; use an unpaired test instead Comparing more than two classification conditions or weights (e.g., multiple cross-habitat weight sets) — a single paired t-test handles only one bespoke vs. uniform contrast at a time The input is already aggregated (e.g., a single mean error rate per condition) — the test requires the per-sample values http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A single-sided paired t-test that compares per-sample classification error rates (and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities) from bespoke species-level taxonomic weighting against uniform genus-level classification in q2-feature-classifier, testing whether bespoke weights significantly improve species-level accuracy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: A single-sided paired t-test that compares per-sample classification error rates (and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities) from bespoke species-level taxonomic weighting against uniform genus-level classification in q2-feature-classifier, testing whether bespoke weights significantly improve species-level accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two error-rate vectors come from different, unmatched test samples — pairing is required for ttest_rel; use an unpaired test instead Comparing more than two classification conditions or weights (e.g., multiple cross-habitat weight sets) — a single paired t-test handles only one bespoke vs. uniform contrast at a time The input is already aggregated (e.g., a single mean error rate per condition) — the test requires the per-sample values

skills.description: Use when a rarefied OTU/feature table and sample metadata are available and you need an ordination plot plus statistical p-values for every pairwise group comparison of community composition differences.
skills.name: pairwise-group-significance-testing-of-beta-diversity
skills.search_text: pairwise-group-significance-testing-of-beta-diversity Use when a rarefied OTU/feature table and sample metadata are available and you need an ordination plot plus statistical p-values for every pairwise group comparison of community composition differences. The input is raw reads or an unrarefied table — depth must be standardized by rarefaction before beta diversity distances are comparable The metadata lacks a defined grouping column (e.g., Group), so no pairwise between-group comparison can be defined The goal is taxonomy or functional profiling (STAMP, PICRUSt2) rather than community-composition ordination and significance testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 In the EasyAmplicon pipeline, beta diversity distance matrices (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, UniFrac) computed with USEARCH -beta_div are ordinated by PCoA via the beta_pcoa.R script, and the analysis additionally reports pairwise between-group comparison p-values written to beta_pcoa_stat.txt. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: In the EasyAmplicon pipeline, beta diversity distance matrices (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, UniFrac) computed with USEARCH -beta_div are ordinated by PCoA via the beta_pcoa.R script, and the analysis additionally reports pairwise between-group comparison p-values written to beta_pcoa_stat.txt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw reads or an unrarefied table — depth must be standardized by rarefaction before beta diversity distances are comparable The metadata lacks a defined grouping column (e.g., Group), so no pairwise between-group comparison can be defined The goal is taxonomy or functional profiling (STAMP, PICRUSt2) rather than community-composition ordination and significance testing

skills.description: Use when a pangenome or gene-catalog FASTA of coding sequences (e.g. an SGB pangenome .ffn) needs UniRef90/UniRef50 functional annotations before core-gene screening or marker extraction.
skills.name: pangenome-annotation-uniref
skills.search_text: pangenome-annotation-uniref Use when a pangenome or gene-catalog FASTA of coding sequences (e.g. an SGB pangenome .ffn) needs UniRef90/UniRef50 functional annotations before core-gene screening or marker extraction. Input is raw contigs or reads rather than called coding sequences — the cds seqtype assumes a gene-catalog FASTA of CDSs, not unannotated genomic DNA Your DIAMOND databases are the v1.1 files formatted for DIAMOND v0.8 but you run DIAMOND v0.9+ — the README notes these are incompatible The goal is taxonomic profiling of metagenomes itself (use MetaPhlAn 4) rather than functional annotation of a gene catalog http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Annotates SGB pangenome coding-sequence catalogs against UniRef90/UniRef50 (and, per the MetaPhlAn 4 workflow, Uniclust90) using the biobakery uniref_annotator DIAMOND search, appending UniRef accessions to each FASTA header. This annotation step is a prerequisite for building SGB pangenomes and screening species-unique marker genes in the MetaPhlAn 4 database pipeline. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Annotates SGB pangenome coding-sequence catalogs against UniRef90/UniRef50 (and, per the MetaPhlAn 4 workflow, Uniclust90) using the biobakery uniref_annotator DIAMOND search, appending UniRef accessions to each FASTA header. This annotation step is a prerequisite for building SGB pangenomes and screening species-unique marker genes in the MetaPhlAn 4 database pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw contigs or reads rather than called coding sequences — the cds seqtype assumes a gene-catalog FASTA of CDSs, not unannotated genomic DNA Your DIAMOND databases are the v1.1 files formatted for DIAMOND v0.8 but you run DIAMOND v0.9+ — the README notes these are incompatible The goal is taxonomic profiling of metagenomes itself (use MetaPhlAn 4) rather than functional annotation of a gene catalog

skills.description: Use when clustering very large dereplicated amplicon FASTA files (hundreds of millions of unique sequences) with swarm v3 on a multicore host, to parallelize execution via --threads and benchmark wall-clock runtime.
skills.name: parallel-clustering-execution-multithreading
skills.search_text: parallel-clustering-execution-multithreading Use when clustering very large dereplicated amplicon FASTA files (hundreds of millions of unique sequences) with swarm v3 on a multicore host, to parallelize execution via --threads and benchmark wall-clock runtime. The input FASTA is not dereplicated or sequence headers lack occurrence counts (e.g., _1000) — swarm requires each fasta entry to present a number of occurrences to work properly. You need global-similarity-threshold OTU picking (e.g., 97%) — swarm relies on a small local linking threshold d (default d = 1), not a global clustering threshold. Memory-constrained host combined with --fastidious — the fastidious option can increase memory footprint significantly; without -c/-y caps the run may exhaust RAM. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Executes swarm v3 amplicon clustering in multithreaded mode (--threads) on dereplicated, abundance-annotated FASTA input, so that tera-scale datasets such as the UniEuk SSU-rRNA V4 set (~324 million unique sequences) cluster with default parameters (d = 1) in roughly 50 minutes on a 16-core system. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: Executes swarm v3 amplicon clustering in multithreaded mode (--threads) on dereplicated, abundance-annotated FASTA input, so that tera-scale datasets such as the UniEuk SSU-rRNA V4 set (~324 million unique sequences) cluster with default parameters (d = 1) in roughly 50 minutes on a 16-core system.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input FASTA is not dereplicated or sequence headers lack occurrence counts (e.g., _1000) — swarm requires each fasta entry to present a number of occurrences to work properly. You need global-similarity-threshold OTU picking (e.g., 97%) — swarm relies on a small local linking threshold d (default d = 1), not a global clustering threshold. Memory-constrained host combined with --fastidious — the fastidious option can increase memory footprint significantly; without -c/-y caps the run may exhaust RAM.

skills.description: Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon reads whose number-of-passes distribution must vary per read, but the underlying simulator (PBSIM3) accepts only a single np per invocation.
skills.name: parallel-simulation-orchestration
skills.search_text: parallel-simulation-orchestration Use when simulating PacBio HiFi amplicon reads whose number-of-passes distribution must vary per read, but the underlying simulator (PBSIM3) accepts only a single np per invocation. Simulating Illumina or other non-PacBio short-read data — MHASS/PBSIM3 model PacBio HiFi circular-consensus subreads and their error profiles A single fixed pass number is acceptable for all reads — then PBSIM3 can be invoked once directly without the sampling/grouping orchestration No empirical or fitted num-passes distribution is available and the defaults (lognormal mu=3.88, sigma=1.22) are inappropriate for the instrument/run being simulated http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 MHASS technique for driving PBSIM3, which supports only a single pass number per run, by sampling each simulated read's number of passes (np) from an empirical or fitted lognormal distribution and invoking PBSIM3 once per distinct np value, parallelized across CPU cores. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: MHASS technique for driving PBSIM3, which supports only a single pass number per run, by sampling each simulated read's number of passes (np) from an empirical or fitted lognormal distribution and invoking PBSIM3 once per distinct np value, parallelized across CPU cores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Simulating Illumina or other non-PacBio short-read data — MHASS/PBSIM3 model PacBio HiFi circular-consensus subreads and their error profiles A single fixed pass number is acceptable for all reads — then PBSIM3 can be invoked once directly without the sampling/grouping orchestration No empirical or fitted num-passes distribution is available and the defaults (lognormal mu=3.88, sigma=1.22) are inappropriate for the instrument/run being simulated

skills.description: Use when building controlled synthetic microbiome abundance tables to benchmark or validate alpha diversity metrics, especially when singleton/doubleton treatment (DADA2 vs DEBLUR divergence) must be explicitly controlled.
skills.name: parametric-count-distribution-sampling
skills.search_text: parametric-count-distribution-sampling Use when building controlled synthetic microbiome abundance tables to benchmark or validate alpha diversity metrics, especially when singleton/doubleton treatment (DADA2 vs DEBLUR divergence) must be explicitly controlled. Input is already a real amplicon feature table (e.g. QIIME2 BIOM/TSV from DADA2 or DEBLUR) — this skill only creates synthetic tables for metric validation, not real-data processing The analysis requires ACE or Faith on the synthetic data — these could not be recalculated on synthetic datasets due to technical limitations The goal is to compare denoiser outputs (DADA2 vs DEBLUR) on real sequencing runs rather than to probe metric sensitivity to controlled singleton/doubleton structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate synthetic sample-by-ASV count matrices by sampling ASV abundances from parametric distributions (normal, negative binomial, uniform, exponential, Poisson) with explicitly modeled singleton and doubleton counts, to validate the behavior of alpha diversity metrics under controlled abundance structures. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-024-77864-y
skills.summary: Generate synthetic sample-by-ASV count matrices by sampling ASV abundances from parametric distributions (normal, negative binomial, uniform, exponential, Poisson) with explicitly modeled singleton and doubleton counts, to validate the behavior of alpha diversity metrics under controlled abundance structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a real amplicon feature table (e.g. QIIME2 BIOM/TSV from DADA2 or DEBLUR) — this skill only creates synthetic tables for metric validation, not real-data processing The analysis requires ACE or Faith on the synthetic data — these could not be recalculated on synthetic datasets due to technical limitations The goal is to compare denoiser outputs (DADA2 vs DEBLUR) on real sequencing runs rather than to probe metric sensitivity to controlled singleton/doubleton structure

skills.description: Use when an OTU table (samples as columns, OTUs as rows) shows inflated richness from sequencing/PCR errors, and you have OTU centroid sequences from which a similarity match list can be produced for curation.
skills.name: parent-daughter-otu-merging
skills.search_text: parent-daughter-otu-merging Use when an OTU table (samples as columns, OTUs as rows) shows inflated richness from sequencing/PCR errors, and you have OTU centroid sequences from which a similarity match list can be produced for curation. When the goal is to identify single rare species in community data sets — LULU curation is not suitable for this and incurs a small loss of real rare species When no OTU centroid/representative sequences are available to produce a match list, since the algorithm requires sequence similarity to guide co-occurrence testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 The LULU co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation step that identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs (sequence-similar, less abundant, consistently co-occurring with a more abundant 'parent') in an OTU table and merges their read counts into the parent to reduce artefactual OTU inflation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: The LULU co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation step that identifies erroneous 'daughter' OTUs (sequence-similar, less abundant, consistently co-occurring with a more abundant 'parent') in an OTU table and merges their read counts into the parent to reduce artefactual OTU inflation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify single rare species in community data sets — LULU curation is not suitable for this and incurs a small loss of real rare species When no OTU centroid/representative sequences are available to produce a match list, since the algorithm requires sequence similarity to guide co-occurrence testing

skills.description: Use when you have significant-feature call sets from multiple DA tools run on the same datasets and need to quantify and visualize which tools agree, e.g., to build a consensus approach or compare filtering regimes.
skills.name: pcoa-ordination-of-tool-agreement
skills.search_text: pcoa-ordination-of-tool-agreement Use when you have significant-feature call sets from multiple DA tools run on the same datasets and need to quantify and visualize which tools agree, e.g., to build a consensus approach or compare filtering regimes. Your goal is to identify which taxa differ between sample groups in a single dataset, not to benchmark tool agreement — the article's own question ('which taxa significantly differ...?') may be too simple and is a different task Input is a raw count/ASV table rather than per-tool significant-ASV output tables; run_all_tools.sh must first be executed on the dataset(s) Metadata has more than two groupings — run_all_tools.sh specifies a maximum of 2 groupings per dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Skill for benchmarking cross-tool agreement in differential abundance (DA) analysis: pairwise Jaccard distances are computed between the significant-ASV sets produced by each of 14 DA tools across 38 16S rRNA gene datasets, then visualized with principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) to reveal clustering of tools (e.g., edgeR/LEfSe grouping). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Skill for benchmarking cross-tool agreement in differential abundance (DA) analysis: pairwise Jaccard distances are computed between the significant-ASV sets produced by each of 14 DA tools across 38 16S rRNA gene datasets, then visualized with principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) to reveal clustering of tools (e.g., edgeR/LEfSe grouping).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to identify which taxa differ between sample groups in a single dataset, not to benchmark tool agreement — the article's own question ('which taxa significantly differ...?') may be too simple and is a different task Input is a raw count/ASV table rather than per-tool significant-ASV output tables; run_all_tools.sh must first be executed on the dataset(s) Metadata has more than two groupings — run_all_tools.sh specifies a maximum of 2 groupings per dataset

skills.description: Use when you have a rarefied OTU/feature table and sample metadata with a grouping column, and need to visualize between-sample beta diversity and test group separation (e.g., bray_curtis.txt ordination with Group-colored samples).
skills.name: pcoa-ordination-visualization
skills.search_text: pcoa-ordination-visualization Use when you have a rarefied OTU/feature table and sample metadata with a grouping column, and need to visualize between-sample beta diversity and test group separation (e.g., bray_curtis.txt ordination with Group-colored samples). Input is a raw, non-rarefied OTU table — distance metrics require equal-sampling standardization (vegan resampling) first The goal is alpha (within-sample) diversity rather than between-sample beta diversity ordination Only a single sample group exists — pairwise between-group p-value comparison is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Perform PCoA ordination on beta-diversity distance matrices (e.g., Bray-Curtis) within the EasyAmplicon pipeline, producing a colored PCoA plot PDF and a pairwise group-comparison p-value table. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/imo2.42
skills.summary: Perform PCoA ordination on beta-diversity distance matrices (e.g., Bray-Curtis) within the EasyAmplicon pipeline, producing a colored PCoA plot PDF and a pairwise group-comparison p-value table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw, non-rarefied OTU table — distance metrics require equal-sampling standardization (vegan resampling) first The goal is alpha (within-sample) diversity rather than between-sample beta diversity ordination Only a single sample group exists — pairwise between-group p-value comparison is undefined

skills.description: Use when a merged ASV fasta plus occurrence table (ASV i in sample j of replicate k with read count Nijk) from VTAM merge/sortreads may contain chimeras or pseudogenes that must be flagged and eliminated before abundance analysis.
skills.name: pcr-artifact-identification
skills.search_text: pcr-artifact-identification Use when a merged ASV fasta plus occurrence table (ASV i in sample j of replicate k with read count Nijk) from VTAM merge/sortreads may contain chimeras or pseudogenes that must be flagged and eliminated before abundance analysis. Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been merged, demultiplexed, and trimmed by VTAM merge/sortreads — FilterChimera operates on the filter step's fasta inputs The goal is filtering PCR or sequencing errors or low-frequency noise rather than chimeras/pseudogenes — FilterLNF and FilterPCRerror address those occurrences instead Non-reproducible occurrences or whole replicates are the target — FilterMinReplicateNumber and FilterRenkonen handle those, not FilterChimera http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Identifies and removes PCR-derived artifacts — chimeric ASVs, pseudogenes, and spurious indel-containing sequences — from metabarcoding ASV tables using VTAM's FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop, and FilterIndel filters. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Identifies and removes PCR-derived artifacts — chimeric ASVs, pseudogenes, and spurious indel-containing sequences — from metabarcoding ASV tables using VTAM's FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop, and FilterIndel filters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been merged, demultiplexed, and trimmed by VTAM merge/sortreads — FilterChimera operates on the filter step's fasta inputs The goal is filtering PCR or sequencing errors or low-frequency noise rather than chimeras/pseudogenes — FilterLNF and FilterPCRerror address those occurrences instead Non-reproducible occurrences or whole replicates are the target — FilterMinReplicateNumber and FilterRenkonen handle those, not FilterChimera

skills.description: Use when an ASV occurrence table contains low-abundance ASVs suspected to be PCR/sequencing artifacts of more abundant ASVs, and you need to remove occurrences whose read count is a small proportion of a closely matching abundant ASV.
skills.name: pcr-error-detection-sequence-similarity-matching
skills.search_text: pcr-error-detection-sequence-similarity-matching Use when an ASV occurrence table contains low-abundance ASVs suspected to be PCR/sequencing artifacts of more abundant ASVs, and you need to remove occurrences whose read count is a small proportion of a closely matching abundant ASV. The occurrence table has already passed a denoising/clustering algorithm (e.g. DADA2, Unoise, Deblur, Swarm) that explicitly models PCR/sequencing errors — re-running similarity-based error removal risks discarding genuine rare variants. The goal is to remove chimeras, pseudogenes, or indel-containing spurious sequences, which VTAM handles with the distinct FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop, and FilterIndel filters. The occurrence read count is not a small proportion of a closely matching more abundant ASV — such occurrences are not FilterPCRerror candidates and should instead be addressed by replicate-based filters (FilterMinReplicateNumber, FilterRenkonen). http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs VTAM's FilterPCRerror step, which discards ASV occurrences that closely match another ASV with a significantly higher read count, treating them as likely PCR/sequencing errors. In the bat-dataset benchmark this uses a pcr_error_var_prop cutoff of 0.2. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Reconstructs VTAM's FilterPCRerror step, which discards ASV occurrences that closely match another ASV with a significantly higher read count, treating them as likely PCR/sequencing errors. In the bat-dataset benchmark this uses a pcr_error_var_prop cutoff of 0.2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The occurrence table has already passed a denoising/clustering algorithm (e.g. DADA2, Unoise, Deblur, Swarm) that explicitly models PCR/sequencing errors — re-running similarity-based error removal risks discarding genuine rare variants. The goal is to remove chimeras, pseudogenes, or indel-containing spurious sequences, which VTAM handles with the distinct FilterChimera, FilterCodonStop, and FilterIndel filters. The occurrence read count is not a small proportion of a closely matching more abundant ASV — such occurrences are not FilterPCRerror candidates and should instead be addressed by replicate-based filters (FilterMinReplicateNumber, FilterRenkonen).

skills.description: Use when a raw eDNA amplicon OTU count table has PCR replicate-level detection records (sample-by-replicate) and contaminant/sporadic OTUs must be removed prior to taxonomic grouping and downstream community analysis.
skills.name: pcr-replicate-detection-modeling
skills.search_text: pcr-replicate-detection-modeling Use when a raw eDNA amplicon OTU count table has PCR replicate-level detection records (sample-by-replicate) and contaminant/sporadic OTUs must be removed prior to taxonomic grouping and downstream community analysis. Input lacks PCR replicate-level detection records (only a single detection observation per OTU per sample), so a binomial occurrence probability cannot be estimated under the site-occupancy framework. Input is already a decontaminated/filtered OTU table (e.g., blanks already removed by another 'removal of negatives' step); reapplying the <0.8 occupancy filter would risk double-filtering true detections. The analysis goal is to retain rare or sporadically detected taxa (e.g., low-biomass species at the detection limit), since the <0.8 occurrence-probability cutoff will drop exactly such sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 A R-based quality-control skill that treats PCR replicate detections of each OTU as independent binomial draws, estimates a per-OTU occurrence probability under a site-occupancy framework, and removes OTUs with <80% estimated occurrence probability to eliminate contaminant or sporadically detected sequences before taxonomic grouping. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: A R-based quality-control skill that treats PCR replicate detections of each OTU as independent binomial draws, estimates a per-OTU occurrence probability under a site-occupancy framework, and removes OTUs with <80% estimated occurrence probability to eliminate contaminant or sporadically detected sequences before taxonomic grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks PCR replicate-level detection records (only a single detection observation per OTU per sample), so a binomial occurrence probability cannot be estimated under the site-occupancy framework. Input is a pre-filtered feature/MOTU table with no per-replicate detection information, since the ≥2 PCR replicates rule cannot be applied Datasets without PCR replicate structure (single-replicate amplicon runs), where this filtering criterion is undefined Analyses of non-arthropod targets or markers other than the study's mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI primer sets without revalidating the reported read/richness benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Filter a DADA2-inferred MOTU table so that MOTUs are retained only when detected in at least two PCR replicates, per the Thomsen & Sigsgaard (2019) flower eDNA protocol, before taxonomy assignment and richness/read-share summarization. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Filter a DADA2-inferred MOTU table so that MOTUs are retained only when detected in at least two PCR replicates, per the Thomsen & Sigsgaard (2019) flower eDNA protocol, before taxonomy assignment and richness/read-share summarization.

skills.description: Use when comparing performance of two tool versions or configurations (runtime speedup, memory-footprint ratio) on amplicon clustering inputs, or when validating that a faster implementation reproduces prior clustering results exactly.
skills.name: peak-memory-footprint-profiling
skills.search_text: peak-memory-footprint-profiling Use when comparing performance of two tool versions or configurations (runtime speedup, memory-footprint ratio) on amplicon clustering inputs, or when validating that a faster implementation reproduces prior clustering results exactly. The input is a filtered occurrence table or other post-clustering output — this skill benchmarks clustering runs, not downstream tables. The task is clustering quality assessment rather than performance profiling (runtime/memory/identical-output validation). The clustering threshold d >= 2 is required — the >7x speedup and ~50% memory-reduction claims apply to the default d = 1 fast algorithm; a 15% slowdown was observed for d >= 2 in certain conditions (18SV9 dataset). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A benchmarking skill for measuring wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory of a command-line bioinformatics tool (here swarm v3 vs swarm v2) across thread counts on large dereplicated amplicon FASTA datasets, while verifying that outputs remain identical. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for measuring wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory of a command-line bioinformatics tool (here swarm v3 vs swarm v2) across thread counts on large dereplicated amplicon FASTA datasets, while verifying that outputs remain identical.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a filtered occurrence table or other post-clustering output — this skill benchmarks clustering runs, not downstream tables. skills.description: Use when you have mock-community amplicon data with known expected genome/ASV abundances (e.g., Zymo, ATCC 16S, Phylotag) and simulated or real observed counts, and need R2 agreement metrics.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-computation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-computation Use when you have mock-community amplicon data with known expected genome/ASV abundances (e.g., Zymo, ATCC 16S, Phylotag) and simulated or real observed counts, and need R2 agreement metrics. Input is already a curated abundance table and the goal is plotting or taxonomy rather than expected-vs-observed agreement quantification The community lacks ground-truth expected abundances (no known mock composition), so a Pearson R2 against expected values cannot be computed The goal is generating new simulated reads rather than evaluating an existing simulation — use MHASS simulator skills instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes Pearson R2 between expected and observed ASV (or genome-level) abundances to quantify how faithfully MHASS-simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon datasets reproduce real mock-community sequencing, as reported for Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, and Phylotag/16S datasets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Computes Pearson R2 between expected and observed ASV (or genome-level) abundances to quantify how faithfully MHASS-simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon datasets reproduce real mock-community sequencing, as reported for Zymo/Titan-1, ATCC/16S, and Phylotag/16S datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated abundance table and the goal is plotting or taxonomy rather than expected-vs-observed agreement quantification The community lacks ground-truth expected abundances (no known mock composition), so a Pearson R2 against expected values cannot be computed The goal is generating new simulated reads rather than evaluating an existing simulation — use MHASS simulator skills instead

skills.description: Use when you have paired pairwise dissimilarity values (e.g., MSA-based MSD and phylogenetic branch length BLD) between OTU representative sequences and their member reads, and need to quantify agreement at read vs. OTU level.

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-statistics Use when you have paired pairwise dissimilarity values (e.g., MSA-based MSD and phylogenetic branch length BLD) between OTU representative sequences and their member reads, and need to quantify agreement at read vs. OTU level. Input is a raw feature table or abundance matrix rather than paired pairwise dissimilarity values between representative sequences and OTU members. The dissimilarity values have not yet been computed — run the upstream MSD/BLD distance-computation step (QIIME-based OTU picking at 97% followed by MSD and BLD calculation) first. The analysis goal is OTU clustering quality itself (e.g., measuring MSD/BLD compactness against the 0.03 threshold) rather than correlation between two metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Quantifies how strongly two sequence-dissimilarity metrics (MSD-based and BLD-based) agree by computing Pearson correlation coefficients at both the individual read level and the aggregated OTU level for HMP 16S hypervariable regions (V1V3 and V3V5), revealing evolutionary divergence that percent sequence similarity underestimates. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Quantifies how strongly two sequence-dissimilarity metrics (MSD-based and BLD-based) agree by computing Pearson correlation coefficients at both the individual read level and the aggregated OTU level for HMP 16S hypervariable regions (V1V3 and V3V5), revealing evolutionary divergence that percent sequence similarity underestimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw feature table or abundance matrix rather than paired pairwise dissimilarity values between representative sequences and OTU members. skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with no ground-truth composition available (e.g., real environmental data) — r2/L1 cannot be computed without true abundances Analysis of samples with a high proportion of short reads, which MetaMaps does not handle well since reads below the minimum length remain unassigned Read-level assignment accuracy evaluation rather than composition estimation — this skill targets aggregate abundance metrics, not per-read precision/recall

skills.description: Use when you need per-sample, species-level classified taxonomic abundance profiles for a defined environment/habitat (e.g., an EMPO 3 category like human-stool or soil-non-saline) to build bespoke class weights.

skills.search_text: per-habitat-classified-abundance-profiling Use when you need per-sample, species-level classified taxonomic abundance profiles for a defined environment/habitat (e.g., an EMPO 3 category like human-stool or soil-non-saline) to build bespoke class weights. skills.summary: Assembles species-level classified taxonomic abundances for samples from a target habitat (e.g., one of 14 EMPO 3 habitats spanning 21,513 Qiita samples) so that downstream generate_class_weights can produce environment-specific taxonomic weights for q2-feature-classifier's naive Bayes classifier.

skills.description: Use when aligned PacBio HiFi amplicon reads show an unexplained secondary peak in the edit-distance distribution and you need to test whether the excess errors are insertion-specific and position-dependent (e.g., rising near one alignment position) rather than uniformly distributed.

skills.search_text: per-position-indel-error-rate-quantification Use when aligned PacBio HiFi amplicon reads show an unexplained secondary peak in the edit-distance distribution and you need to test whether the excess errors are insertion-specific and position-dependent (e.g., rising near one alignment position) rather than uniformly distributed. Reads have not yet been aligned to a reference sequence — per-position error proportions cannot be tabulated from unaligned FASTQ alone The question is an aggregate error rate or overall read accuracy, not a position-specific insertion/substitution/deletion profile Data are short-read (e.g., Illumina) rather than PacBio HiFi amplicon data, where the terminal insertion profile of this pipeline does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantify insertion, substitution, and deletion error proportions at each alignment position for real and MHASS-simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads, to determine whether a secondary edit-distance peak arises from position-specific (terminal) insertion errors. skills.summary: Quantify insertion, substitution, and deletion error proportions at each alignment position for real and MHASS-simulated PacBio HiFi amplicon reads, to determine whether a secondary edit-distance peak arises from position-specific (terminal) insertion errors. skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not yet been aligned to a reference sequence — per-position error proportions cannot be tabulated from unaligned FASTQ alone The question is an aggregate error rate or overall read accuracy, not a position-specific insertion/substitution/deletion profile Data are short-read (e.g., Illumina) rather than PacBio HiFi amplicon data, where the terminal insertion profile of this pipeline does not apply
