skills.summary: Tests whether microbial communities separate between metadata groupings (e.g., sampling location and size fraction) by running QIIME 2 PERMANOVA (beta-group-significance) on UniFrac distance matrices and extracting pseudo-F and p-values, complemented by Emperor ordination inspection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not yet denoised into a QIIME 2 feature table and rep-seqs artifact (e.g., still raw FASTQ needing the qaqc/DADA2 steps of Tourmaline). You need alpha diversity comparisons within samples rather than between-sample beta diversity group significance. Grouping columns are continuous rather than categorical, so PERMANOVA group separation is not the appropriate test.

skills.description: Use when comparing DA tools' false-positive control on 16S rRNA ASV count tables with two-group metadata, or when validating that a DA pipeline's significant-hit rates are not inflated under randomized (null) groupings.
skills.name: permutation-based-false-positive-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-false-positive-estimation Use when comparing DA tools' false-positive control on 16S rRNA ASV count tables with two-group metadata, or when validating that a DA pipeline's significant-hit rates are not inflated under randomized (null) groupings. Real sample groupings with genuine biological differences — the randomized null is not a perfect representation of real data, so low significant hits here do not prove low practical FDR Analyses where the goal is consensus DA calling on true case/control contrasts rather than tool benchmarking (use the consensus approach of several methods instead) Datasets with more than two sample groupings — the run_all_tools.sh metadata format requires maximum 2 groupings http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark microbiome differential abundance (DA) tools by randomly reassigning case/control labels within a dataset's most frequently sampled group, then measuring the percent of ASVs each tool calls significant — an empirical false-positive rate with no expected group differences. Used in Nearing et al. 2022 to show edgeR (mean 0.69–27.9%) and LEfSe (mean 3.4–5.1%) were outliers on prevalence-filtered 16S rRNA data. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Benchmark microbiome differential abundance (DA) tools by randomly reassigning case/control labels within a dataset's most frequently sampled group, then measuring the percent of ASVs each tool calls significant — an empirical false-positive rate with no expected group differences. Used in Nearing et al. 2022 to show edgeR (mean 0.69–27.9%) and LEfSe (mean 3.4–5.1%) were outliers on prevalence-filtered 16S rRNA data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real sample groupings with genuine biological differences — the randomized null is not a perfect representation of real data, so low significant hits here do not prove low practical FDR Analyses where the goal is consensus DA calling on true case/control contrasts rather than tool benchmarking (use the consensus approach of several methods instead) Datasets with more than two sample groupings — the run_all_tools.sh metadata format requires maximum 2 groupings

skills.description: Use when multiple DA tools have been run independently on several datasets of the same disease/environment and you need to test whether the overlap of significant genera exceeds chance (consistency analysis).
skills.name: permutation-based-null-overlap-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-null-overlap-estimation Use when multiple DA tools have been run independently on several datasets of the same disease/environment and you need to test whether the overlap of significant genera exceeds chance (consistency analysis). Datasets are not from the same environment/phenotype — the article notes 'not all environments and datasets are appropriate for this comparison' (e.g., obesity consistency was no higher than chance for most tools) You need a rigorous null model for individual taxon significance rather than a cross-dataset overlap expectation; the authors flag the random expectation as 'quite simplistic' since it ignores prevalence differences among genera http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Quantifies cross-study consistency of differential abundance calls by comparing the observed number of significant genera shared across all datasets of the same phenotype (e.g., five diarrhea or five obesity datasets) against a permutation-based random expectation, reporting fold-difference and significance per DA tool. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Quantifies cross-study consistency of differential abundance calls by comparing the observed number of significant genera shared across all datasets of the same phenotype (e.g., five diarrhea or five obesity datasets) against a permutation-based random expectation, reporting fold-difference and significance per DA tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not from the same environment/phenotype — the article notes 'not all environments and datasets are appropriate for this comparison' (e.g., obesity consistency was no higher than chance for most tools) You need a rigorous null model for individual taxon significance rather than a cross-dataset overlap expectation; the authors flag the random expectation as 'quite simplistic' since it ignores prevalence differences among genera

skills.description: Use when you have a MOTU-by-sample detection table from metabarcoding and need to test whether local taxonomic richness has saturated or whether more sampling effort would recover additional diversity.
skills.name: permutation-based-rarefaction-analysis
skills.search_text: permutation-based-rarefaction-analysis Use when you have a MOTU-by-sample detection table from metabarcoding and need to test whether local taxonomic richness has saturated or whether more sampling effort would recover additional diversity. You only have read-abundance summaries per location without sample-level detection — the curves require individual sample order permutations. The aim is testing richness differences among locations (use the paper's GLM approach on MOTU richness and square-root transformed read abundances instead). MOTUs have not been filtered (e.g. single-read MOTUs retained), which would inflate rarefaction richness with false positives. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assesses whether eDNA MOTU richness is fully sampled by computing sample-based rarefaction (species accumulation) curves with random permutations, revealing that Caribbean and New Caledonian shark MOTU richness does not plateau. It quantifies sampling sufficiency from presence/absence detection per sample. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assesses whether eDNA MOTU richness is fully sampled by computing sample-based rarefaction (species accumulation) curves with random permutations, revealing that Caribbean and New Caledonian shark MOTU richness does not plateau. It quantifies sampling sufficiency from presence/absence detection per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have read-abundance summaries per location without sample-level detection — the curves require individual sample order permutations. The aim is testing richness differences among locations (use the paper's GLM approach on MOTU richness and square-root transformed read abundances instead). MOTUs have not been filtered (e.g. single-read MOTUs retained), which would inflate rarefaction richness with false positives.

skills.description: Use when you have 16S OTUs (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5 clustered at 97% PSD with QIIME) and need to quantify how compact each OTU is under MSD and BLD rather than the clustering threshold metric.
skills.name: phylogenetic-distance-computation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-distance-computation Use when you have 16S OTUs (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5 clustered at 97% PSD with QIIME) and need to quantify how compact each OTU is under MSD and BLD rather than the clustering threshold metric. When the goal is simply to cluster sequences into OTUs de novo — this skill re-measures existing PSD-clustered OTUs rather than performing the clustering itself When OTUs are already defined by a phylogeny-aware method and their evolutionary compactness under MSD/BLD is not in question When only a single representative sequence per OTU is available without the full member sequence sets — MSD and BLD between representative and members cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Re-measures compactness of OTUs clustered at 97% percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) using two alternative dissimilarity metrics — mean sequence dissimilarity (MSD) and branch length distance (BLD) — between each OTU's representative sequence and all member sequences, exposing poorly clustered OTUs that PSD hides. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Re-measures compactness of OTUs clustered at 97% percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) using two alternative dissimilarity metrics — mean sequence dissimilarity (MSD) and branch length distance (BLD) — between each OTU's representative sequence and all member sequences, exposing poorly clustered OTUs that PSD hides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is simply to cluster sequences into OTUs de novo — this skill re-measures existing PSD-clustered OTUs rather than performing the clustering itself When OTUs are already defined by a phylogeny-aware method and their evolutionary compactness under MSD/BLD is not in question When only a single representative sequence per OTU is available without the full member sequence sets — MSD and BLD between representative and members cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when 16S amplicon reads from pre-clustered OTUs (e.g., HMP V1V3/V3V5 at a 97% similarity threshold) must be placed onto a fixed reference tree to compute MSD and BLD between a representative sequence and all remaining OTU members.
skills.name: phylogenetic-placement-of-16s-amplicon-reads
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-placement-of-16s-amplicon-reads Use when 16S amplicon reads from pre-clustered OTUs (e.g., HMP V1V3/V3V5 at a 97% similarity threshold) must be placed onto a fixed reference tree to compute MSD and BLD between a representative sequence and all remaining OTU members. The goal is to define OTUs de novo by percent sequence similarity (PSD) clustering at 97% — this skill instead evaluates already-clustered OTUs with MSD and BLD. Sequences cannot be placed on a suitable fixed reference phylogeny (placement via pplacer/SEPP is a prerequisite for the MSD alignment and BLD tree). Only taxonomic annotation of a representative sequence is needed; placement-based dissimilarity measurement is unnecessary for representative-sequence annotation workflows. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Places 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., HMP V1V3 and V3V5 OTU members) onto a fixed reference phylogeny using pplacer/SEPP to obtain a placement-induced multiple sequence alignment per OTU, enabling maximum sequence dissimilarity (MSD) and branch length distance (BLD) computation against each OTU's representative sequence. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Places 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., HMP V1V3 and V3V5 OTU members) onto a fixed reference phylogeny using pplacer/SEPP to obtain a placement-induced multiple sequence alignment per OTU, enabling maximum sequence dissimilarity (MSD) and branch length distance (BLD) computation against each OTU's representative sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to define OTUs de novo by percent sequence similarity (PSD) clustering at 97% — this skill instead evaluates already-clustered OTUs with MSD and BLD. Sequences cannot be placed on a suitable fixed reference phylogeny (placement via pplacer/SEPP is a prerequisite for the MSD alignment and BLD tree). Only taxonomic annotation of a representative sequence is needed; placement-based dissimilarity measurement is unnecessary for representative-sequence annotation workflows.

skills.description: Use when individual short 16S reads or OTU member sequences must be assigned lineages via phylogenetic placement on a reference tree, or when BLD between representative and member sequences must be computed for HMP-style V1V3/V3V5 OTUs.
skills.name: phylogenetic-sequence-placement
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-sequence-placement Use when individual short 16S reads or OTU member sequences must be assigned lineages via phylogenetic placement on a reference tree, or when BLD between representative and member sequences must be computed for HMP-style V1V3/V3V5 OTUs. When the goal is only percent-sequence-similarity (PSD) clustering itself — this skill annotates/places already-clustered OTU reads, it does not regenerate OTUs When input is a pre-computed feature table or OTU abundance matrix with no underlying sequence collection — placement requires the actual amplicon sequences When full-length 16S sequences can be aligned de novo — SEPP is specifically designed for inserting short fragments into a fixed reference tree http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Places 16S rRNA amplicon reads or OTU member sequences onto a fixed reference tree using SEPP and pplacer, enabling per-read taxonomic lineage assignment and branch-length-divergence (BLD) computation instead of inheriting the single representative sequence's annotation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Places 16S rRNA amplicon reads or OTU member sequences onto a fixed reference tree using SEPP and pplacer, enabling per-read taxonomic lineage assignment and branch-length-divergence (BLD) computation instead of inheriting the single representative sequence's annotation.

skills.description: Use when you need to determine at which taxonomic or phylogenetic resolution environment (habitat) specificity is captured in a large multi-study 16S dataset such as EMP 16S Release 1.
skills.name: phylogenetic-subtree-entropy-aggregation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-subtree-entropy-aggregation Use when you need to determine at which taxonomic or phylogenetic resolution environment (habitat) specificity is captured in a large multi-study 16S dataset such as EMP 16S Release 1. Input is a clustered-OTU-only table with no exact Deblur tag sequences — the sharp entropy drop at exact-sequence (below 97% identity) resolution cannot be observed Samples lack reliable environment-category metadata, since entropy is computed over the distribution of environment categories per feature The goal is beta-diversity or community-composition comparison rather than resolution-level habitat-specificity assessment Quantifies environment specificity across phylogenetic resolutions by computing Shannon entropy of environment-category distributions per exact Deblur 16S tag sequence and re-computing it after collapsing counts to genera, higher taxa, and phylogenetic subtrees, revealing that specificity is sharpest at the exact-sequence level. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Quantifies environment specificity across phylogenetic resolutions by computing Shannon entropy of environment-category distributions per exact Deblur 16S tag sequence and re-computing it after collapsing counts to genera, higher taxa, and phylogenetic subtrees, revealing that specificity is sharpest at the exact-sequence level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a clustered-OTU-only table with no exact Deblur tag sequences — the sharp entropy drop at exact-sequence (below 97% identity) resolution cannot be observed Samples lack reliable environment-category metadata, since entropy is computed over the distribution of environment categories per feature The goal is beta-diversity or community-composition comparison rather than resolution-level habitat-specificity assessment

skills.description: Use when a filtered, dereplicated, chimera-checked set of representative OTU sequences (e.g. result/otus.fa) must be converted into a phylogenetic tree to enable phylogenetically aware beta diversity (UniFrac) and PCoA ordination.

Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) or an OTU/ASV table that has not yet been aggregated to arthropod-family level per plant species The goal is statistical significance testing of network structure or modularity rather than reproducing the descriptive visualization of family distribution Interaction data are quantitative time-series or individual-based rather than a simple species-by-family detection matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Construct and render a bipartite plant–arthropod-family interaction network from a plant-species × arthropod-family detection matrix using the R bipartite package, reproducing the figure that shows how eDNA-recovered arthropod families (67 families, 14 orders) are distributed across seven sampled plant species. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Construct and render a bipartite plant–arthropod-family interaction network from a plant-species × arthropod-family detection matrix using the R bipartite package, reproducing the figure that shows how eDNA-recovered arthropod families (67 families, 14 orders) are distributed across seven sampled plant species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) or an OTU/ASV table that has not yet been aggregated to arthropod-family level per plant species The goal is statistical significance testing of network structure or modularity rather than reproducing the descriptive visualization of family distribution Interaction data are quantitative time-series or individual-based rather than a simple species-by-family detection matrix

skills.description: Use when flower-sample eDNA metabarcoding replicates must be pooled per plant species to build species accumulation curves and judge whether current sampling effort exhausts arthropod diversity.
skills.name: plant-species-grouped-sample-replication
skills.search_text: plant-species-grouped-sample-replication Use when flower-sample eDNA metabarcoding replicates must be pooled per plant species to build species accumulation curves and judge whether current sampling effort exhausts arthropod diversity. The goal is community composition or clustering of arthropod assemblages by plant species rather than sampling-effort assessment Samples are not flower eDNA replicates traceable to individual plant species, so per-species grouping is impossible Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) rather than an already-built OTU/ASV table http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 Groups flower-sample eDNA replicates by plant species and runs sample-based rarefaction (vegan::specaccum, method='exact') on COI and 16S OTU/ASV tables at species and family levels to test whether recovered arthropod richness saturates with sampling effort. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Groups flower-sample eDNA replicates by plant species and runs sample-based rarefaction (vegan::specaccum, method='exact') on COI and 16S OTU/ASV tables at species and family levels to test whether recovered arthropod richness saturates with sampling effort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is community composition or clustering of arthropod assemblages by plant species rather than sampling-effort assessment Samples are not flower eDNA replicates traceable to individual plant species, so per-species grouping is impossible Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) rather than an already-built OTU/ASV table

skills.description: Use when an OTU table derived from plant ITS2 metabarcoding of soil (or similar) must be validated against paired field-survey species lists, by summarizing per-site taxonomic composition into species-validation categories before and after post-clustering curation.
skills.name: plant-survey-occurrence-table-summation
skills.search_text: plant-survey-occurrence-table-summation Use when an OTU table derived from plant ITS2 metabarcoding of soil (or similar) must be validated against paired field-survey species lists, by summarizing per-site taxonomic composition into species-validation categories before and after post-clustering curation. The goal is to identify individual rare, low-abundance species: LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets No paired field-inventory or reference data exist for the study region, so recaptured/unregistered species categories cannot be defined Input is a sequence file rather than an OTU table with samples as columns and unique OTU ids as row names; clustering (e.g. VSEARCH, SWARM, DADA2) must be done first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Compares OTU-derived per-site plant species inventories (before and after LULU curation) against field-survey species lists by summing occurrence counts into per-site proportions of imperfect reference matches, recaptured, unregistered, redundant, and lost species, as in Table 2 of the 130-site Danish ITS2 validation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Compares OTU-derived per-site plant species inventories (before and after LULU curation) against field-survey species lists by summing occurrence counts into per-site proportions of imperfect reference matches, recaptured, unregistered, redundant, and lost species, as in Table 2 of the 130-site Danish ITS2 validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify individual rare, low-abundance species: LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets No paired field-inventory or reference data exist for the study region, so recaptured/unregistered species categories cannot be defined Input is a sequence file rather than an OTU table with samples as columns and unique OTU ids as row names; clustering (e.g. VSEARCH, SWARM, DADA2) must be done first

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential abundance methods for microbiome count data under known ground truth, needing simulated absolute/relative abundance datasets with controlled FDR and power estimates.
skills.name: poisson-gamma-count-data-simulation
skills.search_text: poisson-gamma-count-data-simulation Use when benchmarking differential abundance methods for microbiome count data under known ground truth, needing simulated absolute/relative abundance datasets with controlled FDR and power estimates. Real observational microbiome data without known true DA status — empirical FDR and power cannot be computed from ground truth in that setting Very small sample sizes such as n=5 per group — the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled there Studies where the proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large — ANCOM-BC may exhibit slightly elevated FDR in that regime http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generate 100 simulated microbiome count datasets under a Poisson-Gamma model for two designs — small unbalanced (n1=20, n2=30) and large balanced (n1=n2=50) — to benchmark differential abundance methods on empirical FDR and power at the 5% nominal level, as in Fig. 4 of the ANCOM-BC paper. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Generate 100 simulated microbiome count datasets under a Poisson-Gamma model for two designs — small unbalanced (n1=20, n2=30) and large balanced (n1=n2=50) — to benchmark differential abundance methods on empirical FDR and power at the 5% nominal level, as in Fig. 4 of the ANCOM-BC paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real observational microbiome data without known true DA status — empirical FDR and power cannot be computed from ground truth in that setting Very small sample sizes such as n=5 per group — the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled there Studies where the proportion of differentially abundant taxa is too large — ANCOM-BC may exhibit slightly elevated FDR in that regime

skills.description: Use when per-location count data (e.g. MOTU richness or sequencing read abundance) must be compared across a categorical sampling factor such as geographic location, and pairwise post-hoc contrasts are needed.
skills.name: poisson-glm-richness-modeling
skills.search_text: poisson-glm-richness-modeling Use when per-location count data (e.g. MOTU richness or sequencing read abundance) must be compared across a categorical sampling factor such as geographic location, and pairwise post-hoc contrasts are needed. The response variable is a non-count diversity index (e.g. Shannon) rather than MOTU richness or raw read counts, where Poisson assumptions do not hold The design involves covariates or continuous predictors rather than a single categorical location factor for Tukey contrasts Input is the raw FASTQ/MOTU table rather than the aggregated per-location richness and read abundance table http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Fit a Poisson generalized linear model with location as a categorical factor to test whether elasmobranch MOTU richness and square-root-transformed eDNA read abundance differ among sampling locations, followed by post-hoc Tukey pairwise contrasts. This reproduces the statistical test used by Bakker et al. (2017) to link shark diversity patterns to anthropogenic pressure levels. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Fit a Poisson generalized linear model with location as a categorical factor to test whether elasmobranch MOTU richness and square-root-transformed eDNA read abundance differ among sampling locations, followed by post-hoc Tukey pairwise contrasts. This reproduces the statistical test used by Bakker et al. (2017) to link shark diversity patterns to anthropogenic pressure levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response variable is a non-count diversity index (e.g. Shannon) rather than MOTU richness or raw read counts, where Poisson assumptions do not hold The design involves covariates or continuous predictors rather than a single categorical location factor for Tukey contrasts Input is the raw FASTQ/MOTU table rather than the aggregated per-location richness and read abundance table

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between discarding rare OTUs (singletons) and co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation when validating amplicon alpha-diversity estimates against independent ground-truth richness data.
skills.name: post-clustering-curation-comparison
skills.search_text: post-clustering-curation-comparison Decision support for choosing between discarding rare OTUs (singletons) and co-occurrence-based post-clustering curation when validating amplicon alpha-diversity estimates against independent ground-truth richness data. When the goal is assessing composition or turnover rather than alpha-diversity — the article notes that discarding the abundance tail may be adequate for composition but 'much less so for alpha-diversity' When the aim is identifying single rare species in a community dataset — LULU curation may not be suitable and carries a small 'cost of curation' in real rare species When no paired independent ground-truth richness data (e.g. field survey) exist to compute correspondence metrics such as R2 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 A benchmarking skill that quantifies how singleton removal compares to LULU post-clustering curation for improving the correspondence between molecular OTU richness and field-survey plant richness. In the source study, singleton removal gave a mean R2 gain of only 0.03 versus 0.27 for LULU across VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP and DADA2 OTU tables from 130 Danish sites. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that quantifies how singleton removal compares to LULU post-clustering curation for improving the correspondence between molecular OTU richness and field-survey plant richness. In the source study, singleton removal gave a mean R2 gain of only 0.03 versus 0.27 for LULU across VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP and DADA2 OTU tables from 130 Danish sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is assessing composition or turnover rather than alpha-diversity — the article notes that discarding the abundance tail may be adequate for composition but 'much less so for alpha-diversity' When the aim is identifying single rare species in a community dataset — LULU curation may not be suitable and carries a small 'cost of curation' in real rare species When no paired independent ground-truth richness data (e.g. field survey) exist to compute correspondence metrics such as R2

skills.description: Use when an OTU table (samples as columns, OTUs as rows with unique row names) over-inflates richness due to PCR/sequencing errors and rare artefactual OTUs, and you want reference-free post-clustering curation before biodiversity analyses.
skills.name: post-clustering-otu-table-curation
skills.search_text: post-clustering-otu-table-curation Use when an OTU table (samples as columns, OTUs as rows with unique row names) over-inflates richness due to PCR/sequencing errors and rare artefactual OTUs, and you want reference-free post-clustering curation before biodiversity analyses. The goal is to identify single rare species in community datasets — LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species, and curation costs a small loss of real rare/low-abundance species You need de novo OTU inference itself — LULU requires an existing OTU table and a pre-computed match list; it does not perform initial clustering Validating against mock communities with known genetic content — this was explicitly flagged as untested future work for LULU http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Curate an already-clustered OTU table by merging erroneous 'daughter' OTUs into more abundant 'parent' OTUs using co-occurrence patterns and sequence similarity (LULU), improving alpha-diversity and taxonomic reliability without needing a reference database. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Curate an already-clustered OTU table by merging erroneous 'daughter' OTUs into more abundant 'parent' OTUs using co-occurrence patterns and sequence similarity (LULU), improving alpha-diversity and taxonomic reliability without needing a reference database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify single rare species in community datasets — LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species, and curation costs a small loss of real rare/low-abundance species You need de novo OTU inference itself — LULU requires an existing OTU table and a pre-computed match list; it does not perform initial clustering Validating against mock communities with known genetic content — this was explicitly flagged as untested future work for LULU

skills.description: Use when you have per-location count data (e.g. MOTU richness or eDNA read counts from metabarcoding) and need statistically justified pairwise contrasts among a categorical grouping factor after a GLM.
skills.name: post-hoc-tukey-multiple-comparison-testing
skills.search_text: post-hoc-tukey-multiple-comparison-testing Use when you have per-location count data (e.g. MOTU richness or eDNA read counts from metabarcoding) and need statistically justified pairwise contrasts among a categorical grouping factor after a GLM. Input is still raw FASTQ or an unfiltered MOTU table — the metabarcoding pipeline (illumincapairedend, ngsfilter, obigrep 120–135 bp, uchime-denovo, sumaclust 99%) must be run and single-read MOTUs removed first The response variable is continuous and non-count-like, making a Poisson GLM inappropriate Only two groups are compared with no multiplicity concern — a simple pairwise test suffices and Tukey correction adds nothing http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits Poisson generalized linear models with location as a categorical factor on shark eDNA MOTU richness and square-root-transformed read abundances, then extracts all pairwise location contrasts with Tukey-adjusted post-hoc comparisons. Used to test whether elasmobranch diversity and read abundance differ significantly among Caribbean and New Caledonia sampling sites. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Fits Poisson generalized linear models with location as a categorical factor on shark eDNA MOTU richness and square-root-transformed read abundances, then extracts all pairwise location contrasts with Tukey-adjusted post-hoc comparisons. Used to test whether elasmobranch diversity and read abundance differ significantly among Caribbean and New Caledonia sampling sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ or an unfiltered MOTU table — the metabarcoding pipeline (illumincapairedend, ngsfilter, obigrep 120–135 bp, uchime-denovo, sumaclust 99%) must be run and single-read MOTUs removed first The response variable is continuous and non-count-like, making a Poisson GLM inappropriate Only two groups are compared with no multiplicity concern — a simple pairwise test suffices and Tukey correction adds nothing

skills.description: Use when comparing pre- and post-LULU-curation OTU tables to assess how many erroneous or taxonomically redundant OTUs (e.g., for single-species genera like Fagus or Calluna) collapse onto parent OTUs and whether read counts are conserved.
skills.name: pre-post-curation-read-count-comparison
skills.search_text: pre-post-curation-read-count-comparison Use when comparing pre- and post-LULU-curation OTU tables to assess how many erroneous or taxonomically redundant OTUs (e.g., for single-species genera like Fagus or Calluna) collapse onto parent OTUs and whether read counts are conserved. When the goal is to identify single rare species in a community dataset — LULU curation may discard rare but real OTUs (the 'cost of curation'), so a pre/post comparison would report their loss as curation effect rather than error removal When the input is not an OTU table paired with an internal match list (e.g., raw FASTQ reads or ASV data without representative sequences) — LULU requires both an OTU table and a match list produced by BLASTn or VSEARCH http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies the homogenizing effect of LULU post-clustering curation by tabulating per-OTU and per-genus read counts in the original versus curated OTU tables, verifying that daughter-OTU reads are folded into their designated more abundant parent OTUs while total read counts per taxon are preserved. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Quantifies the homogenizing effect of LULU post-clustering curation by tabulating per-OTU and per-genus read counts in the original versus curated OTU tables, verifying that daughter-OTU reads are folded into their designated more abundant parent OTUs while total read counts per taxon are preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify single rare species in a community dataset — LULU curation may discard rare but real OTUs (the 'cost of curation'), so a pre/post comparison would report their loss as curation effect rather than error removal When the input is not an OTU table paired with an internal match list (e.g., raw FASTQ reads or ASV data without representative sequences) — LULU requires both an OTU table and a match list produced by BLASTn or VSEARCH

skills.description: Use when a pipeline's taxonomy assignments must be validated against a mock community with known member taxa, and comparable quality metrics (precision, recall, F1) to prior benchmarks are needed.
skills.name: precision-recall-f1-benchmark-scoring
skills.search_text: precision-recall-f1-benchmark-scoring Use when a pipeline's taxonomy assignments must be validated against a mock community with known member taxa, and comparable quality metrics (precision, recall, F1) to prior benchmarks are needed. The dataset is a real environmental community with unknown composition — precision/recall against a truth set is undefined; use ecological metrics (alpha/beta diversity) instead. The pipeline output is already a validated feature/OTU table with published benchmark scores — re-deriving metrics would duplicate existing evaluation. Marker genes other than 16S/18S rRNA processed under conditions where taxonomy assignment (e.g., MIDORI for COI) lacks reference entries for known members, making TP/FP classification unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark scoring of a metabarcoding pipeline's taxonomic output against a mock community with known composition, computing genus-level precision, recall, and F1-score from true/false positives and negatives. Used to quantify how faithfully PEMA's ASV/OTU tables recover the expected taxa of the Bradley et al. 18S algal mock community. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Benchmark scoring of a metabarcoding pipeline's taxonomic output against a mock community with known composition, computing genus-level precision, recall, and F1-score from true/false positives and negatives. Used to quantify how faithfully PEMA's ASV/OTU tables recover the expected taxa of the Bradley et al. 18S algal mock community.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a real environmental community with unknown composition — precision/recall against a truth set is undefined; use ecological metrics (alpha/beta diversity) instead. The pipeline output is already a validated feature/OTU table with published benchmark scores — re-deriving metrics would duplicate existing evaluation. Marker genes other than 16S/18S rRNA processed under conditions where taxonomy assignment (e.g., MIDORI for COI) lacks reference entries for known members, making TP/FP classification unreliable.

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic profiling tools (e.g. MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3, mOTUs 2.6, Bracken 2.5) on synthetic metagenomes such as CAMI 2 or SynPhlAn where the ground-truth species composition is known.
skills.name: precision-recall-f1-evaluation
skills.search_text: precision-recall-f1-evaluation Use when comparing taxonomic profiling tools (e.g. MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3, mOTUs 2.6, Bracken 2.5) on synthetic metagenomes such as CAMI 2 or SynPhlAn where the ground-truth species composition is known. No ground-truth species composition is available (e.g. real environmental or host-associated metagenomes) — OPAL metrics like precision, recall and F1 cannot be computed The task is functional profiling (e.g. HUMAnN-style pathway quantification) rather than species-level taxonomic profiling Input samples are the under-characterized environments the paper flags as still 'highly enriched for sequences not captured even by current uSGBs', where ground-truth-based evaluation of known species is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark species-level taxonomic profilers by feeding each predicted profile plus the synthetic-community ground truth into the OPAL framework to compute per-sample precision, recall, F1, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, RMSE on relative abundances, and true/false-positive counts, then aggregate metrics as mean ± standard deviation across samples. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Benchmark species-level taxonomic profilers by feeding each predicted profile plus the synthetic-community ground truth into the OPAL framework to compute per-sample precision, recall, F1, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, RMSE on relative abundances, and true/false-positive counts, then aggregate metrics as mean ± standard deviation across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth species composition is available (e.g. real environmental or host-associated metagenomes) — OPAL metrics like precision, recall and F1 cannot be computed The task is functional profiling (e.g. HUMAnN-style pathway quantification) rather than species-level taxonomic profiling Input samples are the under-characterized environments the paper flags as still 'highly enriched for sequences not captured even by current uSGBs', where ground-truth-based evaluation of known species is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when evaluating an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline on a mock community with a known taxonomic ground truth and you need quantitative precision/recall/F1 per clustering or ASV-inference condition.
skills.name: precision-recall-metric-computation
skills.search_text: precision-recall-metric-computation Use when evaluating an eDNA metabarcoding pipeline on a mock community with a known taxonomic ground truth and you need quantitative precision/recall/F1 per clustering or ASV-inference condition. The input is an environmental (not mock) community sample with no known ground-truth taxon composition, so TP/FP/FN cannot be defined Taxonomy was assigned only to level above genus, since the PEMA benchmark computed these metrics at genus level http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Benchmark a metabarcoding pipeline against a mock community by computing per-condition precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), and F1 = 2*(precision*recall)/(precision+recall) at genus level, as PEMA did for the Gohl et al. 16S mock community. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Benchmark a metabarcoding pipeline against a mock community by computing per-condition precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), and F1 = 2*(precision*recall)/(precision+recall) at genus level, as PEMA did for the Gohl et al. 16S mock community.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an environmental (not mock) community sample with no known ground-truth taxon composition, so TP/FP/FN cannot be defined Taxonomy was assigned only to level above genus, since the PEMA benchmark computed these metrics at genus level

skills.description: Use when evaluating a metagenomic read classifier (e.g., MetaMaps, Kraken, Centrifuge) on datasets with known ground truth, to quantify strain- and species-level assignment accuracy.
skills.name: precision-recall-metric-computation
skills.search_text: precision-recall-metric-computation Use when evaluating a metagenomic read classifier (e.g., MetaMaps, Kraken, Centrifuge) on datasets with known ground truth, to quantify strain- and species-level assignment accuracy. Samples contain a high proportion of short reads, which MetaMaps' minimizer-based approximate mapping cannot reliably assign (reads below the minimum length remain unassigned) The goal is de novo or novelty detection on samples with many non-characterized entities rather than accuracy benchmarking against known ground truth The dataset has no ground truth, so precision/recall cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes species- and strain-level precision, recall (at read and base level), and precision2 for metagenomic classifiers by comparing their taxonomic assignments against known ground truth, as done to benchmark MetaMaps against Centrifuge, Kraken, Kraken 2, and LAST+MEGAN-LR. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Computes species- and strain-level precision, recall (at read and base level), and precision2 for metagenomic classifiers by comparing their taxonomic assignments against known ground truth, as done to benchmark MetaMaps against Centrifuge, Kraken, Kraken 2, and LAST+MEGAN-LR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples contain a high proportion of short reads, which MetaMaps' minimizer-based approximate mapping cannot reliably assign (reads below the minimum length remain unassigned) The goal is de novo or novelty detection on samples with many non-characterized entities rather than accuracy benchmarking against known ground truth The dataset has no ground truth, so precision/recall cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when several FASTQ filtering/adapter-trimming tools have been run on the same input reads and their outputs must be tabulated and compared on a common metric, e.g. suspected-adapter residue rate vs allowed mismatches.
skills.name: preprocessing-tool-result-aggregation
skills.search_text: preprocessing-tool-result-aggregation Use when several FASTQ filtering/adapter-trimming tools have been run on the same input reads and their outputs must be tabulated and compared on a common metric, e.g. suspected-adapter residue rate vs allowed mismatches. Input is raw unfiltered FASTQ with no per-tool outputs to aggregate — run the filterers first Reads are long-read (Nanopore, PacBio) data — the paper directs such data to fastplong, not the short-read tool comparison Only a single preprocessing tool was used and no cross-tool comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates the filtered FASTQ outputs of multiple FASTQ preprocessing tools (fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, AfterQC, SOAPnuke) into a single benchmark table and comparison figure, scoring each tool by residual adapter content across a mismatch-tolerance sweep. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Aggregates the filtered FASTQ outputs of multiple FASTQ preprocessing tools (fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, AfterQC, SOAPnuke) into a single benchmark table and comparison figure, scoring each tool by residual adapter content across a mismatch-tolerance sweep.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unfiltered FASTQ with no per-tool outputs to aggregate — run the filterers first Reads are long-read (Nanopore, PacBio) data — the paper directs such data to fastplong, not the short-read tool comparison Only a single preprocessing tool was used and no cross-tool comparison is needed

skills.description: Use when you need an empirical head-to-head comparison of FASTQ preprocessing tools, or must quantify how a preprocessor choice affects downstream variant-calling specificity (false-positive counts) on a dataset with a curated truth set.
skills.name: preprocessor-benchmarking
skills.search_text: preprocessor-benchmarking Use when you need an empirical head-to-head comparison of FASTQ preprocessing tools, or must quantify how a preprocessor choice affects downstream variant-calling specificity (false-positive counts) on a dataset with a curated truth set. Reads are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the fastp toolchain here targets short reads; use fastplong instead The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking alone — this skill measures downstream specificity via false-positive variant counts, not preprocessing speed No curated variant truth set exists for the sample, so false positives cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark FASTQ preprocessing tools by running each on the same raw paired-end reads and comparing downstream variant-calling false positives against a curated truth set. Grounded in the fastp paper's comparison of fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt and SOAPnuke on NA12878 (SRR952827). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Benchmark FASTQ preprocessing tools by running each on the same raw paired-end reads and comparing downstream variant-calling false positives against a curated truth set. Grounded in the fastp paper's comparison of fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt and SOAPnuke on NA12878 (SRR952827).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the fastp toolchain here targets short reads; use fastplong instead The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking alone — this skill measures downstream specificity via false-positive variant counts, not preprocessing speed No curated variant truth set exists for the sample, so false positives cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when preparing ASV/OTU abundance tables for differential abundance (DA) testing in microbiome studies where the effect of rare-taxa pre-processing on tool output must be controlled or compared across datasets.
skills.name: prevalence-filtering-16s-count-tables
skills.search_text: prevalence-filtering-16s-count-tables Use when preparing ASV/OTU abundance tables for differential abundance (DA) testing in microbiome studies where the effect of rare-taxa pre-processing on tool output must be controlled or compared across datasets. The goal is computing diversity metrics rather than DA testing — the authors state that whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses is beyond the scope of this work You need a statistically optimal rare-feature cut-off — the 10% threshold was arbitrarily selected and the optimal cut-off is unknown Filtering must depend on the test statistic or be applied after testing — the article stresses filtering should be independent of the test statistic (Independent Filtering) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters rare ASVs from 16S rRNA gene count tables at a prevalence threshold (10% in this study) before running the 14 differential abundance tools, so that tools are tested on features present in a non-trivial fraction of samples and results under filtered vs. unfiltered pre-processing can be compared. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Filters rare ASVs from 16S rRNA gene count tables at a prevalence threshold (10% in this study) before running the 14 differential abundance tools, so that tools are tested on features present in a non-trivial fraction of samples and results under filtered vs. unfiltered pre-processing can be compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is computing diversity metrics rather than DA testing — the authors state that whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses is beyond the scope of this work You need a statistically optimal rare-feature cut-off — the 10% threshold was arbitrarily selected and the optimal cut-off is unknown Filtering must depend on the test statistic or be applied after testing — the article stresses filtering should be independent of the test statistic (Independent Filtering)

skills.description: Use when full-length 16S rRNA reference FASTA sequences (e.g., non-redundant Greengenes v13.8.99) must be trimmed into sub-region amplicons using common microbiome PCR primer pairs for in-silico taxonomic-accuracy comparison.
skills.name: primer-mismatch-tolerant-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: primer-mismatch-tolerant-sequence-extraction Use when full-length 16S rRNA reference FASTA sequences (e.g., non-redundant Greengenes v13.8.99) must be trimmed into sub-region amplicons using common microbiome PCR primer pairs for in-silico taxonomic-accuracy comparison. Input is already sub-region amplicon sequence data or a feature/OTU table — trimming primers again is meaningless The goal is to analyze real sequencing runs (e.g., long-read Nanopore/PacBio mock or in-vivo communities) rather than an in-silico database comparison Reference sequences lack the primer-binding sites flanking the target variable region — no amplicon can be anchored and the extraction step cannot proceed http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts in-silico 16S sub-region amplicons (V4, V1-V3, V3-V5, V6-V9, V1-V9) from full-length 16S reference sequences by trimming with primer-binding-site anchors, tolerating up to 3 primer mismatches. This recreates the exact sequence space a short-read amplicon run would sample, enabling taxonomic-resolution comparison against the full ~1500 bp gene. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: Extracts in-silico 16S sub-region amplicons (V4, V1-V3, V3-V5, V6-V9, V1-V9) from full-length 16S reference sequences by trimming with primer-binding-site anchors, tolerating up to 3 primer mismatches. This recreates the exact sequence space a short-read amplicon run would sample, enabling taxonomic-resolution comparison against the full ~1500 bp gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already sub-region amplicon sequence data or a feature/OTU table — trimming primers again is meaningless The goal is to analyze real sequencing runs (e.g., long-read Nanopore/PacBio mock or in-vivo communities) rather than an in-silico database comparison Reference sequences lack the primer-binding sites flanking the target variable region — no amplicon can be anchored and the extraction step cannot proceed

skills.name: primer-trimmed-query-simulation
skills.search_text: primer-trimmed-query-simulation Use when you need realistic primer-anchored short CO1 query fragments (e.g., 200 bp) from full-length reference sequences to benchmark taxonomic classifiers such as the RDP classifier or top BLAST hit methods on simulated Illumina-like metabarcoding data. When the input queries are already short amplicon reads from real sequencing data rather than full-length reference sequences needing simulation When benchmarking species-rank assignment, since the paper notes no bootstrap cutoff can guarantee 99% correct species-rank assignments (Species = NA for 99% tables) and 200 bp fragments are only scored at the genus rank in this workflow When the target locus is not CO1 and primer sequences/barcode region differ substantially from those in the CO1 Eukaryote training sets Simulates realistic metabarcoding query reads by using CUTADAPT to retrieve primer-trimmed CO1 sequences from the training/reference set and truncating them to 200 bp fragments, mimicking Illumina reads after primer trimming. These simulated queries are then used to benchmark taxonomic assignment speed and accuracy (e.g., RDP classifier vs top BLAST hit). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Simulates realistic metabarcoding query reads by using CUTADAPT to retrieve primer-trimmed CO1 sequences from the training/reference set and truncating them to 200 bp fragments, mimicking Illumina reads after primer trimming. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input queries are already short amplicon reads from real sequencing data rather than full-length reference sequences needing simulation When benchmarking species-rank assignment, since the paper notes no bootstrap cutoff can guarantee 99% correct species-rank assignments (Species = NA for 99% tables) and 200 bp fragments are only scored at the genus rank in this workflow When the target locus is not CO1 and primer sequences/barcode region differ substantially from those in the CO1 Eukaryote training sets

skills.summary: Generates fastp-style FASTQ quality-control reports (JSON + single-page HTML) that profile Q20/Q30, KMER, GC ratio, adapter content and — critically — a duplication-rate metric computed with fastp's array-based paired-end key1/key2 scheme rather than FASTQC's hash tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina NovaSeq, MGI); use fastplong instead Input is already a processed QC artifact (e.g. an existing JSON/HTML report or a feature table) rather than raw FASTQ reads An exact, collision-free per-read duplication census is required — the array-based scheme tolerates hash collisions (~0.01% of reads)

skills.search_text: r-phyloseq-analysis Use when a genus-level ASV abundance table must be grouped by experimental condition (e.g., 16S hypervariable region amplified) and compared for alpha diversity (Shannon, inverse Simpson, Chao1) with non-parametric testing in R. Input is already summarized diversity values or a taxa-composition table without per-sample ASV counts — richness indices like Chao1 cannot be recomputed from collapsed summaries. Data are full-length 16S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic reads with no hypervariable-region grouping variable, since the comparison framework is specifically across region combinations. skills.name: rarefied-count-table-diversity-analysis

skills.description: Use when running DA tools that operate on rarefied count tables (e.g. the rarefied/CLR test variants in a multi-tool comparison) and sample library sizes differ, requiring subsampling to a fixed depth such as 2000 reads.
skills.name: rarefying-read-count-tables
skills.search_text: rarefying-read-count-tables Use when running DA tools that operate on rarefied count tables (e.g. the rarefied/CLR test variants in a multi-tool comparison) and sample library sizes differ, requiring subsampling to a fixed depth such as 2000 reads. When the downstream analysis is not DA testing — the paper states 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work'. When the goal is maximum statistical power or minimal FDR: rarefying has been criticized for reducing statistical power, introducing biases, and yielding high false positive rates with standard tests. When comparing to the paper's unfiltered results — mixing rarefied and non-rarefied variants without reporting pre-processing confounds cross-tool comparisons, since 'results depend on data pre-processing'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Rarefies (subsamples) 16S rRNA ASV read count tables to a fixed depth so that differing library sizes across samples are corrected before differential abundance (DA) testing with rarefied tool variants. The paper applies this within its 14-tool DA comparison at a rarefaction depth of 2000, while acknowledging that rarefying is a heavily criticized, contentious preprocessing choice. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z

skills.description: Use when you have a sample × taxon count table (e.g. plant-species × arthropod-OTU from eDNA metabarcoding) and need a presence/absence-weighted dissimilarity matrix and clustered dendrogram/heatmap to test whether communities group by a categorical factor such as host plant species.
skills.name: raup-crick-dissimilarity-computation
skills.search_text: raup-crick-dissimilarity-computation Use when you have a sample × taxon count table (e.g. plant-species × arthropod-OTU from eDNA metabarcoding) and need a presence/absence-weighted dissimilarity matrix and clustered dendrogram/heatmap to test whether communities group by a categorical factor such as host plant species. The question requires ordination rather than clustering — this study complemented Raup–Crick/average-linkage clustering with RDA, which should be used when a constrained gradient analysis is needed. The abundance table has not been transformed and dominant taxa would overwhelm presence/absence-driven Raup–Crick dissimilarity — apply the cube-root transformation first. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an OTU count table; metabarcoding must be completed first. Computes Raup–Crick dissimilarity between community samples and builds an average-linkage (UPGMA) hierarchical clustering to test whether arthropod eDNA communities recovered from wild flowers segregate by plant species. In this workflow the plant-species × arthropod-OTU count table is cube-root transformed before clustering and rendered as a pheatmap dendrogram. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Computes Raup–Crick dissimilarity between community samples and builds an average-linkage (UPGMA) hierarchical clustering to test whether arthropod eDNA communities recovered from wild flowers segregate by plant species. In this workflow the plant-species × arthropod-OTU count table is cube-root transformed before clustering and rendered as a pheatmap dendrogram.

skills.description: Use when building a CO1 (or similar marker-gene) reference training set for the RDP classifier from NCBI/BOLD records — e.g. curating taxon lists, applying length/keyword filters, and generating FASTA + taxonomy files for classifier training.
skills.name: rdp-training-set-construction
skills.search_text: rdp-training-set-construction Use when building a CO1 (or similar marker-gene) reference training set for the RDP classifier from NCBI/BOLD records — e.g. curating taxon lists, applying length/keyword filters, and generating FASTA + taxonomy files for classifier training. Your goal is to classify query sequences with an already-trained classifier — the repository ships ready-trained rRNAClassifier.properties files and no further training is needed from the user. You need a fully representative reference database — only ~22% of extant Insecta genera have full-length species-rank CO1 barcodes in GenBank, and CO1 lacks a curated community-maintained database like SILVA or UNITE. Your queries are short fragments requiring species-rank calls — species-rank assignments lack a bootstrap cutoff achieving 99% correct assignments for many fragment lengths. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Assembles RDP classifier training sets for animal CO1 metabarcode taxonomic assignment by curating taxon lists from NCBI taxonomy, retrieving CO1 reference sequences from GenBank, filtering and contaminant-screening them, and writing reference FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Assembles RDP classifier training sets for animal CO1 metabarcode taxonomic assignment by curating taxon lists from NCBI taxonomy, retrieving CO1 reference sequences from GenBank, filtering and contaminant-screening them, and writing reference FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to classify query sequences with an already-trained classifier — the repository ships ready-trained rRNAClassifier.properties files and no further training is needed from the user. You need a fully representative reference database — only ~22% of extant Insecta genera have full-length species-rank CO1 barcodes in GenBank, and CO1 lacks a curated community-maintained database like SILVA or UNITE. Your queries are short fragments requiring species-rank calls — species-rank assignments lack a bootstrap cutoff achieving 99% correct assignments for many fragment lengths.

skills.description: Use when comparing eDNA metabarcoding read counts or MOTU richness across discrete sampling locations and you need a Poisson GLM framework with post-hoc Tukey contrasts (multcomp) to test pairwise differences.
skills.name: read-abundance-variance-stabilization
skills.search_text: read-abundance-variance-stabilization Use when comparing eDNA metabarcoding read counts or MOTU richness across discrete sampling locations and you need a Poisson GLM framework with post-hoc Tukey contrasts (multcomp) to test pairwise differences. Input is still raw sequencing output (FASTQ/aligned reads) rather than a collapsed per-location MOTU count table — upstream OBITools/sumaclust processing is required first The response variable is taxonomic assignment or diversity estimates unrelated to counts; the Poisson GLM and square-root transform target MOTU richness and read abundance specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Variance-stabilizing preprocessing and count-modeling step from Bakker et al. 2017 in which eDNA sequence read abundances are square-root transformed before being tested against location with a Poisson generalized linear model, alongside untransformed MOTU richness. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Variance-stabilizing preprocessing and count-modeling step from Bakker et al. 2017 in which eDNA sequence read abundances are square-root transformed before being tested against location with a Poisson generalized linear model, alongside untransformed MOTU richness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw sequencing output (FASTQ/aligned reads) rather than a collapsed per-location MOTU count table — upstream OBITools/sumaclust processing is required first The response variable is taxonomic assignment or diversity estimates unrelated to counts; the Poisson GLM and square-root transform target MOTU richness and read abundance specifically

skills.description: Use when MetaMaps (or a comparable long-read metagenomic classifier) output must be quality-checked against known ground truth, e.g. simulated data or mock communities, to quantify per-read assignment accuracy and composition fidelity.
skills.name: read-assignment-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: read-assignment-accuracy-evaluation Use when MetaMaps (or a comparable long-read metagenomic classifier) output must be quality-checked against known ground truth, e.g. simulated data or mock communities, to quantify per-read assignment accuracy and composition fidelity. Samples with no ground truth (novel environmental samples) — accuracy and r2 cannot be computed, only composition estimated Samples with a high proportion of short reads, which MetaMaps explicitly does not handle well (reads below the minimum length remain unassigned) Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities, where database-sample incongruity invalidates accuracy interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Evaluate MetaMaps classification quality by computing species-level read-assignment accuracy and sample-composition correlation (r2) from its EM classification outputs, e.g. when comparing default vs memory-efficient runs. This verifies that resource-saving modes do not degrade assignment accuracy. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2

skills.description: Use when running the nearinj/Comparison_of_DA_microbiome_methods pipeline on an unfiltered ASV count table where differing per-sample read depths must be equalized before DA testing, or when a rarefied input table (-R) is required by downstream tools.
skills.name: read-depth-threshold-filtering-16s
skills.search_text: read-depth-threshold-filtering-16s Use when running the nearinj/Comparison_of_DA_microbiome_methods pipeline on an unfiltered ASV count table where differing per-sample read depths must be equalized before DA testing, or when a rarefied input table (-R) is required by downstream tools. The downstream analysis is computing diversity metrics or other uses of rarefying — the authors state that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work'. The DA tool explicitly requires absolute, un-rarefied count tables — e.g. the ANCOM documentation warns the input 'is the **absolute** abundance table, do not transform it to **relative** abundance table'. No samples fall below the depth threshold and no filtering is needed — run the no-filtering form 'run_all_tools.sh -A ASV_TABLE.tsv -G METADATA_FILE.tsv -O OUTPUT_FOLDER -R RARIFIED_ASV_TABLE.tsv' instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Filter 16S rRNA ASV count tables by a per-sample read-depth threshold (D = 2000 in the manuscript) and rarefy retained samples to that common depth with the GUniFrac R package, producing the rarefied table consumed by depth-sensitive differential abundance tools such as LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Filter 16S rRNA ASV count tables by a per-sample read-depth threshold (D = 2000 in the manuscript) and rarefy retained samples to that common depth with the GUniFrac R package, producing the rarefied table consumed by depth-sensitive differential abundance tools such as LEfSe and MaAsLin2 (rare).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream analysis is computing diversity metrics or other uses of rarefying — the authors state that 'whether rarefying is advisable for other analyses, such as prior to computing diversity metrics, is beyond the scope of this work'. The DA tool explicitly requires absolute, un-rarefied count tables — e.g. the ANCOM documentation warns the input 'is the **absolute** abundance table, do not transform it to **relative** abundance table'. No samples fall below the depth threshold and no filtering is needed — run the no-filtering form 'run_all_tools.sh -A ASV_TABLE.tsv -G METADATA_FILE.tsv -O OUTPUT_FOLDER -R RARIFIED_ASV_TABLE.tsv' instead.

skills.description: Use when you have MetaMaps per-read mappings of long reads (e.g., HMP7 PacBio/ONT data) against an annotated reference database and need read counts per gene or COG functional category.
skills.name: read-gene-overlap-counting
skills.search_text: read-gene-overlap-counting Use when you have MetaMaps per-read mappings of long reads (e.g., HMP7 PacBio/ONT data) against an annotated reference database and need read counts per gene or COG functional category. The sample has a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small for reliable mapping and end up unassigned The goal is taxonomic composition alone (the WIMP/EM output already gives sample composition; gene-level intersection is unnecessary) The reference database genes lack functional annotations (no COG/gene intervals to intersect against) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Intersects per-read mapping coordinates from MetaMaps long-read metagenomic classification with annotated gene intervals (e.g., eggNOG-mapper COG categories) to aggregate read counts per gene and rank functional categories by abundance. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Intersects per-read mapping coordinates from MetaMaps long-read metagenomic classification with annotated gene intervals (e.g., eggNOG-mapper COG categories) to aggregate read counts per gene and rank functional categories by abundance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample has a high proportion of short reads — reads below the minimum length get minimizer sets too small for reliable mapping and end up unassigned The goal is taxonomic composition alone (the WIMP/EM output already gives sample composition; gene-level intersection is unnecessary) The reference database genes lack functional annotations (no COG/gene intervals to intersect against)

skills.description: Use when you have paired read-level dissimilarity values (e.g., MSD and BLD from HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTUs) and weak read-level correlations, and you need to test whether per-OTU mean aggregation reveals stronger metric concordance.
skills.name: read-level-to-otu-level-aggregation
skills.search_text: read-level-to-otu-level-aggregation Use when you have paired read-level dissimilarity values (e.g., MSD and BLD from HMP V1V3/V3V5 OTUs) and weak read-level correlations, and you need to test whether per-OTU mean aggregation reveals stronger metric concordance. Input is already aggregated to OTU-level means with no read-to-representative dissimilarity pairs available to recompute the read-level baseline. The goal is to build or re-cluster OTUs from sequence similarity rather than to evaluate how dissimilarity metrics (MSD vs BLD) behave across existing OTUs. You need a per-sequence evolutionary divergence measure itself; this skill only correlates and aggregates existing MSD/BLD values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates per-read dissimilarity pairs (MSD and BLD, computed between each OTU representative sequence and its member sequences) to per-OTU means and recomputes Pearson correlations, because OTU-level aggregation strengthens the observed MSD–BLD relationship and exposes evolutionary divergence that MSD underestimates. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Aggregates per-read dissimilarity pairs (MSD and BLD, computed between each OTU representative sequence and its member sequences) to per-OTU means and recomputes Pearson correlations, because OTU-level aggregation strengthens the observed MSD–BLD relationship and exposes evolutionary divergence that MSD underestimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aggregated to OTU-level means with no read-to-representative dissimilarity pairs available to recompute the read-level baseline. The goal is to build or re-cluster OTUs from sequence similarity rather than to evaluate how dissimilarity metrics (MSD vs BLD) behave across existing OTUs. You need a per-sequence evolutionary divergence measure itself; this skill only correlates and aggregates existing MSD/BLD values.

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. metaHIT gut survey samples) need taxonomic classification against reference databases after QC and before or alongside assembly-based binning.

skills.search_text: reference-based-taxonomic-profiling Use when quality-filtered paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. metaHIT gut survey samples) need taxonomic classification against reference databases after QC and before or alongside assembly-based binning. Input reads have not passed quality control (adapters, low-quality reads, phix and host contamination still present) The goal is bin reconstruction or genome-resolved analysis rather than read-level taxonomic classification (use the coverage-based binning route with MetaBAT/MaxBin instead) Data are 16S rRNA amplicon sequences rather than shotgun metagenomic reads (use the mothur/dada2 amplicon workflow) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads against curated reference databases (kraken2, MetaPhlAn2, DIAMOND/NR, MEGAN) as part of the best-practice metagenomics workflow, and extends to functional profiling with HUMAnN2. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bib/bbz155
skills.summary: Classifies quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads against curated reference databases (kraken2, MetaPhlAn2, DIAMOND/NR, MEGAN) as part of the best-practice metagenomics workflow, and extends to functional profiling with HUMAnN2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not passed quality control (adapters, low-quality reads, phix and host contamination still present) The goal is bin reconstruction or genome-resolved analysis rather than read-level taxonomic classification (use the coverage-based binning route with MetaBAT/MaxBin instead) Data are 16S rRNA amplicon sequences rather than shotgun metagenomic reads (use the mothur/dada2 amplicon workflow)

skills.summary: Benchmark MAPseq (v1.2.6) reference-based rRNA classification by comparing its taxonomy and hierarchical OTU (hOTU, 98% identity) assignments on reads of known identity against baseline tools, scoring each with the F½ metric.

skills.search_text: reference-database-fasta-processing Use when a taxonomic-resolution or primer-bias comparison requires excising sub-region 16S amplicons (e.g., V4, V3-V5) in silico from a full-length reference FASTA using known primer-binding sites.
