skills.description: Use when a MetaMaps (MashMap-based) approximate mapping step has produced candidate mapping locations per long read and each candidate must be scored probabilistically to obtain mapping qualities and disambiguate alternative locations.
skills.name: reference-database-minimizer-scoring
skills.search_text: reference-database-minimizer-scoring Use when a MetaMaps (MashMap-based) approximate mapping step has produced candidate mapping locations per long read and each candidate must be scored probabilistically to obtain mapping qualities and disambiguate alternative locations. Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the chosen minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine their mapping locations Only a compositional profile is needed and per-read positional/quality information is irrelevant — k-mer-spectra methods may suffice Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities, where database-sample incongruity dominates and the model lacks an explicit genomic-divergence term http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Scores each candidate long-read mapping location from the minimizer-based approximate mapping stage using a binomial model of shared MinHash intersections, converting per-location probabilities into normalized posterior mapping qualities that sum to 1 per read (as implemented in MetaMaps' second stage). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Scores each candidate long-read mapping location from the minimizer-based approximate mapping stage using a binomial model of shared MinHash intersections, converting per-location probabilities into normalized posterior mapping qualities that sum to 1 per read (as implemented in MetaMaps' second stage).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a high proportion of short reads: reads below the chosen minimum length end up with minimizer sets too small to reliably determine their mapping locations Only a compositional profile is needed and per-read positional/quality information is irrelevant — k-mer-spectra methods may suffice Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities, where database-sample incongruity dominates and the model lacks an explicit genomic-divergence term

skills.description: Use when building taxonomic classifiers for amplicon ASV/OTU queries where species-level accuracy depends on reference class priors — e.g., importing Greengenes 99% reference data into QIIME 2 and assembling EMPO 3 habitat-specific or uniform class_weight inputs for fit-classifier-naive-bayes.
skills.name: reference-database-preprocessing
skills.search_text: reference-database-preprocessing Use when building taxonomic classifiers for amplicon ASV/OTU queries where species-level accuracy depends on reference class priors — e.g., importing Greengenes 99% reference data into QIIME 2 and assembling EMPO 3 habitat-specific or uniform class_weight inputs for fit-classifier-naive-bayes. Ready-made pretrained classifiers for the sample habitat (e.g., animal-distal-gut, soil-non-saline, human-stool) already exist on Zenodo — download them instead of retraining The query data are metagenomic profiles (MetaPhlAn2-style) rather than 16S marker-gene amplicon sequences, since clawback weights are built from marker-gene sample distributions The sample environment lacks sufficient characterization to assemble bespoke weights and no matching readytowear weights exist — use global average weights instead of forcing habitat-specific preparation http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Prepare reference sequence/taxonomy data (e.g., Greengenes 99% OTUs) and environment-specific taxonomic class weights so that a multinomial naive Bayes classifier (scikit-learn MultinomialNB via q2-feature-classifier) can be trained once with bespoke EMPO 3 habitat weights and once with uniform weights for controlled comparison. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: Prepare reference sequence/taxonomy data (e.g., Greengenes 99% OTUs) and environment-specific taxonomic class weights so that a multinomial naive Bayes classifier (scikit-learn MultinomialNB via q2-feature-classifier) can be trained once with bespoke EMPO 3 habitat weights and once with uniform weights for controlled comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ready-made pretrained classifiers for the sample habitat (e.g., animal-distal-gut, soil-non-saline, human-stool) already exist on Zenodo — download them instead of retraining The query data are metagenomic profiles (MetaPhlAn2-style) rather than 16S marker-gene amplicon sequences, since clawback weights are built from marker-gene sample distributions The sample environment lacks sufficient characterization to assemble bespoke weights and no matching readytowear weights exist — use global average weights instead of forcing habitat-specific preparation

skills.description: Use when you have a set of exact amplicon sequences (e.g., Deblur 90-bp V4 tags) and want to compute what fraction of a reference database's sequences they exactly match, or conversely what fraction of your sequences hit the references.
skills.name: reference-database-recapture-analysis
skills.search_text: reference-database-recapture-analysis Use when you have a set of exact amplicon sequences (e.g., Deblur 90-bp V4 tags) and want to compute what fraction of a reference database's sequences they exactly match, or conversely what fraction of your sequences hit the references. Your query sequences are partial-length or expected to differ from references — a 100% similarity global alignment will grossly undercount recapture; use a similarity-threshold or closed-reference OTU picking workflow instead Your sequences have not been error-corrected to exact sequence variants (e.g., raw denoised reads or clustered OTUs), since the recaptured fraction is defined against exact Deblur-derived tag sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Quantifies how much of the unique sequence diversity in existing 16S rRNA reference databases (Greengenes 13.8, SILVA 128) is recaptured by a set of exact environmental sequences — here the EMP Deblur 90-bp V4 tag sequences — via VSEARCH global alignment at 100% similarity. It measures overlap between an exact-sequence catalogue and full-length references without OTU clustering. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of the unique sequence diversity in existing 16S rRNA reference databases (Greengenes 13.8, SILVA 128) is recaptured by a set of exact environmental sequences — here the EMP Deblur 90-bp V4 tag sequences — via VSEARCH global alignment at 100% similarity. It measures overlap between an exact-sequence catalogue and full-length references without OTU clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your query sequences are partial-length or expected to differ from references — a 100% similarity global alignment will grossly undercount recapture; use a similarity-threshold or closed-reference OTU picking workflow instead Your sequences have not been error-corrected to exact sequence variants (e.g., raw denoised reads or clustered OTUs), since the recaptured fraction is defined against exact Deblur-derived tag sequences

skills.description: Use when comparing classifier training sets by taxonomic breadth and database size, or when verifying a published claim like '>3x taxonomic coverage' or 'almost five times as many reference sequences' from raw taxonomy/FASTA files.
skills.name: reference-database-sequence-counting
skills.search_text: reference-database-sequence-counting Use when comparing classifier training sets by taxonomic breadth and database size, or when verifying a published claim like '>3x taxonomic coverage' or 'almost five times as many reference sequences' from raw taxonomy/FASTA files. The goal is to measure classification accuracy or error rates — use leave-one-out or 5-fold cross-validation with bootstrap support cutoffs instead of counting reference records The goal is to actually classify query CO1 sequences — run the RDP classifier with the trained rRNAClassifier.properties file rather than parsing the training files The comparison must be between two recent versions with documented summary statistics (e.g. v4 vs v5 in the README already reports sequence/taxa/species deltas), so recounting from scratch adds little http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Quantifies taxonomic coverage and reference sequence counts of CO1 classifier training sets by parsing their taxonomy and FASTA files, enabling head-to-head verification of coverage claims (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1 vs the March 2013 Insecta Genbank-Genus set from Porter et al. 2014). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Quantifies taxonomic coverage and reference sequence counts of CO1 classifier training sets by parsing their taxonomy and FASTA files, enabling head-to-head verification of coverage claims (e.g. CO1 Eukaryote v1 vs the March 2013 Insecta Genbank-Genus set from Porter et al. 2014).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure classification accuracy or error rates — use leave-one-out or 5-fold cross-validation with bootstrap support cutoffs instead of counting reference records The goal is to actually classify query CO1 sequences — run the RDP classifier with the trained rRNAClassifier.properties file rather than parsing the training files The comparison must be between two recent versions with documented summary statistics (e.g. v4 vs v5 in the README already reports sequence/taxa/species deltas), so recounting from scratch adds little

skills.description: Use when a rebuilt CO1 Eukaryote training set (Arthropoda, Chordata, outgroups) must be checked against a published GitHub/Zenodo release to confirm the reference FASTA and RDP taxonomy files are correctly reconstructed before training or reuse.
skills.name: reference-database-validation-against-deposit
skills.search_text: reference-database-validation-against-deposit Use when a rebuilt CO1 Eukaryote training set (Arthropoda, Chordata, outgroups) must be checked against a published GitHub/Zenodo release to confirm the reference FASTA and RDP taxonomy files are correctly reconstructed before training or reuse. The goal is classifier performance evaluation (leave-one-out testing, cross-validation, bootstrap cutoff calibration) rather than verifying the training-set files themselves Input is a set of query metabarcoding reads to be taxonomically assigned — use the trained classifier directly instead of validating reference files The deposit under comparison is a later version (v3/v4/v5) whose construction differs, e.g. GenBank records filtered for no nucleotide ambiguities and BOLD BIN consolidation with newer Linnean binomials — comparisons across versions will not match http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Validates a reconstructed CO1 reference training set (reference FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files) by downloading the authors' deposited release from the terrimporter/CO1Classifier GitHub repository and diffing sequence identifiers, taxonomic lineages, and rank structure against the reconstruction. This closes the reproduction loop for the CO1 Eukaryote v1 (genus-rank) and v2 (species-rank) RDP classifier training sets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Validates a reconstructed CO1 reference training set (reference FASTA plus RDP taxonomy files) by downloading the authors' deposited release from the terrimporter/CO1Classifier GitHub repository and diffing sequence identifiers, taxonomic lineages, and rank structure against the reconstruction. This closes the reproduction loop for the CO1 Eukaryote v1 (genus-rank) and v2 (species-rank) RDP classifier training sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classifier performance evaluation (leave-one-out testing, cross-validation, bootstrap cutoff calibration) rather than verifying the training-set files themselves Input is a set of query metabarcoding reads to be taxonomically assigned — use the trained classifier directly instead of validating reference files The deposit under comparison is a later version (v3/v4/v5) whose construction differs, e.g. GenBank records filtered for no nucleotide ambiguities and BOLD BIN consolidation with newer Linnean binomials — comparisons across versions will not match

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a FASTQ preprocessing tool: you have paired-end (PE150) FASTQ files from multiple filter tools plus a raw baseline, and need alignment-based metrics (mismatches, clips, single-read maps) against a reference genome to rank the filters.
skills.name: reference-genome-indexing-and-mapping
skills.search_text: reference-genome-indexing-and-mapping Decision support for choosing a FASTQ preprocessing tool: you have paired-end (PE150) FASTQ files from multiple filter tools plus a raw baseline, and need alignment-based metrics (mismatches, clips, single-read maps) against a reference genome to rank the filters. Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the fastp ecosystem explicitly redirects such data to fastplong and BWA-MEM is not the appropriate aligner Your goal is to assess filtering speed or tool runtime alone; the fastp paper benchmarks speed separately (fastp is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic/Cutadapt) without requiring alignment You lack a paired reference genome/aligner setup and only need per-file QC; fastp's built-in JSON/HTML quality profiling covers before/after filtering without mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Align gzip-compressed paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. tool-filtered or raw NS_PE150 data) to the hg19 reference genome with BWA-MEM, then sort, index, and evaluate the BAM with Samtools to quantify mapping quality. This skill underpins tool-comparison benchmarks by converting preprocessing quality into measurable alignment statistics. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Align gzip-compressed paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. tool-filtered or raw NS_PE150 data) to the hg19 reference genome with BWA-MEM, then sort, index, and evaluate the BAM with Samtools to quantify mapping quality. This skill underpins tool-comparison benchmarks by converting preprocessing quality into measurable alignment statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the fastp ecosystem explicitly redirects such data to fastplong and BWA-MEM is not the appropriate aligner Your goal is to assess filtering speed or tool runtime alone; the fastp paper benchmarks speed separately (fastp is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic/Cutadapt) without requiring alignment You lack a paired reference genome/aligner setup and only need per-file QC; fastp's built-in JSON/HTML quality profiling covers before/after filtering without mapping

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) on 16S amplicon mock community data and you need the specific reference indices each profiler–library pairing requires.
skills.name: reference-library-configuration-for-profiler-pairings
skills.search_text: reference-library-configuration-for-profiler-pairings Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2) on 16S amplicon mock community data and you need the specific reference indices each profiler–library pairing requires. Input is already a taxonomic feature table or counts matrix — reference library configuration is upstream of profiling Your profiling targets shotgun metagenomic samples other than 16S mock communities; library preparation and classifier training choices (e.g. region-specific naïve Bayes training) may not transfer You need the newest Greengenes2 or SILVA 138.1 releases — the paper used Greengenes 13_8 (August 2013) and pinned SILVA 138 indices, and Greengenes2 was released only amidst review http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Acquire and configure the correct version-matched reference library (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq 2018/2020) for each profiler in a 16S taxonomic-profiling benchmark, so that every pipeline–library pairing yields a comparable taxon-by-sample counts matrix. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Acquire and configure the correct version-matched reference library (SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, Kraken Standard, RefSeq 2018/2020) for each profiler in a 16S taxonomic-profiling benchmark, so that every pipeline–library pairing yields a comparable taxon-by-sample counts matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomic feature table or counts matrix — reference library configuration is upstream of profiling Your profiling targets shotgun metagenomic samples other than 16S mock communities; library preparation and classifier training choices (e.g. region-specific naïve Bayes training) may not transfer You need the newest Greengenes2 or SILVA 138.1 releases — the paper used Greengenes 13_8 (August 2013) and pinned SILVA 138 indices, and Greengenes2 was released only amidst review

skills.description: Use when deciding whether a full-length rRNA reference database can be made smaller by removing near-identical sequences, and you need to measure the resulting cost in mapping/classification accuracy against ground-truth assignments.
skills.name: reference-sensitivity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: reference-sensitivity-benchmarking Use when deciding whether a full-length rRNA reference database can be made smaller by removing near-identical sequences, and you need to measure the resulting cost in mapping/classification accuracy against ground-truth assignments. The goal is general classification performance rather than sensitivity to reference database composition — use the paper's main benchmark with the full default reference instead. Reads lack ground-truth assignments; F½ accuracy against known identities cannot be computed, so the benchmark is not meaningful. The reference database is a marker set other than full-length rRNA sequences (e.g. protein or functional databases); the redundancy-reduction trade-off was established for rRNA references only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Quantifies how trimming near-identical sequences from a full-length rRNA reference database degrades read-classification accuracy (F½ score) for MAPseq and competing tools, exposing the redundancy-vs-accuracy trade-off (Fig. 1g-h, Supplementary Fig. S2). metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Quantifies how trimming near-identical sequences from a full-length rRNA reference database degrades read-classification accuracy (F½ score) for MAPseq and competing tools, exposing the redundancy-vs-accuracy trade-off (Fig. 1g-h, Supplementary Fig. S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general classification performance rather than sensitivity to reference database composition — use the paper's main benchmark with the full default reference instead. Reads lack ground-truth assignments; F½ accuracy against known identities cannot be computed, so the benchmark is not meaningful. The reference database is a marker set other than full-length rRNA sequences (e.g. protein or functional databases); the redundancy-reduction trade-off was established for rRNA references only.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether OTU mapping results depend on the choice of reference OTU set — e.g., replacing MAPseq's default hOTU reference with UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs built at the paper's identity thresholds.
skills.name: reference-set-sensitivity-comparison
skills.search_text: reference-set-sensitivity-comparison Use when you need to test whether OTU mapping results depend on the choice of reference OTU set — e.g., replacing MAPseq's default hOTU reference with UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs built at the paper's identity thresholds. Input is already an OTU abundance feature table — this skill requires re-running the mapping step against alternative references from raw demultiplexed reads The analysis goal is taxonomic classification accuracy (F½ score) rather than between-run consistency of OTU mapping across reference sets Only a single run/sample is available — between-run Spearman/Pearson correlations and Jaccard overlaps require multiple runs to pair http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A benchmarking skill that quantifies how swapping the OTU reference set (e.g., the default pre-clustered hOTU reference vs. ab initio UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs) changes between-run consistency of MAPseq OTU mapping, measured as pairwise between-run Spearman/Pearson abundance correlations and Jaccard overlaps of detected OTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that quantifies how swapping the OTU reference set (e.g., the default pre-clustered hOTU reference vs. ab initio UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs) changes between-run consistency of MAPseq OTU mapping, measured as pairwise between-run Spearman/Pearson abundance correlations and Jaccard overlaps of detected OTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an OTU abundance feature table — this skill requires re-running the mapping step against alternative references from raw demultiplexed reads The analysis goal is taxonomic classification accuracy (F½ score) rather than between-run consistency of OTU mapping across reference sets Only a single run/sample is available — between-run Spearman/Pearson correlations and Jaccard overlaps require multiple runs to pair

skills.description: Use when short 16S amplicon reads (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5) clustered into OTUs by PSD at 97% sequence similarity need per-read phylogenetic placement on a fixed reference tree to test representative-based annotation.
skills.name: reference-tree-construction
skills.search_text: reference-tree-construction Use when short 16S amplicon reads (e.g. HMP V1V3/V3V5) clustered into OTUs by PSD at 97% sequence similarity need per-read phylogenetic placement on a fixed reference tree to test representative-based annotation. When the input is already a feature/OTU table without the underlying sequence reads — placement requires individual read sequences When the analysis goal is OTU clustering itself rather than auditing representative-based OTU annotation (use PSD/MSD/BLD dissimilarity analyses instead) When reads are full-length 16S sequences that can be aligned directly into the reference alignment without fragment-aware placement http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3300 Build a fixed 16S rRNA reference tree and alignment using the RAxML/PASTA/FastTree 2 lineage of reference-tree construction, then use it as the backbone for short-amplicon read placement via SEPP and pplacer to evaluate per-read taxonomic assignments inside 97% PSD OTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Build a fixed 16S rRNA reference tree and alignment using the RAxML/PASTA/FastTree 2 lineage of reference-tree construction, then use it as the backbone for short-amplicon read placement via SEPP and pplacer to evaluate per-read taxonomic assignments inside 97% PSD OTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a feature/OTU table without the underlying sequence reads — placement requires individual read sequences When the analysis goal is OTU clustering itself rather than auditing representative-based OTU annotation (use PSD/MSD/BLD dissimilarity analyses instead) When reads are full-length 16S sequences that can be aligned directly into the reference alignment without fragment-aware placement

skills.description: Use when a taxa x time-point read-proportion table from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing contains taxa detected at several genetic loci, and you need an amplification-bias-insensitive relative abundance index per taxon per time point.
skills.name: relative-abundance-aggregation-across-loci
skills.search_text: relative-abundance-aggregation-across-loci Use when a taxa x time-point read-proportion table from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing contains taxa detected at several genetic loci, and you need an amplification-bias-insensitive relative abundance index per taxon per time point. Input is already a normalized, zero-to-one-scaled relative abundance index — re-applying the within-taxon max division would flatten true abundance variation. Each taxon is detected by only a single locus, so there is nothing to ensemble-average; use the per-locus index directly. The goal is absolute organismal abundance: the index captures only proportional changes, since amplification biases and variable template abundances mean read proportions do not equal organismal abundance. http://edamontology.org/topic_3959 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Constructs an ensemble per-taxon abundance index from multilocus eDNA metabarcoding time-series data by within-taxon, within-locus zero-to-one scaling of read proportions followed by averaging across loci. This mitigates taxon-specific amplification bias so proportional abundance changes across the 8 Monterey Bay sampling time points can be compared. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Constructs an ensemble per-taxon abundance index from multilocus eDNA metabarcoding time-series data by within-taxon, within-locus zero-to-one scaling of read proportions followed by averaging across loci. This mitigates taxon-specific amplification bias so proportional abundance changes across the 8 Monterey Bay sampling time points can be compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized, zero-to-one-scaled relative abundance index — re-applying the within-taxon max division would flatten true abundance variation. Each taxon is detected by only a single locus, so there is nothing to ensemble-average; use the per-locus index directly. The goal is absolute organismal abundance: the index captures only proportional changes, since amplification biases and variable template abundances mean read proportions do not equal organismal abundance.

skills.description: Use when computing taxon detection sensitivity for 16S amplicon mock communities (e.g., the 136-sample benchmark of DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 against SILVA/Greengenes/Kraken Standard/RefSeq libraries) and low-abundance ground-truth taxa must be excluded via a >=0.
skills.name: relative-abundance-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: relative-abundance-threshold-filtering Use when computing taxon detection sensitivity for 16S amplicon mock communities (e.g., the 136-sample benchmark of DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 against SILVA/Greengenes/Kraken Standard/RefSeq libraries) and low-abundance ground-truth taxa must be excluded via a >=0. The input is raw 16S FASTQ reads rather than a taxon counts matrix paired with a mock community ground-truth composition table The goal is read assignment specificity, which is computed as the fraction of reads assigned to expected taxa and does not apply the 0.1% ground-truth abundance cutoff The dataset lacks a synthetic mock community with known composition, so no ground-truth abundance threshold can be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Filters the mock-community ground-truth taxa to those present at >=0.1% relative abundance before computing per-sample taxon detection sensitivity, so sensitivity is judged against taxa that are reliably expected rather than against trace-level components distorted by experimental noise. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Filters the mock-community ground-truth taxa to those present at >=0.1% relative abundance before computing per-sample taxon detection sensitivity, so sensitivity is judged against taxa that are reliably expected rather than against trace-level components distorted by experimental noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw 16S FASTQ reads rather than a taxon counts matrix paired with a mock community ground-truth composition table The goal is read assignment specificity, which is computed as the fraction of reads assigned to expected taxa and does not apply the 0.1% ground-truth abundance cutoff The dataset lacks a synthetic mock community with known composition, so no ground-truth abundance threshold can be defined

skills.description: Use when you have a DADA2-derived ASV abundance table for a mock community with known composition and need to quantify how observed relative read abundances deviate from expected taxon proportions.
skills.name: relative-read-abundance-computation
skills.search_text: relative-read-abundance-computation Use when you have a DADA2-derived ASV abundance table for a mock community with known composition and need to quantify how observed relative read abundances deviate from expected taxon proportions. Input is raw sequencing reads or pre-denoising data — the skill operates on final ASV tables produced after DADA2 denoising, quality filtering, and chimera removal Samples are environmental/natural communities with no known ground-truth composition — there is no expected composition to join against You need absolute taxon abundances rather than within-sample relative read abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compute per-taxon relative read abundances from dadasnake/DADA2 ASV tables of mock community runs (prokaryotic ERR777696, fungal PRJNA626434) and compare them against ground-truth community compositions to assess whether read abundances reflect true taxon abundances. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Compute per-taxon relative read abundances from dadasnake/DADA2 ASV tables of mock community runs (prokaryotic ERR777696, fungal PRJNA626434) and compare them against ground-truth community compositions to assess whether read abundances reflect true taxon abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or pre-denoising data — the skill operates on final ASV tables produced after DADA2 denoising, quality filtering, and chimera removal Samples are environmental/natural communities with no known ground-truth composition — there is no expected composition to join against You need absolute taxon abundances rather than within-sample relative read abundances

skills.description: Use when a prediction task over high-dimensional feature tables (e.g., Deblur BIOM counts vs. EMPO labels) needs a rigorous out-of-fold accuracy estimate rather than a single train/test split.

skills.search_text: repeated-cross-validation-model-evaluation Use when a prediction task over high-dimensional feature tables (e.g., Deblur BIOM counts vs. EMPO labels) needs a rigorous out-of-fold accuracy estimate rather than a single train/test split. The question is unsupervised structure discovery (e.g., beta-diversity ordination) with no labelled response variable The feature table has not been preprocessed to match the training distribution (e.g., unrarefied counts or chloroplast sequences retained), making accuracy estimates incomparable to the reported benchmarks Sample size per class is too small for 10-fold stratification, so fold-wise label imbalance invalidates the accuracy comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Evaluates supervised classifiers (e.g., random forest on EMP microbial community features) using repeated k-fold cross-validation and reports confusion-matrix-based accuracy against published reference values. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Evaluates supervised classifiers (e.g., random forest on EMP microbial community features) using repeated k-fold cross-validation and reports confusion-matrix-based accuracy against published reference values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is unsupervised structure discovery (e.g., beta-diversity ordination) with no labelled response variable The feature table has not been preprocessed to match the training distribution (e.g., unrarefied counts or chloroplast sequences retained), making accuracy estimates incomparable to the reported benchmarks Sample size per class is too small for 10-fold stratification, so fold-wise label imbalance invalidates the accuracy comparison

skills.description: Use when you have an ASV-by-sample-by-replicate occurrence table with read counts and need replicate-level abundance values to apply low-frequency-noise (LNF) cutoffs before filtering occurrences.
skills.name: replicate-level-abundance-computation
skills.search_text: replicate-level-abundance-computation Use when you have an ASV-by-sample-by-replicate occurrence table with read counts and need replicate-level abundance values to apply low-frequency-noise (LNF) cutoffs before filtering occurrences. Input is already a filtered occurrence table or an ASV table without replicate-level read counts, so Nijk/Njk and Nijk/Ni cannot be computed The analysis goal is PCR-error removal rather than low-frequency-noise removal — FilterPCRerror discards occurrences by ASV match/read-count comparisons, not by abundance cutoffs http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-occurrence abundance metrics (absolute read count Nijk, relative abundance within sample-replicate Nijk/Njk, and relative abundance within ASV Nijk/Ni) from the ASV occurrence table, which underpin VTAM's FilterLNF low-frequency-noise removal. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Computes per-occurrence abundance metrics (absolute read count Nijk, relative abundance within sample-replicate Nijk/Njk, and relative abundance within ASV Nijk/Ni) from the ASV occurrence table, which underpin VTAM's FilterLNF low-frequency-noise removal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered occurrence table or an ASV table without replicate-level read counts, so Nijk/Njk and Nijk/Ni cannot be computed The analysis goal is PCR-error removal rather than low-frequency-noise removal — FilterPCRerror discards occurrences by ASV match/read-count comparisons, not by abundance cutoffs

skills.description: Use when reproducing published sequencing-depth and ASV/taxonomy counts from a 16S rRNA amplicon study — e.g., validating ~100,000 reads/sample, 1,568,227 ASVs per region, and 114 taxonomies from deposited FASTQ files.
skills.name: reported-results-reproduction-from-publication
skills.search_text: reported-results-reproduction-from-publication Use when reproducing published sequencing-depth and ASV/taxonomy counts from a 16S rRNA amplicon study — e.g., validating ~100,000 reads/sample, 1,568,227 ASVs per region, and 114 taxonomies from deposited FASTQ files. Raw FASTQ files or pipeline code are not deposited in a public repository, so the reported counts can only be transcribed from the paper rather than reproduced The goal is a new biological comparison (e.g., alpha-diversity or NMDS testing between regions) rather than validating the paper's reported read-depth and ASV/taxonomy tallies Input is already a denoised ASV/feature table — re-running the FastQC/Deblur chain would not validate the reported per-sample sequencing depth http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Reproduces a 16S rRNA amplicon study's reported preprocessing statistics — per-sample sequencing depth after Q30 filtering, ASV counts per hypervariable region, and genus-level taxonomy counts — by re-running FastQC, Deblur, and Greengenes-based assignment on the deposited FASTQ files and diffing the recomputed tallies against the published figures. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Reproduces a 16S rRNA amplicon study's reported preprocessing statistics — per-sample sequencing depth after Q30 filtering, ASV counts per hypervariable region, and genus-level taxonomy counts — by re-running FastQC, Deblur, and Greengenes-based assignment on the deposited FASTQ files and diffing the recomputed tallies against the published figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw FASTQ files or pipeline code are not deposited in a public repository, so the reported counts can only be transcribed from the paper rather than reproduced The goal is a new biological comparison (e.g., alpha-diversity or NMDS testing between regions) rather than validating the paper's reported read-depth and ASV/taxonomy tallies Input is already a denoised ASV/feature table — re-running the FastQC/Deblur chain would not validate the reported per-sample sequencing depth

skills.description: Use when a paper reports specific correlation coefficients between community subnetwork properties (e.g., taxon richness of WGCNA subnetworks) and environmental time-series (e.g., chlorophyll a, sea surface temperature) and the task is to independently reproduce those exact statistics.
skills.name: reported-statistic-reproduction-verification
skills.search_text: reported-statistic-reproduction-verification Use when a paper reports specific correlation coefficients between community subnetwork properties (e.g., taxon richness of WGCNA subnetworks) and environmental time-series (e.g., chlorophyll a, sea surface temperature) and the task is to independently reproduce those exact statistics. The upstream WGCNA subnetwork memberships have not yet been computed — compute the subnetworks first via the community-network-analysis skill before correlating richness with environmental variables. The goal is exploratory identification of new correlations rather than verification of pre-specified published statistics; then a full exploratory correlation matrix with multiple-testing correction is more appropriate. The environmental and richness tables are not sample-aligned (e.g., different sampling dates or missing SST/chlorophyll a records), which would invalidate the rank correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Recompute the Monterey Bay eDNA subnetwork-environment Spearman correlations (grey vs chlorophyll a; blue vs sea surface temperature) from the WGCNA subnetwork membership and richness tables and verify the reproduced r and p values against the published statistics (r = -0.76, p = 0.03; r = 0.74, p = 0.04). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Recompute the Monterey Bay eDNA subnetwork-environment Spearman correlations (grey vs chlorophyll a; blue vs sea surface temperature) from the WGCNA subnetwork membership and richness tables and verify the reproduced r and p values against the published statistics (r = -0.76, p = 0.03; r = 0.74, p = 0.04).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The upstream WGCNA subnetwork memberships have not yet been computed — compute the subnetworks first via the community-network-analysis skill before correlating richness with environmental variables. The goal is exploratory identification of new correlations rather than verification of pre-specified published statistics; then a full exploratory correlation matrix with multiple-testing correction is more appropriate. The environmental and richness tables are not sample-aligned (e.g., different sampling dates or missing SST/chlorophyll a records), which would invalidate the rank correlation.

skills.description: Use when auditing OTU compactness: given HMP-style OTUs clustered with PSD at a 97% sequence similarity threshold (V1V3 and/or V3V5 16S regions) plus taxonomic assignments, to compute per-OTU MSD and BLD and detect taxa (e.g. TM7, Cyanobacteria, Lactobacillus, Staphylococcus) whose OTUs exceed a 0.
skills.name: representative-sequence-dissimilarity-profiling
skills.search_text: representative-sequence-dissimilarity-profiling Use when auditing OTU compactness: given HMP-style OTUs clustered with PSD at a 97% sequence similarity threshold (V1V3 and/or V3V5 16S regions) plus taxonomic assignments, to compute per-OTU MSD and BLD and detect taxa (e.g. TM7, Cyanobacteria, Lactobacillus, Staphylococcus) whose OTUs exceed a 0. OTUs were not built with percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) clustering at the 97% threshold — compactness re-measurement of representative-vs-member distances is not the appropriate audit The analysis goal is clustering or de novo OTU generation itself rather than quality assessment of existing OTUs; use QIIME/mothur clustering workflows instead No representative sequence or per-OTU member memberships are available (e.g. only a collapsed feature table), so MSD/BLD against the representative cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Quantifies how 'compact' 16S rRNA OTUs are by computing MSD (mean sequence dissimilarity) and BLD (branch length distance) between each OTU's representative sequence and every remaining member sequence, then aggregating these distances per taxon and per 16S hypervariable region (V1V3 vs V3V5) to expose taxon-specific clustering quality of the 97% PSD HMP OTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: Quantifies how 'compact' 16S rRNA OTUs are by computing MSD (mean sequence dissimilarity) and BLD (branch length distance) between each OTU's representative sequence and every remaining member sequence, then aggregating these distances per taxon and per 16S hypervariable region (V1V3 vs V3V5) to expose taxon-specific clustering quality of the 97% PSD HMP OTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: OTUs were not built with percent sequence dissimilarity (PSD) clustering at the 97% threshold — compactness re-measurement of representative-vs-member distances is not the appropriate audit The analysis goal is clustering or de novo OTU generation itself rather than quality assessment of existing OTUs; use QIIME/mothur clustering workflows instead No representative sequence or per-OTU member memberships are available (e.g. only a collapsed feature table), so MSD/BLD against the representative cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when OTU members were annotated only via a single representative sequence and you need to measure how often member sequences disagree taxonomically, especially for OTUs whose members exceed 3% MSD from the representative.
skills.name: representative-vs-member-taxonomy-comparison
skills.search_text: representative-vs-member-taxonomy-comparison Use when OTU members were annotated only via a single representative sequence and you need to measure how often member sequences disagree taxonomically, especially for OTUs whose members exceed 3% MSD from the representative. Sequences already carry per-sequence taxonomic assignments (no representative-inherited annotation is in use, so there is no disagreement to measure). The analysis goal is OTU quality by sequence divergence alone (MSD/BLD compactness) rather than annotation consistency. Input is de novo unassembled reads not yet clustered into OTUs; representative-vs-member comparison requires pre-existing OTU clusters. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 A QC skill for 16S rRNA OTU analyses that reclassifies every member sequence of each OTU with the RDP Classifier (Greengenes) via QIIME and compares those assignments against the representative sequence's annotation, quantifying how often a single representative's label misrepresents the OTU. It also stratifies the disagreement rate by sequence divergence (MSD >= 0.03) between members and representatives. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/npjbiofilms.2016.4
skills.summary: A QC skill for 16S rRNA OTU analyses that reclassifies every member sequence of each OTU with the RDP Classifier (Greengenes) via QIIME and compares those assignments against the representative sequence's annotation, quantifying how often a single representative's label misrepresents the OTU. It also stratifies the disagreement rate by sequence divergence (MSD >= 0.03) between members and representatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences already carry per-sequence taxonomic assignments (no representative-inherited annotation is in use, so there is no disagreement to measure). The analysis goal is OTU quality by sequence divergence alone (MSD/BLD compactness) rather than annotation consistency. Input is de novo unassembled reads not yet clustered into OTUs; representative-vs-member comparison requires pre-existing OTU clusters.

skills.description: Use when reproducing the review's recommended metagenomic workflow from raw sequencing FASTQ files into taxonomic abundance tables and KO functional profile tables using its companion scripts.
skills.name: reproducible-pipeline-script-execution
skills.search_text: reproducible-pipeline-script-execution Use when reproducing the review's recommended metagenomic workflow from raw sequencing FASTQ files into taxonomic abundance tables and KO functional profile tables using its companion scripts. Input is already a taxonomic or KO feature table — the pipeline consumes raw FASTQ, so re-running KneadData/HUMAnN2 on processed tables is wrong The analysis goal is metatranscriptome, metaproteome, or metabolome analysis, which the review notes are 'not widely accepted due to their high cost and the complex experimental and analysis methods required' and are not covered by this pipeline Only statistical analysis or visualization of existing microbiome results is needed (e.g. alpha/beta diversity, networks, machine learning) rather than feature-table generation from reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Executes the paper's step-by-step reproducible analysis scripts (YongxinLiu/Liu2020ProteinCell) to run the recommended metagenomic pipeline — KneadData cleaning, MetaPhlAn2/Kraken2 taxonomy, HUMAnN2 functional profiling — turning raw FASTQ into taxonomic and KEGG-orthology (KO) feature tables. metabarcoding/v1 10.1007/s13238-020-00724-8
skills.summary: Executes the paper's step-by-step reproducible analysis scripts (YongxinLiu/Liu2020ProteinCell) to run the recommended metagenomic pipeline — KneadData cleaning, MetaPhlAn2/Kraken2 taxonomy, HUMAnN2 functional profiling — turning raw FASTQ into taxonomic and KEGG-orthology (KO) feature tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomic or KO feature table — the pipeline consumes raw FASTQ, so re-running KneadData/HUMAnN2 on processed tables is wrong The analysis goal is metatranscriptome, metaproteome, or metabolome analysis, which the review notes are 'not widely accepted due to their high cost and the complex experimental and analysis methods required' and are not covered by this pipeline Only statistical analysis or visualization of existing microbiome results is needed (e.g. alpha/beta diversity, networks, machine learning) rather than feature-table generation from reads

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a code-quality or software-engineering improvement between two versions of a tool (e.g. swarm v3's 'modernized C++ source code' over v2) and the claim must be reproduced with a measurable score.
skills.name: reproducible-software-evaluation
skills.search_text: reproducible-software-evaluation Use when a paper claims a code-quality or software-engineering improvement between two versions of a tool (e.g. swarm v3's 'modernized C++ source code' over v2) and the claim must be reproduced with a measurable score. The claim to verify concerns runtime performance, memory footprint, or clustering results rather than code quality (for swarm v3, speed and memory claims are evaluated separately as 'more than 7 times faster' and 'reduced memory footprint by up to 50%'). Only one version of the software is available, since the skill requires a paired before/after comparison of two source trees under identical SoftWipe configuration. The software under study has no obtainable clean source checkout (e.g. binaries only), making SoftWipe static source analysis impossible. Quantitatively compare code quality across software versions by running SoftWipe (Zapletal et al., 2020) with an identical configuration on clean checkouts of each source tree, then recording one score record per version (e.g. swarm v2 = 5.2/10 vs swarm v3 = 6.6/10) in a CSV for validation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab493
skills.summary: Quantitatively compare code quality across software versions by running SoftWipe (Zapletal et al., 2020) with an identical configuration on clean checkouts of each source tree, then recording one score record per version (e.g. swarm v2 = 5.2/10 vs swarm v3 = 6.6/10) in a CSV for validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The claim to verify concerns runtime performance, memory footprint, or clustering results rather than code quality (for swarm v3, speed and memory claims are evaluated separately as 'more than 7 times faster' and 'reduced memory footprint by up to 50%'). Only one version of the software is available, since the skill requires a paired before/after comparison of two source trees under identical SoftWipe configuration. The software under study has no obtainable clean source checkout (e.g. binaries only), making SoftWipe static source analysis impossible.

skills.description: Use when comparing normalization methods on simulated count data with known sampling fractions and you need to show, per sample, the residual between observed and method-estimated log sampling fractions as a grouped box plot.
skills.name: residual-distribution-boxplot-visualization
skills.search_text: residual-distribution-boxplot-visualization Use when comparing normalization methods on simulated count data with known sampling fractions and you need to show, per sample, the residual between observed and method-estimated log sampling fractions as a grouped box plot. When the data are raw observed counts with no known (true) sampling fractions — residuals against truth cannot be computed, so only real-data DA testing is appropriate, not this residual comparison When sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Visualize per-sample sampling-fraction residuals as box plots grouped by normalization method (ANCOM-BC, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, TSS), reproducing the paper's Fig. 3 comparison of how well each method removes the bias introduced by differences in sampling fractions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Visualize per-sample sampling-fraction residuals as box plots grouped by normalization method (ANCOM-BC, ELib-UQ, ELib-TMM, CSS, MED, UQ, TMM, TSS), reproducing the paper's Fig. 3 comparison of how well each method removes the bias introduced by differences in sampling fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are raw observed counts with no known (true) sampling fractions — residuals against truth cannot be computed, so only real-data DA testing is appropriate, not this residual comparison When sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled

skills.description: Use when a paired dataset of OTU/ASV tables and independent ground-truth richness surveys (e.g., plant field inventories) is available and the goal is to measure how curation or filtering changes OTU-richness vs species-richness correspondence (R²).
skills.name: richness-correspondence-regression-analysis
skills.search_text: richness-correspondence-regression-analysis Use when a paired dataset of OTU/ASV tables and independent ground-truth richness surveys (e.g., plant field inventories) is available and the goal is to measure how curation or filtering changes OTU-richness vs species-richness correspondence (R²). No paired ground-truth inventory (e.g., field survey species counts) exists to regress OTU richness against, so R² correspondence cannot be computed The goal is taxonomic composition or β-diversity rather than α-diversity correspondence; the paper notes current tail-discarding approaches 'may be adequate for assessing composition and turnover, but much less so for α-diversity' The analysis targets identification of individual rare species — the article warns 'LULU curation may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies how well molecular OTU richness tracks independent field-survey species richness by regressing per-site OTU richness against per-site plant richness (R²) on the 130-site Danish plant ITS2 soil dataset, and uses the R² gain to benchmark singleton removal against LULU post-clustering curation. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Quantifies how well molecular OTU richness tracks independent field-survey species richness by regressing per-site OTU richness against per-site plant richness (R²) on the 130-site Danish plant ITS2 soil dataset, and uses the R² gain to benchmark singleton removal against LULU post-clustering curation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired ground-truth inventory (e.g., field survey species counts) exists to regress OTU richness against, so R² correspondence cannot be computed The goal is taxonomic composition or β-diversity rather than α-diversity correspondence; the paper notes current tail-discarding approaches 'may be adequate for assessing composition and turnover, but much less so for α-diversity' The analysis targets identification of individual rare species — the article warns 'LULU curation may thus not be suitable for identifying single rare species in community data sets'

skills.description: Use when genus-level ASV abundance tables from multiple 16S rRNA hypervariable regions need to be ranked by taxonomic-classification accuracy against a positive-control mock community.
skills.name: roc-curve-classifier-benchmarking
skills.search_text: roc-curve-classifier-benchmarking Use when genus-level ASV abundance tables from multiple 16S rRNA hypervariable regions need to be ranked by taxonomic-classification accuracy against a positive-control mock community. Input data are not genus-level 16S ASV abundances (e.g. metagenomic functional profiles) — the mock-community cross-validation is grounded in 16S rRNA region taxonomy. No positive-control/mock community sample exists in the dataset — ROC cross-validation against ZymoBIOMICS reference taxa cannot be performed. Regions were sequenced with long-read full-length platforms — the MiSeq 300 bp limit that motivated this region comparison does not apply. Benchmark 16S rRNA hypervariable-region taxonomic classifiers by pairwise ROC curve analysis against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community standard, comparing sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC) for each combined region (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-30764-z
skills.summary: Benchmark 16S rRNA hypervariable-region taxonomic classifiers by pairwise ROC curve analysis against the ZymoBIOMICS mock community standard, comparing sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC) for each combined region (V1–V2, V3–V4, V5–V7, V7–V9).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not genus-level 16S ASV abundances (e.g. metagenomic functional profiles) — the mock-community cross-validation is grounded in 16S rRNA region taxonomy. No positive-control/mock community sample exists in the dataset — ROC cross-validation against ZymoBIOMICS reference taxa cannot be performed. Regions were sequenced with long-read full-length platforms — the MiSeq 300 bp limit that motivated this region comparison does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have significant-ASV calls from multiple DA tools (e.g., ANCOM-II, ALDEx2, LEfSe, edgeR, Wilcoxon) plus false-positive analysis tables, and need to score each tool's discriminatory power via AUROC, precision, recall, and F1.
skills.name: roc-curve-computation-differential-abundance-asvs
skills.search_text: roc-curve-computation-differential-abundance-asvs Use when you have significant-ASV calls from multiple DA tools (e.g., ANCOM-II, ALDEx2, LEfSe, edgeR, Wilcoxon) plus false-positive analysis tables, and need to score each tool's discriminatory power via AUROC, precision, recall, and F1. When the goal is to determine which taxa are significantly differentially abundant rather than to benchmark the discriminatory performance of tool calls When the data have not been pre-processed by the paper's pipeline (10% prevalence filtering, filtered/unfiltered dataset runs) — results depend on data pre-processing When only a single tool's calls exist; the skill's purpose is cross-tool comparison of AUROC, precision, and recall Computes per-ASV ROC curves, AUCs, and threshold-binarized precision/recall/F1 to evaluate how well significant ASVs called by each differential abundance (DA) tool discriminate between sample groups, run separately on relative-abundance and CLR-transformed inputs from the 38 filtered 16S rRNA datasets. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Computes per-ASV ROC curves, AUCs, and threshold-binarized precision/recall/F1 to evaluate how well significant ASVs called by each differential abundance (DA) tool discriminate between sample groups, run separately on relative-abundance and CLR-transformed inputs from the 38 filtered 16S rRNA datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to determine which taxa are significantly differentially abundant rather than to benchmark the discriminatory performance of tool calls When the data have not been pre-processed by the paper's pipeline (10% prevalence filtering, filtered/unfiltered dataset runs) — results depend on data pre-processing When only a single tool's calls exist; the skill's purpose is cross-tool comparison of AUROC, precision, and recall

skills.description: Use when comparing OTU mapping reproducibility across sequencing runs, e.g. testing how swapping the default hOTU reference for UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs changes abundance correlations and shared OTU identifications.
skills.name: rrna-abundance-profiling-across-runs
skills.search_text: rrna-abundance-profiling-across-runs Use when comparing OTU mapping reproducibility across sequencing runs, e.g. testing how swapping the default hOTU reference for UCLUST-clustered reference OTUs changes abundance correlations and shared OTU identifications. You only need taxonomy assignment, not OTU-level abundance profiling — plain `mapseq rawseqs.fa > rawseqs.fa.mseq` classification suffices Input is already a feature/OTU count table; re-running the MAPseq mapping would be redundant You intend to change downstream mapping software as the variable of interest — the finding shows UCLUST-reference effects hold 'independent of the downstream mapping software', so this comparison is not a software benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Build per-run rRNA OTU abundance profiles with MAPseq under different reference OTU definitions (default pre-clustered hOTU vs. ab initio UCLUST-derived reference), then quantify between-run consistency via pairwise Spearman/Pearson abundance correlations and Jaccard overlap of detected OTUs. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Build per-run rRNA OTU abundance profiles with MAPseq under different reference OTU definitions (default pre-clustered hOTU vs. ab initio UCLUST-derived reference), then quantify between-run consistency via pairwise Spearman/Pearson abundance correlations and Jaccard overlap of detected OTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need taxonomy assignment, not OTU-level abundance profiling — plain `mapseq rawseqs.fa > rawseqs.fa.mseq` classification suffices Input is already a feature/OTU count table; re-running the MAPseq mapping would be redundant You intend to change downstream mapping software as the variable of interest — the finding shows UCLUST-reference effects hold 'independent of the downstream mapping software', so this comparison is not a software benchmark

skills.description: Use when demultiplexed, quality-filtered rRNA reads (amplicon or shotgun) need taxonomy and hierarchical OTU assignments with per-level confidences, especially on large datasets where runtime matters.
skills.name: rrna-amplicon-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: rrna-amplicon-taxonomic-classification Use when demultiplexed, quality-filtered rRNA reads (amplicon or shotgun) need taxonomy and hierarchical OTU assignments with per-level confidences, especially on large datasets where runtime matters. Input is already a count/abundance table or OTU table — MAPseq classifies raw reads; use its -otutable aggregation on existing .mseq files instead of re-running classification Sequences are not ribosomal RNA reads — MAPseq is designed for rRNA sequences against a full-length reference rRNA database with precomputed OTU clusters A de novo OTU clustering is required without any reference database — MAPseq is a reference-based classifier and cannot cluster reads without references http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Classify demultiplexed rRNA amplicon or shotgun reads against a full-length reference rRNA database using MAPseq v1.2.6, which returns NCBI taxonomy and hierarchical OTU (hOTU) assignments with per-level confidence estimates in a single run. It is chosen because it is up to 30% more accurate (F½ score) and up to one hundred times faster than existing solutions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Classify demultiplexed rRNA amplicon or shotgun reads against a full-length reference rRNA database using MAPseq v1.2.6, which returns NCBI taxonomy and hierarchical OTU (hOTU) assignments with per-level confidence estimates in a single run. It is chosen because it is up to 30% more accurate (F½ score) and up to one hundred times faster than existing solutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a count/abundance table or OTU table — MAPseq classifies raw reads; use its -otutable aggregation on existing .mseq files instead of re-running classification Sequences are not ribosomal RNA reads — MAPseq is designed for rRNA sequences against a full-length reference rRNA database with precomputed OTU clusters A de novo OTU clustering is required without any reference database — MAPseq is a reference-based classifier and cannot cluster reads without references

skills.description: Use when classifying amplicon or shotgun rRNA reads against a full-length reference database with per-read taxonomy/OTU assignments and confidence scores, or when reconstructing the k-mer search, NW alignment, and confidence-estimation stages of MAPseq.
skills.name: rrna-kmer-counting-with-preclustering
skills.search_text: rrna-kmer-counting-with-preclustering Use when classifying amplicon or shotgun rRNA reads against a full-length reference database with per-read taxonomy/OTU assignments and confidence scores, or when reconstructing the k-mer search, NW alignment, and confidence-estimation stages of MAPseq. Input reads are not demultiplexed and quality-filtered rRNA sequences (MAPseq expects previously filtered FASTA input) You need de novo OTU clustering without any reference database — MAPseq is explicitly a reference-based rRNA analysis framework You only need alignment scoring without taxonomy/OTU assignment and confidence estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reimplements MAPseq's k-mer search stage: pre-clustered k-mer counting against a full-length rRNA reference database to generate candidate matches, followed by Needleman-Wunsch alignment of high-scoring segment pairs and computation of per-read classification confidence scores. This is the algorithmic basis for MAPseq being up to one hundred times faster and up to 30% more accurate (F½ score) than existing rRNA classifiers. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx517
skills.summary: Reimplements MAPseq's k-mer search stage: pre-clustered k-mer counting against a full-length rRNA reference database to generate candidate matches, followed by Needleman-Wunsch alignment of high-scoring segment pairs and computation of per-read classification confidence scores. This is the algorithmic basis for MAPseq being up to one hundred times faster and up to 30% more accurate (F½ score) than existing rRNA classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not demultiplexed and quality-filtered rRNA sequences (MAPseq expects previously filtered FASTA input) You need de novo OTU clustering without any reference database — MAPseq is explicitly a reference-based rRNA analysis framework You only need alignment scoring without taxonomy/OTU assignment and confidence estimation

skills.search_text: runtime-memory-profiling Use when reproducing the VTAM vs DALU vs OBIbaR benchmark and you need to measure and compare elapsed time and maxresident memory of each Snakemake workflow (01snkfl_prep.yml through 04snkfl_analysis_obibar.yml) on the same hardware. skills.summary: Profiles the compute cost of the three metabarcoding pipelines (VTAM, DALU, OBIbaR) by measuring user time, system time, elapsed time, CPU %, and maxresident memory for each Snakemake workflow in the vtam_benchmark repository on a fixed 8 CPU / 32 GB RAM desktop, producing a runtime_memory_table.tsv that reproduces the published comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare pipeline accuracy or precision (sensitivity, ASV richness, false positives) rather than compute cost — that requires the min_readcount sensitivity workflows, not the timing wrapper. When the pipelines cannot be run under the same Singularity container and same hardware class, since cross-hardware timing and maxresident memory values are not comparable.

skills.search_text: sample-barcode-assignment Use when simulating multiplexed PacBio HiFi amplicon sequencing data and each sample needs a distinct dual-barcode signature embedded in its template so downstream demultiplexing and ASV workflows can be benchmarked. Input is already demultiplexed per-sample FASTQ/FASTA with barcodes removed — barcode assignment is a pre-sequencing template-construction step, not a demultiplexing step Simulating short-read (e.g. Illumina) amplicon data with single-index barcoding — MHASS implements PacBio HiFi dual-barcoding specifically The user only needs read-level error simulation (PBSIM3 subread accuracy/np distribution) without template construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assigns a unique forward/reverse dual-barcode pair to each simulated sample and concatenates them into PacBio HiFi amplicon templates (A + ForwardBarcode + ForwardPrimer + ASV + RC(ReversePrimer) + RC(ReverseBarcode) + A) so every sample carries a distinct template signature, mirroring real PacBio dual-barcoding strategies. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Assigns a unique forward/reverse dual-barcode pair to each simulated sample and concatenates them into PacBio HiFi amplicon templates (A + ForwardBarcode + ForwardPrimer + ASV + RC(ReversePrimer) + RC(ReverseBarcode) + A) so every sample carries a distinct template signature, mirroring real PacBio dual-barcoding strategies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already demultiplexed per-sample FASTQ/FASTA with barcodes removed — barcode assignment is a pre-sequencing template-construction step, not a demultiplexing step Simulating short-read (e.g. Illumina) amplicon data with single-index barcoding — MHASS implements PacBio HiFi dual-barcoding specifically The user only needs read-level error simulation (PBSIM3 subread accuracy/np distribution) without template construction

Used to verify that composition estimation remains accurate (>94% accuracy, r2 > 0.97) across run modes and memory settings. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Evaluate taxonomic sample-composition estimates produced by MetaMaps by computing the correlation (r2) between estimated taxon frequencies (e.g. EMFrequency/PotFrequency from the .EM.WIMP output) and true or reference composition, alongside species-level read-assignment accuracy. Used to verify that composition estimation remains accurate (>94% accuracy, r2 > 0.97) across run modes and memory settings.

The input table is already rarefied or you plan compositionally-aware methods (e.g., differential abundance tests) where rarefying discards valid low-depth samples below 5,000 sequences The per-study table contains clustered OTUs rather than exact Deblur sequences, since cross-study tracking of the 90-bp V4 tag sequences depends on exact-sequence features Samples have fewer than 5,000 total reads, which cannot meet the rarefaction depth and would be dropped http://edamontology.org/topic_0176 Depth-based QC and normalization for EMP-style 16S feature tables: filter OTUs/sequences with the mc2 rule (minimum sequence count of 2), drop samples below the read threshold, then rarefy to a fixed depth (5,000 observations per sample) so cross-study comparisons are not driven by sequencing depth. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621

skills.search_text: sample-group-label-randomization Use when benchmarking DA tools' false-positive control on 16S rRNA ASV count tables: you need to know which tools (e.g., edgeR, LEfSe) call spurious significant ASVs when group labels carry no real signal. When you need true differential abundance results on real case/control comparisons — randomized labels guarantee no group signal by construction When estimating practical FDR for real sample groupings, since the randomized approach assumes no systematic abundance differences that real groups may contain When data has not been preprocessed (e.g., no 10% prevalence filter applied) and you intend to compare against the paper's filtered-data benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Estimates the false-positive rate of microbiome differential abundance (DA) tools by randomly reassigning case/control labels among samples within the most frequently sampled group of a dataset, so that no true group differences exist, and measuring the percent of ASVs each tool calls significant. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Estimates the false-positive rate of microbiome differential abundance (DA) tools by randomly reassigning case/control labels among samples within the most frequently sampled group of a dataset, so that no true group differences exist, and measuring the percent of ASVs each tool calls significant.

skills.description: Use when the input is an occurrence table of ASVs x samples x technical replicates with read counts and the goal is to remove non-reproducible occurrences by requiring presence in a minimum number of replicates.
skills.name: sample-replicate-grouping-and-counting
skills.search_text: sample-replicate-grouping-and-counting Use when the input is an occurrence table of ASVs x samples x technical replicates with read counts and the goal is to remove non-reproducible occurrences by requiring presence in a minimum number of replicates. The input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been merged, demultiplexed, and run through VTAM's sortreads and filter commands to produce the Nijk occurrence table The analysis goal is to remove whole unreproducible replicates (FilterRenkonen, e.g. by Renkonen similarity) rather than individual non-reproducible occurrences The dataset contains no technical replicates per sample, since the minimum-replicate criterion cannot be evaluated Reconstructs the VTAM FilterMinReplicateNumber logic: group a replicate-structured occurrence table (read counts Nijk of ASV i in sample j and replicate k) by ASV-sample pair, count distinct replicates with non-zero reads, and discard occurrences that fail a minimum-replicate threshold (benchmark: >= 2 replicates) to ensure repeatability of metabarcoding occurrences. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Reconstructs the VTAM FilterMinReplicateNumber logic: group a replicate-structured occurrence table (read counts Nijk of ASV i in sample j and replicate k) by ASV-sample pair, count distinct replicates with non-zero reads, and discard occurrences that fail a minimum-replicate threshold (benchmark: >= 2 replicates) to ensure repeatability of metabarcoding occurrences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been merged, demultiplexed, and run through VTAM's sortreads and filter commands to produce the Nijk occurrence table The analysis goal is to remove whole unreproducible replicates (FilterRenkonen, e.g. by Renkonen similarity) rather than individual non-reproducible occurrences The dataset contains no technical replicates per sample, since the minimum-replicate criterion cannot be evaluated

skills.search_text: seasonal-subnetwork-annotation Use when you have a taxon-by-time abundance index matrix (e.g., 663 taxonomic groups across an 18-month seawater eDNA series) and need to detect correlated-abundance community modules and label them by season. The input is a single-sample amplicon dataset with no temporal replication — WGCNA module detection over correlated abundance shifts requires a time-series of many samples The goal is species-level taxonomic assignment or biodiversity counting rather than community-level network structure — the article notes species-level assignment has lower confidence and that this skill addresses community clustering, not taxonomy The abundance table is already clustered or annotated (e.g., an existing module membership file) — rerunning WGCNA would discard prior assignments Clusters taxa from an eDNA amplicon time-series into seasonal community subnetworks using WGCNA (soft-thresholding power beta=22, topological-overlap hierarchical clustering, Dynamic Tree Cut), then assigns each module a color label and seasonal membership as reported in Djurhuus et al. 2020. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1

skills.description: Use when comparing metabarcoding/denoising pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU vs OBIbaR) on datasets containing mock community and negative control samples, so that false and true occurrences can be labeled and precision/sensitivity quantified.

skills.search_text: sensitivity-precision-evaluation Use when comparing metabarcoding/denoising pipelines (e.g. VTAM vs DALU vs OBIbaR) on datasets containing mock community and negative control samples, so that false and true occurrences can be labeled and precision/sensitivity quantified. The dataset lacks mock community or negative control samples, so occurrences cannot be labeled as true or false positives The goal is pipeline denoising itself rather than cross-pipeline benchmarking — use VTAM filter, DADA2, or OBITools3 directly instead A single pipeline's parameter optimization is needed (use VTAM's optimize command) rather than an evaluation of filtering precision/sensitivity trade-offs http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark metabarcoding pipelines by classifying occurrences as true or false positives against mock and negative control samples, then computing sensitivity TP/(TP+FN) and precision TP/(TP+FP) across minimum read count cut-offs (0, 10, 40, 60) to compare filtering stringency versus detection power. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks mock community or negative control samples, so occurrences cannot be labeled as true or false positives The goal is pipeline denoising itself rather than cross-pipeline benchmarking — use VTAM filter, DADA2, or OBITools3 directly instead A single pipeline's parameter optimization is needed (use VTAM's optimize command) rather than an evaluation of filtering precision/sensitivity trade-offs

skills.description: Use when a duplication rate must be estimated for paired-end FASTQ data or a custom deduplication estimator must be reproduced, specifically fastp's array-based key1/key2 scheme rather than FASTQC's hash-table method.
skills.name: sequence-prefix-hashing-duplication-estimation
skills.search_text: sequence-prefix-hashing-duplication-estimation Use when a duplication rate must be estimated for paired-end FASTQ data or a custom deduplication estimator must be reproduced, specifically fastp's array-based key1/key2 scheme rather than FASTQC's hash-table method. Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the paper explicitly directs such data to fastplong instead of fastp Only single-end FASTQ is available — key1/key2 are defined from a paired-end read (12 bp of read1 + 32 bp of read2), so the scheme does not transfer directly Exact per-read duplicate IDs are needed rather than a rate estimate — the array-based scheme trades a small hash-collision error (~0.01% of reads) for speed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reimplements fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, in which the first 12 bp of read1 form key1 (an offset into a 2^24-entry flagging array D) and the first 32 bp of read2 are packed into a 64-bit key2 counted in array C — unlike FASTQC's hash-table approach. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Reimplements fastp's array-based paired-end duplication evaluation, in which the first 12 bp of read1 form key1 (an offset into a 2^24-entry flagging array D) and the first 32 bp of read2 are packed into a 64-bit key2 counted in array C — unlike FASTQC's hash-table approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the paper explicitly directs such data to fastplong instead of fastp Only single-end FASTQ is available — key1/key2 are defined from a paired-end read (12 bp of read1 + 32 bp of read2), so the scheme does not transfer directly Exact per-read duplicate IDs are needed rather than a rate estimate — the array-based scheme trades a small hash-collision error (~0.01% of reads) for speed

The input table lacks environment-category metadata in the mapping file, so no environment distribution can be computed per feature The goal is within-sample alpha diversity rather than across-environment specificity of individual features Features are clustered OTUs from heterogeneous, non-standardized protocols where exact Deblur sequences cannot be followed across studies http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes Shannon entropy H = -Σ(p_i · log2 p_i) over the distribution of environment categories observed per feature unit (exact Deblur tag sequences, genera, or phylogenetic subtrees) to quantify habitat specificity.
