skills.description: Use when assigning genus-level (or higher) taxonomy to 16S or 18S rRNA OTUs/ASVs from eDNA metabarcoding data, e.g. mock-community or environmental samples processed by PEMA.
skills.name: silva-based-taxonomic-assignment
skills.search_text: silva-based-taxonomic-assignment Use when assigning genus-level (or higher) taxonomy to 16S or 18S rRNA OTUs/ASVs from eDNA metabarcoding data, e.g. mock-community or environmental samples processed by PEMA. Input is COI marker gene data — PEMA uses the RDPClassifier with the MIDORI database (e.g. MIDORI_LONGEST_1.1) instead of Silva, so this skill is the wrong route. Input is ITS (Fungi) marker gene data — PEMA assigns taxonomy using the Unite database, not Silva. Taxonomy has already been assigned and you only need downstream ecological analysis (phyloseq/vegan alpha- and beta-diversity, PERMANOVA). http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Assign taxonomy to 16S/18S rRNA amplicon units (OTUs or ASVs) using the CREST LCAClassifier against the Silva reference database (versions 128 or 132), with an optional phylogeny-based route via a SILVA_132_SSURef reference tree. This is PEMA's alignment-based taxonomic assignment step for ribosomal marker genes. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa022
skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to 16S/18S rRNA amplicon units (OTUs or ASVs) using the CREST LCAClassifier against the Silva reference database (versions 128 or 132), with an optional phylogeny-based route via a SILVA_132_SSURef reference tree. This is PEMA's alignment-based taxonomic assignment step for ribosomal marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is COI marker gene data — PEMA uses the RDPClassifier with the MIDORI database (e.g. MIDORI_LONGEST_1.1) instead of Silva, so this skill is the wrong route. Input is ITS (Fungi) marker gene data — PEMA assigns taxonomy using the Unite database, not Silva. Taxonomy has already been assigned and you only need downstream ecological analysis (phyloseq/vegan alpha- and beta-diversity, PERMANOVA).

skills.description: Use when exact-matching 16S amplicon sequences (e.g., Deblur 90-bp V4 tags) against SILVA and eukaryotic references would inflate or confound the fraction of recaptured reference sequences.
skills.name: silva-non-eukaryotic-sequence-filtering
skills.search_text: silva-non-eukaryotic-sequence-filtering Use when exact-matching 16S amplicon sequences (e.g., Deblur 90-bp V4 tags) against SILVA and eukaryotic references would inflate or confound the fraction of recaptured reference sequences. When the query amplicons include eukaryotic 18S or ITS sequences, since excluding eukaryotic SILVA references would remove legitimate matches When the target reference is Greengenes 13.8, which already contains only bacterial/archaeal sequences and requires no eukaryote filter http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Subsets the SILVA 128 reference database to non-eukaryotic (bacterial and archaeal) rRNA gene sequences before exact-sequence comparison, so that 16S amplicon matches (e.g., EMP Deblur 90-bp tags) are assessed against prokaryotic reference diversity only. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Subsets the SILVA 128 reference database to non-eukaryotic (bacterial and archaeal) rRNA gene sequences before exact-sequence comparison, so that 16S amplicon matches (e.g., EMP Deblur 90-bp tags) are assessed against prokaryotic reference diversity only.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query amplicons include eukaryotic 18S or ITS sequences, since excluding eukaryotic SILVA references would remove legitimate matches When the target reference is Greengenes 13.8, which already contains only bacterial/archaeal sequences and requires no eukaryote filter

skills.search_text: silva-reference-database-configuration Use when running dadasnake (or DADA2/mothur-based classification) on 16S/ITS amplicon FASTQ data and the reference database paths for taxonomic assignment must be set in the config before classification. Input data are fungal ITS amplicons that require UNITE rather than the SILVA SSU reference Classification is to be run against a custom or non-16S database (e.g. NCBI 16S ribosomal RNA at ../DBs/ncbi_16S_ribosomal_RNA) outside dadasnake's tested SILVA defaults http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configures dadasnake's taxonomic classification with the correct reference database — SILVA v.138 (e.g. silva_nr99_v138_train_set.fa.gz, SILVA_SSU_r138_2019.RData) for 16S bacterial/archaeal amplicons or UNITE for ITS — by setting database paths in config.default.yaml and the sample/config files. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giaa135
skills.summary: Configures dadasnake's taxonomic classification with the correct reference database — SILVA v.138 (e.g. silva_nr99_v138_train_set.fa.gz, SILVA_SSU_r138_2019.RData) for 16S bacterial/archaeal amplicons or UNITE for ITS — by setting database paths in config.default.yaml and the sample/config files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are fungal ITS amplicons that require UNITE rather than the SILVA SSU reference Classification is to be run against a custom or non-16S database (e.g. NCBI 16S ribosomal RNA at ../DBs/ncbi_16S_ribosomal_RNA) outside dadasnake's tested SILVA defaults

skills.description: Use when 16S amplicon reads need phylum/domain-level taxonomic assignment via the SILVA rRNA database, or when interpreting reported SILVAngs OTU classifications (e.g. %Proteobacteria, unclassified fractions).

skills.search_text: silva-taxonomic-classification-interpretation Use when 16S amplicon reads need phylum/domain-level taxonomic assignment via the SILVA rRNA database, or when interpreting reported SILVAngs OTU classifications (e.g. %Proteobacteria, unclassified fractions). Input is already a taxonomically assigned feature/OTU table — only interpretation or re-analysis is needed, not re-classification Classifying ITS/eukaryotic reads — this article used a separate 'Classify Sequences' tool with the Warcup V2 training data set at 90% similarity and 75 bp minimum overlap, not SILVAngs Full-length rRNA sequences or isolate genomes where direct SINA/SILVA alignment outside an OTU-clustering pipeline is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Interpret and reproduce SILVA-based taxonomic classification of 16S rRNA metabarcoding reads, understanding how SILVAngs assigns OTUs to phyla via SINA alignment, cd-hit-est clustering, and BLASTn against the SILVA SSU ref database, including the thresholds that leave reads unclassified. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Interpret and reproduce SILVA-based taxonomic classification of 16S rRNA metabarcoding reads, understanding how SILVAngs assigns OTUs to phyla via SINA alignment, cd-hit-est clustering, and BLASTn against the SILVA SSU ref database, including the thresholds that leave reads unclassified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomically assigned feature/OTU table — only interpretation or re-analysis is needed, not re-classification Classifying ITS/eukaryotic reads — this article used a separate 'Classify Sequences' tool with the Warcup V2 training data set at 90% similarity and 75 bp minimum overlap, not SILVAngs Full-length rRNA sequences or isolate genomes where direct SINA/SILVA alignment outside an OTU-clustering pipeline is more appropriate

skills.search_text: simulated-vs-real-read-error-profile-comparison Use when evaluating whether a HiFi amplicon simulator reproduces real-read error behavior: you have raw real and simulated FASTQ reads plus reference sequences, and need per-position insertion/substitution/deletion profiles to detect position-specific error signatures. skills.summary: Compares per-position error profiles (insertion/substitution/deletion proportions) between real PacBio HiFi amplicon reads and MHASS-simulated reads by aligning both read sets to their references and tabulating error types at each alignment position, to verify the simulator reproduces position-specific error signatures such as the Zymo/Titan-1 terminal-insertion profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an ASV/feature count table (counts.tsv, counts_meta.tsv) rather than raw reads — no alignment to a reference is possible, so per-position error decomposition cannot be computed Reads cannot be aligned to a reference sequence, since the skill requires position-resolved error counts along the alignment The goal is a global (non position-specific) error rate summary rather than a position-by-position real-vs-simulated comparison

skills.description: Use when you need to compare the runtime or throughput of FASTQ preprocessors under a fixed, fair setting (single thread, same dataset such as the 9316 M-base B17NCB1 paired-end data) and reproduce the 2-5x speedup claims for fastp.
skills.name: single-thread-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: single-thread-runtime-profiling Use when you need to compare the runtime or throughput of FASTQ preprocessors under a fixed, fair setting (single thread, same dataset such as the 9316 M-base B17NCB1 paired-end data) and reproduce the 2-5x speedup claims for fastp. The goal is to measure multi-threaded or I/O-bound performance — the skill specifically pins runs to a single thread (-w 1) to isolate algorithmic speed. Input data are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio, Cyclone) — the fastp README directs those workflows to fastplong instead. You need functional quality metrics (adapter removal rate, Q30 improvement) rather than runtime/throughput comparison — this skill only profiles speed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark methodology for measuring wall-clock processing time and throughput of FASTQ preprocessing tools (fastp vs FASTQC, Cutadapt, SOAPnuke, AfterQC, Trimmomatic) on a fixed dataset in single-threaded SE and PE modes. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Benchmark methodology for measuring wall-clock processing time and throughput of FASTQ preprocessing tools (fastp vs FASTQC, Cutadapt, SOAPnuke, AfterQC, Trimmomatic) on a fixed dataset in single-threaded SE and PE modes.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers on mock community 16S data and you need to know whether sensitivity and specificity trade off or co-vary, and which profiler-library pairings sit in the high-both quadrant.

skills.search_text: species-level-sensitivity-specificity-comparison Use when benchmarking taxonomic profilers on mock community 16S data and you need to know whether sensitivity and specificity trade off or co-vary, and which profiler-library pairings sit in the high-both quadrant. Input is raw reads or ASV/OTU tables rather than an already-computed per-pairing metrics table — the skill compares summary benchmark metrics, not raw classifications The goal is de novo taxonomic profiling of a real (non-mock) community rather than benchmarking profilers against mock-community ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmark profiler/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes, SILVA, RefSeq/Kraken Standard) on mock 16S communities by comparing species-level sensitivity and specificity, then quantify their co-movement with Spearman correlation and quadrant scatterplots to identify pipelines that dominate the high-sensitivity/high-specificity region. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Benchmark profiler/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes, SILVA, RefSeq/Kraken Standard) on mock 16S communities by comparing species-level sensitivity and specificity, then quantify their co-movement with Spearman correlation and quadrant scatterplots to identify pipelines that dominate the high-sensitivity/high-specificity region.

skills.description: Use when a SILVAngs-derived OTU abundance table with taxonomic assignments must be compared between two sample groups (e.g., inflow- vs. pond-water) to identify significantly different species-level taxa.
skills.name: species-level-t-test-significance-screening
skills.search_text: species-level-t-test-significance-screening Use when a SILVAngs-derived OTU abundance table with taxonomic assignments must be compared between two sample groups (e.g., inflow- vs. pond-water) to identify significantly different species-level taxa. The input is raw FASTQ data rather than an OTU abundance table — pre-processing (BBmerge, BBduk, SILVAngs classification) must happen first. The comparison spans more than two sample groups or uses paired samples; a simple two-sample t-test on I- vs. P-source relative abundances is not the right design. The goal is beta-diversity or geographic-distance testing (Mantel test with IBD v1.52 and XLSTAT 2017) rather than species-level abundance differences. Screens species-level OTU relative abundances for significant differences between inflow- (I-source) and pond-water (P-source) trout-farm samples using two-sample t-tests in XLSTAT 2017, reproducing the 15 significantly different taxa reported in the paper's Table 1. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Screens species-level OTU relative abundances for significant differences between inflow- (I-source) and pond-water (P-source) trout-farm samples using two-sample t-tests in XLSTAT 2017, reproducing the 15 significantly different taxa reported in the paper's Table 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ data rather than an OTU abundance table — pre-processing (BBmerge, BBduk, SILVAngs classification) must happen first. The comparison spans more than two sample groups or uses paired samples; a simple two-sample t-test on I- vs. P-source relative abundances is not the right design. The goal is beta-diversity or geographic-distance testing (Mantel test with IBD v1.52 and XLSTAT 2017) rather than species-level abundance differences.

skills.summary: Species-level microbial taxonomic profiling of metagenomic shotgun sequencing data using MetaPhlAn 4, a marker-based profiler whose SGB marker database covers 26,970 species-level genome bins derived from 1.01 M prokaryotic reference and metagenome-assembled genomes.

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to recompute species richness de novo from raw FASTQ reads — use the metabarcoding pipeline (SILVAngs, BBmerge, BBduk) instead of extracting reported counts The source article lacks Venn-diagram or per-location segment counts, so no counts can be reconciled The analysis requires continuous abundance or relative-frequency data — this skill handles integer occurrence (presence) counts only

skills.description: Use when MetaPhlAn 4 species-abundance profiles have detected a species (including uncharacterized SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and the goal is to infer strain-level phylogeny, strain sharing, or host-to-host transmission from marker genes.

skills.search_text: strain-level-phylogeny-reconstruction Use when MetaPhlAn 4 species-abundance profiles have detected a species (including uncharacterized SGBs) across many shotgun metagenomes and the goal is to infer strain-level phylogeny, strain sharing, or host-to-host transmission from marker genes. Only species-level taxonomic abundances are needed — plain MetaPhlAn 4 profiling suffices without strain-level marker phylogeny The target species lacks enough reliably detected samples or species-specific markers to support a marker-based consensus phylogeny Environmental, nonhost-associated communities dominated by sequences not captured by current uSGBs, where marker coverage is expected to be poor http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs per-sample strain-level phylogenies from metagenomic marker alignments using StrainPhlAn 4, enabling strain sharing and transmission inference (e.g. mother-to-infant vertical transmission) even for uncharacterized species (uSGBs) detected by MetaPhlAn 4. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs per-sample strain-level phylogenies from metagenomic marker alignments using StrainPhlAn 4, enabling strain sharing and transmission inference (e.g. mother-to-infant vertical transmission) even for uncharacterized species (uSGBs) detected by MetaPhlAn 4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only species-level taxonomic abundances are needed — plain MetaPhlAn 4 profiling suffices without strain-level marker phylogeny The target species lacks enough reliably detected samples or species-specific markers to support a marker-based consensus phylogeny Environmental, nonhost-associated communities dominated by sequences not captured by current uSGBs, where marker coverage is expected to be poor

skills.description: Use when evaluating taxonomy-classification accuracy with environment-specific (clawback) class weights and you need leak-free, abundance-aware train/test splits over reference sequences and empirical samples.
skills.name: stratified-fold-partitioning-of-reference-sequences
skills.search_text: stratified-fold-partitioning-of-reference-sequences Use when evaluating taxonomy-classification accuracy with environment-specific (clawback) class weights and you need leak-free, abundance-aware train/test splits over reference sequences and empirical samples. You need ready-made weights for a common habitat (e.g., animal-distal-gut, soil-non-saline, human-stool EMPO 3 types) rather than benchmarking classification accuracy — use the readytowear pre-trained classifiers instead of running the fold workflow Your empirical samples lack sufficient characterization to assemble bespoke weights — the article recommends average weights from global microbial species distributions in that case Input is a single unstratified pool of sequences where taxon proportions are not estimable per fold — stratification requires enough members per taxon (very small taxonomies must be merged into strata) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A shuffled stratified 5-fold cross-validation design that simultaneously partitions reference sequences and empirical Qiita samples so every fold carries comparable taxon proportions, while guaranteeing a classifier never sees a test sequence that appeared in its training set and never reuses abundances that informed its taxonomic weights. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: A shuffled stratified 5-fold cross-validation design that simultaneously partitions reference sequences and empirical Qiita samples so every fold carries comparable taxon proportions, while guaranteeing a classifier never sees a test sequence that appeared in its training set and never reuses abundances that informed its taxonomic weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need ready-made weights for a common habitat (e.g., animal-distal-gut, soil-non-saline, human-stool EMPO 3 types) rather than benchmarking classification accuracy — use the readytowear pre-trained classifiers instead of running the fold workflow Your empirical samples lack sufficient characterization to assemble bespoke weights — the article recommends average weights from global microbial species distributions in that case Input is a single unstratified pool of sequences where taxon proportions are not estimable per fold — stratification requires enough members per taxon (very small taxonomies must be merged into strata)

skills.description: Use when a taxa-by-sample absolute abundance table contains zeros that may be structural (taxon truly absent in a group) rather than sampling zeros, before computing group log differences or fitting the ANCOM-BC E-M mixture model.
skills.name: structural-zero-masking
skills.search_text: structural-zero-masking Use when a taxa-by-sample absolute abundance table contains zeros that may be structural (taxon truly absent in a group) rather than sampling zeros, before computing group log differences or fitting the ANCOM-BC E-M mixture model. The goal is to test differential abundance of a taxon that is a structural zero in one group — ANCOM-BC is not designed to detect significant differences for such taxa, and they are only summarized via the presence/absence test Zeros are sampling zeros in taxa present (non-zero prevalence) in all groups — neg.lb will not flag them and they should remain in the E-M fit Input is raw unprocessed data: structural-zero classification requires the pre-processed table and asymptotic lower bounds from feature_table_pre_process, and taxa with zero proportion > zero.cut are already removed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identifies taxa that are genuinely absent (structural zeros) in a given experimental group using the asymptotic lower bound (neg.lb) computed by feature_table_pre_process, and masks those taxa–group entries so they are excluded from downstream ANCOM-BC log-scale mean-difference estimation and the E-M bias fit. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: Identifies taxa that are genuinely absent (structural zeros) in a given experimental group using the asymptotic lower bound (neg.lb) computed by feature_table_pre_process, and masks those taxa–group entries so they are excluded from downstream ANCOM-BC log-scale mean-difference estimation and the E-M bias fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to test differential abundance of a taxon that is a structural zero in one group — ANCOM-BC is not designed to detect significant differences for such taxa, and they are only summarized via the presence/absence test Zeros are sampling zeros in taxa present (non-zero prevalence) in all groups — neg.lb will not flag them and they should remain in the E-M fit Input is raw unprocessed data: structural-zero classification requires the pre-processed table and asymptotic lower bounds from feature_table_pre_process, and taxa with zero proportion > zero.cut are already removed

skills.description: Use when calling intragenomic 16S SNPs from per-isolate PacBio CCS full-length 16S alignments where systematic platform errors could inflate SNP counts, and error-artifact positions must be removed before tabulating unique SNP profiles.
skills.name: substitution-frequency-iqr-outlier-filtering
skills.search_text: substitution-frequency-iqr-outlier-filtering Use when calling intragenomic 16S SNPs from per-isolate PacBio CCS full-length 16S alignments where systematic platform errors could inflate SNP counts, and error-artifact positions must be removed before tabulating unique SNP profiles. Variant discovery targets insertions/deletions rather than substitutions — the paper notes a single genuine deletion in one of the seven E. coli strain K-12 substr. MG1655 16S genes, which this substitution-only, IQR-filtered approach cannot recover. Input is short-read sequencing of a 16S variable region (e.g., V4); the paper shows partial sub-regions cannot match the taxonomic resolution of the full ~1500 bp gene, so substitution frequencies lack the accuracy needed for intragenomic copy variant calling. An isolate has fewer than 200 reads aligned by Cross_match to its most-abundant sequence, leaving too sparse a substitution-frequency distribution for a meaningful 9-IQR outlier baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A statistical filter for intragenomic 16S SNP calling that flags candidate SNP positions whose PacBio CCS substitution frequency is a 9-IQR outlier as systematic sequencing-error artifacts and removes them, so that only true 16S gene copy polymorphisms are counted. It underpins the Johnson et al. Figure 4 SNP-profile analysis of cultured human gut isolates. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-13036-1
skills.summary: A statistical filter for intragenomic 16S SNP calling that flags candidate SNP positions whose PacBio CCS substitution frequency is a 9-IQR outlier as systematic sequencing-error artifacts and removes them, so that only true 16S gene copy polymorphisms are counted. It underpins the Johnson et al. Figure 4 SNP-profile analysis of cultured human gut isolates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variant discovery targets insertions/deletions rather than substitutions — the paper notes a single genuine deletion in one of the seven E. coli strain K-12 substr. MG1655 16S genes, which this substitution-only, IQR-filtered approach cannot recover. Input is short-read sequencing of a 16S variable region (e.g., V4); the paper shows partial sub-regions cannot match the taxonomic resolution of the full ~1500 bp gene, so substitution frequencies lack the accuracy needed for intragenomic copy variant calling. An isolate has fewer than 200 reads aligned by Cross_match to its most-abundant sequence, leaving too sparse a substitution-frequency distribution for a meaningful 9-IQR outlier baseline.

skills.description: Use when analyzing full-length 16S amplicon reads (PacBio CCS or Illumina WGS) to detect intragenomic 16S copy polymorphisms, or when validating observed per-position substitution frequencies against a reference genome's copy stoichiometry.
skills.name: substitution-frequency-profiling
skills.search_text: substitution-frequency-profiling Use when analyzing full-length 16S amplicon reads (PacBio CCS or Illumina WGS) to detect intragenomic 16S copy polymorphisms, or when validating observed per-position substitution frequencies against a reference genome's copy stoichiometry. When the goal is resolving intragenomic 16S copy differences mediated by insertions or deletions — the paper notes systematic PacBio CCS deletion errors at homopolymer runs make this unreliable, and one of the seven E. coli K-12 MG1655 16S genes carries a deletion that this substitution-only approach cannot capture.
