skills.name: taxonomic-classifier-benchmarking
skills.search_text: taxonomic-classifier-benchmarking Use when a COI metabarcoding dataset needs taxonomic classification and you must decide which classifier (alignment, kmer, or web API based) assigns the most complete and accurate names against a curated reference database. Input is already a classified feature table or taxonomy artifact — this skill evaluates classification choices, not post-hoc taxonomy reconciliation The marker gene or reference database is non-COI / non-animal (e.g. 16S with SILVA/Greengenes/UNITE) — the benchmark findings are specific to COI with BOLD- and GenBank-derived references You need a single best-practice pipeline rather than a comparison — the article's stated aim is to illustrate how processes are affected by program or parameter choices, not to present one best pathway http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Benchmark taxonomic classifiers (vsearch-SINTAX, q2-feature-classifier's BLAST+LCA and VSEARCH+LCA, Naive Bayes, and the BOLD Classification API) on a known mock community and real bat guano COI ASVs, quantifying relative completeness via Taxonomic Accuracy Rate (TAR) and Taxonomic Discovery Rate (TDR) from class through species ranks. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: Benchmark taxonomic classifiers (vsearch-SINTAX, q2-feature-classifier's BLAST+LCA and VSEARCH+LCA, Naive Bayes, and the BOLD Classification API) on a known mock community and real bat guano COI ASVs, quantifying relative completeness via Taxonomic Accuracy Rate (TAR) and Taxonomic Discovery Rate (TDR) from class through species ranks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a classified feature table or taxonomy artifact — this skill evaluates classification choices, not post-hoc taxonomy reconciliation The marker gene or reference database is non-COI / non-animal (e.g. 16S with SILVA/Greengenes/UNITE) — the benchmark findings are specific to COI with BOLD- and GenBank-derived references You need a single best-practice pipeline rather than a comparison — the article's stated aim is to illustrate how processes are affected by program or parameter choices, not to present one best pathway

skills.description: Use when a publication reports 16S rRNA taxonomic profiling results (relative abundances, OTU/species/phylum counts) and these figures must be converted into a structured composition table with provenance.
skills.name: taxonomic-composition-data-extraction
skills.search_text: taxonomic-composition-data-extraction Use when a publication reports 16S rRNA taxonomic profiling results (relative abundances, OTU/species/phylum counts) and these figures must be converted into a structured composition table with provenance. Input is already a computed feature/OTU table with taxonomy columns — extraction from prose is unnecessary The target community is eukaryotic ITS-based classification (Warcup V2 'Classify Sequences' at 90% similarity, 75 bp minimum overlap), not 16S/SILVA-based prokaryotic composition Absolute abundance or strain-level resolution is required; the source only reports phylum-level relative percentages and OTU counts with some OTUs left unclassified http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Extracts and tabulates domain- and phylum-level prokaryotic composition from 16S metabarcoding results, as demonstrated by SILVAngs classification of trout farm water reads yielding >99% bacterial OTUs dominated by Proteobacteria (75.57%) and Bacteroidetes (14.40%). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-020-80236-x
skills.summary: Extracts and tabulates domain- and phylum-level prokaryotic composition from 16S metabarcoding results, as demonstrated by SILVAngs classification of trout farm water reads yielding >99% bacterial OTUs dominated by Proteobacteria (75.57%) and Bacteroidetes (14.40%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed feature/OTU table with taxonomy columns — extraction from prose is unnecessary The target community is eukaryotic ITS-based classification (Warcup V2 'Classify Sequences' at 90% similarity, 75 bp minimum overlap), not 16S/SILVA-based prokaryotic composition Absolute abundance or strain-level resolution is required; the source only reports phylum-level relative percentages and OTU counts with some OTUs left unclassified

skills.description: Use when the goal is to measure reference database coverage gaps for a taxonomic group (e.g. Insecta genera with full-length CO1 species-rank sequences) and project when the database will saturate.
skills.name: taxonomic-coverage-extrapolation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-coverage-extrapolation Use when the goal is to measure reference database coverage gaps for a taxonomic group (e.g. Insecta genera with full-length CO1 species-rank sequences) and project when the database will saturate. Input sequences are already a curated training set and the goal is classifier accuracy testing (leave-one-out / cross-validation), not database coverage accounting The analysis goal is taxonomic assignment of metabarcode queries (use the RDP classifier / BLAST classification workflow instead) Growth of the reference database is known to be non-linear or driven by discrete projects, making linear extrapolation inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Quantifies how completely a reference sequence database (e.g. GenBank CO1) covers the taxonomic diversity of a clade, by counting rank-level taxa with qualifying sequences across database snapshots, and extrapolates the linear growth rate to estimate time until full coverage. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Quantifies how completely a reference sequence database (e.g. GenBank CO1) covers the taxonomic diversity of a clade, by counting rank-level taxa with qualifying sequences across database snapshots, and extrapolates the linear growth rate to estimate time until full coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already a curated training set and the goal is classifier accuracy testing (leave-one-out / cross-validation), not database coverage accounting The analysis goal is taxonomic assignment of metabarcode queries (use the RDP classifier / BLAST classification workflow instead) Growth of the reference database is known to be non-linear or driven by discrete projects, making linear extrapolation inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you need to explain per-habitat species-level classification error rates (e.g., from bespoke q2-clawback weights) by measuring how often similar sequences from the same habitat originate from different species.
skills.name: taxonomic-distance-computation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-distance-computation Use when you need to explain per-habitat species-level classification error rates (e.g., from bespoke q2-clawback weights) by measuring how often similar sequences from the same habitat originate from different species. The question is sequence similarity (k-mer/alignment distance) rather than how often taxonomically distinct species produce similar sequences in a habitat No habitat-specific weighted reference distribution exists (natural sample types lacking sufficient characterization cannot have bespoke weights assembled) Evaluating genus-level or higher-rank classification error, where the confusion index's species-level distance signal is not the relevant quantity Computes per-habitat 'confusion indices' — the log of expected taxonomic distance between closely similar marker-gene sequence pairs drawn from a habitat's weighted reference distribution — to quantify how often sequences from different species in the same habitat can be confused. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: Computes per-habitat 'confusion indices' — the log of expected taxonomic distance between closely similar marker-gene sequence pairs drawn from a habitat's weighted reference distribution — to quantify how often sequences from different species in the same habitat can be confused.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is sequence similarity (k-mer/alignment distance) rather than how often taxonomically distinct species produce similar sequences in a habitat No habitat-specific weighted reference distribution exists (natural sample types lacking sufficient characterization cannot have bespoke weights assembled) Evaluating genus-level or higher-rank classification error, where the confusion index's species-level distance signal is not the relevant quantity

skills.description: Use when building counts matrices from profiler/reference pairings (QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 vs. SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, RefSeq) and feature taxonomy strings contain empty rank fields above the deepest assigned label.
skills.name: taxonomic-lineage-propagation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-lineage-propagation Use when building counts matrices from profiler/reference pairings (QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 vs. SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, RefSeq) and feature taxonomy strings contain empty rank fields above the deepest assigned label. Feature taxonomy metadata is already complete with every rank (kingdom through species) explicitly labeled — propagation would overwrite database-provided labels Amplicon pipeline outputs ground-truth species-level calls per feature; here the most-used 16S tools cannot produce high quality genus- or species-level calls, so propagation is only an approximation of granularity Reference lineages from a database with no rank-prefix conventions are being merged with Greengenes-prefixed lineages without preserving prefixes — stripping prefixes would break Greengenes-style lineage consistency http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A post-classification step that fills missing taxonomic ranks (family, genus, species) in OTU/feature metadata by propagating the deepest available lineage label along the reference database's taxonomic path, while annotating each feature with its taxonomic best-hit rank (available granularity). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: A post-classification step that fills missing taxonomic ranks (family, genus, species) in OTU/feature metadata by propagating the deepest available lineage label along the reference database's taxonomic path, while annotating each feature with its taxonomic best-hit rank (available granularity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature taxonomy metadata is already complete with every rank (kingdom through species) explicitly labeled — propagation would overwrite database-provided labels Amplicon pipeline outputs ground-truth species-level calls per feature; here the most-used 16S tools cannot produce high quality genus- or species-level calls, so propagation is only an approximation of granularity Reference lineages from a database with no rank-prefix conventions are being merged with Greengenes-prefixed lineages without preserving prefixes — stripping prefixes would break Greengenes-style lineage consistency

skills.description: Use when building a CO1 (or similar marker gene) reference training set from NCBI-derived sequences and each retained sequence needs its associated taxonomic lineage formatted into RDP taxonomy files.
skills.name: taxonomic-lineage-retrieval-and-formatting
skills.search_text: taxonomic-lineage-retrieval-and-formatting Use when building a CO1 (or similar marker gene) reference training set from NCBI-derived sequences and each retained sequence needs its associated taxonomic lineage formatted into RDP taxonomy files. The input is already an RDP-trained classifier (rRNAClassifier.properties) — no lineage retrieval or reformatting is needed, sequences can be classified directly Sequences have not yet passed the 500 bp length filter and human-contaminant screening — lineage formatting of unfiltered sequences would propagate contaminants into the training set The target is BOLD BIN-based or later releases (v4/v5) that mine both GenBank and BOLD with nucleotide-ambiguity filters — a different curation workflow applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Retrieves the full NCBI taxonomic lineage for every retained CO1 reference sequence and formats taxon lists and RDP-compatible taxonomy files so that a training set can be built and validated against a deposited classifier release. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Retrieves the full NCBI taxonomic lineage for every retained CO1 reference sequence and formats taxon lists and RDP-compatible taxonomy files so that a training set can be built and validated against a deposited classifier release.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an RDP-trained classifier (rRNAClassifier.properties) — no lineage retrieval or reformatting is needed, sequences can be classified directly Sequences have not yet passed the 500 bp length filter and human-contaminant screening — lineage formatting of unfiltered sequences would propagate contaminants into the training set The target is BOLD BIN-based or later releases (v4/v5) that mine both GenBank and BOLD with nucleotide-ambiguity filters — a different curation workflow applies

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic/16S profiler reports high-confidence assignments to an unexpected taxon whose abundance correlates with a known community member (here Pearson r = 0.959), suggesting the reference library—not the reads—carries a contaminant.
skills.name: taxonomic-misassignment-root-cause-analysis
skills.search_text: taxonomic-misassignment-root-cause-analysis Use when a metagenomic/16S profiler reports high-confidence assignments to an unexpected taxon whose abundance correlates with a known community member (here Pearson r = 0.959), suggesting the reference library—not the reads—carries a contaminant. The profiler's outputs already agree with the mock community's expected composition — there is no misassignment to root-cause. You are benchmarking profiler/reference-library accuracy on clean libraries rather than diagnosing a specific anomalous taxonomic call. The unexpected taxon call lacks a plausible donor organism in the sample whose abundance could correlate with it (no contamination hypothesis to test). http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A diagnostic procedure for tracing unexpected taxonomic calls (e.g., PathoScope's Tumebacillus flagellatus misassignments in 16S mock-community data) to contamination embedded in the reference database itself, via pairwise BLAST of a suspect taxon's marker gene against the exact RefSeq scaffold. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: A diagnostic procedure for tracing unexpected taxonomic calls (e.g., PathoScope's Tumebacillus flagellatus misassignments in 16S mock-community data) to contamination embedded in the reference database itself, via pairwise BLAST of a suspect taxon's marker gene against the exact RefSeq scaffold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The profiler's outputs already agree with the mock community's expected composition — there is no misassignment to root-cause. You are benchmarking profiler/reference-library accuracy on clean libraries rather than diagnosing a specific anomalous taxonomic call. The unexpected taxon call lacks a plausible donor organism in the sample whose abundance could correlate with it (no contamination hypothesis to test).

skills.description: Use when you have a resolved species list from eDNA metabarcoding and need to verify plausibility by checking each taxon against independent occurrence records for the sampling region (e.g., locality or island-level faunistic data).
skills.name: taxonomic-name-matching
skills.search_text: taxonomic-name-matching Use when you have a resolved species list from eDNA metabarcoding and need to verify plausibility by checking each taxon against independent occurrence records for the sampling region (e.g., locality or island-level faunistic data). The taxon list is unresolved to species level (the concordance check presumes named taxa that can be matched to database records) The sampling region lies outside the geographic coverage of Naturbasen and Fauna Europaea (Danish/European fauna databases) The input is raw sequencing reads rather than a curated, resolved species list http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Cross-references a resolved eDNA taxon list against independent faunistic occurrence databases (Naturbasen/allearter, Fauna Europaea) to validate that metabarcoded arthropod species correspond to documented field records at specific localities. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.4809
skills.summary: Cross-references a resolved eDNA taxon list against independent faunistic occurrence databases (Naturbasen/allearter, Fauna Europaea) to validate that metabarcoded arthropod species correspond to documented field records at specific localities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The taxon list is unresolved to species level (the concordance check presumes named taxa that can be matched to database records) The sampling region lies outside the geographic coverage of Naturbasen and Fauna Europaea (Danish/European fauna databases) The input is raw sequencing reads rather than a curated, resolved species list

skills.description: Use when you have a BIOM abundance table plus sample metadata (e.g., EMP environment types non-saline/saline/animal/plant) and need to test whether taxa at phylum, class, or order level are gained but not lost with increasing sample richness.
skills.name: taxonomic-nestedness-nodf-analysis
skills.search_text: taxonomic-nestedness-nodf-analysis Use when you have a BIOM abundance table plus sample metadata (e.g., EMP environment types non-saline/saline/animal/plant) and need to test whether taxa at phylum, class, or order level are gained but not lost with increasing sample richness. Raw count matrices: the workflow binarizes to presence-absence before computing NODF, so applying it directly to raw abundances or rarefied counts misrepresents the metric Questions about beta diversity, ordination, or source tracking (e.g., SourceTracker2 use cases) rather than nestedness of community composition Datasets lacking environment-type metadata or with too few taxa per sample to support meaningful null-model permutations http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies whether microbial community taxonomic composition is nested across environments by computing the NODF (Nestedness based on Overlap and Decreasing Fill) statistic on binary presence-absence matrices from EMP 16S Release 1, tested against an equiprobable-rows/fixed-columns null model. It reproduces the finding that EMP communities are significantly nested (overall NODF = 0.841 ± 0.018, P < 0.0001). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/nature24621
skills.summary: Quantifies whether microbial community taxonomic composition is nested across environments by computing the NODF (Nestedness based on Overlap and Decreasing Fill) statistic on binary presence-absence matrices from EMP 16S Release 1, tested against an equiprobable-rows/fixed-columns null model. It reproduces the finding that EMP communities are significantly nested (overall NODF = 0.841 ± 0.018, P < 0.0001).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw count matrices: the workflow binarizes to presence-absence before computing NODF, so applying it directly to raw abundances or rarefied counts misrepresents the metric Questions about beta diversity, ordination, or source tracking (e.g., SourceTracker2 use cases) rather than nestedness of community composition Datasets lacking environment-type metadata or with too few taxa per sample to support meaningful null-model permutations

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or compare strain- and species-level read-assignment accuracy (precision, recall, precision2) and composition-estimation accuracy (r2, L1 distance) of long-read metagenomic classifiers on mock or simulated communities with known ground truth.
skills.name: taxonomic-profile-benchmarking
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profile-benchmarking Use when you need to reproduce or compare strain- and species-level read-assignment accuracy (precision, recall, precision2) and composition-estimation accuracy (r2, L1 distance) of long-read metagenomic classifiers on mock or simulated communities with known ground truth. Samples dominated by short reads — the article notes that analysis of samples with a high proportion of short reads is not well addressed by MetaMaps because minimizer sets become too small Samples whose organisms are absent or poorly represented in the reference database — database-sample incongruity (yet-uncharacterized taxonomic entities) is an acknowledged unresolved concern Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities, which the authors state remain challenging http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark long-read metagenomic classifiers and sample-composition estimators (MetaMaps vs Centrifuge, Kraken/Kraken 2, Bracken, LAST+MEGAN-LR) on simulated (i100, p25) and real (HMP7, Zymo, CAMI) datasets against the >12,000-genome RefSeq miniSeq+H database, computing per-read precision/recall and Pearson r2/L1 distance between estimated and true compositions. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-10934-2
skills.summary: Benchmark long-read metagenomic classifiers and sample-composition estimators (MetaMaps vs Centrifuge, Kraken/Kraken 2, Bracken, LAST+MEGAN-LR) on simulated (i100, p25) and real (HMP7, Zymo, CAMI) datasets against the >12,000-genome RefSeq miniSeq+H database, computing per-read precision/recall and Pearson r2/L1 distance between estimated and true compositions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples dominated by short reads — the article notes that analysis of samples with a high proportion of short reads is not well addressed by MetaMaps because minimizer sets become too small Samples whose organisms are absent or poorly represented in the reference database — database-sample incongruity (yet-uncharacterized taxonomic entities) is an acknowledged unresolved concern Complex samples comprising many non-characterized entities, which the authors state remain challenging

skills.description: Use when you have a per-pairing benchmark metrics table (sensitivity, specificity, error score, alpha diversity deviation for each profiler-library combination) and need to determine which metrics are correlated and which pairings occupy the high-sensitivity/high-specificity quadrant.
skills.name: taxonomic-profiler-benchmark-visualization
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profiler-benchmark-visualization Use when you have a per-pairing benchmark metrics table (sensitivity, specificity, error score, alpha diversity deviation for each profiler-library combination) and need to determine which metrics are correlated and which pairings occupy the high-sensitivity/high-specificity quadrant. Input is raw sequencing data or taxonomy calls rather than an already-computed benchmark metrics table — profiling must be run first (e.g., with PathoScope 2 or Kraken 2) before correlations can be computed The analysis goal is per-tool accuracy ranking alone (e.g., which library is most accurate) without examining cross-metric relationships — use a direct benchmark comparison instead The data are single-sample taxonomic profiles rather than aggregated mock-community benchmark metrics across the 136-sample mock community set http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Visualizes and quantifies how benchmark metrics co-vary across 16S profiler/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes/SILVA/RefSeq/Kraken Standard), using Spearman rank correlations of species-level sensitivity vs specificity and error score vs alpha diversity deviation, with scatterplots marking per-pairing centroids. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Visualizes and quantifies how benchmark metrics co-vary across 16S profiler/reference-library pairings (DADA2, QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 x Greengenes/SILVA/RefSeq/Kraken Standard), using Spearman rank correlations of species-level sensitivity vs specificity and error score vs alpha diversity deviation, with scatterplots marking per-pairing centroids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or taxonomy calls rather than an already-computed benchmark metrics table — profiling must be run first (e.g., with PathoScope 2 or Kraken 2) before correlations can be computed The analysis goal is per-tool accuracy ranking alone (e.g., which library is most accurate) without examining cross-metric relationships — use a direct benchmark comparison instead The data are single-sample taxonomic profiles rather than aggregated mock-community benchmark metrics across the 136-sample mock community set

skills.description: Use when a QC'd eDNA OTU table contains taxonomic assignments at mixed ranks and you need Family-or-higher agglomeration, per-row rank annotation, and marine/terrestrial filtering before reporting taxon counts.
skills.name: taxonomic-rank-annotation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-rank-annotation Use when a QC'd eDNA OTU table contains taxonomic assignments at mixed ranks and you need Family-or-higher agglomeration, per-row rank annotation, and marine/terrestrial filtering before reporting taxon counts. Input is already agglomerated at Family or higher rank with rank annotations — re-agglomeration would double-collapse taxa The goal is species-level biodiversity reporting — the paper notes 'the lower the taxonomy assignment, the lower the confidence in that assignment becomes', so species-level claims need expanded reference databases rather than Family-level pooling The dataset is not a multilocus eDNA amplicon time-series and lacks lineage/provenance labels needed to remove terrestrial taxa http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Agglomerates QC'd OTU-level taxonomic assignments from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing to Family-or-higher rank, annotates each agglomerated row with its taxonomic rank, and separates marine from terrestrial taxa so biodiversity totals (663 taxonomic groups; 348 unique marine taxa, 274 at Family level) can be verified against the published time-series dataset. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Agglomerates QC'd OTU-level taxonomic assignments from multilocus eDNA amplicon sequencing to Family-or-higher rank, annotates each agglomerated row with its taxonomic rank, and separates marine from terrestrial taxa so biodiversity totals (663 taxonomic groups; 348 unique marine taxa, 274 at Family level) can be verified against the published time-series dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already agglomerated at Family or higher rank with rank annotations — re-agglomeration would double-collapse taxa The goal is species-level biodiversity reporting — the paper notes 'the lower the taxonomy assignment, the lower the confidence in that assignment becomes', so species-level claims need expanded reference databases rather than Family-level pooling The dataset is not a multilocus eDNA amplicon time-series and lacks lineage/provenance labels needed to remove terrestrial taxa

skills.description: Use when validating OTU tables (raw or LULU-curated, e.g. from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2) against ground-truth survey data, and you need to measure how many OTUs redundantly represent the same species.
skills.name: taxonomic-redundancy-quantification
skills.search_text: taxonomic-redundancy-quantification Use when validating OTU tables (raw or LULU-curated, e.g. from VSEARCH, SWARM, CROP or DADA2) against ground-truth survey data, and you need to measure how many OTUs redundantly represent the same species. No reference-database assignments exist for the OTUs — the article's redundancy metric is defined via OTU-to-GenBank species assignment and cannot be computed without them The goal is identifying individual rare species rather than community-level biodiversity metrics — the authors note LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species Input is a taxon-free abundance matrix without OTU ids matching the centroid sequences, so OTUs cannot be linked to GenBank assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies taxonomic redundancy of an OTU table — the degree to which multiple OTUs map to the same species via reference-database (GenBank) assignments — as a validation metric for post-clustering curation with LULU. In the Frøslev et al. plant ITS2 study, redundancy dropped from 22–81% before curation to 6–13% at the 97% clustering level after LULU. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-017-01312-x
skills.summary: Quantifies taxonomic redundancy of an OTU table — the degree to which multiple OTUs map to the same species via reference-database (GenBank) assignments — as a validation metric for post-clustering curation with LULU. In the Frøslev et al. plant ITS2 study, redundancy dropped from 22–81% before curation to 6–13% at the 97% clustering level after LULU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference-database assignments exist for the OTUs — the article's redundancy metric is defined via OTU-to-GenBank species assignment and cannot be computed without them The goal is identifying individual rare species rather than community-level biodiversity metrics — the authors note LULU curation may not be suitable for identifying single rare species Input is a taxon-free abundance matrix without OTU ids matching the centroid sequences, so OTUs cannot be linked to GenBank assignments

skills.description: Use when assigning genus-rank taxonomy to primer-anchored CO1 amplicon sequences (~100-650 bp) and you need high-confidence assignments with a controlled false positive rate rather than accepting the top BLAST hit.
skills.name: taxonomic-sequence-classification
skills.search_text: taxonomic-sequence-classification Use when assigning genus-rank taxonomy to primer-anchored CO1 amplicon sequences (~100-650 bp) and you need high-confidence assignments with a controlled false positive rate rather than accepting the top BLAST hit. You need species-rank assignments for short fragments: Table 2 gives NA (no cutoff achieves 99% correct assignments) for species rank, so use genus or more inclusive ranks for 200 bp reads Query sequences are expected to be absent from the reference database (e.g. quarantine screening for unstudied local biota): the classifier cannot classify taxa not in the training set and false negatives occur when congeneric sequences are missing Your input is already an OTU/ASV feature table with taxonomy — no per-sequence classification step is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences using the RDP naive Bayesian classifier with pre-trained CO1 Eukaryote reference sets, and benchmark it against the top BLAST hit method; the RDP approach reduces the false positive rate from nearly 100% (top BLAST hit) to 34% while running ~19x faster. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to CO1 metabarcode sequences using the RDP naive Bayesian classifier with pre-trained CO1 Eukaryote reference sets, and benchmark it against the top BLAST hit method; the RDP approach reduces the false positive rate from nearly 100% (top BLAST hit) to 34% while running ~19x faster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need species-rank assignments for short fragments: Table 2 gives NA (no cutoff achieves 99% correct assignments) for species rank, so use genus or more inclusive ranks for 200 bp reads Query sequences are expected to be absent from the reference database (e.g. quarantine screening for unstudied local biota): the classifier cannot classify taxa not in the training set and false negatives occur when congeneric sequences are missing Your input is already an OTU/ASV feature table with taxonomy — no per-sequence classification step is needed

skills.description: Use when you hold two or more RDP classifier training sets (a taxonomy file plus a FASTA file each) and need to verify claims about how many taxa and reference sequences each covers.
skills.name: taxonomic-training-set-parsing
skills.search_text: taxonomic-training-set-parsing Use when you hold two or more RDP classifier training sets (a taxonomy file plus a FASTA file each) and need to verify claims about how many taxa and reference sequences each covers. You need to classify new query sequences with the RDP classifier rather than characterize training set contents — use the trained rRNAClassifier.properties files directly instead. Your training set is not formatted as an RDP-style taxonomy file plus FASTA pair (e.g. you only have BLAST or SINTAX formatted references, which the README distributes separately as of v5.0.0). You are comparing v1 and v2 CO1 training sets for species-rank assessment — the v2 species-trained set has different singleton proportions (33% vs 23% singleton genera) and requires rank-aware comparison, not simple genus counting. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Parses RDP classifier training sets (taxonomy and FASTA reference files) from the CO1Classifier releases to quantify taxonomic coverage (unique taxa at genus rank) and reference sequence counts, enabling direct comparison against older training sets such as the March 2013 Insecta Genbank-Genus classifier. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-018-22505-4
skills.summary: Parses RDP classifier training sets (taxonomy and FASTA reference files) from the CO1Classifier releases to quantify taxonomic coverage (unique taxa at genus rank) and reference sequence counts, enabling direct comparison against older training sets such as the March 2013 Insecta Genbank-Genus classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to classify new query sequences with the RDP classifier rather than characterize training set contents — use the trained rRNAClassifier.properties files directly instead. Your training set is not formatted as an RDP-style taxonomy file plus FASTA pair (e.g. you only have BLAST or SINTAX formatted references, which the README distributes separately as of v5.0.0). You are comparing v1 and v2 CO1 training sets for species-rank assessment — the v2 species-trained set has different singleton proportions (33% vs 23% singleton genera) and requires rank-aware comparison, not simple genus counting.

skills.description: Use when a counts matrix built from a profiler/reference pairing has features with incomplete taxonomies (e.g., an order-level-only lineage) and downstream genus- or species-level benchmarking requires every rank field populated with an explicit -hit granularity annotation.
skills.name: taxonomy-rank-prefix-parsing
skills.search_text: taxonomy-rank-prefix-parsing Use when a counts matrix built from a profiler/reference pairing has features with incomplete taxonomies (e.g., an order-level-only lineage) and downstream genus- or species-level benchmarking requires every rank field populated with an explicit -hit granularity annotation. Input features already carry non-empty labels at every rank (k__ through s__), so no propagation is needed The goal is a genuine genus/species-level assignment rather than a propagated best-hit label — propagated fields overstate the available granularity (e.g., an order-only hit does not become a true species call) The profiler output does not expose a traceable taxonomic hierarchy, so lineage strings cannot be parsed rank-by-rank http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Parses per-feature lineage strings from 16S profiling outputs (QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 against SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, and RefSeq) rank-by-rank, propagates the deepest available taxonomic label into every higher-rank field, and annotates each feature with the deepest rank reached (taxonomic best hit). This enables consistent family/genus/species comparison across profiler-by-reference-library combinations. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Parses per-feature lineage strings from 16S profiling outputs (QIIME 2, Mothur, PathoScope 2, Kraken 2 against SILVA 138, Greengenes 13_8, and RefSeq) rank-by-rank, propagates the deepest available taxonomic label into every higher-rank field, and annotates each feature with the deepest rank reached (taxonomic best hit). This enables consistent family/genus/species comparison across profiler-by-reference-library combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features already carry non-empty labels at every rank (k__ through s__), so no propagation is needed The goal is a genuine genus/species-level assignment rather than a propagated best-hit label — propagated fields overstate the available granularity (e.g., an order-only hit does not become a true species call) The profiler output does not expose a traceable taxonomic hierarchy, so lineage strings cannot be parsed rank-by-rank

skills.description: Use when building shuffled stratified 5-fold splits over reference sequences and empirical samples (e.g., Qiita habitats) and some taxonomy labels lack enough members to be stratified on their own.
skills.name: taxonomy-stratum-merging-via-confidence-weighted-voting
skills.search_text: taxonomy-stratum-merging-via-confidence-weighted-voting Use when building shuffled stratified 5-fold splits over reference sequences and empirical samples (e.g., Qiita habitats) and some taxonomy labels lack enough members to be stratified on their own. All taxonomies have sufficient members for scikit-learn StratifiedKFold stratification, so no merging is needed You only need off-the-shelf taxonomic weights and can use readytowear pre-trained classifiers instead of running the clawback cross-validation workflow Your goal is plain k-fold CV that ignores taxon proportions and empirical abundances — stratification and stratum merging are unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Within the empirical-abundance-aware stratified 5-fold cross-validation of q2-clawback, taxonomies with too few reference members to support StratifiedKFold are merged into strata, with stratum membership decided by imbalanced-learn's confidence-weighted voting. This keeps every fold carrying comparable taxon proportions while preserving abundance-aware class weights. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12669-6
skills.summary: Within the empirical-abundance-aware stratified 5-fold cross-validation of q2-clawback, taxonomies with too few reference members to support StratifiedKFold are merged into strata, with stratum membership decided by imbalanced-learn's confidence-weighted voting. This keeps every fold carrying comparable taxon proportions while preserving abundance-aware class weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All taxonomies have sufficient members for scikit-learn StratifiedKFold stratification, so no merging is needed You only need off-the-shelf taxonomic weights and can use readytowear pre-trained classifiers instead of running the clawback cross-validation workflow Your goal is plain k-fold CV that ignores taxon proportions and empirical abundances — stratification and stratum merging are unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when you have 99%-similarity MOTU representative sequences (post sumaclust, single-read MOTUs removed) and need each MOTU assigned to the most specific consistent taxon and merged with per-sample read counts into one table.
skills.name: taxonomy-table-integration-with-read-counts
skills.search_text: taxonomy-table-integration-with-read-counts Use when you have 99%-similarity MOTU representative sequences (post sumaclust, single-read MOTUs removed) and need each MOTU assigned to the most specific consistent taxon and merged with per-sample read counts into one table. Input is raw or unclustered reads — taxonomic assignment should be done on MOTU representative sequences, not individual reads Reference database is not formatted for OBITools (no obitax taxonomy); ecotag cannot resolve taxon names without it The marker region resolves species uniquely (no 100% multi-species matches) — then simple best-hit assignment suffices and MOTU splitting is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Assigns MOTU representative sequences to taxa by running ecotag (OBITools) against a BOLD-derived COI reference database, then aggregates the ecotag output into a per-MOTU table joining MOTU IDs, per-sample read counts, and assigned taxonomy. This is the step that turns delimited MOTUs into a taxonomically interpretable abundance table for eDNA metabarcoding studies. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-017-17150-2
skills.summary: Assigns MOTU representative sequences to taxa by running ecotag (OBITools) against a BOLD-derived COI reference database, then aggregates the ecotag output into a per-MOTU table joining MOTU IDs, per-sample read counts, and assigned taxonomy. This is the step that turns delimited MOTUs into a taxonomically interpretable abundance table for eDNA metabarcoding studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unclustered reads — taxonomic assignment should be done on MOTU representative sequences, not individual reads Reference database is not formatted for OBITools (no obitax taxonomy); ecotag cannot resolve taxon names without it The marker region resolves species uniquely (no 100% multi-species matches) — then simple best-hit assignment suffices and MOTU splitting is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when the FASTQ-derived occurrence table is replicate-structured (each sample sequenced in >=2 PCR replicates) and non-reproducible ASV occurrences must be removed before downstream ecological analysis.
skills.name: technical-replicate-occurrence-filtering
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-occurrence-filtering Use when the FASTQ-derived occurrence table is replicate-structured (each sample sequenced in >=2 PCR replicates) and non-reproducible ASV occurrences must be removed before downstream ecological analysis. Samples lack technical replicates (e.g. single-replicate designs), so replicate reproducibility cannot be assessed The input is already a filtered ASV-per-sample count table with no replicate dimension — applying a replicate threshold would be meaningless The goal is controlling contamination or index hopping, which in VTAM is handled by negative-control/mock-sample filters rather than the replicate filter http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Filters metabarcoding occurrence tables (ASV i, sample j, replicate k with read count Nijk) by requiring each ASV-sample occurrence to appear in a minimum number of the sample's technical replicates, as implemented by VTAM's FilterMinReplicateNumber. Non-reproducible occurrences are discarded to ensure repeatability and reduce spurious detections. metabarcoding/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.01.034
skills.summary: Filters metabarcoding occurrence tables (ASV i, sample j, replicate k with read count Nijk) by requiring each ASV-sample occurrence to appear in a minimum number of the sample's technical replicates, as implemented by VTAM's FilterMinReplicateNumber. Non-reproducible occurrences are discarded to ensure repeatability and reduce spurious detections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack technical replicates (e.g. single-replicate designs), so replicate reproducibility cannot be assessed The input is already a filtered ASV-per-sample count table with no replicate dimension — applying a replicate threshold would be meaningless The goal is controlling contamination or index hopping, which in VTAM is handled by negative-control/mock-sample filters rather than the replicate filter

skills.description: Use when simulating between-sample abundance variability for genome-derived ASV counts in MHASS-style PacBio HiFi amplicon data, i.e. when converting genome molarity values into replicate-specific abundance matrices.
skills.name: technical-replicate-variability-emulation
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-variability-emulation Use when simulating between-sample abundance variability for genome-derived ASV counts in MHASS-style PacBio HiFi amplicon data, i.e. when converting genome molarity values into replicate-specific abundance matrices. The input is already an observed ASV count/feature table — variability should come from data, not from the metaSPARSim R1-preset model. You need true biological replicate heterogeneity rather than MHASS's emulated model where negative-dispersion samples become identical replicates before technical sampling. Simulating sequencing platform noise (read errors, number of passes) rather than between-sample abundance variability — use the PBSIM3 and num-passes (empirical or lognormal, mu 3.88 / sigma 1.22) components instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements MHASS's genome-aware abundance variability step: a negative binomial model using metaSPARSim's R1 preset values predicts each ASV's squared coefficient of variation between samples from its expected abundance, with NA dispersion estimates emulated as zero variability so replicates are identical before technical sampling. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf656
skills.summary: Implements MHASS's genome-aware abundance variability step: a negative binomial model using metaSPARSim's R1 preset values predicts each ASV's squared coefficient of variation between samples from its expected abundance, with NA dispersion estimates emulated as zero variability so replicates are identical before technical sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an observed ASV count/feature table — variability should come from data, not from the metaSPARSim R1-preset model. You need true biological replicate heterogeneity rather than MHASS's emulated model where negative-dispersion samples become identical replicates before technical sampling. Simulating sequencing platform noise (read errors, number of passes) rather than between-sample abundance variability — use the PBSIM3 and num-passes (empirical or lognormal, mu 3.88 / sigma 1.22) components instead.

skills.description: Use when comparing the processing speed of FASTQ preprocessors (e.g. fastp, FASTQC, Cutadapt, SOAPnuke, AfterQC, Trimmomatic, umis, UMI-tools) on the same dataset and you need a defensible throughput table.
skills.name: throughput-calculation
skills.search_text: throughput-calculation Use when comparing the processing speed of FASTQ preprocessors (e.g. fastp, FASTQC, Cutadapt, SOAPnuke, AfterQC, Trimmomatic, umis, UMI-tools) on the same dataset and you need a defensible throughput table. Input is not FASTQ preprocessing (e.g. alignment or variant calling throughput) — the published ratios apply to FASTQ preprocessing tools only The goal is to compare output quality/filtering behavior rather than speed; time measurements alone say nothing about result equivalence Datasets or threading configurations differ between tools, making wall-clock times incomparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark FASTQ preprocessing tool throughput by recording wall-clock execution times on a fixed dataset and converting them to reads/second or GB/minute, as done to show fastp is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic/Cutadapt and ~2.7x faster than umis and ~6.1x faster than UMI-tools for UMI preprocessing. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty560
skills.summary: Benchmark FASTQ preprocessing tool throughput by recording wall-clock execution times on a fixed dataset and converting them to reads/second or GB/minute, as done to show fastp is 2-5x faster than Trimmomatic/Cutadapt and ~2.7x faster than umis and ~6.1x faster than UMI-tools for UMI preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not FASTQ preprocessing (e.g. alignment or variant calling throughput) — the published ratios apply to FASTQ preprocessing tools only The goal is to compare output quality/filtering behavior rather than speed; time measurements alone say nothing about result equivalence Datasets or threading configurations differ between tools, making wall-clock times incomparable

skills.description: Use when a rank-based co-occurrence network built from proportional-abundance time-series (taxa × environmental properties) needs multiple-testing-corrected significance thresholds, e.g. thousands of pairwise Kendall tau comparisons.
skills.name: time-series-co-occurrence-significance-thresholding
skills.search_text: time-series-co-occurrence-significance-thresholding Use when a rank-based co-occurrence network built from proportional-abundance time-series (taxa × environmental properties) needs multiple-testing-corrected significance thresholds, e.g. thousands of pairwise Kendall tau comparisons. When the goal is taxonomic detection or abundance estimation itself rather than significance-thresholding of co-occurrence statistics — the article notes amplification bias, inhibitors, and variable template abundances affect taxa detection, and 'no method—including this one—identifies all taxa in an ecosystem' When the time-series is too short to support 100-permutation null estimation with enough power — the article states 'longer time-series needed to increase power and validity' When interpreting network edges as confirmed biological interactions: 'Network connectivity does not necessarily indicate interaction' A permutation null-model procedure that assigns empirical p-values to pairwise Kendall's tau rank correlations computed over an 18-month Monterey Bay eDNA proportional-abundance time-series and applies Benjamani-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, yielding a corrected significance threshold of tau = 0.70. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: A permutation null-model procedure that assigns empirical p-values to pairwise Kendall's tau rank correlations computed over an 18-month Monterey Bay eDNA proportional-abundance time-series and applies Benjamani-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, yielding a corrected significance threshold of tau = 0.70.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is taxonomic detection or abundance estimation itself rather than significance-thresholding of co-occurrence statistics — the article notes amplification bias, inhibitors, and variable template abundances affect taxa detection, and 'no method—including this one—identifies all taxa in an ecosystem' When the time-series is too short to support 100-permutation null estimation with enough power — the article states 'longer time-series needed to increase power and validity' When interpreting network edges as confirmed biological interactions: 'Network connectivity does not necessarily indicate interaction'

skills.description: Use when a taxon-by-sample abundance index table spanning many time points needs to be partitioned into correlated-abundance modules (e.g. subnetworks), starting from a taxon-by-taxon correlation structure with WGCNA soft-thresholding.
skills.name: topological-overlap-matrix-clustering
skills.search_text: topological-overlap-matrix-clustering Use when a taxon-by-sample abundance index table spanning many time points needs to be partitioned into correlated-abundance modules (e.g. subnetworks), starting from a taxon-by-taxon correlation structure with WGCNA soft-thresholding. Input is raw sequencing reads or an unnormalized amplicon table — the method requires the processed proportional-abundance index table, not FASTQ or filter-stage data Data are a single-snapshot community composition (no temporal dimension) — seasonal membership of modules cannot be assigned from temporal abundance patterns without a time-series The goal is detecting direct predator-prey interactions — the article notes that whether co-occurrence reflects direct interactions or a common response to an external driver is unclear, so modules should not be read as interaction evidence http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies WGCNA (weighted gene correlation network analysis) to an eDNA amplicon-index abundance time-series to cluster 663 Monterey Bay taxa into co-occurring subnetworks (modules) via a topological overlap dissimilarity matrix and dynamic tree cut, reproducing the paper's six seasonally-coherent communities. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-14105-1
skills.summary: Applies WGCNA (weighted gene correlation network analysis) to an eDNA amplicon-index abundance time-series to cluster 663 Monterey Bay taxa into co-occurring subnetworks (modules) via a topological overlap dissimilarity matrix and dynamic tree cut, reproducing the paper's six seasonally-coherent communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or an unnormalized amplicon table — the method requires the processed proportional-abundance index table, not FASTQ or filter-stage data Data are a single-snapshot community composition (no temporal dimension) — seasonal membership of modules cannot be assigned from temporal abundance patterns without a time-series The goal is detecting direct predator-prey interactions — the article notes that whether co-occurrence reflects direct interactions or a common response to an external driver is unclear, so modules should not be read as interaction evidence

skills.description: Use when an unfiltered ASV count table (TSV) plus a two-column sample-group metadata TSV must be turned into depth-normalized inputs for run_all_tools.sh, i.e., when samples have unequal read depths and a common rarefaction depth must be chosen and enforced.
skills.name: tsv-metadata-table-handling
skills.search_text: tsv-metadata-table-handling Use when an unfiltered ASV count table (TSV) plus a two-column sample-group metadata TSV must be turned into depth-normalized inputs for run_all_tools.sh, i.e., when samples have unequal read depths and a common rarefaction depth must be chosen and enforced. The count table is already rarefied or sample depths are equal — re-subsampling would discard data without benefit. The metadata file has more than two columns or more than two groupings; run_all_tools.sh expects a two-column TSV with maximum 2 groupings. The downstream analysis is one for which rarefying is out of scope (e.g. the article explicitly leaves open whether rarefying is advisable prior to computing diversity metrics). Prepares TSV-formatted ASV count tables and two-column metadata tables for the 14-tool differential abundance pipeline, including subsampling (rarefying) every sample to a common per-sample read depth (D = 2000 in the manuscript analysis) so that all samples have equal library size before DA testing. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-022-28034-z
skills.summary: Prepares TSV-formatted ASV count tables and two-column metadata tables for the 14-tool differential abundance pipeline, including subsampling (rarefying) every sample to a common per-sample read depth (D = 2000 in the manuscript analysis) so that all samples have equal library size before DA testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count table is already rarefied or sample depths are equal — re-subsampling would discard data without benefit. The metadata file has more than two columns or more than two groupings; run_all_tools.sh expects a two-column TSV with maximum 2 groupings. The downstream analysis is one for which rarefying is out of scope (e.g. the article explicitly leaves open whether rarefying is advisable prior to computing diversity metrics).

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple profiler/library pairings on per-sample benchmark metrics and you need statistically corrected pairwise significance calls (e.g., ranking Kraken 2 vs. DADA2/QIIME 2/Mothur/PathoScope on 136 mock community samples).
skills.name: tukey-corrected-posthoc-contrast-analysis
skills.search_text: tukey-corrected-posthoc-contrast-analysis Use when comparing multiple profiler/library pairings on per-sample benchmark metrics and you need statistically corrected pairwise significance calls (e.g., ranking Kraken 2 vs. DADA2/QIIME 2/Mothur/PathoScope on 136 mock community samples). When the input is already a table of pairwise contrasts or significance calls — no model fitting is needed When the analysis goal is raw per-sample metric computation (sensitivity/specificity/NRMSE per sample) rather than statistical comparison of pairings When observations are not nested by a shared unit (e.g., no repeated measurement of the same mock community sample), in which case a random intercept of sample is not warranted http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fits linear mixed-effects models to per-sample benchmark metrics (sensitivity, specificity, NRMSE, alpha diversity) across profiler/reference-library pairings and extracts all pairwise Tukey-adjusted post hoc contrasts, reproducing the significance tables used to rank 16S taxonomic profilers. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41598-023-40799-x
skills.summary: Fits linear mixed-effects models to per-sample benchmark metrics (sensitivity, specificity, NRMSE, alpha diversity) across profiler/reference-library pairings and extracts all pairwise Tukey-adjusted post hoc contrasts, reproducing the significance tables used to rank 16S taxonomic profilers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a table of pairwise contrasts or significance calls — no model fitting is needed When the analysis goal is raw per-sample metric computation (sensitivity/specificity/NRMSE per sample) rather than statistical comparison of pairings When observations are not nested by a shared unit (e.g., no repeated measurement of the same mock community sample), in which case a random intercept of sample is not warranted

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomes contain an uncharacterized species-level genome bin (uSGB) detected by MetaPhlAn 4 and you need strain-level resolution — phylogeny reconstruction, strain sharing, or transmission inference — without a cultured isolate reference.
skills.name: uncharacterized-species-strain-profiling
skills.search_text: uncharacterized-species-strain-profiling Use when shotgun metagenomes contain an uncharacterized species-level genome bin (uSGB) detected by MetaPhlAn 4 and you need strain-level resolution — phylogeny reconstruction, strain sharing, or transmission inference — without a cultured isolate reference. The species of interest has a cultured isolate reference genome — a reference-based strain analysis may be more appropriate than uSGB marker-based profiling. The target uSGB is not reliably detected by MetaPhlAn 4 in enough samples to support marker alignment and phylogeny (too few positive samples). The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic/strain-level profiling — use HUMAnN instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Profiles and performs strain-level phylogenetic analysis of taxonomically uncharacterized species (uSGBs) by combining MetaPhlAn 4 species detection with StrainPhlAn 4 marker-based consensus tree reconstruction, enabling strain-sharing and transmission inference (e.g. mother-to-infant vertical transmission of Lachnospiraceae SGB4894). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Profiles and performs strain-level phylogenetic analysis of taxonomically uncharacterized species (uSGBs) by combining MetaPhlAn 4 species detection with StrainPhlAn 4 marker-based consensus tree reconstruction, enabling strain-sharing and transmission inference (e.g. mother-to-infant vertical transmission of Lachnospiraceae SGB4894).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species of interest has a cultured isolate reference genome — a reference-based strain analysis may be more appropriate than uSGB marker-based profiling. The target uSGB is not reliably detected by MetaPhlAn 4 in enough samples to support marker alignment and phylogeny (too few positive samples). The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic/strain-level profiling — use HUMAnN instead.

skills.description: Use when profiling shotgun metagenomic samples with MetaPhlAn 4 and you need to quantify the fraction of reads explained (including reads mapping to uSGBs), or when comparing MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 explainable-read fractions across environments.
skills.name: unclassified-reads-estimation
skills.search_text: unclassified-reads-estimation Use when profiling shotgun metagenomic samples with MetaPhlAn 4 and you need to quantify the fraction of reads explained (including reads mapping to uSGBs), or when comparing MetaPhlAn 4 vs MetaPhlAn 3 explainable-read fractions across environments. The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic profiling — MetaPhlAn is a taxonomic profiler; use HUMAnN for functional profiles. The sample comes from environmental, nonhost-associated, or under-studied microbial communities where sequences remain highly enriched for those not captured even by current uSGBs — explainable-read gains will be limited and interpretation should be cautious. Input is already a species-level relative-abundance table from another profiler and no re-profiling with MetaPhlAn 4 is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Runs MetaPhlAn 4 with its unclassified-reads estimation feature enabled so that shotgun metagenomic reads assigned to taxonomically unidentified species-level genome bins (uSGBs) are counted as 'explainable', quantifying how much more of each sample MetaPhlAn 4 profiles versus MetaPhlAn 3. metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41587-023-01688-w
skills.summary: Runs MetaPhlAn 4 with its unclassified-reads estimation feature enabled so that shotgun metagenomic reads assigned to taxonomically unidentified species-level genome bins (uSGBs) are counted as 'explainable', quantifying how much more of each sample MetaPhlAn 4 profiles versus MetaPhlAn 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional profiling (genes/pathways) rather than taxonomic profiling — MetaPhlAn is a taxonomic profiler; use HUMAnN for functional profiles. The sample comes from environmental, nonhost-associated, or under-studied microbial communities where sequences remain highly enriched for those not captured even by current uSGBs — explainable-read gains will be limited and interpretation should be cautious. Input is already a species-level relative-abundance table from another profiler and no re-profiling with MetaPhlAn 4 is needed.

skills.description: Use when a mock-community ASV or OTU feature table (e.g. from DADA2, Deblur, or VSEARCH clustering of 181 bp COI amplicons) still retains unexpected 'miss' or partial mock variants after denoising, and abundance-based filtering must remove them.
skills.name: unexpected-sequence-variant-removal
skills.search_text: unexpected-sequence-variant-removal Use when a mock-community ASV or OTU feature table (e.g. from DADA2, Deblur, or VSEARCH clustering of 181 bp COI amplicons) still retains unexpected 'miss' or partial mock variants after denoising, and abundance-based filtering must remove them. Input is raw demultiplexed reads or FASTQ files with no feature table yet — denoising/clustering must precede this filtering step The dataset has no biological mock community, so the per-library fixed integer for the extra filter cannot be empirically derived from 'miss' variant maxima The goal is filtering a reference database (e.g. by clustering radius or taxonomic completeness), not abundance filtering of a feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A two-stage abundance filtering procedure from O'Rourke et al. (2020, Ecology and Evolution) that removes unexpected mock-community sequence variants (e.g. 'miss' and partial ASVs) from denoised/clustering COI metabarcoding feature tables by combining a standard low-abundance filter with a per-library fixed-integer subtraction. metabarcoding/v1 10.1002/ece3.6594
skills.summary: A two-stage abundance filtering procedure from O'Rourke et al. (2020, Ecology and Evolution) that removes unexpected mock-community sequence variants (e.g. 'miss' and partial ASVs) from denoised/clustering COI metabarcoding feature tables by combining a standard low-abundance filter with a per-library fixed-integer subtraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw demultiplexed reads or FASTQ files with no feature table yet — denoising/clustering must precede this filtering step The dataset has no biological mock community, so the per-library fixed integer for the extra filter cannot be empirically derived from 'miss' variant maxima The goal is filtering a reference database (e.g. by clustering radius or taxonomic completeness), not abundance filtering of a feature table

skills.description: Use when profiling shotgun metagenomes with MetaPhlAn 4 and the analysis goal is to quantify or compare prevalence/abundance of uncharacterized (unidentified) SGBs (uSGBs) across cohorts, lifestyles, or host conditions.
skills.name: unidentified-species-bin-quantification
skills.search_text: unidentified-species-bin-quantification Use when profiling shotgun metagenomes with MetaPhlAn 4 and the analysis goal is to quantify or compare prevalence/abundance of uncharacterized (unidentified) SGBs (uSGBs) across cohorts, lifestyles, or host conditions. skills.summary: Quantify the prevalence and abundance of taxonomically unidentified species-level genome bins (uSGBs) in metagenomic cohorts profiled with MetaPhlAn 4, whose extended marker set covers 26,970 SGBs from 1.01M reference and metagenome-assembled genomes, 4,992 of which are taxonomically unidentified at the species level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a species/feature abundance table rather than raw shotgun reads — MetaPhlAn 4 profiling of FASTQ input is the prerequisite step, not re-applicable. When the target community is environmental, nonhost-associated, or under-studied, where sequences may not be captured even by current uSGBs per the article's discussion. skills.description: Use when a denoised QIIME 2 feature table (.qza) and representative sequences (.qza) are available together with sample metadata, and the goal is to test or visualize community separation between metadata-defined groups via UniFrac ordination and PERMANOVA.
skills.name: unifrac-ordination-visualization
skills.search_text: unifrac-ordination-visualization Use when a denoised QIIME 2 feature table (.qza) and representative sequences (.qza) are available together with sample metadata, and the goal is to test or visualize community separation between metadata-defined groups via UniFrac ordination and PERMANOVA. The feature table and representative sequences have not yet been produced by denoising (no .qza artifacts) — UniFrac requires aligned representative sequences, so run qaqc/repseqs steps first. The goal is taxonomic assignment or alpha diversity summarization rather than between-sample (beta) diversity ordination and group-separation testing. The metadata file lacks the grouping columns (e.g., location or size fraction) needed for beta-group-significance PERMANOVA tests. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute UniFrac beta-diversity distance matrices, PCoA ordinations, and PERMANOVA beta-group-significance tests with QIIME 2 to test whether 16S amplicon communities separate by sample metadata groupings (e.g., location: Open Water vs. Western Boundary; size fraction: 0.22-um vs. 5.0-um), and visualize the ordination interactively as an Emperor plot viewable through QIIME 2 viewer. metabarcoding/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac066
skills.summary: Compute UniFrac beta-diversity distance matrices, PCoA ordinations, and PERMANOVA beta-group-significance tests with QIIME 2 to test whether 16S amplicon communities separate by sample metadata groupings (e.g., location: Open Water vs. Western Boundary; size fraction: 0.22-um vs. 5.0-um), and visualize the ordination interactively as an Emperor plot viewable through QIIME 2 viewer.

skills.search_text: weight-divergence-linear-regression Use when evaluating whether taxonomic class weights assembled for one environment remain useful for samples from another: you have per-habitat q2-clawback weight sets, per-combination species-level error rates, and need to model error rate as a linear function of weight divergence. The query samples' source habitat has bespoke q2-clawback weights available — use those directly instead of testing cross-habitat transfer You only need genus-level classification accuracy; the article's species-level error-rate gains (25% to 14%) are the target of this regression, not genus-level behaviour You only need to assemble weights (fetch_Qiita_samples / generate_class_weights) without measuring how weight mismatch degrades accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies how naive Bayes species-level classification accuracy degrades as a function of the divergence between applied taxonomic class weights (e.g. cross-habitat q2-clawback weights) and the source habitat's bespoke weights. The data have not been pre-processed and structural zeros not identified — WLS on raw compositional counts without masking struc.zero entries yields a biased delta Sample sizes are very small (e.g. n = 5 per group), where the article notes ANCOM-BC may not perform well and FDR is not controlled The goal is taxon-specific bias correction (differential sequencing efficiencies, as in SECOM/ANCOM-BC2) rather than the sample-specific sampling-fraction offset of ANCOM-BC v1.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A weighted least squares (WLS) estimator of the sampling-fraction bias term delta in ANCOM-BC, providing both a point estimate of the mean difference of log sampling fractions between groups and a variance approximation that can be benchmarked against the E-M estimate (bias.em). metabarcoding/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-17041-7
skills.summary: A weighted least squares (WLS) estimator of the sampling-fraction bias term delta in ANCOM-BC, providing both a point estimate of the mean difference of log sampling fractions between groups and a variance approximation that can be benchmarked against the E-M estimate (bias.em).
